### 1.1  Club Guarantees and SBLCs


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *In Club Guarantee and SBLC, a consortium of lenders (participants) issues a guarantee or SBLC to the borrower (or associated borrowers) under a single agreement. Each lender in the group shares a portion of a risk that is associated with the Guarantee or SBLC undertaking. The consortium appoints an ...*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Balance Treatment*, *Bank Role*, *Currency*, *Customer*, *Negative Rate*, *Operand*, *Own Share*, *Participant Accounting Type* ... +2 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

In Club Guarantee and SBLC, a consortium of lenders (participants) issues a guarantee or SBLC to the borrower (or associated borrowers) under a single agreement. Each lender in the group shares a portion of a risk that is associated with the Guarantee or SBLC undertaking. The consortium appoints an agent bank (agent) to manage the Guarantee or SBLC undertaking. The Agent liaises with the borrower on behalf of all the lenders in the syndicate and distributes the payments received from the borrower among the lenders.

The agent (also known as issuing bank) issues a single letter of Guarantee or SBLC on behalf of all the participating lenders . The issuing bank generates a schedule for each participant based on their respective percentage of share in the Guarantee or SBLC agreement. The agent bank sometimes bear the credit risk associated with the Guarantee or SBLC.

The main responsibilities of an agent bank includes:

- Monitoring the performance of the borrowing group.
- Monitoring the covenants and notifying the participants.
- Sending notifications to the other participants on events such as issuance of the Guarantee or SBLC undertaking, amendment request interest rate changes, early termination etc.
- Distributing cash flows to other participants upon repayments.

The Participant Property Class defines and manages the participants information for a Guarantee or SBLC. The main bank which grants the undertaking to the customer is the agent bank and the other lenders are the participant banks. These participating banks can have the role as participant, sub-participant or risk participant in the Guarantee or SBLC. A participant (not necessarily the agent) can share its portion wholly or partially with the sub-participants which are the lenders outside the consortium. The Participant Role field in Participant Property Class defines whether the lender is a part of the consortium as a participant), or not (sub-participant).


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This section details the configuration required for Club Guarantees and SBLCs using Participant Property Class.

The Participant Property Class holds the share details of various lenders participating in the club Guarantee or SBLCs. Here users can define the lender’s role and their beneficiary details for paying their share of fees and commissions upon repayment from the borrower.

The Participant Accounting Type field in Participant product condition captures the accounting style for the participants and depending on the value set in this field, the guarantees module performs the accounting entries to maintain the Participant balances. The options in this field are Memo and Contingent. Once defined, Participant Accounting Type cannot be changed later.

When participants are defined for Guarantee or SBLC products, the Balance Treatment field in the Account Property Class is set as Participant while creating an arrangement.


#### 🔧 Working With

This section details the processing of the club Guarantee or SBLCs with respect to the tabs involved in it. Participants vary for each individual arrangement and according to the type and size of the agreement, their share contribution, fees, etc. are agreed upon by the borrower, agent, and the participants. Therefore, all the details in the Participant Property Class are captured at the arrangement level. The following tabs in Participant Property Class allows the user to capture the various Participant details.

The Transact owning bank’s (Own bank) role is defined in the Bank Role field in Participant Property Class , which can either be Agent, Agent Cum Participant or Participant.

The Participant Role field in Participant Property Class defines the participant’s role whether it is a participant or sub-participant. Other information like participant, share amount and so on can be defined in their respective fields as is shown in the screenshot below:

There can be single or multiple participants in a Guarantee or SBLC. The system updates the share percentage of the participants including the own bank’s share amount on validation.

> **⚠️ Note:** The Own Share field needs to be defined when the Banks Role field is set as Participant.

It defines the participant’s settlement instructions like currency specific beneficiary account to credit the participant in case of borrower repayment (can be different for different currencies), payment order product for repayment and so on.

The agent bank uses the Skim rate to assign different commissions to the participants than what is being repaid by the borrower. These skims can be reported to a different income P&L. Skim tab records the participant skim details. If the skim is not defined, then the commissions charged to the applicant is distributed to the participants based on their share percentages.

In Skim, Operand is set to Sub as the Skim Rate is subtracted from the rate being repaid by the borrower and distributed to the participants. Therefore,

The skim rates can be different for different participants and for different properties for the same participant.

The Negative Rate field specifies if the Skims must be blocked in case the All-in-Rate results in a negative rate after deducting the skims. The options allowed in the Negative Rate field are:

1. No - Rate for the participant is set as zero and commissions are not shared with them.
2. Block Margin - Rate for the participant is applied as borrower rate and skim rate is ignored.

The agent bank distributes the fees collected from the applicants amongst the participants based on their share percentage. However, some fees and charges may not be distributed among all the participants, or the rates might vary for different participants. In such cases, Charges tab in Participant Property Class is used to define either the rate, ratio or percentage of charge that is distributed to each participant.

Rate - Specifies the fee rate per participant. The rate is calculated on the current commitment amount of that participant.

Amount - Specifies the fee amount per participant.

Ratio - Specifies the fee ratio per participant. For each participant, it is calculated as a percentage of the total fee charged to the applicant.

The below screenshot shows that the 60 percentage of the STAMPFEE collected from the applicant is paid to Intercapital (100280), and the rest 40 percentage to the Citigroup (100299). Similarly, USD 2,500 is given to Intercapital (100280) as AMENDMENTFEE. If the fields in Charge tab are not defined, the system distributes all the charges among the participants based on their share percentages.

> **⚠️ Note:** Fees paid by the participants (Rate and Amount values) can be greater than the total fees collected from the applicant.

This tab captures the own bank and agent bank’s beneficiary details on the following conditions.

- When the own bank’s role is agent or agent cum participant, then the own bank’s beneficiary details are captured.
- When the own bank’s role is participant, then both the own bank and agent bank’s beneficiary details are captured.

> **⚠️ Note:** The agent bank’s beneficiary details are captured only when the own bank’s role is participant.

1. When Own Bank Role Is Agent and Participant Accounting Type is Memo

The bank registers and issues a performance guarantee for USD 1 million. The Bank Role field is set as agent. ABN Amro Securities and Nomura Securities are the two participants with a share of USD 750,000 and USD 250,000 respectively. The system collects a new arrangement fee of USD 200 from the applicant and distributes it among the participants on a pro-rata basis. The registration and issuance of the new arrangement is shown in the below screenshots.

The below screenshot shows the Guarantee Overview screen with the participants after authorising the arrangement.

The individual Participant Overview screens for the participants are shown in the below screenshots.

The balances for the borrower and Participants are listed in the Contract wise Balances ( EB.CONTRACT.BALANCES.BALANCE) enquiry as shown in the below screenshots.

The system raises information balances with the suffix INF for customer and for participants as the Participant Accounting Type field is set as ‘Memo’. The new arrangement fee is distributed among the two participants based on their share percentages as the Charges tab of Participant Property class was not defined.

1. When Own Bank Role is Agent Cum Participant

The bank registers and issues a financial guarantee for USD 1 million. The Bank Role field is set as agent cum participant. ABC securities and MNO securities are the two participants with a share of USD 500,000 and USD 200,000 respectively. Own bank has a share of USD 300,000. A new arrangement fee of USD 200 is collected from the participant. The new arrangement fee distributed with RST securities and XYZ securities are USD 100 and USD 200, respectively.

The Contract wise balances for the arrangement is shown in the screenshot below:

The system collects a new arrangement fee of USD 200 from the applicant which is less than the charges repaid to the customers. The agent pays the Skim to the participants. Skim is the difference in the two charge amounts that are collected from the borrower and repaid to the participants.

The bank registers and issues a financial guarantee for USD 1 million. The Bank Role field is set as participant. The own bank has a share of USD 300,000 and the sub-participant has a share of USD 100,000.

### 1.2  Early Termination of Guarantees and SBLCs


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *In Transact, early termination activity is used to close or cancel a Guarantee or SBLC undertaking before its expiry. On termination, all the accrued fees are made due for payment. The system collects all the dues associated with the underlying Guarantee or SBLC along with the early termination fee ...*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Arrangement*, *Expire To Maturity Period*, *Expiry*, *Maturity Date*, *Waive Bill Type*, *Waive Class*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

In Transact, early termination activity is used to close or cancel a Guarantee or SBLC undertaking before its expiry. On termination, all the accrued fees are made due for payment. The system collects all the dues associated with the underlying Guarantee or SBLC along with the early termination fee if any. The system discharges the bank’s liability on the termination of the guarantee.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

Banks can collect an early termination fee from the applicant by using Charge and Activity Charge Property Classes. Banks can set an Activity Charge for Early Termination and when they trigger early termination activity the fee is made-due for collection.

Refer Activity Charges in Arrangement Architecture to know more about the Activity Charges.


#### 🔧 Working With

Bank triggers the early termination from the New Activity tab in the Arrangement Overview screen. Users must input the current system date to initiate early termination. Users can also update or change the settlement instructions for auto settlement of charges or commissions that are made-due by triggering the early termination activity. After early termination, the system updates the Expiry and Maturity Date of the underlying arrangement in the AA.ARR.TERM.AMOUNT application to the current date and the Expire To Maturity Period field is updated as 0.

The system reverses the contingent entries or the commitment balances for the Guarantees or SBLC arrangement and releases the bank from its liability.

The below screenshot shows that the contract balances of the EB.CONTRACT.BALANCES.BALANCE enquiry for a guarantee arrangement after early termination. The current and total commitment balances for the arrangement becomes zero.

When the customer enters the settlement instructions for auto-settlement of commissions and charges, the system settles all the bills and moves the arrangement to pending closure status.

If the settlement instructions are not given, all the fees and charges are made-due after early termination and the arrangement moves to expired status. The status moves to pending closure only after the settlement of the dues.

If the customer triggers the early termination within the cooling period, then all the accrued interest and charges can be written off by providing appropriate details in the Waive Class and Waive Bill Type fields of the Closure Property Class.


#### 📋 Tasks

Related topics:

- Perform Early Termination of Issued Guarantee (AA) (Corporate)

Guarantee or SBLC arrangement can be terminated early using GUARANTEE.EARLY.TERMINATE.ARRANGEMENT activity. The user must settle the unpaid dues before early termination.

### 1.3  Guarantee


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Guarantee imposes a primary obligation on the issuer to compensate the beneficiary on demand when the applicant / instructing party fails to perform the contract. Standby Letter of Credit (SBLC) is a legal undertaking that Guarantees a bank's commitment of payment to a beneficiary on presentation of...*
> 
> **Applications:** `CURRENCY`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Accounting Mode*, *Accrue Amort*, *Accrue Period*, *Amount*, *Applicable Rules*, *Applicable Rules Text*, *Arrangement*, *Available Amount* ... +20 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

Guarantee imposes a primary obligation on the issuer to compensate the beneficiary on demand when the applicant / instructing party fails to perform the contract. Standby Letter of Credit (SBLC) is a legal undertaking that Guarantees a bank's commitment of payment to a beneficiary on presentation of the valid claim request.

The three major parties to Guarantee or SBLC are :

- Principal or Applicant or Instructing Party – Requests the issuance of Guarantee or SBLC, that is, the liable party of the guarantee or SBLC undertaking.
- Guarantor – Bank or any other institution or a person who issues the Guarantee or SBLC.
- Beneficiary – Party in whose favour the Guarantee or SBLC is issued.

Guarantees or SBLC product line is a part of the Temenos Transact Corporate Lending suite of products in AA, which provides various features that a financial institution can offer to its customer. It supports an entire range of Guarantees or SBLC business or transaction needs with configurable conditions. Temenos Transact is flexible to allow adding a new Guarantee or SBLC products to it to meet the bank’s future requirements.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The Guarantee Product Line provides a high-level definition of the business components (Property Classes) that are required to construct the Guarantee or SBLC products.

The Guarantee Product Line is pre-defined and is delivered by Temenos. Existing users are aware that the Product Line is defined by the Property Classes present in it . The bank or the financial institution can use these building blocks of functionality to offer their Guarantee or SBLC product to their customers. The line attributes for Guarantee Product Line are as follows:

| Line Attributes | Description |
|---|---|
| CCY | Indicates the Product Line deals with the amount |
| Replay | Indicates the Product Line that supports reverse and replay |

The Group Level attribute in AA.PRODUCT.GROUP of the Guarantees Product Line is used to differentiate between a contingent liability and a contingent asset. The Group Level is set as Contingent Liability when issuing a Guarantee or SBLC.

The Guarantees Product Line supports the following Property classes:

The Customer Property Class is used to record the parties involved in the Guarantee or SBLC. There can be multiple parties to the Guarantee or SBLC undertaking. Both the applicants and the instructing party are the beneficial owners, who are the customers of the Guarantee or SBLC undertaking. Beneficiary of the Guarantee or SBLC and receiving bank are the other parties involved in the guarantee or SBLC undertaking.

It is a mandatory property class of the Guarantees Product Line . Only single account property can be defined for each guarantee product.

It is used to,

- Specify the account description or title and the classification details of the Guarantee or SBLC contract.
- Register and maintain the underlying account record that is used to store the Guarantee commitment balances.

The Account property class supports the following balance prefix and suffixes in the Guarantees Product Line.

- Due
- Aged
- Unallocated Credit

When a new guarantee is issued, the following commitment balances are raised.

- Total Commitment - This debit balance represents the total commitment offered to the borrower of the Guarantee or SBLC contract by the financial institution. The increase or decrease in the commitment amount affects the balance.
- Current Commitment - This debit balance represents the amount that remains unutilised by the guarantee contract.

The total and current commitment balances are reversed at the expiry of the Guarantee or SBLC .

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Amount | Specifies the amount of the guarantee contract. It cannot be zero or negative |
| Expiry Date | Specifies the validity or expiry date of the Guarantee contract. Indicates that the banks can define a relative date with respect to the arrangement date of the contract as the expiry date of the contract (For example, R_ARRANGEMENT+6M ). |
| Update.Commit.Limit | Indicates that the limit is attached to a guarantee product to control the exposure of the bank to a particular customer. System defaults this attribute to ‘YES’ if the guarantee is linked to a limit |
| Expire To Maturity Period | Defines the claim period (grace period beyond the validity period of the Guarantee to make a demand for the default from the bank) for the Guarantee or SBLC contract. It can be either in days, weeks, months or years. |
| Term | Defines the period until when the Guarantee or SBLC arrangement remains valid and negotiable. It can be either in days (D), weeks (W), months (M), or years (Y). |

The Charge is an optional Property Class and is used for levying charges and commissions on the guarantee contract.

Multiple charges can be levied under a Guarantee or SBLC undertaking. These charges can be a flat or a calculated charge (usually a percentage of the guarantee amount). The charge currency can be either the same or different to the Guarantee arrangement. Various charges that can be levied on a guarantee contract are listed below:

- One time charge – Guarantee processing fees, Fee collection on Stamp due under the issuance of hard copy guarantee, transaction fee, ad-hoc fees, and Legal approval Fee etc.
- Charge based on an event – Issuance of guarantee Fee, Amendment Fee, guarantee cancellation fee etc.
- Scheduled Charges – Recovery of Issuance fee at the beginning of every quarter.
- Rule break charge – Penal Charges for overdue fee or commission .

These charges are collected upfront or amortised over a period or collected at the end during the maturity of the guarantee contract.

The Activity Charges is an optional Property Class for the Guarantees Product Line. It allows calculation of charges and commissions based on certain activities performed on the arrangement and requires a Charge Property to be attached for each activity.

The below are the examples of Activity Charges under a Guarantee or SBLC undertaking.

• Issuance Fee

• Amendment Fee

The Charge Override is an optional Property Class for the Guarantees Product Line. The Guarantee or SBLC commission is negotiated or waived by the banks at the arrangement level by triggering the charge override. This waiver or negotiation of the commission is an ad-hoc request.

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Swift | It is an optional field, which is used to capture the terms and conditions details of the guarantee. It is an optional text field which is limited to 150 lines and each line can hold a maximum of 65 characters. |
| Applicable Rules | It is a mandatory field, which is used to set the pre-defined codes. It holds the details of the governing law, under which capacity of the Guarantee or SBLC undertaking is issued. Valid predefined codes are: ISPR NONE OTHR UCPR URDG |
| Applicable Rules Text | It is a text field that captures the narrative clauses when the predefined code is OTHR. |

It is an optional property class in Guarantees. It is used to specify the exchange rate that needs to be applied to a guarantee or standby letter of credit arrangement when the undertaking is in a different currency than the facility arrangement.

Facility can be in one currency and the borrower can make a drawing under the facility in another predefined currency. For example, a facility commitment is in GBP, but the system allows the borrower to make a Guarantee or SBLC under it in GBP and USD. When the system issues a drawing (in USD), the exchange rate is used to convert the USD amount to GBP which is the Facility currency. The exchange rate determines the facility utilization amount by the guarantee or SBLC when it is issued under the facility in a different currency.

The system automatically defaults the exchange rate from the CURRENCY application when the rates are not defined during arrangement creation. Based on the value in the On Activity & Exchange Rate Tolerance fields in Exchange Rate Property Class, banks can override the defaulted rates as per their requirement. The exchange rate tolerance is usually defined at the facility level, which acts as a spread to the applied exchange rate. When new exchange rate falls

- Outside the tolerance level, then the new rate is applied on the arrangement.
- Within the tolerance level, then the existing exchange rate remains the same.

The following are the examples that supports the exchange rate tolerance.

When the bank has a bilateral facility as follows:

- Facility commitment amount = GBP 10,000,000.00
- Guarantee Issued under the facility =USD 2,500,000.00

An FX rate of 1.22 is entered in Exchange Rate field of Exchange Rate property class while creating the arrangement. The Facility utilization is

The available Facility balance after the drawing is shown below:

When the FX rate is entered as 1.24 (by using the Change Exchange Rate activity) on April 3, then the new facility utilization amount is shown below:

The available facility balance was GBP 7,950,819.67. After the repricing, the available balance is GBP 7,983,870.97 (GBP 10,000,000.00 – GBP 2,016,129.03) as the exchange rate changes from 1.22 to 1.24.

When the bank has a bilateral facility as follows:

- Facility commitment amount = GBP 10,000,000.00.
- The FX Tolerance is set as 1 percent.
- Guarantee issued under the facility =USD 2,500,000.00

An FX rate of 1.22 is entered in Exchange Rate field of Exchange Rate property class while creating the arrangement. The Facility utilization is

The available Facility balance after the drawing is shown below.

When the FX rate is entered as 1.215 (by using the Change Exchange Rate activity) on April 3, with the FX Tolerance set as 1%, the rate can move between the following spread:

1% of the previous FX rate of 1.22 = 0.0122 (1% of 1.22).

The floor and cap values for exchange rate spread is calculated by the system using this value of 0.0122 as below:

The new FX rate can be between 1.2078 (1.22-0.0122) and 1.2322 (1.22+0.0122)

The rate of 1.215 is within that tolerance, and therefore the existing FX rate of 1.22 remains and the facility utilization balance stays the same. The system applies the FX Tolerance rate against the actual FX rate currently in place for each subsequent repricing. In this example, it is 1.22.

When the Bank has a Bilateral Facility as follows:

- Facility commitment balance = £10,000,000.00
- The FX Tolerance is set as 1%.
- Guarantee issued under the facility =USD 2,500,000.00

An FX rate of 1.22 is entered while creating the arrangement in the Exchange Rate property class. The Facility utilization is

The available Facility balance after the drawing is shown below.

First Repricing Beyond the tolerance

The FX rate is entered as 1.24 on April 3 using the change exchange rate activity. The FX Tolerance has been set as 1%, that is the FX rate can move between the following spread on the previous FX rate:

The new FX rate can be between 1.2078 and 1.2322. The rate of 1.24 is not within that tolerance and so the new FX rate of 1.24 is used. New Facility utilization amount is shown below.

The Available balance is GBP 7,950,819.67. After the repricing, the available balance is GBP 7,983,870.97 (GBP 10,000,000.00 – GBP 2,016,129.03). For the next repricing, the system applies the FX Tolerance rate against the actual FX rate currently in place, which in this example is 1.24.

Second Repricing Within the tolerance

The FX rate is entered as 1.245 on May 4 using the change exchange rate activity.

1% of the previous FX rate of 1.24 = 0.0124

The new FX rate can be between 1.2276 and 1.2524. The rate of 1.245 is within that tolerance, and therefore the existing FX rate and the facility utilization balance remains the same. For the next repricing, FX Tolerance rate is applied against the actual FX rate currently in place, which in this example is 1.24.

Refer Exchange Property Class to know more about the Exchange Property Class.

It is an optional Property Class and is used for enabling the rule-based restrictions at the arrangement level.

The Interest is an optional Property Class for Guarantees Product Line. It enables charging interest style fees or commissions for the undertaking . The commissions or fees are as follows:

- Flat rate
- Variable rate
- Periodic rate

The Interest condition is forward dated. The bank or financial institution defines different Interest conditions at different periods during the lifetime of the contract.

It is an optional Property Class and is used to capture taxes that are to be applied on commission or charges of the Guarantee or SBLC based on the Tax code or condition.

Payment Schedule is an optional Property Class for Guarantees Product Line and used to schedule the collection of fees and commissions in the following ways:

- Collected on a pre-defined frequency by specifying the start date and end date using fixed dates or relative options such as R_Arrangement, R_Expiry, R_Maturity, and so on. without defining frequencies.
- Collected with minimum and maximum tariffs and can be collected beyond expiry.
- Collection of commissions is waived when it falls below the minimum tariff.
- Interest style fees or commissions are collected as upfront fees or commissions.

It is an optional Property Class, which is used for sequencing the order of bills payment. It is also used for sequencing the order of settlement when the customers pay the charges or commissions. When a customer makes a payment, the entire due amount may not be satisfied. The Payment Rules Property Class is used to define the method by which a single payment is applied to multiple bills and multiple amount types.

It is an optional Property Class and is used for sequencing the order of bills payment for settlement when charges or commissions are paid to the customers by the bank.

It is a mandatory Property Class for the Guarantees Product Line. It is used to define,

- Accounting rules for the Product and controls the link between the accounting events generated by the Property Class actions
- Accounting allocation rules to be applied to these events at every stage of the Guarantee or SBLC life cycle.

It is an optional Property Class and is used to enable the ageing process of the outstanding bills when it is not paid by the customers. It allows the user to define the ageing period, statuses, and accounting treatment of the outstanding balances.

The Settlement is an optional Property Class, which is used for specifying the settlement instructions of commission and charges of guarantee or SBLC undertaking. Settlement can be handled by linking any Temenos Transact account or the account and bank details of another bank by using Direct Debit and beneficiary of the customer. The Default Settlement Account is considered as the default account for both Pay-in and Pay-out activities if the Pay-in or Pay-out accounts are not specified. If the Pay-in or Pay-out accounts are specified then those accounts take precedence over the specified default settlement account.

It is an optional Property Class and is used to map the transaction codes of the Temenos Transact to AA.ARRANGEMNT.ACTIVITY, so that the non-AA modules can trigger the relevant AA activities.

It is an optional Property Class and is used for enabling fees, charges subvention, subsidies, discounts, or waivers in a Guarantee or SBLC undertaking if the borrower satisfies certain criteria or rules.

Banks can allow 1% concession on the guarantee issuance fees to all the corporate customers belonging to the Pharmaceutical sector. So, when the standard issuance fee is 5% of the guarantee amount, all the customers belonging to the pharmaceutical sector can avail of Guarantee products at 4% of the guarantee amount.

| Branch | Issuance fee collected |
|---|---|
| North | USD 800 |
| No branch set | USD 1000 |

It is an optional Property Class and is used to define multi-dimensional pricing for interest style fees and commissions which is then applied to the Guarantee or SBLC at the arrangement level.

Pricing Grids are configured by selecting criteria, which is used to determine the margin (for interest) and rate (for fee) to apply to a Property. It is comprised of elements that determine the criteria for one or more elements to specify what is set on the interest condition. The user can select both the user-defined data criteria and their order of precedence

It is an optional Property Class and is used to attach the limit record to the Guarantee or SBLC undertaking to control the exposure of the Guarantee or SBLC. Banks can set up single or shared limits as per their preference.

A record in Limit is created in the LIMIT application and then attached to the Guarantee product using the Limit Product Condition at the product or arrangement level.

It is an optional Property Class for the Guarantees Product Line and is used to specify the account officer or relationship manager for the Transact Customers. It enables the user to define:

- Product
- Arrangement specific officers
- Officer’s roles
- Primary officer
- Additional officer

It is an optional Property Class and is used to evaluate the customer’s eligibility conditions for a guarantee or SBLC product based on certain rules. In Transact, a record in EB.CONTEXT is created based on which, the rules are defined using Rules Engine. EB.RULES.VERSION and EB.RULES are created in the system after the rules are validated.

Discounts on guarantee options are available only for customers who belong to the iron and steel sector.

It is an optional Property Class for the guarantee’s Product Line which allows banks to extend the core processing of arrangement activities by adding user-defined routines.

It is an optional Property Class and used to capture or adjust the commitment balances while migrating or porting the guarantee or SBLC contracts from Legacy to Transact. The actions such as Capture Bill, Adjust Bill, etc., helps in capturing the bill and its balances into the new system.

It is a mandatory Property Class and is used to specify the Guarantee or SBLC arrangement account’s closure conditions.

If the bank prefers to close the account in ten days after the Guarantee or SBLC contract’s expiry date with no outstanding balances, then the guarantee arrangement is closed automatically or manually, based on what is defined at the closure product condition.

It is an optional Property Class that is used to define the look and feel of the Transact screens, that is, the types of Transact versions (screens) displays for each property during various arrangement activities. The versions are defined at Property class, Property and Activity levels.


#### 🔧 Working With

This section details about the Guarantees.


##### Registering the Issuance of a Guarantee or SBLC

Registering the issuance of guarantee involves capturing the basic details of the Guarantee or SBLC undertakings such as the parties involved, amount, expiry date, fee, commission and the terms and conditions.

The Guarantee or SBLC flow begins when registering the issuance of undertaking is registered by the issuing bank to cover the applicant’s risk of non-performance or non-payment of dues. The undertaking is booked as a contingent liability in the issuing bank books.

The Customer property class records all the parties involved in a Guarantee or SBLC undertaking along with their respective roles. The applicant and the instructing party of a Guarantee or SBLC are defined in the Customer attribute and their role in the Customer Role attribute. The Other Party attribute and its associated fields capture the other parties involved in the Guarantee or SBLC undertaking such as the beneficiary or receiving bank.

The attributes of the Swift Property class captures the contractual details of a Guarantee or SBLC undertaking including the terms & conditions.

The Amount attribute in the Term Amount property class is captures the commitment amount of a Guarantee or SBLC undertaking. The expiry date of a Guarantee or SBLC is mentioned in the Expiry Date attribute. Banks can also define a relative date with respect to the arrangement date of the contract as the expiry date of the undertaking (For example, R_ARRANGEMENT+6M). The Expire To Maturity Period attribute defines the claim to expiry period for the undertaking and the system calculates the maturity date of the Guarantee or SBLC undertaking by adding the Expire To Maturity Period to the Expiry Date of the contract.

If Term is defined instead of Expiry Date , on validating the arrangement, the system automatically defaults the Expiry Date by adding the Term to the Effective Day of the contract. The system defaults the Term automatically when Expiry Date is defined by subtracting the Effective Date from the Expiry Date.

Banks can define either the Term or Expiry Date during arrangement creation. If Term is defined system automatically defaults the corresponding Expiry date and vice-versa.


###### Charges & Commissions

Banks collect Guarantee or SBLC fees based on the risk that is associated with the undertaking and collects other processing and handling fees. These charges and commissions (interest style fees) are configured and collected in AA by making use of property classes such as Charge, Interest, Activity Charges and so on.

Multiple charges can be levied under a guarantee or SBLC undertaking. These charges can be collected upfront, scheduled on a regular frequency, on the occurrence of a specific activity or on breaching certain terms and conditions of the product.

The charges are fixed or calculated or a combination of both and are calculated on tiered amounts.

Banks can accrue or amortise the charges over a period. Charges can be amortised by setting the Accrue Amort field is ‘AMORT’ and the Accrue Period as ‘MATURITY’ or defining a valid period (such as 1M, 1Y etc.) in the Account Property Class.

Booking of charge to income (PL) is amortised and the income is distributed to numerous periods based on the amortisation term set in the AA.PRD.DES.ACCOUNTING record and the accrual frequency set in the AA.ACCRUAL.FREQUENCY for the specific Charge Property.

If the Accrue Amort field is set to ‘AMORT’ and the Accrue Period is set to ‘1Y’, then the system amortises the charge till the end of the defined Accrue Period and the accrual depends on the frequency set for the Charge Property. A record in EB.ACCRUAL is created when a charge is amortised and holds the details of amortisation of charges such as the amount of charge, charge property, start or end date of amortisation, frequency, and accrual particulars.

The charge amount can be in a currency that is different from the currency of Guarantee or SBLC based on the bank’s requirements. If the currency defined in the arrangement and the currency of the charge is different, then the system raises an override when the customer commits the arrangement.

The system converts the base amount to charge currency equivalent and calculates the charge amount. The final charge amount is again converted to the requesting currency equivalent. The converted amount is calculated using the mid-rate.

The Tier Groups field defines the calculation method of charge amount for the currency. This field accepts two values namely, BANDS and LEVELS.

Rule Break Charges:

Banks specify periodic rules in specific product conditions. For example, penal charges for overdue fees or commissions. When the user links such periodic rules in a Product Condition, it is possible to link a Charge Property to collect it when the rule is broken. The charge can be a fixed amount or calculated on a base amount.

Activity Charges:

It defines the charges that need to be applied when an activity is triggered on the arrangement. A charge property needs to be attached to each of the said activities and when the said activity is triggered , banks collect the charges.

Issuance fee is collected during registering the issuance of the Guarantee or SBLC, or Amendment fee is collected when there is any amendment to the Guarantee or SBLC commitment amount or any amendment to the expiry date of the Guarantee or SBLC.

The charges applied to certain activities are grouped and collected in regular frequencies.

Commissions (Interest style fees) are levied on a Guarantee or SBLC undertaking using the Interest Property class. Banks levy fixed, floating, periodic, or custom interest rates on the Guarantee or SBLC undertaking. Margins are added to the above base rates as per the requirements.

The interest rates are calculated daily by defining in the Interest Basis field. Banks define a compounding frequency for the Interest rates.

Commissions or Interest style fees are scheduled to be collected at regular intervals by defining the Payment frequency in the Payment Schedule property class. Banks can define a start and end date for collecting the interest amount in the Payment Schedule property class.

When the bank sets the Accounting Mode attribute as ‘Advanced’ in the Interest Property Class and the Payment Mode field to ‘Advance’ in AA. PAYMENT.TYPE, then the commissions are collected as upfront fees during the creation of the Guarantee or SBLC arrangement .

The bank defines the forward dated interest conditions that take effect at different periods during the lifetime of the contract as the Interest property class Type is set as Forward Dated

Assuming that the bank issuing the Guarantee or SBLC chooses to debit the commission of the underlying Guarantee or SBLC at the time of issuance of the Guarantee or SBLC, that is, the commission is collected upfront on the arrangement start day.

Issue date: 24/02/2020

Expiry date: 24/06/2020

Rate 0.15% per month to be charged upfront

Amount: USD 100,000

Interest Basis: E

Mode : Advance

On 24th Feb 2020, the commission amount USD 50 {100,000*0.15%*(121/365)} is collected as an upfront fee and transferred to the bank’s P&L.


###### Expiry of the Guarantee or SBLC

Expiry Date is defined in the Term Amount property class. It is the period until which the Guarantee arrangement remains negotiable. On reaching expiry, the Guarantee status is marked as ‘Expired’. Reversal of the liability balances occurs only after the arrangement reaches maturity. On the maturity date of the Guarantee or SBLC, the bank is released from all its contingent liabilities and the system raises a credit entry to reverse the contingent liability of the bank. The maturity date of the Guarantee or SBLC arrangement is calculated by adding the Expire to Maturity Period to the Expiry date of the undertaking.

The Expiry Date and Maturity Date of the arrangement are the same if the Expire to Maturity Period of the undertaking is not defined or 0. After maturity, the Guarantee or SBLC is moved to ‘Pending Closure’ if all the charges & commissions are settled. If all the charges & commissions are not settled, the status is moved to ‘Expired’.


###### Amendment of Guarantee or SBLC

Banks can amend the Guarantee or SBLC commitment amount and its expiry date after registering the issuance of the Guarantee or SBLC when requested by the concerned parties.

Increase or Decrease of the commitment amount:

- Banks use the GUARANTEE-INCREASE-TERM.AMOUNT & GUARANTEE-DECREASE-TERM.AMOUNT activities to increase or decrease the Guarantee or SBLC commitment amounts respectively.
- The Change Amount attribute in the Term Amount Property Class is used to increase or decrease the commitment amount of the Guarantee or SBLC arrangement.
- The Change Amount attribute represents the amount to be increased or decreased on the original amount.
- The input in this attribute must be greater than zero to increase the commitment amount and less than zero to decrease the commitment amount.

- The Total and Current commitment balances and the Limit details are updated based on the increase or decrease in the Guarantee or SBLC amount.
- Any calculated commissions or charges associated with the Guarantee or SBLC commitment amount are recalculated and are made due for collection.

> **⚠️ Note:** When the commissions are already paid upfront, the system does not recalculate the excess amount paid by the applicant for a refund.

Change of the Guarantee or SBLC expiry date:

- Bank extend or curtail the expiry date (term) of the Guarantee or SBLC undertaking using the Change Term activity.
- GUARANTEES-CHANGE.TERM-TERMAMOUNT activity is used to change the Expiry Date and the Expire to Maturity Period of the Guarantee or SBLC arrangement.

- During extension of the Guarantee or SBLC Expiry Date, commissions are recalculated, and the additional commission amount is made-due for collection using Payment Schedule.

### 1.4  Misc


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Guarantee imposes a primary obligation on the issuer to compensate the beneficiary on demand when the applicant / instructing party fails to perform the contract. Standby Letter of Credit (SBLC) is a legal undertaking that Guarantees a bank's commitment of payment to a beneficiary on presentation of...*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction


#### 📖 Introduction

Guarantee imposes a primary obligation on the issuer to compensate the beneficiary on demand when the applicant / instructing party fails to perform the contract. Standby Letter of Credit (SBLC) is a legal undertaking that Guarantees a bank's commitment of payment to a beneficiary on presentation of the valid claim request.

The three major parties to Guarantee or SBLC are :

- Principal or Applicant or Instructing Party – Requests the issuance of Guarantee or SBLC, that is, the liable party of the guarantee or SBLC undertaking.
- Guarantor – Bank or any other institution or a person who issues the Guarantee or SBLC.
- Beneficiary – Party in whose favour the Guarantee or SBLC is issued.

Guarantees or SBLC product line is a part of the Temenos Transact Corporate Lending suite of products in AA, which provides various features that a financial institution can offer to its customer. It supports an entire range of Guarantees or SBLC business or transaction needs with configurable conditions. Temenos Transact is flexible to allow adding a new Guarantee or SBLC products to it to meet the bank’s future requirements.


##### Product Configuration

This is covered as part of feature configuration. There is no specific product configuration.


##### Illustrating Model Parameters

Model Parameters are not applicable for this module.


##### Illustrating Model Products

Guarantees Product Line provides Financial Guarantee, Financial SBLC, Performance Guarantee, and Performance SBLC functionality for Temenos Transact . This module allows the user to create Financial Guarantee, Financial SBLC, Performance Guarantee, and Performance SBLC by using the AA Framework under Guarantees Product Line.

| S.No. | Product Name | Product Attributes |
|---|---|---|
| 1. | Contingent Liabilities | Financial Guarantee Financial SBLC Performance Guarantee Performance SBLC |

### 1.5  Share Transfer in Guarantee and SBLC


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *In a Club Guarantee and SBLC, some banks in the consortium prefer to either reduce their share in the syndication or to completely sell off their share, by transferring the share to an existing bank in the syndication or to a completely new bank. Share transfer in Arrangement Architecture helps the ...*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Arrangement*, *Buy Participant*, *Own Bank*, *Participant Role*, *Sell Participant*, *Share Percentage*, *Transfer Amount*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

In a Club Guarantee and SBLC, some banks in the consortium prefer to either reduce their share in the syndication or to completely sell off their share, by transferring the share to an existing bank in the syndication or to a completely new bank. Share transfer in Arrangement Architecture helps the bank to achieve this.

Transfer of shares can be done in two ways:

- Assignment sell - The transfer is done with the knowledge of the borrower and the other participants. The new lender who buys the shares is the participant.
- Participation sell - The transfer need not be done with the knowledge of the borrower and other participants. The new lender who bought the shares are the silent or sub-participant in the undertaking.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

Share transfer is a transaction class. It is not necessary to be attached at the product designer level to perform share transfer at the arrangement level unlike the other property classes. Hence, the user need not configure anything to initiate share transfer.


#### 🔧 Working With

The participants in a Club Guarantee and SBLC can sell their share either wholly or partially to others using the share transfer in AA.

The user initiates the share transfer from the Guarantees Overview screen. Share Transfer can be done on a back date, current date, or a future date. The user inputs the Share Transfer’s effective date in the Share Transfer window. The system prompts to define the buyer and seller information in the Share Transfer Property Class upon validation as shown in the below screenshot.

If the Own Bank is the buyer or seller, then the user must select the Buy or Sell options respectively.

The user defines the Participant account number in the Sell Participant field, if share transfer is initiated for a participant. The buyer details are defined in the Buy Participant field. The buyer is either an existing participant or a new participant.

For a new participant, the user updates the buyer role under the Participant Role field and the beneficiary details in the Settlement Instructions tab as a part of the share transfer activity.

The share amount is defined in the Transfer Amount field.

Buy Back option allows the Agent bank to buy all the shares from the participants or the sub-participants While doing a share buy-back, all other fields in Share Transfer Property Class are left blank. After buy-back, the system maintains only the due and delinquent balances of the participants And the commitment balances of the participants become zero.

The Skims tab records the Skim rates for the buyer.

> **⚠️ Note:** Share transfer amount cannot be greater than the participants commitment amount.

Transferring Shares from own bank to participant

The bank registers and issues a financial guarantee for USD 1 million. The user sets the Bank Role is set as agent cum participant and its share is USD 500,000 (50%). ABN Amro (100112) and Nomura Securities (100114) are the two other participants with a share of USD 200,000 (20%) and USD 300,000 (30%) respectively. The Guarantee Overview screen and the generated accounting entries for the participants are shown in the screenshots below.

Now, own bank wants to sell its share worth USD 50,000 to ABN Amro securities. This is achieved by initiating a share transfer from the Guarantee Overview screen. As own bank is the seller, the user sets the Own Bank field to Sell and the information of ABN Amro securities are captured in the Buy Participant field.

The accounting entries below after share transfer shows that the own bank’s share has reduced by USD 50,000 and that of ABN Amro securities has increased by the same.

The Share Percentage field of own bank and ABN Amro securities after share transfer is 45 percentage & 25 percentage respectively. This is seen in the Guarantees Overview screen as shown in the screenshot below.

Transferring Shares from Participant

In the above example, if Nomura securities sells its share worth USD 100,000 to ABN Amro securities, then in the Share Transfer window the ID of Nomura securities’ is mentioned in the Sell Participant field and that of ABN Amro securities in the Buy Participant field.

The accounting entries post share transfer is shown in the screenshot below.

The updated share percentage of the participants is seen in the Guarantees Overview screen as shown in the screenshot below.

> **⚠️ Note:** When Guarantees or SBLCs are created under a facility, share transfer is captured only at the facility level. The share transfer captured at the facility level flows down to the underlying guarantees and SBLCs.


#### 📋 Tasks

Related topics:

- Perform Share Transfer for Standalone Guarantee (AA) (Corporate)

Banks prefer to reduce or completely sell their share in club guarantee, by transferring it to the existing banks or to a completely new bank using share transfer.

### 2.2  ProductBuilder


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The Arrangement Architecture (AA) module provides a flexible framework that allows to create new Temenos Transact modules. The application provides a business component based architecture for managing products. Arrangements is part of the Retail Banking suite of products.*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction


#### 📖 Introduction

The Arrangement Architecture (AA) module provides a flexible framework that allows to create new Temenos Transact modules. The application provides a business component based architecture for managing products. Arrangements is part of the Retail Banking suite of products.

The main features of the AA module are:

- Ability to build families of products
- Ability to inherit properties from the product family structure
- Ability to determine the properties that a product is comprised of
- Control of default values to be applied for product arrangements
- Dated conditions for products
- Full control of scope of negotiation between product and arrangement conditions
- Control of negotiation of attributes over time
- Design or Proof or Publish life-cycle for product management

Read the Property Classes user guide for more details on individual classes.

---


### 2.3  Charges and Commissions


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Sections:** 🔧 Working With


#### 🔧 Working With

The users can configure the charges to be due on the first, next, or last payment. The charges are triggered on occurrence of a specific activity and it is due to the customer as per the configuration.

If a user has set the charge collection on the next payment, but the system levies the charge on creation of the contract, it is still due only on the next payment date, that is, it is not due immediately. It is scheduled to be collected on the first payment date as per the schedule configuration.

Alternatively, if a user configures the collection of charge on the first payment, but the first payment date lapses when the customer triggers an activity, the system raises an override and schedules the charge along with the next upcoming payment.


##### Collecting Fee for External Event

The Record Event activity class registers an external event manually in the system. In asset financing, the financial institution can collect a delivery fee when the asset is delivered to the lessee or customer. This is an external event and not connected to the system. The user can manually register the event in the system using ASSET.FINANCE-RECORD.EVENT-ARRANGEMENT. Similarly, below activities are used for collecting charges for external events:

- Failed collection of the asset: At the end of the term, if the lessor is unable to collect the asset, the financial institution levies a charge for the failure of collection of assets. The activity can be registered in the system using ASSET.FINANCE-RECORD.FAILED.COLLECTION-ARRANGEMENT activity. A failed collection fee is levied on the arrangement when the user triggers this activity manually.
- Payment return fee: Lease payments scheduled for collection from an external system might fail due to various reasons like account unavailability or insufficient funds. System triggers ASSET.FINANCE-RECORD.DD.RETURN-ARRANGEMENT activity to register the payment failure. The user can configure a payment return fee on occurrence of this activity.

User creates an arrangement with the condition that the system collects the delivery fee when the ASSET.FINANCE-RECORD.EVENT-ARRANGEMENT activity is triggered.

Delivering the asset to the lessee is an external event. The user triggers ASSET.FINANCE-RECORD.EVENT-ARRANGEMENT in the system to register this external event. System prompts an alert message that a fee is levied for the activity.

System schedules the delivery fee to be collected along with the first payment.

### 2.4  Hybrid Pooling


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Key Fields:** *AA Bundle ID*, *Align Dates*, *Alt Acct Id*, *Alt Acct Type*, *Alt Id Type*, *Alternate Id*, *Alternate Id Type*, *Back-to-Back FX* ... +27 more
> 
> **Sections:** 🔧 Working With


#### 🔧 Working With

The below are the different process to create a hybrid cash pool:

| Process | Activity | System/User |
|---|---|---|
| Create pool in pending live | BUNDLE-NEW.OFFER-ARRANGEMENT | Orchestration service |
| Create accounts in pending live | ACCOUNTS-NEW.OFFER-ARRANGEMENT | Orchestration service |
| Set go live date for pool | BUNDLE-UPDATE.LIVE.DATE-PRODUCT.BUNDLE | User |
| Set go live date for accounts in pool (be spoke) | BUNDLE-RESTRUCTURE-BUNDLE.HIERARCHY | User |
| Bring accounts to Live | ACCOUNTS-NEW-ARRANGEMENT | Scheduled by orchestration service and processed by COB orchestration process |
| Bring pool to live | BUNDLE-NEW-ARRANGEMENT | User/CB Orchestration process |
| Add standalone account | ACCOUNTS-TRANSFORM-ARRANGEMENT | Scheduled by orchestration service and processed by COB orchestration process |
| Remove pool account | ACCOUNTS-TRANSFORM-ARRANGEMENT | Scheduled by orchestration service and processed by COB orchestration process |
| Close pool account | ACCOUNTS-SETTLE-PAYOFF | Scheduled by orchestration service and processed by COB orchestration process |

This section describes the steps and sequences to be followed, to manually create the various account part of a BN pool structure.

The navigation is as follows,

- Product Catalog.
- Select Product Catalog from the User Menu

> **⚠️ Note:** These accounts (including the master account bundle arrangement) can be created forward dated. They are activated by the system at SOD on that date.

Create CT accounts in the desired currencies.

- Switch off settlement instructions on pay-in and pay-out sides.

Create a new bundle arrangement under the master account product.

- Attach the CTs to the product bundle.
- Identify the currency of the master account and choose the corresponding CT account to be the recipient of the bundle.

Create summary or transaction account in the order of the hierarchy.

- The parent must be created first before creating the child.
- If TR1 has its parent as CS1, which has its parent as SA1, then SA1 is created, followed by CS1 and then TR1.
- Once an account is created, its parent can only be set or changed through the purpose built internal restructuring activity.
- Normal Update-Account activity cannot be used.
- Similarly, once an account is created, the bundle arrangement (master account) and link account number (CT account) can be updated through the purpose built External Restructuring Activity.
- Switch off settlement instructions on pay-in and pay-out sides.
- Once the accounts are created, the normal workflow on updating their conditions are to be followed through the arrangement overview. The new activity drilldown links to setup, Bank interest or fees or schedule and settlement Internal interest or fees or schedule and settlement conditions.


###### Generating IBAN

When the Bundle for the master account product is created in Draft status and when it is subsequently moved to the New Offer status, the IBAN is generated based on the values defined for Generate Iban and Alt Id Type . The IBAN can be seen in the AA.ARRANGEMENT record of the underlying contract.

As displaying the entire IBAN Value on the card is not feasible, it displays few characters of IBAN and appends it with three dots , for example, GB12DEMO60161300087537 is displayed as GB12DEMO6061…; on hovering over the text it displays the full string value.

The Alternate Id Type and Alternate Id of the Alt Id Types can be viewed in the expand header of each card. For the accounts other than master, T24.IBAN value gets displayed on the card instead of Account ID. If T24.IBAN value is available, the Alt Acct Type and Alt Acct Id get displayed on the expand card header.

When creating the CT accounts except for Limit (in case of MCCFor SCCF or MCF or SCF) is updated, no other special attribute needs to be specified to attach it to a master account, since it is done through the UPDATE-PRODUCT.BUNDLE activity. The user does this activity directly on the bundle arrangement (master account).

Once the CTs and MAs are created, when creating SA or CS or TR or MTR, it is important to capture the pool and hierarchy details via the purpose built attributes in Account property.

The following is a screenshot of a TR being created new, attached to an existing Pool under SA1 as its parent. The navigation for this could either be from the Product Catalog or the Master Account Overview.

The Master account is the bundle arrangement.

- If the account added or created is in a different Temenos Transact company than the master account, then the master account reference must be captured suffixed with its company mnemonic. In the example above, since the master account is in Temenos Transact Company BNK, it must be captured as AA1710732QS1/BNK for the system to recognise it.
- Linked Account number is the CT Account. If left blank and if a valid CT in this currency exists, then the system would default it. If a value is entered, the system validates that it is a valid participant in this Bundle Arrangement and that its currency matches this account’s currency.

- Parent account is used to capture the parent in the hierarchy. It is an optional field and when left blank, it mean the account being created would be added to the pool directly under the master account level.
- If a value is entered, the system would validate that it is, A valid member of the Bundle Hierarchy An allowed parent of this account Enabled for multi-currency if its currency is different from that of this account’s currency

In case of opening CS or SA, the above rules hold true except for the Linked Account Number (for which input is allowed).

The accounts in the BN pool can be internally moved (at any point). To facilitate this, the ACCOUNTS-CHANGE.PARENT-ARRANGEMENT activity is initiated from the New Activity menu.

During this process happens, the balances from the previously linked parent account is also transferred.

The above screenshot shows a TR account linked to SA account 2000003347. The SA and linked TR account’s balances are the same.

From the New Activity menu in the TR account, the User activity ACCOUNTS-CHANGE.PARENT-ARRANGEMENT is initiated.

For a restructuring, this activity runs at COB, hence, the Effective Date needs to be day + 1. The new parent account is changed to 2000003355, which is the new SA account. After authorisation and a COB is run, the restructure process is initiated.

The above screenshot shows that the balance (USD 88,592.08) is moved from (2000003347) to (2000003355) account.

This section enables the user to understand creation of BN pool.

BN structure creation process starts from creating a master arrangement in a draft status. The user can provide the necessary details to create the master arrangement by selecting the NEW STRUCTURE tab in Graphical User Interface (GUI). Mandatory information is Product Name, Country (on which the Master arrangement is created), Currency (master account) and Structure Name (optional).

To create a new BN structure, from the GENERAL TRADING screen,

1. Click NEW STRUCTURE .
2. Enter the mandatory information and then click CREATE . The master arrangement is created in view mode.
3. Click to add new accounts to BN structure. The symbol is enabled.
4. Click to add new accounts to the BN structure. The Add Account to Structure pop-up window opens.
5. Select the respective account type to add a new accounts to the pool. Standalone accounts can be selected and added to the BN structure by filtering the accounts by Currency.
6. Click to add multiple accounts to the pool. Example: To add two SA accounts, select the currency and company from the drop-down list. Once the account placed holder is created, click OK to create the placeholder card in GUI.
7. Click Save to save the BN pool structure in GUI. GUI passes the information to Temenos Transact to store the placeholder details. The user can save the changes in GUI after the BN pool structure is approved by corporate. When the user saves the Master arrangement in GUI, Temenos Transact does not any validation.

The BN structure can be edited and updated with new accounts and removal account by selecting the edit options. The Draft BN structure can be edited with the following details.

- Adding new placeholders
- Removing placeholder accounts
- Changing Parent details
- Adding Standalone accounts
- Adding a new parent placeholder for child accounts

Click Validate and Commit . The CT placeholders are created automatically. CT account is opened in Master account company for each currency of TR accounts.

To disconnect account placeholder, Click on each cards. The account card is removed immediately from the BN pool structure. When the Summary Account (SA) or Currency Summary (CS) placeholders are removed from BN pool, the child accounts are linked to the immediate parent. The parent accounts can be removed along with the child accounts from BN pool.

> **⚠️ Note:** Account number is not generated in Temenos Transact, hence the conversion of TR account to standalone is not possible.

To add standalone accounts to BN pool, click on the respective cards.

> **⚠️ Note:** This icon is enabled only for Master or SA or CS accounts.

Standalone accounts can be added under SA and CS account or directly under the master arrangement without any parent. Until the BN pool becomes live, the standalone account terms and conditions remains the same. Once the live date reaches, the account is converted to TR and the new product conditions applies. The account number remains the same as standalone account and only the change product activity is triggered.

Export. The BN structure can be exported as PDF, HTML, Excel, Power Point and Word. The exported BN structure is produced with the corporate customer for any modifications or changes in the structure. BN structure can be exported during Draft, Preliminary and Live status.

Go Preliminary to move the pool to preliminary. To move the pool to Preliminary status, the Pool Orchestration Service is run after committing the Activity. Once the Go Preliminary is triggered on a particular BN pool, the user can click on top-left and GUI displays the GUI landing page.

Once the preliminary process completed, the status of BN pool structure is moved and updated as Preliminary. Account number is generated on each placeholder and appears on each cards. Temenos Transact generates CT account automatically for each currency of TR accounts.

Click Edit to update the Terms and Conditions.

This section enables maintenance of cover control

This option is available in Tools menu. Click Edit to update the cover control setup. Accounts part of BN pool are listed as tree view and the changes can be updated in each account. Cover control on CT accounts are not applicable and hence the options are not enabled. Enable Apply settings to sub-structure to copy the cover control setup to child accounts.

Credit check is set for internal or external transactions or both. When the options is Null, the credit is applied during the transaction processing. Click Save to update the changes in Temenos Transact.

Click Edit to add new SA,CS,TR or MTR accounts in preliminary BN structure. The similar process is followed in Draft to add new accounts in preliminary. The user can commit the changes once the placeholders are created. Once the BN pool is committed in GUI, account number is generated immediately in Temenos Transact and appears on each card. The user can update the terms and conditions for the new account created in BN Pool.

To sets the Global Go Live Date from CARD VIEW Click Go Live on top-right of the BN Pool structure in GUI.

In the below screen, the Global Go Live is set for Bundle arrangements and the custom Go Live date option is for individual accounts part of BN Pool structure. Set the Global Go Live Date first and then the customer go live date, else an error message is displayed. Custom Go Live date is an optional input, participant accounts in BN pool goes live with the same date as Master or Bundle go live. When the go live date is set for individual accounts, then the accounts are live only on that particular date. Transactions are not allowed until the accounts are moved to LIVE.

The Custom go live date can be the same as Master live date as or later than Master live date. Temenos Transact displays an error message when the customer go live date is before Master live date.

This section enables maintenance of CT Accounts

CT Account

CT accounts provides static information of accounts such as CUSTOMER NAME, CUSTOMER ID, ACCOUNT NUMBER, STATUS and SCHEDULED CHANGES. CT expand card also has an option to setup or amend the interest conditions. When the limit is available for the CT account, GUI allows editing of limit on CT accounts.

CT Account Transactions

CT Account balances

Limit Conditions

To update or amend the limit records, click Edit. Once the changes and amendments are done, click Commit to submit the changes in Temenos transact.

Interest Conditions

Click Interest conditions on CT account in expand view, the version of Interest calculations are launched. The interest activity can be set with immediate effort or for a future effective date. On committing the changes, GUI passes the information to Temeons Transact to update interest details.

Summary Account/Currency Summary

SA account provides the static information of accounts such as CUSTOMER NAME , CUSTOMER ID , ACCOUNT NUMBER , STATUS and SCHEDULE CHANGES . It provides the combined balances of all the child accounts linked under the SA accounts. It is multi-currency accounts; hence, any allowed currencies can be linked to SA. When the SA account is having a multi-currency child accounts, then the balance is combined to SA account currency. SA expand card can setup or amend interest conditions and internal cover control.

When the user clicks on Interest condition, the respective version is launched to update the internal interest conditions. Manage Limit option allows the user to setup the internal and external cover control. Manage limit version is launched and the GUI allows to update and commit the changes.

TR Account

Expanded view of TR account provides the static information of accounts such as CUSTOMER NAME , CUSTOMER ID , ACCOUNT NUMBER , STATUS and Schedule Changes. TR account provides the balances and transactions of the respective TR accounts. The user can view the transactions by providing the start and end date. TR expand card can setup or amend interest conditions and internal cover control.

When the user clicks on Interest condition, the respective version is launched to update the internal interest conditions. Manage Limit option allows the user to setup the internal and external cover control. Manage limit version is launched and the GUI allows to update and commit the changes.

TR Account Transfer Services

Setting Future Internal STO/Sweeps

On selecting the Transfer services, the process remains the same. Refer Transact process flow.

The below screenshot shows a new TR attached to an existing pool under SA1 as its parent. The navigation for this is from the Product Catalog or the Master Account Overview.

The master account is the bundle arrangement.

When the account added or created is in a Temenos Transact company different from the master account, the master account reference should be captured and suffixed with its company mnemonic. In the above screenshot, since the master account is in Temenos Transact company BNK, it must be captured as AA1710732QS1/BNK for the system to identify.

Linked Account Number is the CT account. If this field is left blank and when a valid CT in this currency exists, then the system defaults it.

- When a value is entered in this field, the system checks if it is a valid participant in the bundle arrangement and currency matches the account’s currency.

Parent Account is used to capture the parent in the hierarchy. It is an optional field and when left blank, the account created is added to the pool directly under the master account level. When a value is entered in this field, the system validates if it is,

- A valid member of the bundle hierarchy
- An allowed parent of this account
- Enabled for multi-currency (if the currency is different from that of the account’s currency)

> **⚠️ Note:** The above rules hold true when opening CS or SA, (except for the Linked Account Number for which input is not allowed).

The AA.BUNDLE.HIERARCHY.DETAILS (system maintained table) is used for any investigation or analysis purposes or to know the pool structure on a given date.

Posting transactions on a BN pool is possible through the transaction account (that has External Posting set as Yes).

> **⚠️ Note:** The system blocks any direct posting on CS or SA or CT.

Whenever a transaction is posted in a TR account, the core accounting engine does the following:

- Makes a posting on the TR as a memo posting and diverts it as a real entry in the corresponding CT account (specified in Link AC Number field in Account Property)
- Replicates the same memo entry in the parent of the TR (specified in the Parent Account field in Account Property) and its parent and so on up to the top level parent.

Internal or external transactions are controlled by the Transaction Type attribute in TRANSACTION table. This and the internal cover control attributes in Limit property class drives the validations on these transactions for TR or CS and SA accounts.

To make a bundle go live, enter the current or future date in the Master Live Date field.

- If the current date is given, run the AA.POOL.ORCHESTRATION.SERVICE service to make the pool go live online.
- If the current date is given but service is not run, the bundle does not go live during the End of Day processes. In this case, to make the bundle go live, enter the current date, the following day (and run the service), or a future date in the Master Live Date field .
- If a future date is given, the bundle goes live during the SOD process of the given date.

When the user updates rate through Preferential Pricing FX condition, (with a date effective in the future), the new rates are available to all TRs from that date.

When the user updates rate in Preferential Pricing FX condition, with a date effective in the past (T-3),

In the CUSTOMER.MASS.BLOCK application, the user can provide the AA Bundle Arrangement ID in the AA Bundle ID field to block all the accounts, which are part of that bundle for transaction processing.

In case of BN, by entering the AA Bundle Arrangement ID and committing the record, all currency top accounts, which are part of that bundle is blocked for transaction processing (posted against transaction accounts, which are part of the same BN structure).

Example: A BN structure is created in the system with master account arrangement bundle ID as AA171075RFH6.

This bundle arrangement has two currency top accounts: AA17107RHMWK (EUR) and AA17107BB6H6 (USD).


###### Block Entire Cashpool structure (GUI)

To block the entire BN structure, select Emergency Block from Tools menu. Select SUSPEND CASHPOOL to block all accounts, which are part of the respective bundle for transaction processing.

> **⚠️ Note:** To block the BN pool, Start date is a mandatory field. Expiry date is an optional field.

Suspend can be done with future start date and expiry date. Once the Temenos Transact reaches the particular Start of Day (SOD), all the accounts which are part of that Bundle are blocked for Transactions. Fund transfer, standing order and sweeping scheduled (between the accounts in the bundle structure) are also suspended.

Once the BN pool structure is blocked, further maintenance on accounts is also suspended and the structure blocked message is displayed.

To unblock the BN structure, select Unblock Structure from the Tools menu. Enter the date in the Expiry date field and provide the reason and click UNBLOCK STRUCTURE button.

> **⚠️ Note:** The date in Expiry date can be current or future date and when,

- Current date is provided, the structure is unblocked immediately and the user can perform transactions on BN accounts.
- Future date is provide, Temenos Transact removes the blocked status during the start of day of the particular end date.

To block the sub-structure, Select Emergency Block from Tools menu and click BLOCK ACCOUNT OR SUB- STRUCTURE . By selecting the parent accounts GUI blocks the child accounts linked under the parent account. In Temenos Transact child accounts are not blocked and only parent account is blocked. When the user initiates the transaction on TR accounts, Temenos Transact displays an error message and further transactions are not allowed. Enter date in Start date and Expiry date fields to block the sub-structure and a particular account. Temenos Transact allows to block the sub-structure or an account with future start date and end date.

When the user selects the parent account, the child accounts linked under the parent are selected automatically and in GUI, the status is shown as blocked.

Once the sub-structure and accounts are blocked, the status is updated on each account and the tool tip is shown on each card with the date on which the account is blocked. When the parent is blocked, the child account details are also updated as blocked in GUI.

Block details are updated in card and tree view.

To unblock sub-structure or an account, select Unblock Account or Sub Structure . The blocked accounts are selected by default. The user can deselect an account when there is no need to unblock. Enter the Expiry date and click UNBLOCK ACCOUNTS to commit the changes in Temenos Transact. Expiry date can be current or future dated. When current date is used to unblock the account, it is unblocked immediately and Temenos Transact allows to initiate transactions.

BN pool GUI structure is refreshed with the changes in Temenos Transact and the blocked status is updated in GUI. Once the account is unblocked, the strike line on an account is removed immediately.

A CUSTOMER.MASS.BLOCK record is created to block the two CT accounts starting 18 April 2017, until 19 April 2017.

By giving the bundle arrangement ID and committing this record, the CT accounts are blocked and no transactions are posted against any transaction accounts linked to these currency top accounts.

The accounts are unblocked by giving the expiry date and an unblocking code.
