The Integrity Check Days attribute in Bundle Hierarchy Property Class is used to schedule an evaluation on ‘n’ number of days before an event is triggered in the bundle.

The first integrity check is run ‘n’ number of days before go live date for a pool in preliminary status.

This validation runs on continuous basis ‘n’ number of days before every event in the Bundle.

> **⚠️ Note:** Integrity check days are calculated as ‘n’ working days.

- Integrity check orchestrates the validations from MA level to the underlying accounts in the hierarchy.
- The system triggers the Activity Class BUNDLE-INTEGRITY.CHECK-ARRANGEMENT to run the integrity check.
- The user can trigger ad-hoc integrity checks by manually running the activity class for integrity check. The system automatically runs the pool orchestration service and generates integrity report.

- Validations are run on the bundle and results are recorded in AA.POOL.EXCEPTION.LOG. The record ID is Arrangement Number-INTEGRITY.REPORT.

- It is possible to query on this table using the bundle (arrangement) number. This displays a single screen that contains all the validations related to all the accounts in the bundle, especially the failures

- Drilldown to the individual accounts are available to take correction actions.

The below are the validations based on pool events.

A complete scan is carried out when go live date is set.

When the live date is given (not null), the scan is carried out at the pool level.

- Pool cannot go live without even a single CT.
- CT cannot exist without MA and TR.

The system validates,

- If the bank is working on the dates in which pool has tasks scheduled at SOD
- If previous calendar date is a working day

- A warning message giving the childless CS or SA or CT is closed automatically
- Currency availability in weighted rate calculation (CT and SA) CT: When 4 CTs are in bundle but only three currencies are specified in custom type in Recipient CT Interest property, then exception message is raised for the missing custom type in that currency SA: Validates if all the currencies for which balance is maintained in ECB, are specified in the custom type

- Currency market rate for currencies in secondary currency market Takes recipient’s secondary currency market, and scan through CURRENCY table in recipient CT company for each allowed currency of the bundle and see if there is a rate definition for this secondary currency market. An exception is recorded for the missing rate definition

- Settlement account validation All properties, payment types have settlement accounts (payment schedule, activity charges and rule break charges) Settlement and counter booking belong to the same pool and currency, the status of those accounts for the date (this account’s go live date atleast) required Settlement account specified in bundle settlement Settlement instruction switched on (if not, warning message) Settlement and counter booking account should be available for the go live date of the CS or SA or TR During new offer of SA or CS, a new offer TR can be attached as a settlement account but it must be set to go live for the SA or CS Go live date

When an account is linked to the pool, the below validations are performed:

- External sweeps are set for the account
- External STOs are set for the account
- Account with negative balance (error is raised when TR account is linked)
- AC pre closure validations are performed
- Account is scheduled for closure TR has external sweep or STO

When an account is delinked from the pool, the below validations are performed:

- Internal sweeps are set for the account
- Internal STOs are set for the account
- AC Pre closure validations
- Account scheduled for closure TR has internal sweep or STO

During the closure of an account, the below validations are performed:

- Negative balance in account
- Sweeps setup in account
- Accounts has a record already in AC block closure


###### Closure of entire pool structure (GUI)

BN pool can be closed during Draft, Preliminary and Live status. To close the BN pool structure, right-click the 3 dots on Master card and select Close Entire Pool . Closure of live BN pool online is not possible. It is possible on the next business day or on a future date.

Closing the preliminary BN pool is done online and future scheduling is not possible. Master arrangement and SA, CS, TR or MTR accounts linked to the pool is closed online and Tree or Card view is updated accordingly. GUI displays a warning message to the user before closing the entire BN pool. When the user clicks on YES, GUI passes the information to Temenos Transact and the accounts are closed.

Cross pool event go live date against destination pool go live date and parent go live date is validated and exceptions are logged in case of breach.

> **⚠️ Note:** When these validations are not met, exception log is updated with a warning message.

Cross-pool movements of the Sub-structure

When arrangement is part of a hierarchy of accounts such as, a cash pool hierarchy, the arrangement interest, charge and capitalisation frequencies need to be set (not at product level but at another arrangement higher up in the hierarchy). In a cash pool structure, this means setting conditions for inheritance at the (parent or grandparent) or (pool or currency specific concentration level).This helps in easy maintenance of these conditions in a single place instead of having to deal with the individual arrangements at the lowest level, which also happen to be the normal transaction accounts.

### 2.5  Risk Participation


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Type*
> 
> **Sections:** ⚙️ Configuration


#### ⚙️ Configuration

A Participant Property of property Type as Risk Participant is created to add risk participant to a loan contract and then add it to the product at the product designer level.

For adding the fund participants and risk participants, two separate properties need to be created and added to the product, that is, one property with property Type set as Participant and the other with Type as Risk Participant as shown in the below screenshot.

> **⚠️ Note:** A single Participant property cannot have both the Participant and Risk Participant property types.

The bank user creates separate properties for the fund participants and risk participants, and they are added to the Participant Property class at the product group level. At product designer level, both the properties have their respective product conditions attached to them.

> **⚠️ Note:** If property type is not selected the system defaults it to Participant.

The user configures the following property classes, to calculate the Risk fees, Risk Margin and Flat Fees for the bilateral contracts or club loan contracts.

Interest Property Class is used to define the risk fees and risk margin and it can accrued and paid to the Risk participant.

To differentiate the risk participant’s Risk Fee and Risk Margin property from the other regular interest properties, the Interest property, which is created for paying out risk fee or margin consists of the Risk Participant property type along with existing Non Customer property type.

The screenshot below shows the Non Customer Interest Properties created to pay the risk margin and risk fees to the risk participant.

Charge property class is used to define the flat fees that is to be paid to the risk participants. It can be configured as an activity charge or as a scheduled charge, which can be defined in the Payment schedule.

To differentiate the Charge property that is used for paying flat fees to the risk participants from the other regular charge properties, the Charge property created for paying out the flat fees consists of the ‘Risk Participant’ property type along with existing ‘Non Customer’ and ‘Credit’ property type.

The screenshot below shows the Non Customer Charge Property created to pay the flat fees to the risk participant.

The properties created are attached to the respective Property Class of the Product in the Product Group as can be seen below

In the Product Designer, appropriate Product Conditions are attached to the Interest and Charge Properties which are attached to the Product are shown below:

The screenshot below shows the calculation source balance is defined for the Interest properties.

Once the product is published, the bank uses the risk fees and risk margin at the arrangement level.

> **⚠️ Note:** Irrespective of the bilateral or club contract with risk participants, a syndication settlement account is created. The risk fees and margin to be paid out are initially credited to the syndication settlement account and then a payment order created to pay out the funds to the respective risk participants.

### 2.6  Share Transfer


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *In a syndicated or club loan, some banks prefer to reduce their share in the loan or completely sell off their share, by transferring it to the existing banks in the loans or to a completely new bank. This can be done using share transfer.*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Buy Participant*, *Consent Party*, *Consent Type*, *Consent required*, *Min Trade %*, *Min Trade Amt*, *Own Bank*, *Sell Participant* ... +3 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | 🔧 Working With


#### 📖 Introduction

In a syndicated or club loan, some banks prefer to reduce their share in the loan or completely sell off their share, by transferring it to the existing banks in the loans or to a completely new bank. This can be done using share transfer.

Transfer of shares can be done in two ways:

- Assignment sell – The transfer is done with the knowledge of the borrower and other participants. The new lender who bought the shares acts as an assignee.
- Participation sell – The transfer need not be done with the knowledge of the borrower and other participants. The new lender who bought the shares acts as a sub-participant or a risk participant. Sub participation – The original participant or seller owns the risk of default from the borrower side as well as the sub-participant side. Risk participation – The original participant or seller continues to lend the borrower but the risk of default from the borrower side is borne by the risk participant for which they receive a fee income.

In club loans, an agent acts as a moderator between the borrower and the group of lenders. If a participant transfers its share with the approval of the borrower, then the agent performs the share transfer and maintains the accounts for the changes done during the share transfer in the system and for the new participant. The agent might charge a fee to do the share transfer. In case if the participant sells to lenders without the knowledge of borrower and other lenders, then they do the share transfer only in their system and the new participant acts as a sub participant or risk participant.


#### 🔧 Working With

The user can initiate the share transfer activity by clicking on the arrow mark available beside each of the participant in the Overview screen of the facility or drawing contract as shown in the following screenshot:

The user has to provide the details of the buyer and the seller in the respective fields in the Share Transfer Property Class. If own bank is a buyer or seller, then the Own Bank field should be updated with either BUY or SELL option.

If Temenos Transact owning bank acts as an agent or agent cum participant and share transfer happens between the participants, then both the Sell Participant and Buy Participant fields must be updated.

When the buyer is a new participant and not an existing participant in the contract, then the user should update the role of the buyer under the Participant Role field and his beneficiary details in the Settlement Instructions tab as part of the share transfer activity.

Any skims for interest or fee agreed as part of the share transfer is recorded in the SKIMS tab. The transfer amount has to be entered in the Amount field.

The maximum amount that can be transferred from an existing participant can be the sum of available commitment amount (CUR COMMITMENT) and the outstanding amount (CUR ) excluding the amount which has been made due (DUE ).


###### Examples:

Consider a term loan of USD 1M created for a customer on January 1, 2019. The loan consists of two participants:

- RBS – Own bank who is an agent cum participant and responsible for 20% of commitment amount
- SEK Bank of Sweden – Participant (Participant ID – 100001) responsible for 80% of commitment amount.

Consider a disbursement of USD 600,000 has been made already. Therefore, the balances will be as below:

On January 15, 2019, a principal of USD 100,000 is made due and repayment is yet to be made. Now, the balances will look as below.

Consider, on January 15, 2019, the SEK bank performs a share transfer of USD 300,000 to Deutsche Bank (Participant ID - 100002) who is a new participant to the loan.

Now, SEK bank’s available amount for transfer is not 800,000, which is their total share in this contract. Rather, they are eligible to transfer only 720,000, which is the sum of available commitment (320,000) and utilised commitment (480,000) excluding the delinquent balance (80,000).

Out of their available amount for transfer (720,000), SEK transfers 300,000 only to Deutsche bank. So, the ratio at which share transfer is performed can be calculated as below:

(300,000/720,000)*100 = 41.6666666666667% (Rounded to 13 decimal places)

Total commitment of the buyer is minimum of either the transfer amount or the seller’s (CUR + UTL ). Here, TOT of the new buyer is calculated as Minimum of (300,000, (320,000 + 480,000)) = 300,000.

The available commitment CUR of the buyer is calculated as CUR of the seller * transfer Ratio. Here, the available commitment of the buyer CUR = 320,000 *41.6667 % = 133,333.33

The utilized commitment (UTL ) of the buyer = the total commitment (TOT ) of the buyer - the available commitment (CUR ) of the buyer. Here, UTL = 300,000 –133,333.33 = 166,666.67

The principal outstanding with the customer (CUR ) of the buyer = CUR of the seller * Transfer Ratio. In the example,

CUR (B) = 400,000* 41.6667 = 166,666.67

The overdrawn commitment (OVD ) of the buyer = Transfer amount - (CUR of the buyer + UTL of the buyer). Here, OVD of the buyer is 300,000 – (133,333.3333 + 166,666.6667) = 0

Finally, the balances look like below post share transfer.

After the share transfer is done, the interest calculation of the transferred amount is done for the buying participant from the day of effective share transfer. The interest accrued until that date remains with the seller participant bank.

Share transfer after Partial Disbursement

Consider a term loan of USD 1M created for a customer on April 18, 2023. The loan consists of two participants:

- Own bank who is an agent cum participant and responsible for 20% of commitment amount
- Abn Amro Securities (Cust ID: 100112)– Participant (Participant ID – 100112) responsible for 80% of commitment amount.

The system capitalises the activity charge of USD 500 creating for upfront when the arrangement and disburses a loan amount of USD 600,000 to the borrower.

Borrower balance is shown in the screenshot below.

Own bank’s balance is shown in the screenshot below.

Participant 100112’s balance is shown in the screenshot below.

Consider that the own bank performs a share transfer of USD 120,000 to JP Morgan Chase (Participant ID - 100115) who is a new participant to the loan on April 19, 2023.

Now, own bank’s Maximum transferrable amount is

CUR (80,000) + CUR (120,100) = USD 200,100.

Formula to calculate the new participant balances after the share transfer is

Transfer Ratio (TR) = (Transfer Amount / Max Transferrable amount) * 100%.

Here, the transfer ratio = (120,000/200,100) * 100% = 59.97%.

Total commitment of the buyer is minimum of either the transfer amount or the seller’s (CUR + UTL ) *Transfer Ratio. Here, TOT of the new buyer is calculated as Minimum of (120,000, [(80,000+120,000) *59.97%] =119,940.03

> **⚠️ Note:** When the Update Commit on Capitalization is set as ‘Overdrawn’, the total commitment of the buyer is calculated considering the transfer ratio. When the Update Commit on Capitalization is set as ‘Current and Overdrawn’, TOT of the new buyer is Minimum (Transfer Amount, (CUR + UTL ) Whereas, Update Commit on Capitalization is set as ‘Overdrawn’, TOT of the new buyer is Minimum (Transfer Amount, [CUR + UTL ] *Transfer ratio)

The available commitment CUR of the buyer is calculated as CUR of the seller * Transfer Ratio. In the example, the available commitment of the buyer CUR = 80,000*59.97% = 47,976.01.

The Utilized commitment (UTL ) of the buyer is calculated as the total commitment (TOT ) of the buyer minus the available commitment (CUR ) of the buyer. In the example, UTL = 119,940.03 – 47,976.01 = 71964.02

The principal outstanding with the customer (CUR ) of the buyer is calculated as CUR of the seller * Transfer Ratio. In the example, CUR (B) = 120,100 * 59.97% = 72,023.98

The overdrawn commitment (OVD ) of the buyer is calculated Transfer amount minus (CUR of the buyer plus UTL of the buyer). In the example, OVD of the buyer is 120,000 – (47,976.01 + 71,964.01) = 59.97.

Formula to calculate the new participant balances after share transfer is

Here, the transfer ratio = (120,000/200,100) * 100% = 59.97%.

###### Third Party Consent for Assignment Trades

Assignment type of trade requires consent from the borrower, agent, and other relevant stakeholders in the syndication. Participant property class defines the requirement of the consent and the parties from whom the consent is required.

The Third Party tab comprises of the following fields:

- Consent Type – Indicates the type of the consent given
- Consent Party – Indicates the party who is giving the consent
- Consent Given – Indicates whether the consent is given or not (Yes or No). If consent given is ‘No’, assignment transfer will not be allowed for that arrangement.
- Consent Date – Indicates the date on which the consent is given

The Third-Party tab captures the consent status and the consent date for an assignment type of trade.

The Consent Type and Consent Party fields are defaulted automatically in the Share transfer Property Class when defined in Participant Property Class. It is mandatory to define the Consent given and the Consent date fields in Share transfer Property Class to initiate an assignment transfer, that is transfer of shares to existing or new participants.

If the Consent required is set as ‘No’ in Participant Property Class, it is not mandatory to define anything under the Third Party tab.

> **⚠️ Note:** If Min Trade Amt or Min Trade % is specified in Participant Property Class, the same are validated in Share Transfer Property Class once the amount is defined. Third Party tab is not valid for participation (sub-participants) or risk participant transfer.

### 2.7  CorpLendingUA


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The Corporate Lending User Agent (UA) allows users to interact with Corporate Lending. It provides a holistic and end-to-end view of the features including Upcoming Transactions & Covenants, Past Dues, Needs Attention, Quick Views & Actions, and so on. It is a Role-based interface that provides diff...*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

The Corporate Lending User Agent (UA) allows users to interact with Corporate Lending. It provides a holistic and end-to-end view of the features including Upcoming Transactions & Covenants, Past Dues, Needs Attention, Quick Views & Actions, and so on. It is a Role-based interface that provides different views for Maker and Checker roles respectively. It is also possible to download the Corporate Lending data in CSV format from the listing screens.

The Corporate Lending User Agent fetches data quickly by utilising Unified User Experience (UUX-based). The Corporate Lending User Agent provides the following features,

- Quick Links - Buttons and hyperlinks that help the users to navigate to the appropriate Transact Explorer screens.
- Upcoming Transactions and Covenants - Displays the upcoming maturing loans, interest rate fix, covenant documents, drawdowns in the next 7/14/21/28 days.
- Past Dues - Displays bills which are overdue in type such as principal overdue, principal interest overdue, penalty interest overdue and fees overdue.
- Quick Views and Actions - Provides the placeholder for the user to enquire the information such as Maturity Date , Payment Date, Outstanding amount/Utilised Amount and so on for a customer or an account. The data displayed in the flex table is based on the Transaction type (Deal/Facility/Drawing) chosen by the Corporate Officer/ Corporate Manager. This feature also displays drilldowns based on the transaction type selected which helps the Corporate Officer or Corporate Manager to navigate to Transact Explorer.
- Needs Attention - Displays the overdue covenants and conditions, expiring facilities and loans which are being rolled over.
- Pending Requests - Provides the list of deals, facilities, drawings, secondary loan trading’s, facility repayments and drawing repayments waiting for approval from corporate manager .
- Pending Authorization - Provides the list of deals, facilities, drawings, secondary loan trading’s, facility repayments and drawing repayments waiting for authorisation.
- Enquiries - Displays the required enquires which are necessary for the corporate lending. Buttons and hyperlinks help the customer to navigate to the appropriate enquires in Transact Explorer.

Corporate UA is a plug-in user agent that is part of Temenos Explorer. Read Temenos Explorer User Guide for more information on the usage of the general functions of Temenos Explorer.


##### Role-Based User Access

As the Corporate Lending User Agent provides role-based views, a user can access the Corporate Lending UA tabs based on the following roles.

| Maker (CORPOFFICER) | Checker (CORPMANAGER) |
|---|---|
| Dashboard Quick Links Upcoming Transactions and Covenants Past Dues Quick Views and Actions Needs Attention Pending Requests Enquiries | Dashboard Upcoming Transactions and Covenants Past Dues Quick Views and Actions Needs Attention Pending Authorization Enquiries |


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The following section describes the setup required for enabling the Corporate Lending User Agent.


##### Pre-requisites

1. Download the Corporate Lending war from the latest artifact id-Corporate Lending UA. Default Path: http://utppcjdprdfctry.temenosgroup.com:8080/job/EPD-Factory/job
2. Download the latest Keycloak version from below and extract it. https://developer.temenos.com/temenos-explorer/docs/developer/keycloak/overview
3. Download the latest UTP pack having corporate lending IRF provider war fix. Also make sure the deployment folder has the tb server, irf provider, and transact explorer wars.


##### Configuring Corporate Lending UI War File

To connect with the UA, ensure the below Keycloak configuration is in TA_Config.js file (..\\CorporateLending.war\TA_config.js)


##### Setting up Keycloak

1. To change the port id , navigate to: ..\\keycloak-xx\standalone\configuration\.
2. Change the http port number to in standalone.xml and standalone-ha.xml file.
3. Use start.bat command to enable the Keycloak from keycloak-xx folder(…\\keycloak-xx\)
4. Create Keycloak admin user.
5. Login with admin user (Username:admin/Password:admin).
6. Go to realm and click Add to import the json under realm settings in Keycloak.
7. Realm, client, roles, and users are already created and imported as a json .
8. After importing the json, make sure CorporateLending and TransactExplorer clients are available as shown below .
9. Ensure Roles and users are also imported correctly as shown below .


##### Enabling Embedding using TE Configuration

Read Integrating Keycloak with OpenID Connect for more information on configuring TE for single sign on.

After the TE configuration is completed, ensure that Corpmanager/Corpofficer users are available in Transact with the pre-authenticated attribute set in the USER application.


##### Creating Keycloak Username

1. Create a user in Keycloak. Provide username and firstname as corpmanager.
2. Add an attribute. Provide Key as t24son and Value as corpmanager
3. Click the Credentials tab and provide password as 123456.

### 2.8  BilatertalClubConversion


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *A facility that involves more than one lender is called a club facility. Whereas in a bilateral facility, the own bank solely funds the customer. In a club facility, some banks prefer to reduce their share in facility or completely sell off their share by transferring it to the existing banks in the...*
> 
> **Applications:** `AA.BILL.DETAILS`, `AA.INTEREST.ACCRUALS`, `AA.PRD.DES.PARTICIPANT`, `AA.PRODUCT.DESIGNER`, `EB.ACCRUAL`
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

A facility that involves more than one lender is called a club facility. Whereas in a bilateral facility, the own bank solely funds the customer. In a club facility, some banks prefer to reduce their share in facility or completely sell off their share by transferring it to the existing banks in the facility or to a new bank. However, in a bilateral facility the bank prefers to reduce their share in the facility or completely or partially sell off their share by transferring it to a new bank. In a bilateral facility, the transferring of the share is facilitated through external share transfer, that is, selling the own bank’s share to the external participant. Therefore, the external participant becomes the lender for the facility. Further, the own bank acts as the agent bank in the facility. It provides the instruction to the lender bank on the funding and other activities with regards to the facility.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The Participant property class captures the participant shares in the arrangement. Hence, the user system has to attach the Participant property class and its associated product condition to the facility and all the loan products used to create a loan under the facility. The user performs this in AA.PRODUCT.DESIGNER to enable the share transfer to sell assets to the external participants. This is illustrated below.

- Update the own bank nostro details currency-wise in the Participant product conditions for all the currencies of the product.
- Set the participant’s accounting type ( Part Accting Type ) as Contingent or Memo in the Participant product condition ( AA.PRD.DES.PARTICIPANT ), by default Transact selects Memo.
- Attach the Participant product condition to the facility and drawing products as below. The facility product details are:

The loan product details are:

> **⚠️ Note:** Like a club facility and loan, the Accounting product condition and allocation rules should be updated in these facility and loans.


#### 🔧 Working With

### 2.9  Borrowing Base Facility


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *A borrowing base facility is a type of credit facility that a financial institution offers to a borrower based on the value of assets held by the borrower’s company, which is referred to as the borrowing base. The amount of credit granted is determined based on the value of the collaterals. The coll...*
> 
> **Applications:** `AC.BALANCE.TYPE`, `COLLATERAL`, `COLLATERAL.ACCOUNT`, `COLLATERAL.POOL`, `EB.CONTRACT.BALANCES`, `LIMIT`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Agreement Date*, *Amount*, *Available Amt*, *Category*, *Commitment Type*, *Commitment Utilisation*, *Consequence*, *Currency* ... +28 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

A borrowing base facility is a type of credit facility that a financial institution offers to a borrower based on the value of assets held by the borrower’s company, which is referred to as the borrowing base. The amount of credit granted is determined based on the value of the collaterals. The collateral value may change over time, and the system updates the related limits per collateral change.

The collaterals are the assets that the borrower pledges to a financial institution as a security for the facility. The collaterals can comprise different types of assets like account receivables, inventory, equipment, and other properties.

The financial institution can apply a haircut on the collateral to arrive at the realizable value of the assets. It can increase or decrease the collateral values, which in turn increases or decreases the facility exposure.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The Limit property class allows a user to link and track the facility’s online limit against the collateral value.

The Fixed Variable field in the Limit property class specifies whether the underlying facility’s utilization limit must be fixed or variable based on the collateral value. This field is applicable only if the limits are auto-created. If the user sets the value as ‘Variable’, the system updates the auto-created limit as Variable. Else, it is updated as ‘Fixed’.

> **⚠️ Note:** This Fixed Variable field is applicable only for the facility product and not for a deal or any other product lines.

The Maintain Limit Balance field in the Limit property class specifies whether the balances of the underlying limit, such as Online Limit in LIMIT , must be maintained in the facility. When the user checks this field, the LIMIT application hands off the Online Limit to the facility. The system tracks the changes and updates them in the TOT in EB.CONTRACT.BALANCES of the facility during COB. The user can levy charges to the borrower based on this balance.

> **⚠️ Note:** The user must select the Maintain Limit Balance field when the Fixed Variable field is set as ‘Variable’.

Refer to the Limit feature for more information on the Limit structure.


##### Accounting Condition of Limit Property for Facility Product

The screenshot below shows the configuration of the Limit property in a facility product.

The user can configure the following balance types in the FACILITYCOLLATERAL record in AC.BALANCE.TYPE based on the Term Amount property defined in the facility product.

- CUR
- UTL
- OVD

In the COLLATERAL.POOL application, the user can link the facility to collateral, based on which COLLATERAL.POOL fetches the facility commitment balances using the Exposure Id field.

The user can configure the soft balance types to calculate and collect fees on the utilized limit, available limit, and overdrawn limit of the facility arrangement.

#### 🔧 Working With

Collateral Management in Transact allows the financial institution to manage collaterals pledged by the borrower as a security for the borrowing base credit facility. The bank can create collaterals in the following structure by creating records in the following applications.

- COLLATERAL – Specifies the asset pledged by the borrower.
- COLLATERAL.ACCOUNT – Enables the user to group collaterals and applies a haircut. The collateral account value is calculated using the following formula.
- COLLATERAL.POOL – Enables the user to group the collateral accounts and link them to the facility. The collateral pool value is calculated using the following formula.

Refer to the Corporate Collateral Pool feature for more information on Corporate Collateral Pool.

When a borrowing base facility is created, the facility automatically creates the variable limit. When the user links the facility to the Exposure Id field in COLLATERAL.POOL , the system automatically updates the limit ID in the Exposure Limit field in COLLATERAL.POOL . After the facility is linked to COLLATERAL.POOL , the system updates the balances such as Online Limit , Available Amt , and Secured Amount in LIMIT . The system leverages the variable limit to cap the drawings under the facility to the extent of the collateral value.

> **⚠️ Note:** After updating the variable limit, the COLLATERAL.POOL does not allow the user to add any additional values in Exposure Id or Risk Exclusion Id .

Refer to the Creating Limit Products feature for more information on the process of creating the Limit products.

The system updates the limit online for the following events,

- Link Facility with Collateral Pool
- Change in Collateral value
- Increase/Decrease Facility
- Add/Remove Collaterals
- Add/Remove Collateral Accounts
- Change in Haircut

For other events such as Collateral, Collateral Account, Collateral Pool Expiry, and Revaluation of assets linked to Collateral, the user assess the latest values at the close of business or the next allocation.

The system introduces a new activity class, FACILITY-UPDATE.BALANCE-LIMIT to update the limit balance TOT in EB.CONTRACT.BALANCES of the facility during COB for all the above-mentioned limit balance updating events.

Based on the TOT balance, the system calculates other balances, such as utilized limit, available limit, and overdraw limit, to collect fees on the facility.

### 2.10  Cashflow Netting


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Cashflow Netting is a financial technique used by businesses to simplify and consolidate multiple cash flows like payables and receivables between parties into single net payment. It reduces the number of transactions, minimises transaction costs, and improves efficiency in cash flow management.*
> 
> **Applications:** `AA.ATTRIBUTE`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Cashflow Netting*, *Net Settlement Activity*, *Net Settlement activity*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

Cashflow Netting is a financial technique used by businesses to simplify and consolidate multiple cash flows like payables and receivables between parties into single net payment. It reduces the number of transactions, minimises transaction costs, and improves efficiency in cash flow management.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The user configures the facility-level sub-arrangement condition to enable Cashflow Netting for drawdown and rollover transactions.

> **⚠️ Note:** To define Cashflow Netting under the sub-arrangement condition at the facility-level, CASHFLOW.NETTING record must be available in AA.ATTRIBUTE as shown below.


#### 🔧 Working With

To enable the Cashflow Netting functionality,

Cashflow Netting (Y/N) and Net Settlement Activity are used at the Term Amount Property at the drawing-level.

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Cashflow Netting | Indicates whether Cashflow Netting is applicable or not, this feature helps to consolidate multiple cash inflows and outflows thereby reducing the volume of individual transactions. |
| Defaults to the value specified in the Sub Arrangement Conditions at the facility level for drawing products. |  |
| Net Settlement Activity | Specifies the activity that performs Cashflow Netting . Accepts a valid facility activity related to payment rules or payment priority properties. This is applicable only when the cash flow is enabled. |
| The Net Settlement Activity is configured at the drawing product level. |  |

When Cashflow Netting is set to ‘Yes’ and an activity is defined in the Net Settlement Activity , the system applies transaction netting during drawdown (LENDING-AUTO.DISBURSEMENT- ) and rollover (LENDING-CAPTURE-SPLITS.MERGES) activities.


##### Cashflow Netting during Drawdown

This section explains the Cashflow Netting for drawdown with facility-level dues and drawing-level dues with charges and drawdown fees.

The user creates a facility with USD 10M commitment amount and a term of 5 years with an outstanding due of USD 27,500.00

The Co-ordination Fee and related tax due amount is raised.

The user creates Drawing 1 with USD 3M commitment amount and a term of 2 years with an outstanding due of USD 5,000.00

The system raises the Maintenance Fee due amount.

The user creates Drawing 2 with USD 4M commitment amount and a term of 3 years with Cashflow Netting enabled with an outstanding due of USD 9,000.00.

Cashflow Netting is defaulted from the facility sub-arrangement condition as shown below.

The Maintenance Fee of USD 5,000.00 is applied as a Flat Charge.

The Auto Disbursement Fee of 0.10% is applied to the transaction amount.

A Maintenance Fee is applied upon the creation of a new lending arrangement and an Auto Disbursement fee is charged during the auto disbursement process, as specified in the Activity charges.

The system credits the Disbursement amount to the borrower's account as specified in the settlement instructions.

An override message is displayed, when committing the record, indicating the total due amount is settled against the facility and its associated drawings.

An overview of the drawing for which Cashflow Netting is enabled ensuring all respective dues settled during auto disbursement is shown below.

The Maintenance and Auto Disbursement Fees are settled, reducing their balances to zero.

After Drawing 2 is created with Cashflow Netting enabled, the total dues of USD 41,500.00 of the facility, existing drawing, and current drawing is handed over to the facility and the dues are repaid based on payment rules or payment priority. The remaining amount of USD 3,958,500.00 is settled to the borrower's account.

The outstanding dues are as follows:

Facility - USD 27,500.00

Drawing 1 - USD 5,000.00

Drawing 2 - USD 9,000.00

Total - USD 41,500.00


##### Cashflow Netting for Rollover during Club Loans

This section outlines the Cashflow Netting process for rollovers in club loans with an additional amount, including facility-level dues, drawing-level dues, charges, and drawdown fees.

The user creates a Facility with USD 10M commitment amount and a term of 5 years with an outstanding due of USD 33,000.00

The Co-ordination Fee and the associated tax amounts is raised to the owning bank and participant bank based on their respective shares of the commitment amount.

The user creates Drawing 1 with USD 6M commitment amount and a term of 4 years with an outstanding due of USD 5,000.00. Cashflow Netting is enabled, but netting is not applied to this drawing due to a manual disbursement.

The Maintenance Fee due amount is raised to the owning bank and participant bank based on their respective shares of the commitment amount.

> **⚠️ Note:** After processing manual disbursement, the status of the club loan is updated from ‘Not Disbursed’ to 'Current,' and corresponding CURACCOUNT entries are generated.

Drawing 1 is split into two separate drawings, each with an additional amount by triggering Split or Merge activity.

The user creates Drawing 2 with an additional amount of USD 1 million, and Drawing 3 with an additional amount of USD 2 million, by splitting the original drawing.

Once the record is committed, the status is updated to ‘Processing’.

The system runs the Splits Merges Service BNK/AA.SPLITS.MERGES.SERVICE.

The system updates the status of the newly created drawings as ‘Success’ as shown below.

After the split activity, Drawing 1 is moved to expired status as shown in the screenshot below.

The system creates Drawing 2 with USD 2M commitment amount and an additional amount of USD 1M with Cashflow Netting enabled with an outstanding due of USD 1,000.00.

An override message is displayed, that indicates the total due amount settled against the facility and its associated drawings.

Cashflow Netting is defaulted from the facility sub-arrangement condition as shown below.

The Auto Disbursement Fee of 0.10% is applied to the transaction amount.

An Auto Disbursement Fee is charged during the Auto Disbursement process, as specified in the Activity Charges.

The system credits the Disbursement amount to the borrower's account as specified in the settlement instructions.

An overview of drawing 2 for which Cashflow Netting is enabled, ensuring all respective dues are settled during auto disbursement.

Auto Disbursement fees are settled, reducing their balances to zero.

After Drawing 2 is created with Cashflow Netting enabled, the total dues of USD 39,000.00 of the facility, existing drawing, and current drawing are handed over to the facility and the dues are repaid based on payment rules or payment priority. The remaining amount of USD 961,000.00 is settled to the borrower's account.

The outstanding dues are as follows:

Facility - USD 33,000.00

Drawing 1 - USD 5,000.00

Drawing 2 - USD 1,000.00

Total - USD 39,000.00

The user creates Drawing 3 with USD 4M commitment amount and an additional amount of USD 2M with Cashflow Netting enabled with an outstanding due of USD 2,000.00

An override message is displayed, that indicates the due amount is being settled against Drawing 3 only, as Drawing 2 is already settled with the total due amount for the facility and its associated drawings.

Cashflow Netting is defaulted from the facility sub-arrangement condition as shown below.

The Auto Disbursement Fee of 0.10% is applied to the transaction amount.

An Auto Disbursement Fee is charged during the auto disbursement process as specified in the Activity Charges.

The system credits the Disbursement amount to the borrower's account as specified in the settlement instructions.

An overview of drawing 3 for which Cashflow Netting is enabled, ensuring all respective dues are settled during auto disbursement.

Auto disbursement fees are settled, reducing their balances to zero.

After Drawing 3 is created with Cashflow Netting enabled, current drawing dues of USD 2,000.00 are handed over to the facility and the due is repaid based on payment rules or payment priority. The remaining amount of USD 1,998,000.00 is settled to the borrower's account.


##### Limitations on Cashflow Netting

There are several limitations to enable Cashflow Netting , like

- Cashflow Netting is not applicable for manual disbursement.
- Deal level dues are not considered for netting.
- Dues across facilities are not considered for netting.
- Cashflow Netting will not happen for drawings whose currency is different from facility currency.
- Rollover activity without commitment increase is not considered for Cashflow Netting .
- A flat fee for auto disbursement is charged twice during the auto disbursement activity. Alternatively, a flat fee can be applied as a new arrangement fee.


##### Cashflow Netting Validations

- If Cashflow Netting is enabled at the facility-level, an error message appears as ‘Cash flow netting is allowed only for Lending products’ during proofing of the product.
- If Cashflow Netting is provided as 'Yes' in the facility sub-arrangement condition and Net Settlement Activity is ‘blank’ at the drawing product level, an error message appears as, 'Net Settlement activity is mandatory' at drawing arrangement level.
- If Net Settlement Activity is provided with a value other than appropriate repayment activity, an error message appears as 'Invalid activity for cash flow netting'.
- If Net Settlement activity is provided in the drawing product level and Cashflow Netting is blank, an error message appears as 'Cash flow Netting is mandatory' at the drawing arrangement level (This occurs when Cashflow Netting is not defined in the sub-arrangement condition of the facility).
- When the user tries to create a facility in USD currency and drawdown in EUR currency with Cashflow Netting enabled, then an error message appears as 'Cash flow netting is permitted only when the drawdown currency is same as the facility currency'.
- When the user tries to enable Cashflow Netting for a standalone drawing, then an error message appears as 'Cash flow netting is allowed only for drawings under facility'.
- When the user tries to enable Cashflow Netting for a club loan under facility with the Banks Role as Participant, then an error message appears as 'Cash flow netting is not allowed for Banks Role as Participant'.


#### 📋 Tasks

There are no Tasks available for Cashflow Netting feature.


#### 📊 Outputs

There are no Outputs available for Cashflow Netting feature.

### 2.11  Combined Bills


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Facility can have one or more drawing arrangements, with each mortgage (drawing) arrangement having its own payment schedule, which generates bills when items are due for payment. To provide a single source of billing to a customer and enable for single repayment, it is required that the bills gener...*
> 
> **Applications:** `AA.PAYMENT.TYPE`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Combine Bill At Parent*, *Combine Bills At Parent*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

Facility can have one or more drawing arrangements, with each mortgage (drawing) arrangement having its own payment schedule, which generates bills when items are due for payment. To provide a single source of billing to a customer and enable for single repayment, it is required that the bills generated at the mortgage arrangement (drawing) level with the same due date are consolidated to a single facility level bill using the facility’s account number.

If settlement is configured with Direct Debit (DD) or Payment Order, then a single DD or order is generated for the consolidated bill. The bills will be combined only when the customers or owners are the same in facility and drawings, that is, when the customer attribute of Sub Arrangement rules is set to All Parent Customer(s) or Owner(s).


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The Payment Schedule Property Class defines the combined bills at facility level.

> **⚠️ Note:** This happens when the owners or customers and bill date of the particular bills are same under a facility.

To generate the combined bills at facility level, set Combine Bill At Parent to Yes on each payment type in AA.PAYMENT.TYPE

To combine the bills of the underlying arrangements at the facility level, the user must configure the following drawing conditions.

- The customer of the drawings whose bills are to be combined must be the same.
- The currency of the drawings whose bills are to be combined must be the same.
- Set Combine Bills At Parent to Yes on each Payment Type in AA.PAYMENT.TYPE used in the drawings.
- The system bill type of the drawings should be same.
- The bills of the drawings must be issued on the same day (with or without advance bills produced).
- The bills drawings must be made due on the same day (with or without deferred bills setup).


#### 📋 Tasks

There are no Tasks available for Combined Bills feature.

Combined bills .

This enquiry displays the combined bill details of the multiple drawing arrangements created under facility arrangement.

Combined payment schedule feature at facility consolidates the repayment schedules of all the drawings under the facility. It aggregates the payments that fall on the same date and of same currency.

So, when facility has multiple arrangements under it, the schedule will be combined at the facility level. The drill down against each payment date launches an enquiry that provides the component-wise breakup of the payments. Enquiry provides break-up on each arrangement to which the payment components belong to.

### 2.13  Combined payoff


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Facility pre-closure is a process when a customer repays all the loans under a facility before the loan tenure ends. For example, the pre-closure of a mortgage loan indicates that the customer is willing to close the mortgage loan before the completion of its repayment period.*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Arrangement*, *Closure Reason*, *Credit Amount*, *Settle Dues*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

Facility pre-closure is a process when a customer repays all the loans under a facility before the loan tenure ends. For example, the pre-closure of a mortgage loan indicates that the customer is willing to close the mortgage loan before the completion of its repayment period.

This option can be executed on Facility when the customer wants to close a contract with the bank for reasons, such as getting a new mortgage loan or change of ownership in underlying property. Pre-closure can also be done for non-paying assets. Single Payoff statement gets generated at facility level with individual bill IDs for drawings.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The Payoff Property Class generates the payoff statement at the Facility arrangement level. The Payment Priority condition is configured to trigger settle payoff activity in the individual arrangements. When Payment Priority is triggered, a part of settle payoff transaction allocates, the Payoff bill amount to the individual arrangements.

The settlement activity for regular repayment under FACILITY-APPLYPAYMENT-PAYMENT.RULES Activity Class is entered in Facility product. While settling the payment, Temenos Transact applies the payment to the loans under the facility. Settle Act is the settlement Activity for calculating the payoff amount either in simulation mode or when the arrangement is paid-off in live using Settle Activity of Payoff Property Class.

> **⚠️ Note:** Pre-closure charge must be configured only on this Activity.

The Settle Dues field specifies the bills that are due between simulation date and payoff effective date should be considered as settled. When set to Yes, the payoff amount does not consider the due amount while calculating the payoff amount.

During pay-off,

- The funds are appropriated based on the payment rule defined in the Payoff condition.
- When the funds are exhausted and there are unsettled balances in the loan, the tolerance check is done.
- If the short fall amount is less than or equal to the tolerance defined (as % or amount), the shortfall amount is written off.
- The write-off sequence is from the property or balance with the least priority. It moves from the least priority to the highest priority.


#### 📋 Tasks

Related topics:

- Lending Processes (Corporate)

Facility can have one or more drawing arrangements with each drawings arrangement having its own payment schedule, generating bills when items are due for payment. Single repayment is enabled for the bills generated at the drawings arrangement level with the same due date are consolidated to a single facility level bill and is enabled using the facility’s account number. Combined Payoff can be executed on Facility when the customer wants to close a contract with the bank before its maturity. Pre-closure can also be done for non-paying assets. Single Payoff statement gets generated at facility level with individual bill IDs for drawings.

| Find Facility Arrangements | Enter facility arrangement ID in the Arrangement field. Click the FIND button. Click the Overview icon corresponding to a record. |
| Arrangement Overview (Facility) | Click the RUN icon corresponding to the Request Payoff activity. |
| Calculate Payoff | Select a value in the Closure Reason field. Click the Validate icon to check for errors and overrides. Click the Commit icon. Run the BNK/AA.SIMULATION.SERVICE simulation service. |
| Arrangement Overview (Facility) | Click the View icon corresponding to the Payoff statement activity. |
|  | AA Pay-off . |
| Facility Pay-off | Enter values in the following fields: Credit Account Debit Account Number Payment Currency Payment Amount Payment Execution Date Click the Validate icon to check for errors and overrides. Click the Commit icon. |

### 2.15  Covenants and Conditions


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Covenants and Conditions are the conditions, which a borrower needs to fulfill to extend the facility or a drawing. A Covenant must hold true throughout the life of an arrangement (for example, a Deal or Facility) and should be validated on a certain frequency. A Condition must be true to allow cert...*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Arrangement*, *Bill Produced*, *Complex Data Element*, *Consequence*, *Covenant Notice Days*, *Data Routine*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

Covenants and Conditions are the conditions, which a borrower needs to fulfill to extend the facility or a drawing. A Covenant must hold true throughout the life of an arrangement (for example, a Deal or Facility) and should be validated on a certain frequency. A Condition must be true to allow certain activities to occur.

Various Conditions that a bank may receive for a corporate customer are:

- Does not additional debt
- Pays taxes on time
- Maintains a Debt Service Ratio
- Maintain an LTV
- Pays salaries to employees on time
- Risk Rating of BBB or above

Covenants and Conditions must be proven, by providing an evidence that the borrower is in compliance. This evidence can be one-time or on a recurring frequency.

This functionality deals with the ability to control the drawdowns which have evidence requirements that the borrower of the bank must submit. Before entering into a loan contract, the borrower agrees to submit certain documents and also accepts few conditions proposed by the bank failing which the bank can decide some consequence that the borrower has to face.

The requirements of the bank might not be constant throughout the life of the contract. For example, the bank would prefer the borrower to initially maintain a debt to equity ratio of less than 0.5%. Later, the bank can revise it to less than 1%.

The borrower is not complaint in case of,

- Conditions - An activity such as a new drawing (Example: lending or guarantee), can be prohibited.
- Covenant - The facility can be set to zero.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

Read Evidence class and Evidence requirement set up from the Origination module – OA as a pre-requisite to set the Product Conditions under Evidence Property Class.

The Evidence Property Class is configured to check the covenants and conditions during the life cycle of a contract. Evidences is validated during creation of a new arrangement, update activity and closure of activity. Evidence Property Class is applicable for Deal, Facility and Drawing and Guarantees Product Lines and it is an optional property class.

The evidence requirement is captured in EV.EVIDENCE.REQUIREMENT . The category of the evidence requirements are created in EV.REQUIREMENT.CATEGORY (virtual table). The consequences are the actions taken by the bank in situations where the covenants and conditions are not satisfied. So, the consequences are tagged to AA.ACTION for which the activity type is configured as Evidence Check in the relevant record of AA.ACTIVITY.CLASS .

This table enables the bank user to create customised evidence template as per the requirement of the bank.

For example, if a bank enters into a loan contract with a construction company. As per the contract, the loan amount is scheduled to be disbursed at regular intervals. Before each disbursement, the bank must verify the progress of the construction and check if the amount utilised is not more than the percentage of construction completion. An example evidence template for this is shown in the below screenshot.

This is the table where the system creates a record for the evidence condition.

This table enables the user to publish the record of evidence class. The status must be Completed Successfully once it is published as shown in the below screenshot.

This tables enables the user to create a record for any related evidence requirement.

In reference to the above example, the bank may prefer the borrower to stay compliant with a condition, where the difference between the drawdown percentage and the construction readiness percentage shall not exceed 5. Therefore, the borrower must submit the construction readiness report (main evidence) and additionally maintain a variance of less than 5.

This additional requirement related to the variance percentage falls under the related requirement category. In this example the drawdown percentage is tracked from the loan contract and the construction readiness percentage is taken from the evidence submitted by the borrower.

So, two records have to be created for the related evidences in AA.DATA.ELEMENTS . For the drawdown percentage an AA.LOCAL.GET.UTILISED.RATIO API is defined in the Data Routine field to calculate the utilised percentage from the loan contract as on date. Similarly, another data element for construction readiness percentage is created.

This table enables the bank user to create a record which defines various requirements to be satisfied for a particular evidence. Consider the same example. where the user creates a record for the construction readiness report (main evidence) as shown in the below screenshot.

> **⚠️ Note:** Here, the requirement is that the borrower has to submit this report when a particular event takes place, for example, while creating a new loan contract or during disbursement, and so on.

Similarly, another record namely,variance percentage for the related evidence is created as shown in the below screenshot.

> **⚠️ Note:** Here, the borrower of the bank has to stay compliant in the accepted variance specified in the contract.

The Complex Data Element field enables the bank to attach conditions involving complex calculations where the data must be fetched from multiple tables.

In the above example, the variance percentage is the difference between drawdown percentage and construction readiness percentage . During runtime, the system has to fetch the following details to calculate and check the variance percentage.

- Drawdown percentage from the loan contract
- Construction readiness percentage from the evidence submitted as on that date

A condition is created and attached to the EVIDENCE property under the respective loan product. Read the Evidence property class and Covenant Conditions feature for more information..

The below configuration in the Covenant tab implies that the borrower of the bank has to submit a borrower base certificate every year on a recurring basis effective from the start date of the contract. The Covenant Notice Days field is set to 10D, to imply that the system raises a notice 10 days prior to the actual due date of the evidence. (Enquiry needs to be pulled by the user).

> **⚠️ Note:** The evidence once submitted is not requested or made due by Transact upon every due date in the future. The system makes use of the already submitted evidence until the user submits a new evidence when made available.

The first half of the configuration in the Condition tab implies that the construction readiness report is due on creating a drawing contract and while issuing the disbursement bills before every disbursement scheduled under the contract.

And the second half of the configuration in the Condition tab is a related evidence requirement, where the borrower must maintain a variance percentage which should not exceed 5. If the variance percentage exceeds 5, then the disbursement is stopped as defined in the Consequence field.

When the bank user prefers to make an evidence condition due few days prior to the actual disbursement date, then the Bill Produced field in the Payment Schedule Property Class is configured as shown in the below screenshot.

As per this condition, the first disbursement happens on Apr 30, followed by other disbursements on May 31, Jun 30 and Jul 31. Transact generates the disbursement bill 10 days prior to each disbursement, so for the disbursement scheduled on Apr 30, the bill is generated on Apr 20.

If the evidence condition is set as due on the event of issuance of disbursement bill, then the evidence condition which is dependent on the disbursement bill activity is also due 10 days in advance.

Add the forward dating type to the Evidence property attached to the loan product. The evidence condition which needs to be in effect at present and later, both can be added when creating the contract or later using this feature.

Covenants and Conditions are the conditions, which a borrower needs to fulfill to extend a loan. A Covenant must hold true throughout the life of an arrangement (for example, a Deal or Facility) and should be validated on a certain frequency. A Condition must be true to allow certain activities to occur. Covenants and Conditions must be proven by providing an evidence that the borrower is in compliance. This evidence can be one-time or on a recurring frequency.

#### 📖 Introduction

Facility is part of the Corporate or Retail Banking AA suite of products. Facility arrangement helps the bank to record the terms and conditions of the agreement between the bank and its customers, relating to the loan sanctioned. Activities such as New Arrangement, Preclosure, Take Over, Facility Repayment, Combined Bills, Combined Schedule, Charge Off and so on can be performed on arrangements.

Guarantees and SBLCs are non-fund-based drawings where the facility availability is dropped without cash remit. But the credit risk of the Guarantee or SBLC is like the funded drawings (lending). The complete life cycle of a Guarantee is embedded in the Facility module. The life cycle of a Guarantee includes:

- Creating a deal and facility.
- Registering the issuance of the guarantee.
- Collection of fees and commissions.
- Facility maintenance and closure.

##### Proof and Publish

A product must be proofed and published to view the product in Product Catalog. Read the Product Builder user guide for more information. Alternatively, it can also be proofed and published using the AA.PRODUCT.MANAGER application.

### 2.17  Customer Negotiation for Facility


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The AA.ARR.CUSTOMER table,*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

The AA.ARR.CUSTOMER table,

- Identifies if there is more than one customer to the arrangement.
- Stores the tax liability, limit allocation and GL allocation at arrangement level.

The bank can do the following:

- Change the facility ownership based on the customer request.
- Add or remove a customer to the facility ownership.
- Change the ownership of the facility customers.
- Add other customers to an account with a specific role (power of attorney or joint holder).

The Change Customer Activity (FACILITY-CHANGE-CUSTOMER) can be used to change the customer of or to add new customers to the facility. These customers are facility holders and the eligibility rule is evaluated for all the customers during the Change Activity. When the ownership is moved, it impacts the limit provided to the facility. This activity triggers a change in the limit details required for the new customer.

The Update Customer Activity (FACILITY-UPDATE-CUSTOMER) changes or updates the other parties of the account. The role of the other party has to be specified. For example, another customer can be added as a guarantor.

Lending structure calls for series of restrictions, rights and obligations on borrower and lender group, relating to commitment of fund and how funding occurs against various commitments. One among them is structuring the borrower group at drawing level. The financial institution (FI) requires the restriction of minimum and maximum number of customer allowed for the product. This restriction is achieved using existing functionality negotiation rules.

### 2.18  Deal


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *A deal or bilateral credit agreement is an agreement between two parties, the lender and the borrower, who agree to certain terms and conditions and their rights and obligations. The agreements are governed by the Loan Market Association (LMA) and LSTA documentation standards depending on the nature...*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Customer Role*, *Customer, Currency*, *Date*, *Group Level*, *Limit Id*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

A deal or bilateral credit agreement is an agreement between two parties, the lender and the borrower, who agree to certain terms and conditions and their rights and obligations. The agreements are governed by the Loan Market Association (LMA) and LSTA documentation standards depending on the nature of the agreement. As business situations are volatile, the credit agreements are not static. The borrower or lender can re-negotiate the terms and conditions over time and hence an Amendment or Restructure can be affected, that is, the new terms and conditions must be updated systematically.

The structure starts at the deal. The most fundamental aspect is the Facilities that make up the deal and are drawn down using the drawing products. Some of the features of deal are:

- It can contain a single customer or multiple customers, and the facility or facilities created from the deal can be with any or all of the customers based on the definition at deal.
- A Facility is a restriction of the deal commitment or terms. Multiple arrangements or facilities are possible under a single deal.
- The facility currency can be different from the deal currency, based on the definition at deal.
- The facility or facilities under the deal or credit agreement can have their own unique terms and attributes, as long as they are a subset of the deal conditions as the deal is the agreement that contains all the terms and conditions.
- Drawings under a Facility must be requested by the borrower. Prior to funding the drawing, the facility agent on a club or syndicated loan checks the terms and conditions of the credit agreement for the said facility and funds the draw if compliant.
- Drawings represent any form of funding or utilisation under a commitment. Drawings under a credit agreement include on balance sheet items (loans, deposits, repos) and contingent liability (off Balance Sheet) items such as Standby Letter of Credit (SBLCs).

The complete lifecycle of a loan beginning with the deal (bilateral credit agreement) creation, facility creation, loan booking, disbursement, collection, maintenance till closure is all embedded in the Facility module. It supports an entire range of lending features with configurable conditions.

The financial institution can design a variety of Deal products to cater to the requirement of various customer segments. The Temenos three-layer product configuration mechanism (that is, Product Line, -Product Group and Product), which is available in the Product Builder application, supports product designing and configuration. This application helps the financial institution to deliver the product on time. Temenos’ robust arrangement architecture helps to minimise the time consumed to go to market with the product and modify the characteristics of the product as and when required, with flexible configuration and with minimal customisation approach.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

A deal (bilateral credit agreement) uses the Facility Product Line for creation of products. The following section describes the Deal product configuration.


##### Property Classes

The Facility module in AA.PRODUCT.LINE provides high-level definition of the business components (Property Classes) required for Facility Product Line, out of which only the following are applicable for Deal products.

> **⚠️ Note:** The Product Lines are defined by Temenos and cannot be modified.

The financial institution then uses the business components to build individual Deal products based on the customer target segment requirements. The list of Property Classes applicable to the Deal product group are:

| Activity charges | Activity restriction | Agent commission |
| Interest | Overdue | Payment rules |
| Payout rules | Pricing rules | Periodic Charges |
| Sub Arrangement Condition | Sub-limit | Tax |
| Transaction rules |  |  |


##### Product Group Setup

As both Facility and Deal products use the same Facility product line, there is a Group Level attribute that can be marked as Deal if the product created is a Deal product.


#### 🔧 Working With

The following section describes the creation of a deal arrangement, drawing rules, covenants and conditions and accounting as well.


##### Creating Deal Arrangement

The Facility product line is used to configure a Deal product. This allows the financial institutions to create a deal or credit agreement that helps the customers to take multiple facilities under the deal (using the same or different facility products) with each facility arrangement having its own unique conditions. From the product catalogue, the user selects the Deal product and creates a Deal arrangement. Then, the user enters the mandatory field values like Customer, Currency and other optional fields and validates the record. The fields like Date and Customer Role , if not defined are auto-populated on validation. The arrangement conditions like attaching a Limit Id to the customer, commitment amount and term for the Deal can be defined.

The user has to provide the validation limit in the Limit Id field in Deal and the utilisation limit is created automatically while creating a Facility under a deal.

The Deal arrangement created allows the user to create multiple facility arrangements under a deal. To create a Facility, click New Facility in the Deal overview screen.

The products available to utilise under the Deal as defined in the Sub-Arrangement rules Property Class are listed.

When the user clicks the New Arrangement icon against the product, the new Arrangement screen is displayed. The master Deal ID gets auto-populated to denote that this is the child-arrangement. While creating a Facility under a deal, the utilisation limit is created for the facility amount automatically if the serial number is given as NEW in the Limit Property Class. Read the Facility Creation user guide for more information.

The Facility amount cannot be higher than the Deal total commitment amount. Multiple drawings can be created under a single Deal arrangement either with the same currency of Deal or multi-currency facilities based on the allowed currency in the Sub-Arrangement Rules Property Class.


##### Drawing Rules

The Sub-Arrangement Rules Property Class defines the conditions for the sub-arrangements (Facility/lending) of the deal. Sub-Arrangement Rules are used to apply conditions while creating new Facility and lending arrangements under a Deal. It is possible to restrict the customer, currency and product of the drawings arrangements created under the Deal. Sub- arrangement rules restrict the user to create a Facility or Lending under a deal with different customer, currency and products.

There are various options to define the rules for the allowed customer, allowed currency and allowed products. It can be used to:

- Allow drawings only for beneficial owners, parent customers or certain allowed list of customers.
- Allow drawings only in the parent or Facility currency or in certain allowed list of currencies.
- Allow drawings of any product or certain allowed list of products.

Read Sub Arrangement rules PC for more information on the use of each option for Customer, currency and product.


##### Covenants and Conditions

The Evidence Property Class defines the covenants and conditions for the sub-arrangements (Facility/lending) of the deal. Covenants and Conditions are used to apply conditions while creating new Facility and lending arrangements under a deal.

Refer Covenants and Conditions PC and for more information.


##### Accounting

The Corporate Lending (AA) module utilises the framework of rule based accounting to generate its accounting movements. The accounting functionality is used by all financial products and controls the link between accounting events and allocation rules to be applied to these events. The adjustments in Interest and Charges across accounting periods can be booked in a different Profit and Loss head, for better accounting. It is possible to report the Income and Expense arising out of Negative rates in a different Profit and Loss head. Charges collected or paid to the customer can be accounted either in customer’s home branch or the loan origination branch. The waivers or discounts in charges can be accounted separately or as a net entry.

The Corporate Lending module utilizes the framework of rule based accounting to generate its accounting movements. Funds can be settled using Settlement Property Class, Payment rules and Payout rules setup. For transactions within AA framework soft accounting drives the accounting setup and transaction codes for accounting entries. Both debit and credit transactions can be posted to the loans using account based applications such as Teller or Funds Transfer. The transaction codes of the respective application is mapped with AA.ACTIVITY in Activity Mapping Property Class. Further, accounting is based on Activity triggered using the Payment rules and Payout rules, respectively

Deal Accounting

After the deal (Credit agreement) is booked in Temenos Transact, accounting entries are not raised for the deal amount. Only when the Facility or Lending arrangements are created under the deal, the accounting entries are raised as shown below.

Deal Balances

When the new deal (credit arrangement) is booked, the commitment amount is not booked and no accounting entries are raised.
