### 2.19  Defining Default SSI


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The Corporate Lending suite now enables booking of deals and facilities with multiple borrowers or currencies. Arrangement Architecture (AA) facilitates this, by letting the user to define the default settlement account or beneficiary ID based on the customers and/or currencies at the deal and/or fa...*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Arrangement*, *Beneficiary*, *Beneficiary ID*, *Def Account*, *Def Beneficiary*, *Def Ccy*, *Def Customer*, *Default Po Product* ... +4 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

The Corporate Lending suite now enables booking of deals and facilities with multiple borrowers or currencies. Arrangement Architecture (AA) facilitates this, by letting the user to define the default settlement account or beneficiary ID based on the customers and/or currencies at the deal and/or facility level.

Furthermore, the default settlement instructions defined at the deal or the facility level flows down to the underlying facility or drawings. Based on the customer and currency of the child arrangement, the default settlement account or beneficiary ID is validated and defaulted only if the PAYIN / PAYOUT Account or Beneficiary ID details in the Settlement Property Class are left blank in the child arrangement.

> **⚠️ Note:** Default settlement instructions need not be defined at the Drawings level.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

To inherit the default settlement instructions from the Deal to Facility level and/or from Facility to Drawings level, the Source Property and Target Property of the Settlement Property Class should be defined in the Inheritance Product Condition.

The user has to configure the Inheritance Product Condition as explained in the following sections.

> **⚠️ Note:** Tracking type of property is not allowed in Inheritance Property class.


##### At Facility Level

When the Target Property and Source Property of the Inheritance Product Condition are set as SETTLEMENT and Inheritance is set as Yes, it enables inheritance of the settlement instructions from Deal To Facility, that is, this set up considers the Facility arrangement as the Target.


##### At Drawings Level

When the Target Property and Source Property of the Inheritance Product Condition are set as SETTLEMENT and Inheritance is set as Yes, it enables inheritance of the settlement instructions from the Facility to Drawings, that is this set up considers the Drawing arrangement as Target.

The following attributes in the Settlement Product Condition defaults the settlement instructions to the child arrangements in line with settlement details captured in Inheritance Product Condition.

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Def Ccy | Specifies the currency of the arrangement for which the settlement instruction applies. It has to be a valid currency from the CURRENCY table. It is multi-value field and input is optional. |
| Def Customer | Specifies the customer of the arrangement for which the settlement instruction applies. It must be either a valid customer number or customer mnemonic of a customer on the CUSTOMER table. It is multi-value field and input is optional. |
| Def Account | This is the default settlement account field. This field is part of the multi-value set for defining the default settlement instructions. This can be specified for each settlement customer and currency wise. This account is used if there is no pay-in or pay-out account/beneficiary is specified in the settlement instructions. |
| Def Beneficiary | Specifies the default beneficiary id for the customer and currency specified. This beneficiary is used for incoming and outgoing transactions if pay-in or pay-out account/beneficiary details are not given. It has to be a valid record from the BENEFICIARY table. Input to this field is mandatory , when the Default Po Product field is not blank. |

> **⚠️ Note:** At the product designer level the Settlement property should be defined as Non-tracking.


#### 🔧 Working With

The user can define standard settlement instructions (SSI) using the multi-value set of fields: Def Customer , Def Ccy and its respective Def Account , Def Beneficiary either at the Deal or the Facility level as shown in the below screen shot.


##### Inheritance of SSI - Deal to Facility

When a Facility arrangement is created from a Deal, the default settlement instruction is inherited into the Facility from the master arrangement , that is, Deal. The flow is similar, when a Drawing arrangement is created from a Facility. The default settlement instructions inherited from the master arrangement are illustrated below:

The inheritance of default settlement instructions from Deal to Facility is shown below:


##### Inheritance of SSI - Facility to Drawings

During the repayment of principal, interest or charges, if the PAYIN / PAYOUT Account or Beneficiary details are not defined in the Settlement Property Class of the child arrangement, then the Def Account or Def Beneficiary values are used in the settlement instruction. The order of precedence is:

- Priority 1 – Customer and Currency
- Priority 2 – Customer
- Priority 3 – Currency
- Priority 4 – Generic Definition (Default Account and Default Beneficiary defined without default customer and currency.

The user can apply the settlement instructions at the child arrangement level from Deal to Facility, and the workflow applies for Facility to Drawings as well.

Consider a Facility arrangement is in USD. Transact uses the USD account as the settlement account among the multiple default settlement instructions defined, based on the order of precedence of the arrangement customer.

USD account is not defined specifically for the customer 100301. Hence the generic account is applied while settlement.

The Inheritance of default settlement instruction from Facility to Drawings is shown below:

The Upfront fee is settled on Apr 19, 20201 as shown below.

The entry below shows the debit from A/C number 113832. This depicts the inheritance of default settlement instruction from Facility to Drawings.


#### 📋 Tasks

The Settlement Property Class allows the user to define the default settlement instructions for the drawings in the facility. These instructions are used to apply the conditions while creating new lending arrangements under a facility. These values also get inherited to the drawing arrangements created under the facility.

### 2.22  Exchange Rate Tolerance


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *A borrower can draw a facility in an alternate pre-defined currency other than the facility currency. When a Facility commitment currency is GBP, the Borrower is allowed to make drawings in both GBP and USD. When a USD borrowing occurs, a foreign exchange rate must be provided to convert back to GBP...*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

A borrower can draw a facility in an alternate pre-defined currency other than the facility currency. When a Facility commitment currency is GBP, the Borrower is allowed to make drawings in both GBP and USD. When a USD borrowing occurs, a foreign exchange rate must be provided to convert back to GBP as it is the Facility currency. The system defaults this FX rate using a rate table that the user updates or manually inputs.

During the time of Contract creation, the system applies an FX Tolerance rate to the contract. The user must refer this FX Tolerance when the FX rates are re-calculated for the drawings in the future. This FX Tolerance can either be a percentage or an actual FX rate movement. The system gives a warning when the difference between the old and the new FX rate falls outside the specified tolerance, and if the new FX rate is within the FX Tolerance, the existing FX rate remains the same.

In addition, a credit agreement permits the commitment amount to be exceeded due to the fluctuations with the FX rate. For example, when a Facility is fully utilized, and at the time of repricing an alternate currency drawing, the change in the FX rate (outside of the FX Tolerance range) exceeds the Commitment amount, the system only warns the user by generating an override but lets the user to continue. At Facility level, this will result in the commitment to get overdrawn.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The Exchange Rate Tolerance feature has no specific configuration to be set up. The parameter applications are setup at the implementation stage.


#### 🔧 Working With

The below section details the Exchange Rate Tolerance in Lending.


##### Handling Scheduled FX Rate Fix - Within Tolerance

Consider the user creates an offer contract under a facility in GBP currency. The FX rate in the currency table on the date of offer creation is 1.8376 as shown in the below screenshot.

The user enters the FX rate as 1.7 and the tolerance value as 0.2 during creation of offer as shown in the below screenshot.

Tolerance calculation

- Cap value: 1.9 (1.7+0.2)
- Floor Value: 1.5 (1.7-0.2)

Since the user given rate (1.7) is within the above tolerance, the existing rate of the contract remains the same when the offer goes live.


##### Handling Scheduled FX Rate Fix - Breaching Tolerance

Consider the user creates an offer contract under a facility in GBP currency. The FX rate in the currency table on the date of contract creation is 1.8376 as shown in the below screenshot.

The user enters the FX rate as 1.3 and the tolerance value as 0.2 as shown in the below screenshot during offer creation.

Tolerance calculation

- Cap value: 1.5 (1.3+0.2)
- Floor Value: 1.1 (1.3-0.2)

Since the value in the currency table (1.8376) breaches the tolerance of the existing rate (Floor 1.1; Cap 1.5), the system applies the value in the currency table to the contract after the offer goes live as shown in the screenshot below.


##### Handling Manual Rate Fix - Within Tolerance

When the borrower has a Bilateral Facility for USD 500,000.00 with a bank, and the initial drawing made for EUR 100,000.00, then by default the system picks the FX rate on the day of drawing creation (1.0476) from the currency table while creating the loan arrangement and applies to the contract.

After the drawdown under the facility, the ECB balance where the system converts the loan of EUR 100,000.00 to USD 104,760.00 with FX 1.0476 is shown in the screenshot below:

When the user triggers the change exchange rate activity manually, then the contract opens with the existing rate of 1.0476.

The tolerance value calculated using the existing rate is shown below:

- Existing Rate: 1.0476
- Tolerance: 5%
- Value: 0.05238
- Floor: 0.99522 (1.0476-0.05238)
- Cap: 1.09998 (1.0476+0.05238)

The user edits the rate to 1.09, which is within the above calculated tolerance.

The system accepts the rate entered by the user (1.09) and applies the same rate to the contract as shown in the screenshot below:

The system updates the ECB balance after the FX rate change to 1.09 under the loan arrangement.

The ECB Balance where the system converted the loan amount of EUR 100,000.00 to USD 109,000.00 with FX 1.09 is shown in the screenshot below:


##### Handling Manual Rate Fix-Breaching Tolerance

When the borrower has a Bilateral Facility for USD 500,000.00 with a bank, and the initial drawing made for EUR 100,000.00, then the system picks the FX rate on the day of contract creation (say1.0476) from the currency table while creating the loan arrangement and applies to the contract.

After the drawdown under the facility, the ECB balance where the system converts the loan of EUR 100,000.00 to USD 104,760.00 with FX 1.0476 is shown in the screenshot below.

When the user triggers change exchange rate activity manually, then the contract opens with the existing rate of 1.0476. The tolerance value calculated using the existing rate is shown below:

- Existing FX rate: 1.0476
- Tolerance Value: 0.10
- Floor: 0.94760 (1.0476-0.10)
- Cap: 1.14760 (1.0476+0.10)

The user edits the rate to 1.20, which breaches the tolerance. Even though the rate breaches the tolerance, the user entered rate of 1.20 is applied to the contract.

When the rate breaches the tolerance, the system throws a warning and checks if the user wants to continue.

The system updates the ECB balance after the FX rate change to 1.20 under the loan arrangement. The ECB balance where the system converted the loan amount of EUR 100,000.00 to USD 120,000.00 with FX 1.20 is shown in the screenshot below.


#### 📋 Tasks

There are no Tasks available for Exchange Tolerance Feature.

### 2.23  Facility Charges


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Charges can be scheduled on,*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Accrue / Period*, *Accrue Amort*, *Accrue Period*, *Action*, *Activity*, *Application Method*, *Arrangement*, *Calc Type* ... +4 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

Charges can be scheduled on,

- Regular frequency
- Occurrence of a specific activity
- Breaching the terms and conditions accepted during arrangement creation.

Charges can be fixed amount or calculated amount or combination of both and it is calculated on tiered amounts from the facility. It can be accrued or amortised over a period. It can be negotiated while processing Facility arrangements. It can be collected on facility and it can be skipped or ignored at drawing level.


##### Upfront Fee Accounting Treatment at Facility

The upfront fee accounting treatment at facility describes the accounting treatment applicable to commitment fee and loan origination fee in bank books. As per IFRS9 standards, the loan originating fee received by the lender for commitment under an undrawn term facility must defer the postings or fee to the Profit and Loss (P&L) account until the drawdown date.

Later, the postings are recognized based on the drawdown’s cash flow. The loan originating fee is also considered for calculating Effective Interest Rate (EIR) of the drawdown.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This topic enables the user to understand the facility level charges.


##### Regular Charges – Frequency Based

The user can set up a charge, which is charged in a fixed frequency. The charge can be fixed amount or calculated based on a commitment amount. The user can have different tiers to calculate the charges based on the source balance on which it is calculated. The user can set the Tier Type as Level and Calc Type as Percentage to calculate the unutilised amount. If the requesting currency and the currency defined in Currency field are different, then the system converts the base amount to charge currency equivalent and calculates the charge amount.


##### Activity Based Charges

It defines the charges that need to be applied when an activity is triggered on Facility arrangement. Activity charges are fixed amount or calculated from the facility amount. Once the arrangement is committed by setting Application Method to Due, the activity charges are due for payment and bill is generated. The activity for which this charge being calculated should be mentioned in the Activity field. For example, to setup an activity for creation of new facility, the Activity field is set as FACILITY-NEW-ARRANGEMENT.


##### Accounting Property Class

Facility New arrangement fee can be set as Amort or Accrue in Accrue / Period field. Arrangement fee is amortised throughout the period of the Facility arrangement.


##### Upfront Fee for Accounting Treatment at Facility

To initiate the accounting for the upfront fee, the user can configure the Charge and Accounting property conditions in Facility and Drawings respectively.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Action | TRANSFER.AMORT |
| Accrue Amort | Amort Defer |
| Accrue Period | MATURITY or EXPIRY |

To configure Charge and Accounting conditions:

1. Create an allocation rule record in AC.ALLOCATION.RULE with Event Type set to CHARGE.RECEIVE.AMORT.ACC.

1. In the Accounting product conditions for Drawings, add the RECEIVE.AMORT action to the Charge property class in the Defaults Values tab. This action receives the fee from the facility to drawings.

1. In AA.PRD.CAT.ACCOUNTING , map the allocation rule record with the RECEIVE.AMORT charge type.
2. Proof and publish the products. Read the Products Builder section for more information.

> **⚠️ Note:** The user has to ensure that Drawings has the Reporting property conditions to support amortization based on EIR and IFRS9 reporting.


#### 📋 Tasks

Related topics:

- Lending Processes (Corporate)

Charges can be fixed or calculated amount or combination of both and it is calculated on tiered amounts from the facility. It can be:

- Accrued or amortised over a period
- Negotiated while processing Facility arrangements
- Collected on facility
- Skipped or ignored at drawing level

### 2.24  Facility Closure


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Facility is closed automatically during Close of Business (COB) process if there is no debit balance in a loan account on the maturity date. The loan is then treated as closed. If debit balance in the loan account continues even after the maturity date, then the bank can charge penalty fee on the ou...*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Arrangement*, *Closure Method*, *Closure Period*, *Closure Type*, *Posting Restrict*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

Facility is closed automatically during Close of Business (COB) process if there is no debit balance in a loan account on the maturity date. The loan is then treated as closed. If debit balance in the loan account continues even after the maturity date, then the bank can charge penalty fee on the outstanding debit balance.

The Arrangement records are moved from the AA.CUSTOMER.ARRANGEMENT to the AA.CUSTOMER.ARRANGEMENT.HIST on closure of a facility. Records are moved from the AA.CUSTOMER.ARRANGEMENT.HIST to the AA.CUSTOMER.ARRANGEMENT during a history restore.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The system automatically closes the account associated with facility arrangement when,

- All balances associated with the facility and underlying drawing or lending arrangements becomes zero.
- The arrangement matures (provided all the balances are settled).

This is defined in the Closure Type field. The bank can specify a date from which the Arrangement is identified for closure and after which the closure activity is triggered. The system schedules the closure activity based on the period mentioned in the Closure Period field.

The bank can select the mode of closing the arrangement account in the Closure Method field. The options available are:

- Automatic – The system triggers the closure activity on maturity or on the day the balances are settled depending on the value selected in Closure Type . Hence, it is mandatory to set the Closure Type field as Maturity or Balance.
- Manual – The user triggers the closure activity manually.

The bank has to restrict all transactions to the account as the account is identified for closure using the Posting Restrict field. Values in the range of 90 - 99 is allowed, which pertains to account closure posting restrict.


#### 📋 Tasks

Related topics:

- Close Facility Arrangement (Corporate)

Facility Closure allows the financial institution to close a facility. An arrangement can be closed when it reaches its maturity date or when all the balances get settled . Once the balances of the facility and loans are settled, the facility arrangement status moves from Authorised to Expired and then to Closed.

### 2.25  Facility Commitment


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Facility Commitment describes commitment amount and tenure for which the Facility is sanctioned by the bank. The bank decides the Facility sanctions based on the documentary proof. Commitment balances maintained at the Facility level are total commitment, utilised commitment, unutilised commitment, ...*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Amount*, *Arrangement*, *Change Amount*, *Commit Amount Available*, *Commitment Type*, *Expiry Date*, *Reason*, *Start Date* ... +2 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

Facility Commitment describes commitment amount and tenure for which the Facility is sanctioned by the bank. The bank decides the Facility sanctions based on the documentary proof. Commitment balances maintained at the Facility level are total commitment, utilised commitment, unutilised commitment, unavailable commitment and available commitment.

The financial institution may restrict the drawing ability of the borrower, because allowing the borrower to withdraw the amount till the day before maturity may lead to failure in repayment of loan before maturity or even to bad loans. To avoid such situation, the lender can define an expiry date for the facility. Facility expiry date is the date after which the borrower is not allowed to make any new drawings under the facility or use the unutilised amount of the existing drawings.

Commitment suspension is the process of blocking the commitment for a temporary period. During this period, the borrower cannot avail any more drawings under this facility but can avail new drawings only after the commitment suspension is revoked or unblocked. The commitment suspension can be system or user triggered activity.

Commitment schedule is defined in Term Amount Property Class with amount and start date. It is defined at arrangement level and is available only from the commitment schedule start date. It is increasing or decreasing schedule. When it is defined, the whole amount is not available for the user on day 1 and based on the commitment schedule defined, the commitment amount is released and the user can create drawings under a facility. When the user sets the Commitment Type field as Unavailability Schedule, the commitment amount defined is not available for period defined in commitment schedule.

Using the Update Commit Limit field in Term Amount Property Class, the user can block the limit for the commitment amount of the arrangement during arrangement creation itself. Allowed values are No and Yes. When set to,

- Yes - Commitment Available field is blocked (that is, unutilised commitment) of the limit record.
- No - Commitment Available field is not blocked of the limit record.

> **⚠️ Note:** When a value is not selected, the default setting is none and limit record is not blocked.

When this field is defined as negotiable in the Product Condition, the user can enter the value at the arrangement level. When the Limit Property is attached to the facility product, the Update Commit Limit field in the Term Amount Property Class is defaulted to Yes. When this field is set as Yes, the contingent utilisation of the limit is blocked in the Commit Amount Available field of the limit record.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

Term Amount Property Class (PC) defines the commitment given to a contract.

- The Amount field in the Term Amount PC defines the commitment (maximum) amount of the Arrangement.
- The Term field in the Term Amount PC defines the commitment term of the Arrangement.

The commitment balances maintained are based on the Term Amount PC. The amount specified becomes the total commitment of the arrangement.


##### Modifying Commitment Amount

The Change Amount field in the Term Amount PC is used to increase or decrease the commitment amount of the arrangement during the life cycle using the INCREASE or DECREASE action. This field signifies the amount to be increased or decreased on the original amount. To increase, the value entered in this field has to be greater than zero. To decrease, has to be lesser than zero.


##### Modifying Term

The Change Term Activity allows the user to modify (that is, increase or decrease) the term of an Arrangement, subject to the negotiation rules.

> **⚠️ Note:** Commitment amount and term can be modified during the life cycle of the Arrangement, subject to negotiation rules, periodic rules and the current outstanding amount.


##### Commitment Expiry

The Expiry Date field in the Term Amount PC defines the last date after which the commitment is not available for making new drawings under the facility or making further disbursement under a lending arrangement. The available commitment of the facility and lending arrangements is reduced to zero after the expiry date. It can be set at both product and arrangement levels. The expiry date can be relative or fixed date. The below screenshots show commitment amount at,


##### Commitment Suspension

The commitment suspension can be set up as system or user triggered activity. Similarly, unblocking or revoking the commitment suspension is system or user triggered activity.

For example, The bank user has restricted the number of active drawing as five under a facility and when the user creates five drawings under a facility, the facility commitment amount should be blocked. When an active drawing is closed, the facility commitment should be unblocked. This is configured using Activity Restriction Property Class and attaching it to the product.

This Activity Restriction Product Condition can be attached to the product.

The user triggered activity can be done using the ‘New Activity’ in the overview screen.


##### Commitment Schedule and Unavailability Schedule

The Commitment Type field is set as Commitment Schedule and then the user can set the Start Date and Amount fields. The Commitment Type is multi-value and commitment schedule can be for multiple periods. The ‘Commitment Schedule’ and ‘Unavailability Schedule’ are defined while creating individual Facility arrangements.

The below examples enable the user to understand the increase and decrease in commitment schedule.

The commitment gradually increases every year and reaches full amount by the end of the term.

A total commitment of 10 million is agreed between the Financial Institutions (FI). The Borrower Group (BG) is updated at the facility level on the start of sixth year and remains the same till the end of the facility expiry date.

The commitment gradually decreases every year from the start of a particular period.

A total commitment of 10 million is fully available to the BG as soon as the facility become effective in the first year and gradually decreases from the start of sixth year and keeps decreasing till the expiry date.

The commitment gradually increases every year and goes to full amount in the middle of the contract period and then starts decreasing gradually till the expiry date.

A total commitment of 10 million is updated at the facility level only on the start of third year and remains until seventh year and the total commitment amount starts decreasing from the eighth year.


#### 📋 Tasks

Related topics:

- Lending Processes (Corporate)

Commitment balances maintained at the Facility level are total commitment, utilised commitment, unutilised commitment, unavailable commitment and available commitment.

### 2.26  Facility Commitment Amortisation Schedule


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The user can generate principal due bills to the borrower at the drawings level based on the facility repayment amount defined at the facility.*
> 
> **Applications:** `AA.PAYMENT.TYPE`, `LIMIT`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Amount*, *Attribute*, *Bill Type*, *Category*, *Commitment Type*, *Consequence*, *Currency*, *Customer* ... +22 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

The user can generate principal due bills to the borrower at the drawings level based on the facility repayment amount defined at the facility.

The amount and frequency of the facility-level repayment are defined by the user using Payment Schedule at the facility level. The amount can either be system calculated or user-defined. Based on this, the system performs a commitment reduction on the due date at the facility. The user raises an auto-settle bill at the facility for the amount of commitment reduction.

The system calculates a Retaining Percentage, which indicates whether the facility is excessively utilised or not. Any value of 100% and above indicates that the facility is within the set limit. Any value less than 100% indicates excess utilisation of the facility. For example, if the Retaining Percentage is 94%, it indicates that the facility is excessively utilised for 6% (100%-94%). In such cases, the system raises the principal due bills at the drawing level to collect the excessively utilised principal amount from the borrower.

Whenever there is a change in the facility commitment amount due to user-initiated activities like facility commitment increase, decrease and change schedule, the facility repayment amount defined at the facility is recalculated and principal bills are also recalculated by the system based on the new facility repayment amount.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The Payment Schedule property class is used to define the frequency and amount of facility-level repayment.

The payment type used to define the facility-level repayment should have Mand Property Class set as TERM AMOUNT and system Bill Type set as COMMITMENT as shown below.

> **⚠️ Note:** Facility-level repayment can be defined only for the principal amount. The system supports the facility-level repayment when the value of Calc Types is LINEAR or ACTUAL. The recommended configuration for the facility-level repayment in Term Amount Property Class is Current and Overdraw at both facility and drawings. Combined bills feature is not supported for facility-level repayment contracts. Commitment schedule is not supported for facility-level repayment contracts.


#### 🔧 Working With

When a facility-level repayment is defined by the user at the facility, then on the scheduled dates, an auto-settle bill is raised at the facility for the amount defined, and the facility commitment is reduced by the same amount. After this, the system calculates a retaining percentage, as below.

If the Retaining Percentage is less than 100%, then the excessive utilisation at the drawings due to this commitment reduction is billed to the borrower by the system.

The TOTFACOMMITMENT, UTLFACOMMITMENT and OVDFACOMMITMENT values highlighted in yellow in the screenshot help the system to calculate the Retaining Percentage of 17.3010381 considering USD 2,500,000 is the facility repayment amount defined.

To calculate the excessive utilisation at the facility or the billing amount at the drawings with Update Commitment set up as Yes in Term Amount Property Class:

1. Calculate TOTDWCOMMITMENT to be retained in the drawing after commitment reduction. The CURDWCOMMITMENT and CUR values highlighted in yellow in the below screenshot help the system to calculate the Retaining TOTDWCOMMITMENT. Retaining TOTDWCOMMITMENT = USD 500,000 as shown below.
2. Calculate the Drawing Commitment Reduction Amount. This amount is reduced from the Drawing commitment. Drawing Commitment Reduction Amount = USD 2,400,000, as shown in the below screenshot.
3. Calculate the Principal Bill Amount to be raised. As a result of the above drawing commitment reduction, if any overdue arises (OVDDWCOMMITMENT), this overdue amount is billed. If there are any drawing principal dues (DUE ) already present, then the amount to be billed is the difference between the overdue amount (OVDDWCOMMITMENT) and the due amount (DUE ) already present at the drawings. The OVDDWCOMMITMENT and DUE values highlighted in yellow in the below screenshot help to calculate the excess utilisation bill value of USD 2,290,000.

To calculate the excessive utilisation at facility or the billing amount at the drawings with Update Commitment set up as No in the Term Amount Property Class:

1. Calculate the Retaining Percentage. The TOTFACOMMITMENT, UTLFACOMMITMENT and OVDFACOMMITMENT values highlighted in yellow in the below screenshot help to calculate the Retaining Percentage as 17.3611111 considering USD 2,500,000 as the facility repayment amount defined.
2. Calculate the Retaining Outstanding Principal (CURACCOUNT). The Retaining Percentage and Outstanding Principal (CURACCOUNT) values highlighted in yellow in the below screenshot help to calculate the Retaining CURACCOUNT value of USD 500,000.
3. Calculate the principal bill amount to be raised. New due amount gets added to the previously present due amount if any. The Outstanding Principal (CUR ) and the Retaining Outstanding Principal (Retaining CUR ) values highlighted in yellow in the below screenshot help to calculate the excess value of USD 2,380,000.

- When the user creates guarantees and lending drawings under the same facility, the system does not apply the retaining percentage on guarantees. It is recommended to use a separate facility for guarantees and lending drawings.
- When the user creates a drawing with Update Commit Limit as Yes, the system considers this as the commitment utilized at the facility even when there is no disbursement performed under the drawings. It might result in raising bills in other drawings even if the overall unbilled principal outstanding is within the expected commitment level. To avoid this, it is recommended to create drawings with Update Commit Limit set as No.


##### Facility and Drawings in Same Currency

Consider the bank opens a facility for a borrower for USD 3 million. The borrower chooses the facility to support facility-level repayment for an amount of USD 2,500,000. This is scheduled at the facility in the Payment Schedule using the new facility repayment payment type. Therefore, on the due date, USD 2,500,000 is reduced from the Facility commitment. Any excess amount in the drawings calculated as part of this facility commitment reduction is billed and should be paid by the borrower.

If the borrower takes two drawings under the facility:

- Drawing 1 is taken for USD 2 million with Update Commitment set up as Yes. The amount disbursed from Drawing 1 is USD 1,900,000.
- Drawing 2 is taken for USD 1 million with Update Commitment set up as No. The amount disbursed from Drawing 2 is USD 900,000.
- Drawing 1 has a principal due of USD 10,000 and Drawing 2 has a principal due of USD 20,000 on the same date when the facility-level repayment is defined.
- On the date of contract creation and disbursement, the balances at the facility and drawings 1 and 2 are as below.

On the facility-level repayment date, an auto-settle bill is raised by the system at the facility for USD 2,500,000. So, the facility commitment is reduced by USD 2,500,000. The system calculates the retaining percentage and if it is less than 100%, the excess amount at drawings is billed to the borrower.

The bills and balances after commitment reduction as a result of facility-level repayment are shown below:

The auto-settle bill at the facility is as below.

- Retaining % = (500,000/(2800000+100000-10,000-20,000))*100=17.42160279%
- Retaining TOTDWCOMMITMENT=17.42160279%*(100,000+1,890,000) =USD 346,689.90
- Drawing commitment reduction amount = 2,000,000-346,689.90=USD 1,653,310.10
- Principal bill to be raised as part of facility-level repayment = 1,553,310.10-10,000 =USD 1,543,310.10

The principal bill for USD 10,000 is the principal due at drawings level and the principal bill due for USD 1,543,310.10 is the result of commitment reduction as part of facility-level repayment.

- Retaining % = (500,000/(2800000+100000-10,000-20,000))*100=17.42160279%
- Retaining outstanding Principal=17.42160279%*880,000 =USD 153,310.10
- Principal Bill to be raised as part of facility-level repayment = 880,000- 153,310.10=USD 726,689.90

The principal bill for USD 20,000 is the principal due at drawings level and the principal bill due for USD 726,689.90 is the result of commitment reduction as part of facility-level repayment.


##### Multicurrency Contract

Consider the bank opens a USD facility for a borrower for USD 3 million. The borrower chooses the facility to support facility-level repayment for an amount of USD 2,500,000. This is scheduled at the facility in the Payment Schedule using the facility repayment payment type. So, on the due date, USD 2,500,000 is reduced from the facility commitment. Any excess amount in the drawings calculated as part of this facility commitment reduction is billed and should be paid by the borrower.

If the borrower takes two drawings under the facility.

Drawing 1 is a GBP contract taken for 1 million with Update Commitment set up as ‘Yes’. The amount disbursed from Drawing 1 is GBP 900,000.

Drawing 2 is taken for USD 1.2 million with Update Commitment set up as ‘No’. The amount disbursed from Drawing 2 is USD 700,000.

Drawing 1 has a principal due of GBP 10,000 and Drawing 2 has a principal due of USD 20,000 on the same date of facility-level repayment defined.

On the date of contract creation and disbursement, the balances at the facility and drawings 1 and 2 are as below:

On the facility-level repayment date, an auto-settle bill is raised by the system at the facility for USD 2,500,000. So, the facility commitment is reduced by USD 2,500,000. The system calculates the Retaining Percentage and if it is less than 100%, the excess amount at drawings is billed to the borrower.

The bills and balances after commitment reduction as a result of facility-level repayment are illustrated below.

The auto-settle bill at the facility is as below.

To calculate retaining percentage, all balances should be in the facility currency. So, the due balance of Drawing 1 used in the calculation should be converted to USD currency. Drawing 1 has a due balance of GBP 10,000. The exchange rate is 1.2226. So, after conversion it becomes USD 12,226(10,000*1.226)

- Retaining %= (500,000/(500,000+1,422,600-12,226-20,000))*100=26.44979247%
- Retaining TOTDWCOMMITMENT=26.44979247%*(100,000+890,000) =GBP 261,852.95
- Drawing commitment reduction amount = 1,000,000-261,852.95=GBP 738,147.05
- Principal Bill to be raised as part of facility-level repayment = 638,147.05-10,000 =GBP 628,147.05

The principal bill for GBP 10,000 is the principal due at the drawings level and the principal bill due for GBP 628,147.05 is the result of commitment reduction as part of facility-level repayment.

- Retaining % = 26.44979247%
- Retaining outstanding Principal=26.44979247%*680,000=USD 179,858.59
- Principal Bill to be raised as part of facility-level repayment = 680,000- 179,858.59=USD 500,141.41

The principal bill for USD 20,000 is the usual principal due at the drawings level and the principal bill due for USD 500,141.41 is the result of commitment reduction as part of facility-level repayment.


#### 📋 Tasks

The user can generate principal due bills to the borrower at the drawings-level based on the facility repayment amount defined at the facility. The user defines the amount and frequency of the facility-level repayment using Payment Schedule at the facility level. The amount can either be system calculated or user-defined. Based on this, the system performs a commitment reduction on the due date at the facility.

### 2.27  Facility Level Performing to Non Performing


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Suspension refers to the temporary halt of financial transactions like restricting further disbursements or drawdowns, when the bank anticipates that there are chances for the customer to default. Thus, the income generated from transactions is posted in the internal account instead of showing it as...*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

Suspension refers to the temporary halt of financial transactions like restricting further disbursements or drawdowns, when the bank anticipates that there are chances for the customer to default. Thus, the income generated from transactions is posted in the internal account instead of showing it as profit in the P/L account temporarily because these activities may resume in the future.

Resumption refers to the process of restarting or reinstating a suspended facility or drawing. This can happen after a temporary halt that occurred due to suspension, overdue bills, or defaulted payments.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

There is no specific configuration to be setup at feature level.


#### 📋 Tasks

There are no Tasks available for Facility Suspension and Resumption feature.


#### 📊 Outputs

Suspension refers to the temporary halt of financial transactions like restricting further disbursements or drawdowns, when the bank anticipates that there are chances for the customer to default. Resumption refers to the process of restarting or reinstating a suspended facility or drawing.

Additionally, a facility contract can also be moved from another bank for various reasons. The facility is a credit limit offered to...*

#### 📖 Introduction

When Temenos Transact replaces the legacy banking software of the bank, the existing contracts are moved from legacy system to continue with the day-to-day operations. Additionally, a facility contract can also be moved from another bank for various reasons. The facility is a credit limit offered to a borrower or group of borrowers. The facility contract holds the commitment and fees or charges associated with the commitment amount.

The facility is utilised by drawing requests. So when a facility contract is migrated, the underlying drawing contracts are also migrated. Since each implementation is different, the take-over or the migration strategy is also different. A generic approach is followed during the design and execution of such migrations.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

Balance Maintenance Property Class is used to take over or migrate contracts to Temenos Transact Arrangement Architecture. Read Balance Maintenance Property Class for more information.


#### 📋 Tasks

There are no Tasks available for Facility Migration feature.


#### 📊 Outputs

There are no Outputs available for Facility Migration feature.

### 2.29  Facility Repayment


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *AA supports settling of multiple bills at facility level using Payment Priority Property class. The user can settle multiple drawings bills through Facility Arrangement. This can be done by debiting transact customer account or using external account in another bank of the customer. While settling t...*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Apply Payment*, *Payin Account*, *Payin Settlement*, *Payment Type*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

AA supports settling of multiple bills at facility level using Payment Priority Property class. The user can settle multiple drawings bills through Facility Arrangement. This can be done by debiting transact customer account or using external account in another bank of the customer. While settling the payment using facility account or arrangement, bills are settled based on the condition defined in Payment Priority Property Class. If multiple drawings and bills are pending, Transact applies payment priority rules and the payment is settled.

Individual drawings bills can be settled using the arrangement IDs. Refer Retail Lending user guide for more details.

During repayment, the outstanding bills are settled based on the setup in Payment Priority Product Condition attached to the facility or drawings arrangement product. If there are multiple outstanding bills from multiple arrangements (for example: LIBOR drawing and financial guarantee) created under the facility, then settlement happens based upon the payment priority rule. Charge-off balances are also included during settlement.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

Read Payment Priority PC condition for more information.

Payment Priority is used to define the order of repayment of underlying drawing.

The user can define settlement instructions payment type-wise for auto-repayments.

For auto repayment of combine bills, the user must set the below values and enter the account number in Payin Account .

- Payment Type as COMBINE.BILL
- Payin Settlement as Yes

When the bill is due, the system auto-settles it by debiting the account number in Payin Account .

Direct Debit Mandate is an authorisation given to the bank by the borrower to collect future payments using Direct Debit. Refer Direct Debit for more details.

The user creates the DD mandate for the facility by entering the required fields as shown below.

> **⚠️ Note:** The repayment of combined bills using the DD mandate works if bills produced are defined to be issued before the due date as advanced bills or deferred by a few days. If the bills are issued on the same date, repayment using the DD mandate does not work as expected.

The user executes the DD mandate a day before the bill is made due, based on the configuration. The system parks the bill amount in UNCACCOUNT of the facility. The user configures Apply Payment in the payment schedule condition of the facility.

When the DD mandate credits the unspecified credit account, the bills made due are settled using the activity defined in Apply Payment in the Product Conditions - PAYMENT SCHEDULE.

### 2.30  Internal Portfolio Allocation in Facility


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The bank attaches multiple internal portfolios or business units as part of the facility and loan arrangement. It allows a bank or financial institution to assess the overall exposure of their portfolios and recognize their revenue or income sector-wise.*
> 
> **Applications:** `AA.BILL.DETAILS`, `AA.INTEREST.ACCRUALS`, `AA.PRODUCT.DESIGNER`, `EB.CASHFLOW`, `EB.CONTRACT.BALANCES`, `ECB`, `IAS.CLASSIFICATION`, `LOAN.PORTFOLIO`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Amc*, *Amount*, *Application order*, *Balance Treatment*, *Bank Role*, *Branch*, *Buy Back*, *Buyer Participant* ... +38 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

The bank attaches multiple internal portfolios or business units as part of the facility and loan arrangement. It allows a bank or financial institution to assess the overall exposure of their portfolios and recognize their revenue or income sector-wise.

A typical bank’s organization and its credit risk book structure are shown in the image below.

Portfolios that operate under each branch are the Profit Centre, Cost Centre, or Business units within that branch or entity. The bank assigns every loan or facility in a branch’s book to one or more portfolios and shares the profits earned among the portfolios on a pro-rata basis based on their funding contribution.

Banks or financial institutions can recognize their exposure to loans, income earned, and total revenue from a facility or loan portfolio-wise. It helps the bank to plan and restructure its portfolio exposures efficiently.

Portfolio Allocation in a bilateral facility or a club facility work similarly, except that, club facility has contributions from external participants apart from the internal portfolios


##### Risk Participation

A facility is associated with a credit risk as there is a chance for the borrower to default on the repayments of the loans under the facility. The banks must ensure that the borrower repays without fail.

The banks mitigate the risk exposure in the facility by selling it to other banks. The banks that share the risk exposure from the owning bank are called risk participants.

A portfolio can sell its risk exposure to the risk participants, either fully or partially, so the risk exposure is shared between the banks accordingly. The portfolio can sell its risk to one or more risk participants.

The same risk participant cannot buy shares from multiple portfolios.


##### IFRS Reporting for Portfolio Allocation

International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) is a set of rules to define the structure in which the accounting entries of the business are set. Invertors and Companies adopt these standards to display the transactions and accounting entries in a more transparent way. The user can have different IFRS classification nature for different portfolios involved in the Facilty.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The user configures the LOAN.PORTFOLIO and the Participant PC to help the banks with the new facility with internal portfolio allocation.


##### LOAN.PORTFOLIO

Banks need to store the basic details such as Branch , Department , and the active status of the internal business units or portfolios in the LOAN.PORTFOLIO application, as shown in the image below.

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Ifrs Classification | Defines the classification of contract based on IFRS standard. It must be a valid record from IAS.CLASSIFICATION . Once created, it cannot be modified. |
| Ifrs Subtype | Defines the sub-type for the corresponding classification defined in Ifrs Classification . It cannot be amended at arrangement-level. |
| Market Key | Defines the market rate to calculate the NPV based on future cash flow information. It can either be fixed rate or periodic variable rate This field is mandatory if Ifrs Classification holds any value. |
| Market Margin | Defines the NPV based on the future cash flow information. |
| Margin Operand | Defines the operation performed when calculating the rate using the market margin value. Allowed values are ADD and SUB. |
| Branch | Defines the company to which the business unit belongs. |
| Department | Defines the internal department. |
| Portfolio Id | Defines the portfolio for which the IFRS classification is defined and reporting is performed. |

A portfolio can be in either ‘Active’ or ‘Inactive’ status. While creating a portfolio, the default status is ‘Active’. While attaching a portfolio to a facility arrangement, only active portfolios can be attached to the facilities.

> **⚠️ Note:** Changing the status of the Portfolios from active to inactive will not affect the business of the existing facilities that are attached to the portfolios. Those portfolios cannot be attached to any new facilities being created. If the bank wants to remove the portfolio being made inactive from the existing facilities, then it should do a share transfer from that particular portfolio to another portfolio.


##### Participant PC

Participant Property Class captures the portfolios that are part of that facility arrangement and their share in that arrangement. The system has to attach the Participant Property Class and its associated product condition to the loan product in AA.PRODUCT.DESIGNER to enable the Portfolio Allocation.

The own bank's share in a facility or loan is split among the internal portfolios. Thus, the bank user should ensure that the sum of all the portfolios share should equal to the own share.

While creating a loan, the own bank can choose the primary portfolio by providing the portfolio ID in the Primary Portfolio field. If the user does not input any value, the system defaults the first portfolio as primary portfolio.

Refer to Configuring Risk Participation for Bilateral Loan for more information on risk participation in facility with Internal portfolios.


##### Reporting Property Class

Reporting Property Class provides information on cash movements of assets and liabilities. It is used to define the IFRS classification and sub-type to be used, along with any margin to be added while calculating the EIR so that it is on par with the market rate. The fields in LOAN.PORTFOLIO are used to create and capture the reporting classification details of the portfolios. These fields are used to update the Reporting PC while creating the arrangement.

Reporting PC supports IFRS classification for each portfolio. These fields of the Reporting PC are added to LOAN.PORTFOLIO . The Portfolio Id field (multi-value) can be defined using the fields given in LOAN.PORTFOLIO .

> **⚠️ Note:** For a loan without internal portfolios, the system considers the IFRS classification defined in the first multi-value set.

When the Facility arrangement is created with internal portfolios as part of the arrangement and the reporting condition in the product is tracking, then the system defaults the IFRS classification details defined in LOAN.PORTFOLIO in the Reporting arrangement condition of the facility. The user cannot edit the details at the arrangement-level.

If there is more than one portfolio of the own bank funding the facility, then the above fields in LOAN.PORTFOLIO must be multi-valued and the details are defaulted based on the portfolios. If the reporting property in the arrangement is non- tracking, then the system directly fetches the Ifrs Classification and Ifrs Subtype for each portfolio from LOAN.PORTFOLIO . The user can edit the details at the arrangement-level.

The below screenshot shows a Portfolio application record.

Reporting condition is attached at the product designer for the Loan product.


##### Internal Portfolio Allocation in Bilateral Facility

To sub-allocate the facility among portfolios,

- The Participant Property Class captures the participants shares in the arrangement.
- The user must attach the Participant Property Class and its associated product condition to the facility and all the loan products that were used to create a loan under the facility in AA.PRODUCT.DESIGNER to enable the share transfer to sell assets to the internal participants.

Under the Participant product condition, to allocate the bilateral and club loan facility,

1. Update the owning bank's nostro details currency-wise in Participant product conditions for all the currencies of the product.
2. Update the participant’s accounting type as 'Contingent or Memo' in the Participant product condition (AA.PRD.DES.PARTICIPANT), by default the transact picks ‘Memo’ as the Participant accounting type.
3. Attach the Participant product condition to the facility and drawing products as below. The screenshot below is an example of the facility product. The screenshot below is an example of the loan or drawing product. Similar to a bilateral facility and loan, the Accounting product condition and allocation rules should be updated in these facility and loan products.


#### 🔧 Working With

This section details about the facility creation and drawing creation, disbursement, and charges.


##### Creating Facility

While creating a facility arrangement, the bank can decide to assign its commitment to one or more internal portfolios.

The portfolios for each contract are different, and the user decides it based on the nature of the commitment, the size of the deal, their share contribution, holding type, and so on. Thus, the details of the portfolios are captured at the arrangement level using Participant Property Class.

The bank must define the following in the Participant arrangement condition to assign the commitment to the portfolios:

- Its total share in the Own Share field
- Each portfolio in the Portfolio ID field
- The portfolio’s share in the Portfolio Amount field
- The Balance Treatment field in the Account condition as ‘Participation’. It is a parameter level setup to denote that the bank is using the portfolios as part of the arrangement.
- Bank Role in Participant
- Own Nostro currency and account
- PO product details
- The Primary Portfolio field denotes the primary portfolio in the arrangement to which the skims and tax are posted. If the bank doesn't define the primary portfolio, the first portfolio defined is considered as the primary portfolio

> **⚠️ Note:** If the user creates a facility without any portfolios as a part of the arrangement contract, then portfolios cannot be added later in the lifetime of the arrangement. Thus, if the bank wants to bring in more portfolios later, then it must attach the entire commitment to a default portfolio during the arrangement creation.

Refer to Creating Facility Arrangement for more information on facility creation.

The bank user can view the portfolio balances by opening the Facility Overview screen - 'View Portfolio Balances' option under Financial in Participation Enquiry.

When the user creates a facility with portfolios, it contains multiple ECB records.

The image below shows a record of the total amount of the facility contract committed to the borrower, which is the information balance. The ECB ID is the Account Number.

The images below show a record of each portfolio with their share in the facility. Each Portfolio balances are real-time values available as the system records that in the banks’ book. The portfolios’ ECB ID would be in the format as the Account Number*Customer_ID*Portfolio_ID.

> **⚠️ Note:** Portfolios in a bilateral facility or a club facility work similarly, except that, in a club facility, each external lender or participant has an ECB record with their balances.

Refer to the Introduction to Club Loans for more information on Club Loans.


##### Creating Drawing

When a user commits the portfolios to a share in the facility, the system sets that the portfolios are obliged to fund the same percentage of share in all the drawings that the user creates under that facility.

So, when the user creates a drawing under the facility, the system defaults the portfolio’s committed share percentage in a facility to the drawings created under the facility. The user cannot modify the share percentage at the drawings level.

Based on the borrowers’ loan commitment amount, the system defaults the portfolios’ share on a pro-rata basis.

Refer to Drawings under Facility for more information on creating a drawing.

Like a facility, when the user creates drawings with portfolios as a part of it, it contains multiple ECB records.

The image below shows a record of the total amount of the drawing contract committed to the borrower with the information balances.

The images below show a record of each portfolio with their share in the drawing. Each Portfolios balances are real values and are recorded in the bank’s book.

When the bank disburses a loan, the system debits each portfolio’s share and credits the same to a suspense account. From the suspense account, the system disburses the entire amount to the borrower’s account.

All other activities like facility expiry, maturity, and so on perform in the same way as a facility without internal portfolios. For example, when a facility reaches the expiry, the system reduces the available commitment in all the portfolios ECB to zero.

When the user disburses the loan, the system debits each portfolio based on their share in the loan and credits the amount to a suspense account (internal account). The system credits the total disbursement amount to the borrower from the suspense account.

When a bank disburses a loan to a customer either partially or fully, each portfolio contributes a percentage of the amount for disbursement based on the shared commitment percentage committed in the arrangement.

Loan disbursal process are the same as the Retail loans. Refer to the Loan Disbursement guide for more information on loan disbursal.

Charges can be scheduled on a regular frequency based on the occurrence of a specific activity or breaching the terms and conditions of the product features. These charges can be fixed charges, calculated amount or a combination of both.

The system distributes the charge levied and collected from the borrower on a loan or facility among the portfolios based on the information captured in the Portfolio-Charges section. It is possible to set up the definition in the following ways:

1. Pro-rata Distribution - If the charge–related set of fields in the Participant condition is not defined, then the system distributes charges on a pro-rata basis based on the current commitment share percentage of the participants.
2. Non-pro-rata Distribution - If the charge–related set of fields in the Participant condition is defined, then the system distributes charges on a non pro-rata basis.

Start

- Pro-rata Charges
- Non-Pro-rata Charges

The system splits the charges received from the borrower among the internal portfolios based on their commitment share percentage by default.

When the user creates a club loan for USD 10 million, with multiple portfolios as a part of the loan, the loan is shared among the participants and internal portfolios, as shown in the image below.

If an upfront fee of 0.1% (USD 10,000) is collected from the borrower, then the charges for each portfolio are calculated as below.

The formula to calculate the share of charge for each portfolio is,

Where, Current commitment = CUR + UTL + OVD

- Charge Share of Portfolio 120021 = (4,000,000/10,000,000) * 10,000 = USD 4,000
- Charge Share of Portfolio 120031 = (6,000,000/10,000,000) * 10,000 = USD 6,000

While creating a loan with portfolios, a bank can distribute the charges among the loan's internal portfolios on a non-pro-rata basis by using the Charges tab in the Participant property class.

To distribute the charge to a specific portfolio, banks must enter the Portfolio ID in the Participant field in the "OWN-PortfolioID" format.

When a charge is distributed to internal portfolios in a non-pro-rata manner, it is possible to distribute more than 100% or less than 100% of the actual charge due.

If Charge due amount is USD 100000, the distributed charge for all portfolios together can be USD 120000 or USD 80000.

In such a case the profit or loss resulting from the charges allocated greater than the actual charge due from the borrower (loss) or the charges allocated lesser than the actual charge due from the borrower (profit) is posted to the profit and loss account of the Primary Portfolio .

Primary Portfolio field in the Skims tab is configured to specify which portfolio is responsible for any profit or loss resulting from the charges that were distributed on behalf of all the other portfolios.

Following are the options available for non-pro rata distribution of charge:

A charge can be distributed as a percentage of the Total commitment amount that each portfolio and other participants have contributed to the loan.

> **⚠️ Note:** Using the Source Property field in AA.PRODUCT.DESIGNER application, it is possible to configure other balance as the source for the charge calculation instead of total commitment of the facility.

To distribute a charge as a percentage, the charge property must be mentioned in the Charge field, the portfolio ID must be defined in the Participant field in "OWN-PortfolioID" format, and the percentage of share must be defined in the Rate field.

The share of the charge is calculated by,

Portfolio’s Share of Charge = Rate (%) * Total Commitment of the portfolio

1% for Portfolio 120031= 6,000,000*1%= USD 60,000

A charge can be distributed by mentioning the actual amount that will be distributed to each portfolio and the other club loan participants.

To distribute a charge amount wise, the charge property must be mentioned in the Charge field, the portfolio ID must be defined in the Participant field in "OWN-PortfolioID" format, and the amount to be allocated for each portfolio must be defined in the Amount field.

A charge can be distributed by dividing the charge as a Ratio for each portfolio and other loan participants.

To distribute a charge as a Ratio, the charge property must be mentioned in the Charge field, the portfolio ID must be defined in the Participant field in "OWN-PortfolioID" format, and the ratio for each portfolio must be defined in the Ratio field.

The sum of the ratio mentioned for all the portfolios and other participants must be equal to 100. The charge amount is split into the mentioned ratio, and it is distributed to the respective internal portfolios and other participants.

When a loan is disbursed based on the portfolio’s share amount, the interest is accrued and recognised as an income against each portfolio. The accruals are posted in EB.CONTRACT.BALANCES of each portfolio.

Skim is a profit component using which own bank can assign different interest rates to the participant banks, other than the borrower’s interest repayment. The difference between the borrower’s interest and the interest skim is an income to the own bank. Own bank reports the skims to a different income PL.

“Bank must define the following under Skim in Participant section:

- Participant ID.
- The property for which skims/margins are to be applied. Only Interest property is allowed.
- Skim/margin Operand to be used.
- Skim margin rate that needs to be applied for the participant share.

In the below example, own bank sets a skim of 0.20 for the participant bank (Customer ID: 100112).

The system defines the skim portfolio as 120021.

> **⚠️ Note:** If the own bank has not set any skim portfolio, the system considers the first portfolio in the arrangement as the skim portfolio.

When the interest accrues, own bank calculates the borrower’s interest at 1.228 and the participant bank's interest at 1.028 (that is, the difference between the borrower’s interest rate and the skim rate of 0.20).

Sample screenshots of interest accrual records:

- Borrower
- Participant

The own bank’s system accrues this interest skim separately from the participant’s balance and posts the skim to the 120021 portfolio.

The 120021 portfolio's ECB has a separate skim entry.

When a payment is due, the system generates a bill with the amount to be paid and is sent to the customer for repayment. The system creates the customer’s bill with the share of each portfolio. The customer’s bill is shown in the screenshot below.

The Portfolio 120021’s bill is updated as shown in the screenshot below.

The Portfolio 120031’s bill is updated as shown in the screenshot below.

When the bill is made due, the system raises corresponding accounting entries for each portfolio. Then, the customer’s ECB is updated as shown in the screenshot below.

The Portolio 120021’s ECB is updated as shown in the screenshot below.

The Portfolio 120031’s ECB is updated as shown in the screenshot below.

When the customer makes the payment, the system settles each portfolio’s outstanding amount based on the share. Once the customer repays the amount, the system marks Settle Status in AA.BILL.DETAILS as SETTLED.

In the case of prepayment, the system settles each portfolio’s balances (on prorate basis) based on its outstanding share on the loan. Read Settlement of Bills and Loan Prepayments in Retail Lending for more information on repayment and prepayment respectively.

During payoff, the system settles all the balances and updates Settle Status in AA.BILL.DETAILS to PENDING CLOSURE. Payoff is generated through either AA.SIMULATION.CAPTURE application. Read Payoff in Property Class for more information.”

Read Combined Payoff in Facility for more information on facility payoff and Loan Pre-closure in Retail Lending for more information on loan payoff.

When the borrower’s business is bankrupted, then the bank considers the business as bad debt and decides to write-off the lend assets.

When a bank discovers that a borrower cannot repay a loan partially or completely, the unpaid bills or outstanding balance in an arrangement is written-off and the whole arrangement can also be written-off. While writing-off, the bank writes-off the borrower, participants’ and internal portfolio share in the arrangement. But only the portfolio share is recorded as a loss in the own bank’s book.

In transact, the banks can either write off a balance fully or partially, a bill, or an entire contract.

The bank writes off the outstanding balance in the arrangement when the write-off balance activity is executed. It is recognised as a loss in own bank’s book.

The financial institution applies tax on the interest and the charge amount levied on a contract and calculates the different types of tax such as, service tax, withholding tax, and so on. The tax can be calculated on interest and charges and this component is included as a part of the bill amount.

For the facility and the loans with internal portfolios, the tax calculated for interest and the charges is applied on the borrower balances based on the tax definition and collected as part of the primary portfolio's bill. The tax balances are maintained in EB.CONTRACT.BALANCES as non-contingent for own book.

Consider a club loan of USD 100 million is credited to a borrower, where the ‘Participant-1’ share is USD 75 million and the own bank share is USD 25 million.

- The interest amount of USD 925.21 is due on 18 Apr 2023.

##### Share Transfer

A bank can have multiple internal portfolios as part of its facility. During the facility's lifetime, the owning bank may decide to increase or decrease its exposure in the facility or sell off its share completely by transferring it to the existing banks in the loans or to a new bank. It can be done using share transfer.

The user can perform share transfer by selecting Share Transfer under Participation from the Facility Overview screen

> **⚠️ Note:** Irrespective of the availability of the internal portfolios in the facility, the calculation of shares to be transferred to the buyer is the same. Refer to the Share Transfer user guide to know more about calculation.

Internal share transfer allows the bank to transfer the shares between two internal portfolios, that is, selling and buying portfolios. The selling portfolio is an existing portfolio that holds a share in the facility. The buying portfolio is either an existing portfolio in the facility or a new portfolio that the bank adds into the facility through the share transfer. The activity FACILITY-FUND.TRANSFER-SHARE.TRANSFER is triggered.

The user must select the Transfer Type field as ‘Internal Transfer’ when the share is transferred between two internal portfolios.

Consider a borrower with a facility of 10 Million USD. The bank has split the share internally as 4 Million USD and 6 Million USD among two of its portfolios, ‘BNK-Corporate’ (Portfolio ID: 120021) and ‘BNK – Treasury’ (Portfolio ID: 120031), respectively.

Consider that the owning bank transfers 1 Million USD from the ‘BNK-Treasury’ portfolio (Portfolio ID: 120031) to a new portfolio, ‘BNK – Investment Portfolio’ (Portfolio ID: 120041).

The ECB of the ‘BNK-Treasury’ portfolio (Portfolio ID: 120031) before the share transfer is shown in the screenshot below.

The owning bank triggers an internal share transfer, as shown in the screenshot below.

The balances of the portfolios after the share transfer are shown in the screenshot below.

After the internal share transfer, the ECB of the ‘BNK-Treasury’ portfolio (Portfolio ID: 120031) and the ‘BNK – Investment Portfolio’ portfolio (Portfolio ID: 120041) are shown in the screenshots below.

BNK -Treasury Portfolio

BNK – Investment Portfolio

> **⚠️ Note:** During the internal transfer, the user should not set any value to the owning bank's Bank Role field, and the set of fields available in the Skims and Settlement Instructions tab.

The external share transfer allows the user to transfer the shares between one of the portfolios and an external participant bank. The portfolio can be either a buyer or a seller of the shares. The activity FACILITY-FUND.TRANSFER-SHARE.TRANSFER is triggered.

The user must select the Transfer Type field as ‘External Transfer’ when the share is transferred between a buyer or a seller portfolio and an external participant bank.

Consider a facility with three portfolios as a part of it.

Consider that the owning bank decides to sell 2 Million USD from the ‘BNK-Treasury’ portfolio (Portfolio ID: 120031) to an external participant (say ABN Amro Securities).

The ECB of the ‘BNK-Treasury’ portfolio (Portfolio ID: 120031) before the share transfer is shown in the screenshot below.

The owning bank triggers an external share transfer, as shown in the screenshot below.

During the external share transfer, the bank must specify the owning bank's role. If the owning bank role is set as ‘Sell’, then the bank should specify:

- The portfolio that is selling its share in the Seller Participant field and
- The external participant who buys the share in the Buyer Participant field.

If the owning bank role is set as ‘Buy’, then the bank should specify:

- The portfolio that is buying the share in Buyer Participant and
- The external participant who is selling in Seller Participant .

If the buyer is a new external participant, then the bank must specify the participant’s role and the settlement instructions.

The ECB of the arrangement and the portfolios after the share transfer are shown in the screenshots below.

The ECB of the ‘BNK-Treasury’ portfolio (Portfolio ID: 120031) and the external bank ABN securities are shown in the screenshots below.

BNK – Treasury Portfolio

ABN Amro Securities

When the own bank is the agent bank, it may need to record the share transfer between two of the participant banks, so that it can maintain the participant books with updated balances. It will also help the own bank in requesting disbursements or repaying the participant banks accurately.

These types of share transfer is just an adjustment of the participant banks shares, as the own bank has no financial transactions, apart from agent-related charges if any, as part of their share transfer.

The user must select the Transfer Type field as ‘Adjustments’ when the share is transferred between two external participant banks.

Refer to the Share Transfer user guide for more information on Share Transfer.

A bank having multiple portfolios as part of a facility can decide to buy back all the shares from one or all portfolios or participants.

- An internal buyback occurs when the bank buys back its internal portfolio’s share.
- An external buyback occurs when the bank buys back the external participant banks’ shares.

The activity FACILITY-FUND.TRANSFER-BUYBACK will be triggered for buyback of shares. The following section illustrates the internal and external buyback options available.

When the owning bank prefers to buy back all the shares of one or all the portfolios in the arrangement and transfer them to a particular portfolio, it is referred to as an internal buyback. The bank has to specify the portfolio to which all the shares should be transferred.

Consider the following example, where the bank chooses to buy back all the shares from Portfolio 120031 to Portfolio 120021 and the bank specifies the values as shown in the below screenshot.

Set the Transfer Type field to Internal transfer. Select the Buy Back option along with the buying and selling portfolio ( Seller Participant and Buyer Participant ).

> **⚠️ Note:** The Transfer Amount field should be left blank as it is a complete buyback of shares.

When the bank chooses to buy back shares from all the portfolios to a particular portfolio, it should follow the same steps, except that the Seller Participant field must be left empty, as shown in the below screenshot.

Once the buyback is complete, all the transferable shares are moved to Portfolio 120021.

When the owning bank prefers to buy back all shares of one or all external participants in the arrangement and transfer them to a particular portfolio, then it is referred to as an external buyback. The bank should specify the portfolio to which all the shares should be transferred.

Consider the following example, where the bank chooses to buy back all the shares from the participant bank (Customer ID 100112) to Portfolio 120021 and the bank specifies the values as shown in the below screenshot.

Set the Transfer Type field as External transfer. Select the Buy Back option along with buying portfolio and the selling external participant ( Seller Participant and Buyer Participant ).

> **⚠️ Note:** The Transfer Amount field should be left blank as it is a complete buyback of shares.

When the bank chooses to buy back shares from all the external participant banks to a particular portfolio, it should follow the same steps, except that Seller Participant should be left empty, as shown in the below screenshot.

Once the buyback is complete, all the transferable shares are moved to Portfolio 120021.

##### IFRS Reporting for Club Loans with Portfolios

Loan that has a default IFRS condition is considered for reporting in bilateral and club loans. When the loan has internal portfolios, the system skips the default condition and considers only the portfolio related IFRS classification for reporting. The user creates a record in EB.CASHFLOW separately for portfolios with the below record ID format.

* *

While creating the Facility arrangement with multiple portfolios,

- The user cannot edit Ifrs Classification and Ifrs Subtype derived from LOAN.PORTFOLIO . The user can edit other fields such as Market Key , Market Margin , and Margin Operand .
- Under the Participant property, the system defaults Primary Portfolio in the Charges and Skims tabs with the first portfolio unless entered manually.
- The system updates the record in EB.CASHFLOW for the basic lifecycle of the loans such as disbursement, prepayment, repayment, schedule change, and Interest rate change for each portfolio.

When the user updates Skim Rate defined for the own bank by triggering the Update Skim for Participant activity, the system updates the EB.CASHFLOW record of the primary portfolio with the skims received from all the participants. The system does not update EB.CASHFLOW record with the skims for other portfolios.

When a loan with internal portfolios and reporting condition is split into ‘n’ number of loans, the system,

- Splits the portfolio share in the existing loan and moves to ‘n’ number of loans in the user-defined ratio.
- Updates the records in EB.CASHFLOW for all the portfolios in the existing loan.
- Creates records in EB.CASHFLOW for all the portfolios based on their share for ‘n’ number of loans.

Similarly, when ‘n’ number of loans are merged into a single loan, the system creates a record in EB.CASHFLOW for the new loan.


###### IFRS Takeover

When a contract without an IFRS classification is taken over from a legacy system, the bank should trigger LENDING-TAKEOVER.CASHFLOW-REPORTING portfolio wise. That is, the bank can take over the Reporting portfolio-wise. When triggering the activity, the bank defines the portfolio ID in the Portfolio ID field in the AA.ARRANGEMENT.ACTIVITY screen, for which cashflow takeover is to be done.

The system defaults the portfolios IFRS nature in the reporting PC. The IFRS set of fields of other portfolios, other than the portfolio for which takeover is being done, and IFRS type and sub type fields of that portfolio is not editable. The system enables the following fields,

- Respective portfolio’s Market Key , Market Operand , and Market Margin
- METHOD
- EIR
- AMC

The takeover method can be captured along with the respective EIR or AMC field based on the takeover method for the portfolio defined in the contract. When the activity is committed, the system updates a EB.CASHFLOW record for that portfolio.

> **⚠️ Note:** If the bank wants to allocate a IFRS classification for the same cost center, for which it initially did not have any IFRS defined, then the bank should create a new portfolio record for the cost center with the required IFRS classification and then do a share transfer. Later, it can initiate the above activity to capture the EIR and AMC values.
