### 2.31  Limits


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The sanctioned limit is the total exposure that the bank can take on a particular client for facilities offered by the bank. Limits are recorded or controlled using the Limit Property Class (PC) in Facility arrangements. Validation and utilisation limits are created and attached to Facility arrangem...*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Limit Account*, *Limit Style*, *Single Limit*, *Update Commit Limit*, *Update Commitment Limit*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

The sanctioned limit is the total exposure that the bank can take on a particular client for facilities offered by the bank. Limits are recorded or controlled using the Limit Property Class (PC) in Facility arrangements. Validation and utilisation limits are created and attached to Facility arrangements. Transact can validate the utilisation limit amount when further drawings are created. The system prompts override or error message when the drawing amount exceeds.

Defining the Limit structure is part of the credit agreement. The corporate and retail should have a single limit structure with multiple sub limits. This helps the Financial Institution (FI) or banks to,

- Tailor their limit structure and the sublimit for different lending purpose of the client.
- Hold a single cap limit for the individual or group on top of the lending structure for restricting commitment, currency, product and customer instead of having multiple limit.

This cap limit needs to be attached to the deal or the facility for the overall exposure that the FI or banks can take against the individual customer or the group. The bank further structuring of sub limits for controlling the drawings under the facility, (that is, sublimit on currency, borrower or product). This guide provides insight information about limit being attached with the facility and its implication in drawing arrangement.

The user can link limit structure to the facility and its underlying drawings. When facility and drawing are restricted to a single customer, the limit record of the customer is attached to facility and its drawings. For corporate group or facility defined with multiple customers, the LI Limit record to be attached to the facility instead of customer limit.

Temenos Transact automatically defaults the limit ID from the facility to the underlying drawings to link the same limit to both facility and drawings. The validation to check if the limit product is suitable for the account category is defined in Limit Parameter. That is, the limit reference defined at the facility level is linked to the loan even if the limit product is not suitable for loan product as per limit parameter definition. This is handled by passing the Facility category code to limit parameter check instead of the drawings account category.

To affect the contingent portion of the limit when a facility is created, the Update Commitment Limit field in term amount gets defaulted to ‘Yes’ for Facility product, when limit property is attached at the product level. When facility is created, the contingent portion of the limit is immediately utilised (that is, the limit is fully reserved for the commitment amount of the Facility). When drawings are created (without disbursement) under the facility, the same limit record gets defaulted in the drawing level. The contingent portion of the,

- Facility for the drawn portion is released
- Drawing is utilised.

On disbursement,

- Contingent portion of the drawing for the disbursed amount is released
- Non-contingent portion of the disbursement amount is utilised

> **⚠️ Note:** This utilisation and release of the blocked limit depends on the setup of the Update Commitment Limit field at the drawing level.

The Limit related information are set in the Limit PC. The user should attach the Limit reference in the Limit Product Condition to default it at the arrangement level. Alternatively, it can be defined as negotiable in the Product Condition so that the user can attach the limit record at the arrangement level. Apart from attaching the limit record, the usage of limit can be restricted to one arrangement by setting the Single Limit field as Yes. It cannot be shared among other arrangements.

The Limit Style field in the Limit Property Class updates or maintains the limit balances by default for:

- Arrangement pertaining to Facility Product Lines
- Drawing arrangement with master arrangement ID pertaining to Facility Product Line

The Limit Account field in the ACCOUNT application is selected by default for maintaining limit balances for the respective facility or drawing account.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The limit conditions and limit references are defined at Product Condition level. The limit reference is captured at arrangement level. Limit Property Class is optional and only if it is attached, then the Update Commit Limit field is enabled. The Facility can be revolving or non-revolving.

The Update Commit Limit field is set as Yes at Product Condition, and arrangement level it is defaulted automatically.

### 2.32  Misc


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The Facility module is part of the Transact Retail and Corporate Banking suite of products. It allows the financial institution to book multiple drawings in different currencies under the same facility. The complete life cycle of a loan beginning with the facility creation, loan booking, disbursemen...*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction


#### 📖 Introduction

Related topics:

- APIs
- Temenos Transact Services

The Facility module is part of the Transact Retail and Corporate Banking suite of products. It allows the financial institution to book multiple drawings in different currencies under the same facility. The complete life cycle of a loan beginning with the facility creation, loan booking, disbursement, collection, facility maintenance and closure is embedded in the Facility module. It supports an entire range of lending features with configurable conditions. The credit agreement acts as the base for creating a Facility.

Some of the highlights of Facility module are as follows:

- Temenos Transact allows to create different types of Facilities (revolving and non-revolving)
- Supports additional borrowers on top of the primary borrower.
- Multiple arrangements or loans are possible under single Facility.
- Multi–Currency Facility enables drawings in different currencies.
- Flexible interest conditions (which includes fixed or floating or periodic interest rates) can be created at the product condition level. Unlimited interest types such as principal interest and penalty interest can be created. New interest types can be configured by the financial institution.
- Different types of charges and respective accounting methods.
- Combined repayment schedule catering to multiple drawings at the Facility level.
- Combined billing and settlement, statements and payoff.
- When a payment is credited to a Facility, a Payment Priority PC determines how the payment amount is allocated between the Facility and its mortgages (drawings).
- Fully integrated rule-based overdue and aging process.
- Amendment activities at the Facility level as part of Facility maintenance includes changing the interest rate, repayment schedule, Facility commitment and maturity date,
- Changes can be done at Facility level for back value date. Additionally, Temenos Transact does the reversal of the transactions after back value date and replays those in the same sequence of order.
- Ability to accept payments and disburse loans using any Temenos Transact application and/or a channel that allows the specification of a Temenos Transact account for transactions. As a result, disbursal and repayment can be from accounts in any currency.
- Automating billing of the dues from the repayment schedule.
- Enables full repayment, partial repayment, pre-payment and payment in advance.
- Utilises rules-based accounting, allowing flexible configuration of entry or balance generation in Temenos Transact .

and Product), which is available in the Product Builder application supports product designing and configuration. This application helps the financial institution to deliver the product on time. Temenos Transact robust Arrangement architecture helps to minimise the time consumed to go to market with the product and modify the characteristics of the product as and when required, with flexible configuration and with minimal customisation approach.

The Temenos Transact product equips banks to,

- Define various product conditions for Facility and create different type of Facilities based on target customer requirements
- Provide a very powerful and user-friendly framework that supports diverse interest, fee and transaction charges setup
- Integrate with Temenos Transact pricing and offer a very efficient preferential pricing (pricing grid) tool, configurable based on customer segmentation
- Amend, reverse or update Arrangements with effective date as back date with recalculation and adjustment, if required
- Settle the disbursement of loan amount to multiple accounts in multi-currency
- With role-based home pages for users - with an option for custom set of screens, enquiries or menus as required by a user to carry on with the day-to-day operations


##### Configuring Facility

The below section describes the Facility product configuration.

| Column 1 | Column 2 | Column 3 |
|---|---|---|
| Account | Accounting | Activity Charge |
| Activity Presentation | Activity Mapping | Activity Messaging |
| Alerts | Balance Maintenance | Closure |
| Change Product | Customer | Eligibility |
| Limit | Officers | Payoff |
| Payment Schedule | Pricing Grid | Payment Priority |
| Settlement | Sub Arrangement Rules | Statement |
| Term Amount | Sub-Limit | Exchange Rate |
| Sub Arrangement Condition | Evidence |  |


##### Illustrating Model Parameters

Product Conditions of a Property Class are evaluated to bring out the features of the Property Class. The values in the Product Condition are made default in an arrangement during its creation. The negotiability or default values and other restrictions are also defined in the Product Condition. These Product Conditions with the Properties derived from the Property Classes are grouped together to build products.

Product Conditions are dated and some of them have currency as part of their ID. When currency forms part of the Product Condition ID, then the user has to create different conditions for each currency in which the product is available. When a new condition is created or an existing condition is amended, then the user has to proof and publish the product to which the condition is linked.

Model Parameters consists of:

The Account Property Class is used by all products, which are account based. This Property Class primarily controls the description of the account. The Account Property allows the user to define and control balance treatment, posting restriction, linked account number (for memo accounts), currency market, date convention related setup for the account.

Although the account names are account specific, generic titles can be defaulted from the product and can be replaced or given additional detail at the arrangement level. Each Temenos Transact product defined and processed in Arrangement Architecture (AA) can have a single ACCOUNT Property defined.

The Accounting Property Class is used by all products. AA uses activity-based accounting. Each Property has different actions, which require accounting. For each action, a corresponding allocation rule definition is required. Allocation rules can be defined either at Property or Property Class level. The categories to which the interest or charges have to be posted are also defined in this Product Condition. In Model Bank, the charges are amortised.

The Activity Presentation is an optional Property Class that allows to define versions used for various Properties during arrangement activities. The versions can be defined at Property Class, Property and Activity levels.

The Activity Mapping Property Class provides the link between external applications and arrangement activities when a transaction is performed on an arrangement account. A debit or credit to an arrangement account triggers the applications such as, Funds Transfer, Teller, Clearing, and so on, which are linked by relevant transaction codes using this Product Condition.

The Activity Messaging Property Class is used to link the Soft Delivery module to AA module. Messages are sent based on the role and activity performed on an arrangement. This record allows either specific Activities or Activity Classes to be defined and linked to the records of EB.ADVICES .

The Activity Charge Property Class defines the charges that has to be applied when a particular activity is triggered on the arrangement. The charges so applied can be made due, capitalised or deferred. In the model bank, for a Term Facility product Upfront Fee and Coordination Fee are applied when a new arrangement is created.

The Alerts Property Class is used by all products. It enables alerts to be sent to the customer for various activities in an arrangement. Alerts can be subscribed at the arrangement level by using EB.ALERT.REQUEST . Multiple owners of the arrangement are allowed to subscribe different alerts on that arrangement. The subscription of alerts can be restricted based on the role of the customer in that arrangement.

The Balance Maintenance Property Class allows the user to capture bills and balances and adjust the balances of the bill for the contracts, which have been taken over from existing legacy system or Temenos Transact Lending module into Temenos Transact AA module. The actions such as, CAPTURE.BILL, ADJUST.BILL, and so on, help in capturing the bill and its balances into the new system.

The Closure Property Class defines the rules and behavior for processing closure of an arrangement. An arrangement account can be closed automatically or manually and it is defined in the product condition. On reversal of a new arrangement, closure is triggered automatically.

The Change Product Property Class is used by all products, which allow for a change of product during their lifecycle. When a new product is applied to the existing arrangement, the user loses all the negotiations done as part of the old product. This table allows a list of products to which the old product can change and also define time-scales as to when the event should happen.

The Customer Property Class is used by all products. This Property Class is used to define all the parties involved in an arrangement and their respective roles. The customer is always defined at the arrangement level. Each arrangement can have one or more legal owners defined in OWNER.

The Eligibility Property Class is used to evaluate eligibility of a customer for a specific product based on a set of rules. The eligibility evaluation is triggered at a given frequency or when there is a static change for the customer. In Temonos Transact, first the EB.CONTEXT has to be created. Based on this, rules are defined using Rules Engine. Once these rules are validated, the EB.RULES.VERSION and EB.RULES are created in the system.

Evidence (Covenant and Conditions) Property Class refers to conditions, which a borrower must comply with to avail a Facility or a Loan. A Covenant must be valid throughout the life of an Arrangement (for example, Deal or Facility) and it must be validated on a certain frequency. A Condition must be true for certain activities to occur. Evidences is validated during creation of a new arrangement, update activity and closure of activity. Evidence Property Class is applicable for Deal, Facility and Drawing Product Lines and it is an optional Property Class.

The evidence requirement is captured in EV.EVIDENCE.REQUIREMENT . The category of the evidence requirements are created in EV.REQUIREMENT.CATEGORY (virtual table). The consequences are the actions taken by the bank in situations where the covenants and conditions are not satisfied. So, the consequences are tagged to AA.ACTION for which the activity type is configured as Evidence Check in the relevant record of AA.ACTIVITY.CLASS .

The Limit Property Class primarily controls the use of Limit module by the product. The user can set up single or shared limit and can define Limit Reference applicable for a specific product such that the same is set as default in an arrangement. For a new limit, at the arrangement level, the user should provide New in the Limit Serial field. Further limits can be set to use the Limit module or it can be managed only within the arrangement architecture framework.

The Officers Property Class enables the user to define:

- Product
- Arrangement specific officers
- Officer’s roles
- Primary officer
- Additional officer

Each Temenos Transact product defined and processed in AA can have a single OFFICERS Property defined.

The Payoff Property Class is used to produce a payoff statement, which is given to a customer when a loan payoff is considered. It shows the current status of the account, including the updated accrued interest and penalty applicable, if any. An expiry date can be defined for the payoff statement and the loan statement shows the additional daily interest to be charged till the expiry date. The payoff amount is calculated by using the simulation framework.

The Payment Schedule Property Class is used by all products which have amounts billed (that is, made due or capitalised or pay). A Payment Schedule can be comprised of one or more payment definitions with conditions such as, payment type and method, arrangement properties, dates and amounts. The AA.PAYMENT.TYPE file is used to define the standard payment types such as, Constant, Combine Bill and Combined interest, and so on, which can be used by a product. This payment type is then attached to each payment schedule definition. The start and end date can be specified. The user can specify the repayment of arrangement to commence after ‘n’ months from the arrangement date or ‘n’ months before the maturity or ‘n’ months after the change product or reset and rollover has happened.

The Pricing Grid Property Class applies to the Facility and Lending Product Lines. The Pricing Grid Property Class provides a mechanism to define the criteria used to determine the margin(s) or spread(s) for interest or fee that apply to base rates at the various levels of the credit agreement such as, deals, facility and drawing. Pricing Grids can be configured by selecting criteria, which is used to determine the margin (for interest) and/or the rate (for fee) to apply to a Property. A Pricing Grid is comprised of elements that determine the criteria for one or more elements to specify what is set on the interest condition. The user can select both the user-defined data criteria and their order of precedence. Grids can be defined at the deal, facility and/or drawing levels.

- Deal level Pricing Grids defines the rates for Deal level fees.
- Facility Level Pricing Grids defines the rates for Facility level fees and the margins for drawings level interest.
- Drawing Level Pricing Grids defines the margins for drawings level interest.
- Pricing Grids that are defined for Facility level can be negotiated at the Drawings level

The Payment Priority Property Class is used by Facility Product Line to define the order in which the combined repayment is allocated between the facility dues on the facility and dues on drawings under the facility. Combined payment received at the Facility level is allocated to individual Drawing arrangements based on the rules defined in this Property Class. The user can create multiple drawings under a single Facility and the bills will be combined at facility level. The user can make a single payment using Facility arrangement and is allocated to each drawings based on the rules set in Payment Priority. The priority is based on different factors such as, Product Group, product, bill date, bill type and so on.

The Settlement Property Class is used for various Product Lines to control the settlement related functions of all the Product Lines. Settlement can be handled by linking any Temenos Transact account, the account and bank details of another bank by using Direct Debit and beneficiary of the customer. The Default Settlement Account is considered as the default account for both Pay-in and Pay-out Activities, if the Pay in or Pay out account is not specified. But, if the accounts are specified for the Pay-in or Pay-out, then those accounts precedes over the specified default settlement account.

The Sub-Arrangement Property Class allows the user to define the conditions for the Sub Arrangements (drawings) of the facility. The Sub-Arrangement Rules Property Class is available for the Facility Product Line. This Property Class enables to set rules for the sub-arrangements under a master arrangement.

It is attached to the Facility product to control the allowed customers, currencies and products of the drawings under the Facility. Similarly, it is attached to the Deal product to control the allowed customers, currencies and products of the facility and drawings under the Deal.

The Sub Arrangement Condition Property class is used to define condition or validation for processing or creating Drawing Arrangements. Banks can define various criteria in Sub-Arrangement condition either at deal or facility level. When a drawdown is created under a Facility, the system validates against the conditions and raises override or error message whenever any condition is breached.

The Statement Property class is used to define the legacy ACCT.STATEMENT feature at AA level. Statements may be produced daily (every working day), every 1-9 weeks, twice a month (on the 15th and the last day of the month) or every 1-12 months on any day of the month. Up to nine statement cycles may be specified for each Account and each statement cycle is independent. In addition to this, special interim statements can be enabled. This property class also controls if advices are to be produced or not, when interest and charges are applied, and whether detailed interest statements (interest scale) should be produced.

The Term Amount Property Class is used by financial products which involve an amount of money that is lent for a specified period of time. This property class controls the commitment made by the bank to the customer.

Sub Limits Property class allows the user to define the multiple shadow limits within the facility or utilisation limit by restricting or allocating the limit, based on the risk factors or criterions. At the time of creating the facility arrangement, the sub-limit(s) limit record will be created as per the definition in the sub-limits PC. The restrictions and allocations are regulated based on the risk elements, borrower, currency and product (Product, Product group, and Product line).

Exchange Rate property class is to define the Exchange Rate (FX), Rate Tolerance and Prior Days, Advance FX Fix Activity, and so on to support the Advance FX fixing requirement.


##### Illustrating Model Products

Facility Product Line provides Term Facility and Revolving Facility functionality for Temenos Transact . This module allows the user to create Term Facility and Revolving Facility by using the AA framework under the Facility Product Line.

| Product Name | Product Attributes |
|---|---|
| Credit Line Facility | Credit Line Facility product with default term as 10 years and Revolving as Payment. |
| Corporate Facilities | Revolving Facility Term Facility |
| Digital Mortgage Facilities | Digital Mortgage Facility - The facility product can have drawings created under Mortgage group or Home Equity group. |

### 2.34  Pricing Grid


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Pricing of a loan depends on various criterions like loan type, loan amount, borrower’s credit rating, and so on. Pricing Grid Property Class in AA evaluates and arrives at the eligible interest rate or margin for a loan based on these pre-defined criterion values. It enables a lender to offer the s...*
> 
> **Applications:** `AA.DATA.ELEMENTS`, `EB.API`, `EB.LOOKUP`, `EB.RATING`, `EB.RATING.AGENCY`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Agency ID*, *Arrangement*, *Arrangement Level*, *Arrangement Source*, *Arrangement source*, *Balance*, *Catch all*, *Catch all value* ... +25 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

Pricing of a loan depends on various criterions like loan type, loan amount, borrower’s credit rating, and so on. Pricing Grid Property Class in AA evaluates and arrives at the eligible interest rate or margin for a loan based on these pre-defined criterion values. It enables a lender to offer the same loan product at varied interest rates and margins to different borrowers.

The user can set the criterions as conditional criterions defined with multiple field values. For example, the user can set a margin rate for a specific customer (Criterion 1), currency (Criterion 2), and balance (Criterion 3).

It is also possible to set a margin at the drawing level based on a specific field value from the covenants collected at the facility level.

> **⚠️ Note:** The user can set margin or fixed rate or usage percentage to underlying arrangements using pricing grid.

If there is any change in the said criterion values (for example, change in borrower’s credit rating), system automatically re-evaluates the loan pricing.

It facilitates default pricing so that when the Credit team wants to effect a change from one pricing set of rules to another. This can be accommodated centrally at a deal or facility level with a full audit trail. The correct margin or spread for the drawing is derived from the constructed Facility Pricing Grid (based on the pricing terms in Credit Agreement).


#### ⚙️ Configuration

Pricing is required at,

- Deal level – It applies to Commitment and Ongoing fees.
- Facility level – It applies to Commitment fees.

For interest, the pricing is setup at the facility level as it relates to how the commitment is used. Pricing Grid enables the user to price the arrangement or contract considering different risk factors involved in funding. During the life cycle of the loan, the values of these risk factors (criteria) trigger changes in the rates.

The following are the pricing ratchets that can trigger change in interest rate:

- Date range
- Currency
- Utilised amount at the Facility and/or Drawing level (either Band or Level based condition)
- Risk ratings (Moodys, Dagong, Fitch, SandP etc.)
- Interest property
- Product or Product type
- Rate index
- Financial ratios

To create a Product Condition under the Pricing Grid Property Class, AA.DATA.ELEMENTS and AA.TARGET.ELEMENTS should be setup. The interest or fee change is triggered based on the above criteria and it is defined in AA.DATA.ELEMENTS . Given below are the various fields in AA.DATA.ELEMENTS application and their required configuration:

| Field Name | Description |
|---|---|
| Type | Allowed values are, Field – When the user choses the internal rating criterion, the value should be Field since the system checks for the value of the criterion, (that is, internal rating) in the Customer Rating field of CUSTOMER application. Balance – When the user chooses balance criterion, the value should be Balance, since the system checks for the respective balance type at the arrangement level. Property – When the user chooses interest criterion, the value in this field should be Property to check the relevant property for the values. |
| Data Source | The source of the data can be from any of the following, Arrangement Customer Collateral |
| Arrangement Level | When the Data Source field is set as Arrangement’, then this level should be specified. So that, the system retrieves the data value either from arrangement being processed or from its parent. |
| Arrangement source | When the Data Source field is set as Arrangement, the source should be specified, (the Property Class which the system should check in the arrangement). Allowed values are Interest or Account. |
| Field | Refers to the field in CUSTOMER , LIMIT and COLLATERAL applications or the Arrangement Source field where the data is located. |
| Balance | Refers to the balance that needs to be retrieved. |
| Data type | A system updated field indicating the IN2 type of the field. This allows the UX to understand what type of field needs to be displayed to the user. |
| Data Check File | Updates the application from which the system pre-fetches the actual value. For example, in case of internal rating criterion, the Customer Rating field in the CUSTOMER application must be a valid record from EB.RATING application. |
| Data Selection | If Data Check File is specified, the user can provide selection criteria in this field and the system filters the list of IDs that need to be present to the user. For example, in the case of internal rating criterion, the user specifies AGENCY.ID EQ INTERNAL condition. That is, the records with Agency ID field value as Internal alone is filtered from the EB.RATING table. |
| Catch all | If none of the criteria matches, then this is used as default condition. |
| Catch all value | Captures the value for the default condition. |

The Pricing Grid is not only built to configure multiple trigger events but should also have fields to define the interest values for these criteria when triggered. This is achieved using the AA.TARGET.ELEMENTS table. Given below are the various fields in the AA.TARGET.ELEMENTS table and their required configuration:

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Type | Allowed values are: Fixed Rate – The corresponding rate is captured. Margin Type – The user can choose Margin type, Margin operand and Margin rate. Usage Percentage – The corresponding Usage percentage is captured which is applied on the reference rate to get the effective rate. |
| Data Type | System defaults this field value as IN2. |
| Value Type | Allowed values are Input and Defined. When set as, Input – The user can enter values manually at Arrangement level. Defined – The system fetches the values from the product condition level. |

Ratchet pricing is achieved using the Pricing Grid Property Class specially designed for this purpose. This Property Class is available for Facility Product Line and Lending Product Line.

Pricing Grid Property Class

The attributes of this Property Class are listed below.

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Criteria ID | A multi-value field and the user can select the criterion as defined in AA.DATA.ELEMENTS, in the order of precedence. |
| Target ID | A multi-value field and the user can select the targets as defined in AA.TARGET.ELEMENTS in the order of precedence. |
| Default | The default target value is used if none of the criteria combinations are satisfied at runtime. This is a mandatory field for fixed rate targets and optional input for margin targets. |
| Criteria 1, 2...10 | Stores the grid values of the criterion selected by the user. For example, if the Criteria ID field is set as PROPERTY, then the value in this field can be PRINCIPALINT. |
| Target 1, 2…..10 | Stores the grid values of the target(s) selected by the user. For example, if the Target ID field is set as CUSTOMER.MARGIN, then the value in this field can be 1.5 (margin rate). |

Property is a mandatory criteria as it defines which property the specified rates or margins apply to.

This section details the required configuration for the Borrowing Base Utilisation Percentage.

The CALC.BORROWING.BASE.UTL.PERC routine is added to calculate the utilization percentage of borrowing base. The user creates a criterion BORROWING.BASE.UTILISATION.% in AA.DATA.ELEMENTS and attach it to the routine as shown in the screenshot below.

The user must attach the AA.CALC.BORROWING.BASE.UTL.PERC record to the Data Routine field in AA.DATA.ELEMENTS that is available in the EB.API application, where Protection Level is set as Full and Source Type as Basic.

The screenshot below shows the EB.API/AA.CALC.BORROWING.BASE.UTL.PERC record in the EB.API application.

A bank can configure interest margins in pricing grid based on the covenants and conditions submitted.

Refer to the Configuring Covenants and Conditions section for more information about the configuration of covenants and conditions.

Once the configurations are completed in the Evidence module, the bank can configure AA.DATA.ELEMENTS based on the fields created in the evidence class. To define a criterion based on a value in evidence, the user must configure the record in AA.DATA.ELEMENTS as below:

- Type must be selected as ‘field’.
- Data Source is set as ‘Evidence’ to indicate to the system that the criterion is based on a field in evidence.
- Arrangement Source must be defined with the evidence class from which the criterion value is to be taken.
- Field is defined with the field from the evidence class to be used as the criterion. The system defaults the data type based on the field’s data type in the evidence class.
- Used Prop Class must be set as ‘Pricing.grid’.

A new routine AA.DATA.ELEMENT.COMPARE.RATING is released by Transact to get the least customer rating among the ratings of multiple rating agencies like S&P’s, Moody’s, Fitch’s, and so on. A new record in EB.API application is released as part of the model bank with the same name (AA.DATA.ELEMENT.COMPARE.RATING).

To compare multiple credit ratings and to find the least rating among them, the user creates a data element record as shown below,

1. Configure the following fields in the AA.DATA.ELEMENTS application: Type as Routine Data Source as Customer Arrangement Level as Self
2. Attach the routine in the Data Routine field.
3. Update the data in the Option List field in the "RISK.RATING+ + +…" format. The system compares the customer ratings provided by the rating agencies, that are defined in the option list. Any other ratings provided by the rating agencies are not considered. The rating agency defined in the Option List field should exactly be the same as the agency ID defined in the EB.RATING.AGENCY application.

In the above screen shot, a data element is created to compare the risk ratings of three rating agencies (S&P, FITCH, and MOODY’S). If the bank wants to compare only the ratings of S&P and MOODY’S and ignore the rating of FITCH agency, the Option List field should be defined as ‘RISK.RATING+S&P+MOODY’S’. This way, banks can create various records in the AA.DATA.ELEMENTS table based on the combination of rating agency rankings that needs to be compared.

The ratings from the rating agencies are defined in the EB.RATING application. Each rating has a rating description and the rating agency ID. The field system rankings in the EB.RATING application should be defined by the bank based on their ranking structure.

In addition to the above setup, banks can create the records in the EB.LOOKUP table to show the description to the front-end users. The record must be in the same format as provided in the Option List field in the AA.DATA.ELEMENTS record, followed by the system ranking. This is optional if the bank uses a front-end application to enter the pricing grid criteria and values.

The format for Record ID is "RISK.RATING+ + +…* "

Refer the below screen shot to create a record in the EB.LOOKUP table.

To build a pricing grid at the facility level and to inherit the values of the grid at the Drawings level, a Property is created under the Pricing Grid Property Class and is attached at Facility and Drawing Product Group level.

Create a Product Condition for the interest and set the Use Pricing Grid field to Yes.

Create two properties under Inheritance Property Class. One for the source product (Facility) and another for the target product (Drawing), and attach the same at the Product Group level of facility and drawing separately.

Attach the product conditions of Pricing Grid and Inheritance to the facility and drawing product.


##### ARRANGEMENT

The arrangement created at the facility level reflects the pricing grid defaulted at the Product Condition level. Drawing created under the facility inherits the pricing grid from the facility level and the value of the target property (for example, PRINCIPALINT) is picked up from the facility pricing grid once arrangement is validated. The value of the margin is based on the customer for whom the arrangement is created since the pricing grid is based on the customer rating.

If the rating of the Drawing customer is 2, the margin at the drawing level is 3.5 (refer screenshot below).

The system defaults the margin values when the criterion values does not fit into the existing ones at pricing grid level. In the above screenshot, if the customer rating is neither 1 nor 2 nor 3, then the drawing picks the default rate as the margin.


##### Updating Pricing Grid

When the pricing grid needs to be updated with new target values, the new rate is applicable only for the future drawings under the facility and not the existing drawings. For example, the margin rate for a criterion is changed from 1.5% to 1.75% at the facility level. However, when there are changes in the values of the criterions, the corresponding rate for the new criterion value as per the pricing grid is updated at the drawing level with immediate effect. The user can view the changes post completion of Close of Business (COB).

For example, If the pricing grid is based on internal risk rating of the customer and the customer rate is 1 when the drawing is booked and later changed to 2, then the margin corresponding to the new rating is updated after a COB at the drawing level.

The pricing grid used in this example is based out of the customer rating. The pricing grid can be used more effectively with more number of criterions and target values.

##### Commitment fee as percentage of margin

The bank prefers the charge fees on the facility commitment balances to be a fraction of the interest margins on the loans, that is, the commitment fee for a facility has to be equal to a percentage of current interest margins on the drawings under the facility.

If a bank charges a margin to the customers based on their credit rating, then the commitment fee charged for the loans should be 40% of the interest margin applied on the loans. If the ratings of the customer change in the future, the respective margin and the commitment fees are updated accordingly.

A target element of Type Usage Percentage is created in AA.TARGET.ELEMENTS .

The percentage defined in this target element (USAGE.PERCENTAGE) is applied on the reference rate before the system applies the margin and the other interest adjustments.

| Leverage Ratio | Applicable Margin (in percentage) |
|---|---|
| 0.01 to 1.00 | 1 |
| 1.01 to 2.00 | 2 |
| 2.01 to 3.00 | 3 |
| 3.01 and above | 4 |

The table below shows that the leverage ratio value determines the changes in the margin applicable and commitment fee charge values.

| Leverage Ratio (in percentage) | Margin Applicable (in percentage) | Commitment Fee Charge (in percentage) |
|---|---|---|
| 1.23 | 2 | 0.8 |
| 2.5 | 3 | 1.2 |

The Pricing grid Condition at the facility level will be evaluated whenever the user triggers the activities which affects the UTL , OVD amount and Total Limit amount. A new routine CALC.BORROWING.BASE.UTL.PERC is released to calculate the utilization percentage of borrowing base.

where,

Drawing Overview Screen

According to the Borrowing Base Utilization Percentage formula,

Utilization % Calculation = 3,000,000 / 5,000,000 * 100 = 60%

where, UTL – USD 3M and total limit – USD 5M.

> **⚠️ Note:** The system uses the commitment amount as total limit since the collateral value is greater than the facility commitment amount.

As 60% falls in the third ratchet, the system uses the Margin of 3% Principal margin rate for the Loan.

Case 1.1

When the user performs a repayment of USD 2.5M at the drawing level, the system displays the Facility Overview Screen after repayment as shown in the screenshot below.

Utilization % Calculation = 2,000,000 / 5,000,000 * 100 = 40%

where, UTL – USD 2M and total limit – USD 5M

As 40% falls in the second ratchet, the system uses the Margin of 2% Principal margin rate for the Loan.

When the Borrowing Base Utilisation Percentage changes, the system arrives at the corresponding margin percentage set at the Pricing Grid condition.

| Pricing Tier | Consolidated Leverage Ratio | Applicable LIBOR margin at the drawings |
|---|---|---|
| I |  | 1.00% |
| II | 1.00 to | 1.25% |
| III | 2.00 to | 1.50% |
| ‘Catch all rate’ | 3.00 | 2.00% |
| ‘Default rate’ | NA | 3.00% |

Credit rating is an evaluation of the credit worthiness of a borrower, predicting their ability to pay back the debt, and an implicit forecast of the likelihood of the debtor defaulting. Lenders review the credit rating while considering a loan application is the credit rating.

Credit ratings are typically assigned on a scale of one to seven, with one being the lowest risk and seven being the highest risk. The specific ratings and their meanings may vary depending on the rating agency.

Banks usually compare multiple credit ratings of the customer provided by different credit rating agencies and find the highest risk among them. Based on the highest risk, the banks decide to price the loan, that is, the customer margin is decided based on their highest risk rating.

The pricing grid is enhanced to find the highest risk among the multiple risk ratings defined and to determine the margin based on the highest risk rating.

Consider a corporate customer having three different ratings from three different credit rating agencies.

The system rankings for the corresponding customer ratings by S&P and FITCH agencies are ‘1’, but by Moody’s is ‘2’.

Assume that the below pricing grid is setup to determine the principal interest margin based on the highest risk of the customer. The date element created is used to determine the highest risk rating.

So, while creating a loan the system considers the Margin Rate of 1.20, as 2 is the least system ranking given by MOODY’s among the others.

In the previous example, the system ranking for S&P and FITCH ratings is ‘1’ but for MOODY’s rating is ‘2’. So, the margin of 1.20% is defaulted. Later the rating agencies revises the rating and upgrades the MOODY’s rating. Now all the three ratings have the system ranking as ‘1’.

After COB, the pricing grid is re-evaluated whenever there is a change in the corporate customer ratings and so the margin has been updated from 1.10% to 1.00% in the principal interest of the drawing.

> **⚠️ Note:** If the customer rating does not have any rating agency defined in AA.DATA.ELEMENTS , the system takes the default rate . For example, in AA.DATA.ELEMENTS , the rating agencies to be considered is selected as S&P and FITCH, but in the customer application, only an internal rating and MOODY’s ratings are defined for the customer. In this case, the system takes the default rate.

Pricing Grid is used to adjust the rate of interest or margin based on agreed performance indicators, such as, credit rating, leverage ratio and so on. Interest and fees are the key source of income on a corporate loan and therefore the terms and conditions of these expenses are negotiated with the borrower. The Pricing Grid has layers (ratchets) that are often associated with the risk profile of the borrower, the amount drawn, and dates amongst other things. The correct margin or spread for the drawing is derived from the constructed Facility Pricing Grid based on the pricing terms in Credit Agreement.

### 2.35  Risk Participation for Bilateral Loans


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *A loan is associated with a credit risk as there is a chance for the borrower to default on the repayments. The banks need to ensure that the borrower repay the loans without fail.*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *AbnAmro*, *Amount*, *Arrangement*, *Buy Back*, *Buy Participant*, *Fixed*, *Margin Operand*, *Own Bank* ... +9 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

A loan is associated with a credit risk as there is a chance for the borrower to default on the repayments. The banks need to ensure that the borrower repay the loans without fail.

The banks mitigate the risk exposure in the loan by selling the risk exposure to other banks which eventually helps them to diversify the Risk Portfolio. The banks that share the risk exposure from the owning bank are called Risk Participants.

The owning bank can sell the risk exposure (full or partial) to the risk participants, so that the risk exposure is shared between the banks accordingly.

Risk participants only share the risk and do not provide any funding to the borrower. In case of any default by the borrower, the risk participants pay the amount to the owning bank which then is decided based on the share of the Risk exposure that the Risk Participants hold.

The following are the two types of risk participants:

- Fixed Risk Participants - Risk exposure is based on a specific commitment amount of the Book commitment.
- Variable Risk Participants - Risk exposure is based on a certain percentage of the Book commitment. Though Variable Risk Participant comes with certain percentage of commitment, the system captures only the share amount of that participant and not the percentage.

During a loan sanction, corporate loans might not have risk participants attached to the contract. Later during the life term of the loan, the owing banks may have to make changes in their risk portfolio. They may prefer to increase or decrease their risk exposure in a loan. This section gives a brief description on the following concepts:

- Owning bank decreasing their risk in a loan by selling the risk exposure to risk participants
- Owning bank increasing their risk exposure in the loan by partial or complete buyback of its risk sold to the risk participants

Risk Participants receive income in the following ways and it depends on the agreement between the buying and selling counterparties.

- Flat Fees

- Risk Fees and Risk Margin


##### Write-off for Loans

Bank can write-off a loan or a bill when it has not received the repayment due for a certain period and has to follow the regulatory compliance.

As risk participants cover a portion of the loan, the risk participants pay the written off amount proportionately. These settlements happen outside the loan contract. As the risk participants pay the portion of the loan amount, the corresponding amount should be reduced from their commitment.

A loan contract can be partially or fully written off.

- When the loan is written off completely, then all the risk participants balances are reduced to zero. The bank can write off the entire funding portion it holds irrespective of the risk exposure sold.
- When there is a principal write off, that is, either the outstanding principal amount or a specific bill is being written off, then the risk participant’s balances are reduced proportionately based on the principal amount that is being written off.

In both the cases, the adjusted or reduced amount is settled by the risk participant to the own bank outside the contract.

Bills such as risk fees and risk margin that the own bank needs to pay to risk participants cannot be written off, as it is the own bank’s responsibility to pay those bills.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The user must create a Participant Property of property Type as Risk Participant to add risk participant to a loan contract and then add it to the product at the product-designer level.

For adding the fund participants and risk participants, the user must create two separate properties and add them to the product, that is, one property with property Type set as Participant and the other with Type as Risk Participant as shown in the below screenshot.

> **⚠️ Note:** A single Participant property cannot have both the Participant and Risk Participant property types.

The bank user creates separate properties for the fund participants and risk participants, and they are added to the Participant Property class at the product group level. At product designer level, both the properties have their respective product conditions attached to them.

> **⚠️ Note:** If property type is not selected the system defaults it to Participant.

The user configures the following property classes, to calculate the Risk fees, Risk Margin and Flat Fees for the bilateral contracts or club loan contracts.

Interest Property Class is used to define the risk fees and risk margin and it can accrued and paid to the Risk participant.

To differentiate the risk participant’s Risk Fee and Risk Margin property from the other regular interest properties, the Interest property, which is created for paying out risk fee or margin consists of the Risk Participant property type along with existing Non Customer property type.

The screenshot below shows the Non Customer Interest Properties created to pay the risk margin and risk fees to the risk participant.

Charge property class is used to define the flat fees that is to be paid to the risk participants. It can be configured as an activity charge or as a scheduled charge, which can be defined in the Payment schedule.

To differentiate the Charge property that is used for paying flat fees to the risk participants from the other regular charge properties, the Charge property created for paying out the flat fees consists of the ‘Risk Participant’ property type along with existing ‘Non Customer’ and ‘Credit’ property type.

The screenshot below shows the Non Customer Charge Property created to pay the flat fees to the risk participant.

The properties created are attached to the respective Property Class of the Product in the Product Group as can be seen below

In the Product Designer, appropriate Product Conditions are attached to the Interest and Charge Properties which are attached to the Product are shown below:

The screenshot below shows the calculation source balance is defined for the Interest properties.

Once the product is published, the bank uses the risk fees and risk margin at the arrangement level.

> **⚠️ Note:** Irrespective of the bilateral or club contract with risk participants, a syndication settlement account is created. The risk fees and margin to be paid out are initially credited to the syndication settlement account and then a payment order created to pay out the funds to the respective risk participants.


##### Risk Participant in Guarantees

The user creates a Participant property of Type as Risk Participant to add risk participant to a guarantee contract and then add it to the product at the product-designer level. To add the fund participants and risk participants,

1. The user must create two separate properties as shown below and add them to the product. Set Type as Participant Set Type as Risk Participant A single Participant property cannot have both the Participant and Risk Participant property types.
2. Set Property Class as PARTICIPANT under Product Group.
3. Set Property to PARTICIPANT and RISKPARTICIPANT under Product Designer.

The user creates separate properties for the fund participants and risk participants, and adds them to the Participant property class at the product group-level. At the product designer-level, both properties have their respective product conditions attached to them.

> **⚠️ Note:** If the property Type is not selected, the system defaults it to Participant.

The user configures the following property classes to calculate the risk fees, risk margin, and flat fees for the bilateral contracts or club loan contracts.

Read Interest Property Class section for details regarding Interest property class.

Read Charge Property Class section for details regarding Charge property class.


#### 🔧 Working With

This section describes about selling the risk participation and risk share transfer in bilateral loans.


##### Selling the Risk Participation

The owning banks can make changes to their existing risk portfolio through share transfer by selling or buying risk exposures from other risk participant banks during the life term of the loan.

##### Risk Share Transfer

When the owning bank sells to risk participants, the formulas listed below are used to calculate the maximum amount that can be transferred, share transfer ratio and the balances of risk participants after the share transfer.

At Facility or Standalone Loan

1. Maximum Transferable Amount = Current Commitment of the Owning Bank - Current Commitment of all the Existing Risk Participants

where Current Commitment = CUR + UTL + OVD

1. Share Transfer Ratio= (Share Transfer Amount/Own Bank’s Current Commitment) *100
2. Total = MINIMUM (Transfer Amount | Own Bank’s CUR +UTL +UTL )
3. UR of RP3 = Own Bank’s CUR * Share Transfer Ratio
4. UTL of RP3 = Buyer Participant’s TOT -CUR
5. OVD of RP 3= Transfer Amount- (Buyer Participant’s CUR +UTL

At Drawing under a Facility

The transfer amount at drawing is calculated by the share transfer ratio which is calculated at the facility.

1. Transfer Amount = Own bank's current commitment * Share transfer ratio

Where Current Commitment= CUR + UTL + OVD

1. TOT = MINIMUM (Transfer Amount | Own Bank’s CUR +UTL +UTL )
2. CUR = Share Transfer Ratio*Own Bank’s CUR
3. UTL = Buyer Participant’s TOT -CUR
4. OVD = Transfer Amount-(Buyer Participant’s CUR +UTL

> **⚠️ Note:** When the share transfer is done to an existing risk participant in the contract, the calculated balances are added to the already existing balances of the risk participant to whom the share transfer is done.

When the owning bank buys back its risk from the risk participants, the formulas listed below are used to calculate the maximum amount that can be bought by the owning bank, the share transfer ratio, and the balances of risk participants after the share transfer.

At Facility or Standalone Loan

1. Current Commitment = CUR + UTL + OVD
2. Share Transfer Ratio= (Share Transfer Amount/ Selling RP Current Commitment) *100
3. Total = MINIMUM (Transfer Amount | selling RP CUR +UTL
4. CUR = Selling RP CUR * Share Transfer Ratio
5. UTL = Buyer Participant’s TOT -CUR
6. OVD = Transfer Amount- (Buyer Participant’s CUR +UTL

At Drawing under a Facility

1. Transfer Amount = Selling RP current commitment * Share transfer ratio
2. TOT = MINIMUM (Transfer Amount | Selling RP CUR +UTL
3. CUR = Share Transfer Ratio*Selling RP CUR
4. UTL = Buyer Participant’s TOT -CUR
5. OVD = Transfer Amount-(Buyer Participant’s CUR +UTL

> **⚠️ Note:** The balances derived are subtracted from the existing balances of the risk participants.

##### Risk Margin and Risk Fees Operands

Risk Margin or Risk Fees Operands are available under Risk Participant Property. Default values of Risk fees and Risk margin for the contract can be entered in the respective properties. Banks can alter the default risk fees or margin for a particular risk participant by adding or reducing a margin for that particular risk participant using the Operand field in the risk participant tab.

The following Margin Operand are applicable for Risk Participants.

The Bank reduces the Risk Margin and Risk fees for a specific risk participant using Operand. The value entered in the Margin Rate field is subtracted from the default risk margin and risk fees of the contract to obtain the effective risk margin rate.

If the default risk fees defined in the contract is 0.5% and below definition is given for a risk participant, then the Risk fees paid for the risk participant becomes 0.3%.

It is used to increase the default risk margin or risk fees. The value entered in the Margin rate field add up to the default risk margin or risk fees of the contract.

When the default risk fees defined in the contract is 0.5% and below definition is given for a risk participant, then the Risk fees to be paid for the risk participant becomes 1.3%.

It is used to override the default risk margin or risk fees. The value entered by the user replaces the default risk margin or risk fees of the contract.

When the default risk fees defined in the contract is 0.5% and below definition is given for a risk participant, then the Risk fees to be paid for the risk participant becomes 1%.


###### Calculating Risk Margin and Risk Fees for Bilateral Contracts

A contract with two risk participants ABC Bank (100112) and XYZ bank (100369) is created as a Bilateral Facility on May 24, 2021, for USD 1 million.

When the bank collects the risk fees and risk margin at the facility level , that is in facility arrangement,

- Risk fees is 0.7% (In Risk Fees Interest Property defined at Arrangement level)
- Risk Margin is 0.5% (In Risk Margin Interest Property defined at Arrangement level)
- Risk Margin and Risk fees due once a month
- Payment Schedule defines the frequency of risk margin and risk fees to be paid. Bill type defined in the payment schedule condition must be ‘Internal’.

ABC Bank Risk Participant

When the bank customises the default risk fees or risk margin in the contract specific to Nomura, then it uses the operands in the risk participant property.

- The bank pays an extra 0.8% in addition to the default risk fees(0.7%) defined in the contract as shown in the screenshot below and the risk fees paid to ABC Bank becomes 1.5%.

- The bank pays 1.3% as the risk margin instead of the default 0.5% and so the bank user uses the Operand ‘Override’ as shown in the screenshot below .

###### Calculating Flat Fees for the Bilateral Contracts

If the customer draws USD 600,000 under the facility and the bank pays a flat fee (Non Customer Charge) of USD 5,000 to all the risk participants in the contract for every new drawing taken by the customer under the facility, then the bank makes use of the activity charge to pay this flat fee to the Risk Participant.

Charge payment method in the activity charge condition should be pay . Each risk participant added to the contract is paid out a charge of USD 5,000 which is defined in the charge product condition. On the contrary, in the funded participation, flat fee is paid out pro-rata to the participant banks.

If the bank wants to customise this noncustomer charge for Nomura in the contract, then the bank pays USD 7,000 instead of USD 5,000 to Nomura and USD 5,000 to JP Morgan. For JP Morgan, the charge amount defined in the charge condition is taken by default. For Nomura, changes to the default charge definition is done in the Charges tab under the Risk Participant Property as shown in the screenshot given below.

Flat fees bills that are paid are displayed in the Drawing Overview screen as shown in the screenshot below. The bills are auto settled .


##### Activities for Loan Write-Off

Following are activities for loan write-off:

- LENDING-WRITE.OFF.BILL-BALANCE.MAINTENANCE - Use to write off only the bills of the loan.
- LENDING-WRITE.OFF.BALANCE-BALANCE.MAINTENANCE - Use to write off specific balances of the loan like outstanding principal (partial write off)
- LENDING-WRITE.OFF-BALANCE.MAINTENANCE - Use to write off the entire loan (full write off)
