##### Progressive Payments

The repayment amount in the Calc Amount field can be recalculated upon every repayment. The PROGRESSIVE.PAYMENT value in the Recalculate attribute increments the Calc Amount by the progressive percentage. The On Activity attribute in the Payment Schedule should include the LENDING-MAKEDUE-PAYMENT.SCHEDULE Activity to recalculate the PROGRESSIVE.PAYMENT.

In the example AA.ARR.PAYMENT.SCHEDULE , the Payment Freq attribute is set to 1M and the rate is 2%. This results in the amount calculated each month to increase by 2% every month.

The below ENQ AA.SCHEDULES.FULL enquiry shows the calculated amount for future payments for the above arrangement. This has been increased every month. Percentage Calculation for Principal-only Payments The total granted loan amount can be linearly distributed as Principal-only repayment for the percentage defined for the amortisation period as per the repayment frequency. When a percentage is defined in the Max Percentage attribute, the repayment percentage of original loan principal definition is restricted to maximum of percentage defined. Amortisation Schedule is 100% but the calculation percentage is restricted to the defined percentage. For example, if loan offered to customer was an Interest Subsidy loan, then it is convenient to collect the Principal-only repayments. Illustration Consider the following example. Loan Amount = USD 100,000 on 17 April 2020 Term = 1year Payments = Principal-only CALC Type = Percentage Repayment Frequency = Monthly Max Percentage = 100 Amortisation Schedule is as follows: 15% of 100,000 on the first three payments - 15,000 / 3 = 5000 20% of 100,000 on the next three - 20,000 / 3 = 6666.67 25% of 100,000 on the next three - 25,000/3 = 8333.33 40% of 100,000 on the last three - 40,000 / 3 = 13,333.33 Amortization date Total amount per period Repayment Percentage of original loan principal, % per period 17 May 2020 15000 15 17 June 2020 17 July 2020 17 Aug 2020 20000 20 17 Sep 2020 17 Oct 2020 17 Nov 2020 25000 25 17 Dec 2020 17 Jan 2021 17 Feb 2021 40000 40 17 Mar 2021 17 Apr 2021 The above amortisation conditions can be defined as follows in Payment Schedule product conditions. The payment amount calculation is always based on the outstanding balance and the remaining total percentage. Overriding the Capitalisation Amount The capitalisation process can make an account overdrawn, but such a scenario can optionally be restricted to the extent of available balance on the account. However, this functionality cannot be extended to user-defined checks, for example, a minimum amount definition that might be required for the customer for his living, like a sustenance amount. The system considers the entire available balance during capitalisation. In order to overcome this, an option is provided to validate any other user defined conditions that might be required during capitalisation. During capitalisation of bills, the system validates if the payment type is set as Cap and Inv Alt Payment Method and a user routine is attached in Alt Payment Routine . When both these conditions are satisfied, the available balance and the capitalisation amount are handed over by the core routine to the user attached API. The API further validates and decides if the bill should be capitalised or invoiced. Illustration Consider the pre-conditions listed above are met. A customer has a credit balance of Rs 5000. There is a user definition to have a balance Rs 7000 and above for his sustenance. A debit interest bill is processed for Rs 500. In the above scenario since the sustenance balance is greater than the available balance, the entire billed amount is moved to Inv.


##### Defining Future Conditions at the Arrangement Level

The Type field with FORWARD.DATED value in the AA.PROPERTY.CLASS record allows the user to introduce a new definition at the arrangement level, it will be dated. Once captured with a future date, the system automatically schedules this and during close of business the Scheduled Activity is processed by applying the new condition to the arrangement.

A Show tabs for expansion icon is provided in the tool bar of AA.ARRANGEMENT.ACTIVITY and AA.SIMULATION.CAPTURE screens. It helps the user to identify the property for which the future dated condition can be added.

Future dated condition can either be given by specifying the date of required change or by specifying relative date like ARRANGEMENT / START + 1 month.

1. Click the Show tabs for expansion icon in the tool bar. The Show tabs for expansion icon is disabled after displaying Current tab for the property to which Future Date Conditions are allowed.
2. Click Expand icon from Current tab to add Future Date Conditions. An Option for selecting Fixed Date and Relative Date pops up on the screen.
3. Select month and year for Fixed Date and Arrangement or Start date, offset by day(s), week(s), month(s) and year(s) for Relative Date.
4. Click to confirm the selection. The selected options will be displayed as the description of the Future Date Conditions tab.

> **⚠️ Note:** Multi-Tabs added to a FORWARD.DATE set AA property can be displayed. But there is no option of hiding the Future Date Conditions Tabs.


##### Additional Payments

Additional scheduled payments can be included in the PAYMENT.SCHEDULE Property. Additional payment is defined as the payment scheduled over and above the regular payments.

Additional payments can be given by adding a payment type, and it can be either ad hoc (single) or regular and the amount should be specified in the Actual Amt attribute. The system calculates the Calc Amount field taking into account the additional payment(s) specified.

It is possible to have

- Regular additional payment- An additional payment amount is specified on a recurring basis, such as annually. This amount applies over and above the regular installment amount.
- Regular special payment - An actual payment amount is specified for a regular installment. This amount replaces the regular installment amount.
- The additional amount is paid over and above the normal loan installment. When an additional amount is set in a repayment schedule, the remaining instalments are automatically calculated by the system.
- These payments can be in the middle of an Annuity schedule, or a Single Line Amortisation (SLA) schedule (equivalent to Linear payment type). When the payments are added to such a schedule, the payment amount is calculated to take into account the additional payment(s). The below screen shot displays the AA.PRD.DES.PAYMENT.SCHEDULE . The below screen shot displays additional payments every 3 months in the Payment Schedule.


##### Special Payments

Special payment is the actual amount specified by the user to substitute the regular installment amount for the specific period, either single or regular. This amount has to be specified in the Actual Amt attribute. In the example below, it is possible to schedule the Actual Amt for the specified periods, which substitutes the system Calc Amount . In this case, the system calculates the Calc Amount considering the user scheduled Actual Amt .

##### Deferred Payments

The Defer Period attribute in the Payment Schedule Property Class is used to define deferred payments. It defines how long the scheduled payment should be deferred from original cycled date.

- Date Convention - Forward
- Date Adjustment - Period
- Bill is raised on 2nd Feb with Payment Date as 2nd Feb, Actual Pay Date as 1st Feb, Financial Date as 2nd Feb and Defer Date as 8th Feb.
- Defer Date is calculated as 5 days from Actual Pay Date , which is 6th Feb. As it is holiday, the system again applies Date Convention on top of this date. Hence, the value of Defer date in this case is 8th Feb.
- For Defer Activity (processed on 2nd Feb), accounting entries are raised with Value date as Financial Date.
- The MAKEDUE or CAPITALISE Activity is processed on the Defer Date, which is 8th Feb. Here, the accounting entries are moved to nullify DEF entries and raise real statement entries.

- Date Convention - Forward
- Date Adjustment - Value
- Bill is raised on 2nd Feb with Payment Date as 2nd Feb, Actual Pay Date as 1st Feb, Financial Date as 2nd Feb and Defer Date as 8th Feb.
- Defer Date is calculated as 5 days from Actual Pay Date, which is 6th Feb. As it is holiday, it will again apply Date Convention on top of this date. Hence, Defer date in this case is 8th Feb.
- For Defer Activity (processed on 2nd Feb), accounting entries will be raised with Value date as Financial Date.
- The MAKEDUE or CAPITALISE Activity is processed on the Defer Date which is 8th Feb. Here, accounting entries will be moved to nullify DEF entries and raise real statement entries.


##### Installment Amount for Multiple Disbursement

Loans can have the calculated installment amount as a constant (same) amount based on the full principal amount and the accrued interest on the outstanding principal balance. This constant installment amount is the same amount from the first to the final installment amount as per the payment schedule. The Include Future Disb (INCLUDE.PRIN.AMOUNTS) field is set to Yes only when the installment amount is required to be constant from start date until the maturity date of the contract. Any principal disbursement or repayment scheduled in the future is taken into consideration for the calculation of installment.

Given below is an illustration of the loan that has scheduled disbursements with loan installments set for annuity repayment. Here the user has opted for installment calculations to consider future disbursements.

The schedules are built considering the future disbursements as well.

In the below illustration, the scheduled disbursement is planned, but the total outstanding is repaid before the second disbursement. Hence the second installment is a reduced amount to repay the outstanding and third installments is zero. Regular repayments start after the next disbursement is carried out.

When the flag for considering future disbursements is set, the system adjusts the installment amount automatically during loan life cycle stages. For example, change in disbursement dates, disbursement amount or disbursement percentage, interest rate revisions, maturity date change, payment holiday, change in schedules, prepayments, special payments, special schedules like interest only or principal only, tax or charge included installments, capitalisation of dues during overdue, charge-off, write-off.

During the loan takeover from legacy system, the users set this field as yes to calculate the installment amount considering the future disbursements.


##### Residual Principal in Payment Schedule

The residual amount can be set over the life of a loan contract. When set, it is included in the Principal component of the last installment and the Total Due amount is also adjusted to reflect the residual amount along with other scheduled payments.

The schedule projector includes the residual amount against the Total Due and Principal components and the payment schedule enquiry displays the details of each component.

Consider a loan contract with residual amount ($20000) setup. The effective date of the loan is 17-Apr-2019 and the maturity date is 17-Apr-2020.

The Payment Schedule projector is updated with the residual amount against the last installment and it is included in the Total Due amount as well as the Principal component of the installment.

The drill down on the installment detail shows the break-up of the Total Due amount and it includes the residual amount as a separate line item. Further, as the Principal component also includes the residual amount, the same is seen as a separate entry against the Account Property as shown below.

Read the Payment Schedule Property Class for information on the Residual Amount attribute.

##### Partial Capitalisation of Interest Accruals

In an interest bearing arrangement with Annuity payment type, with Due and Cap setup, the actual amount indicated in the Payment Schedule is only made due and any remaining interest accruals is capitalised. This can be a partial or full capitalisation of interest accrual for that period.

For this kind of repayment patterns, The Alt Payment Method field in AA.PAYMENT.TYPE should be set as Due and Cap. In such Payment Types, in the Payment Schedule, the Payment Method should be set as Due and an Actual Amt can be specified. This Actual Amt is made due on the schedule date.

- When the Actual Amt is zero, all the accruals for that period is capitalised.
- When the Actual Amt is more than zero, that amount is made due and any remaining accruals for that period is automatically capitalised due to the principal.

Two separate bills are raised when the accruals are made due and capitalised. The Actual Amt mentioned is made due and follows the overdue cycle for non-repayments. The remaining accruals are capitalised and a capitalised bill is raised for this part.

When the system automatically calculates the instalment amount by itself, a separate set of associated multi-value fields should be defined with the same Payment Type and the Actual Amt should be left blank.


###### Illustration of a Mortgage Loan

In this illustration, there is a mortgage loan with the first two instalments as full capitalisation ( Actual Amt is 0), the next two instalments make the amount as 100 and remaining is capitalised ( Actual Amt is 100).

For this arrangement, there is a schedule built and the interest component with tax is fully capitalised for the first two schedules. The next two schedules have partial capitalisation. The amount 100, mentioned in the Payment Schedule is made due for interest accruals and the corresponding tax is also made due. The remaining accruals for the period and their respective tax component is capitalised to the principal of the arrangement.

When the Payment Type has Tax Inclusive set to No, the tax component is not included in the amount.

Separate bills are raised for the capitalised and the due component of the instalment. The capitalisation component is immediately settled and the actual amount component is made due. The actual amount component is made due for the instalment amount and If the instalment bill is not settled, this instalment bill undergoes ageing based on the overdue configuration

This arrangement also has fully capitalised interest for the first two schedules. The next two schedules have partial capitalisation. In this Payment Type, the Tax Inclusive attribute is set as Yes.

##### Assigning Default Values to Payment Schedule Conditions

It is possible to pre-construct the schedule configurations and set defaults in the Payment Schedule conditions of the arrangement. Banks can offer a unique amortisation plan to customers to repay a specific different percentage of the principal-only repayment over a certain period, for the granted loan amount. This could be tedious to define it every time at the arrangement creation. The option of setting default values to Payment Schedule feature minimises the overwhelming operations maintenance overhead when a unique percentage has to be populated for arrangements without having to repeat them for every arrangement.

### 3.18  Weighted Average Rate


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *When loans are being disbursed in multiple tranches, each having its own interest rate a Weighted Average Rate (WAR) for the arrangement has to be calculated and applied to the contract after each disbursement .*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction


#### 📖 Introduction

When loans are being disbursed in multiple tranches, each having its own interest rate a Weighted Average Rate (WAR) for the arrangement has to be calculated and applied to the contract after each disbursement .

A weighted average interest rate is an average that is adjusted to reflect the contribution of each loan to the total debt. The weighted average multiplies each loan’s disbursement interest rate by the loan balance and divides the sum by the total loan balance. Each loan’s disbursement interest rate contributes to the weighted average in proportion to the loan’s percentage of the total debt.

The Weighted Average Rate Type of Interest condition enables the calculation of the weighted average rate, which determines the actual effective rate of the arrangement.

### 3.19  Capturing Trade Transaction


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *When the trade product is published in the LOAN.TRADE.PRODUCT application, it moves to Loan Trade Product catalogue, where banks can use it to capture a secondary loan trade. Based on the trade requirement, banks can initiate the following three trade transactions:*
> 
> **Applications:** `LOAN.TRADE`, `LOAN.TRADE.BALANCES`, `LOAN.TRADE.PRODUCT`, `LOAN.TRADE.PRODUCT.CATALOG`, `LOAN.TRADE.REPORT`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Activity*, *Actual Settlement Date*, *Additional Info*, *Agent Bank*, *Agent Bank Benf Beneficiary*, *Agent Bank Benf Ccy*, *Agent Bank Benf PO Product*, *Agent Bank’s ID* ... +77 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

When the trade product is published in the LOAN.TRADE.PRODUCT application, it moves to Loan Trade Product catalogue, where banks can use it to capture a secondary loan trade. Based on the trade requirement, banks can initiate the following three trade transactions:

| Trade Transaction Type | Reasons for using Transaction type |
|---|---|
| Buy | When own bank prefers to buy a loan asset either wholly or partially from another lender in the syndication. |
| Sell | When own bank prefers to sell its portion in the syndication (wholly or partially) to another lender (new or existing participant in the syndication). |
| Transfer | When own bank is an agent and is capturing the trade on behalf of the participants. |

Secondary Loan Trading goes through several stages. It begins with the preliminary booking or capturing the trade to its settlement. The LOAN.TRADE application captures, modifies, executes, updates and settles a secondary loan trade.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The system lists the published trade products in the LOAN.TRADE.PRODUCT.CATALOG as shown in the screenshot below.

The system categorizes the products in the catalogue based on the governing body {Ex: Loan Market (EMEA)}. and As per their requirement , banks can initiate a buy, sell or transfer trade.

Temenos releases an activity class in the AA.CLASS.TYPE.ACTIVITY.CLASS application for each type of trade transaction.

Activities are named instances of activity classes. Banks can create their own activities linked to the activity classes to perform a relevant action like NEW-TRADE.BUY activity created to capture a buy trade.


#### 🔧 Working With

A trade can be captured by initiating a buy, sell or a transfer trade under the chosen product. While capturing a trade, it is mandatory to capture the following minimum details:

Counter Party – Counter party is the seller to a buy trade and buyer to a sell trade and both buyer and seller are counter parties to a transfer trade. Counter party ID mentioned here must be a valid customer in Transact.

- When the Trade is a buy trade, the Counter Party must be a seller because the own bank is trying to buy a portion or whole of the trade that is initiated.
- When the Trade is a sell trade, the Counter Party must be a seller because the own bank is trying to sell a portion or whole of the trade that is agreed.
- When the Trade is a transfer trade, the Counter Party must be a valid portfolio because this feature is only used for the trade between the internal portfolios.

Trade Currency - Currency in which the trade is to be captured. The currency mentioned here should be in the allowed list and should not be in the restricted list as per the configuration in the Loan Trade Product.

Transfer Type – Type of trade which can be Internal, Assignment or Sub or Risk Participation.

Trade Amount – Amount of the trade is mandatory.

Title - This is the Title of the underlying loan to be traded mentioned under Credit agreement details tab. This field gets defaulted automatically if the reference of the underlying loan is defined in the Reference field.

Screenshot of a capture of LSTA-PAR buy trade is shown below for reference:

The LOAN.TRADE application captures a secondary loan in Transact. Trade capture involves capturing the necessary details relevant to the trade like trade date, trade currency, trade amount, settlement & pricing details and so on.

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Trade Id | Specifies the system’s unique reference generated for each Trade captured |
| Activity | Specifies the activity which is performed on a trade based on the trade life cycle |
| Alternate Id | Specifies the external system or market reference of a trade in case it originated from an external system. In Transact, it is created as an alternate key for a trade |
| Product | Specifies the trade product or type and based on this, the related fields are defaulted and maintained for a trade. It must be a valid record in LOAN.TRADE.PRODUCT.CATALOG |
| Governing Law | Helps mainly in querying the trade by jurisdiction. It is updated based on trade product selected |
| Type Of Trade | Updated based on trade product selected and could be either par or distressed |
| Transaction Type | Updated based on the activity. The available options are BUY, SELL and TRANSFER |
| Transfer Type | Specifies the type of the transfer for a trade. The available options are Internal Assignment Risk participation Sub participation |
| Counter Party | Specifies the trade counterparty ID. It is a mandatory field, and it must be a valid customer in Transact |
| Counter Party Role | Based on the transaction type, the system defaults the counterparty role upon the validation of the trade. For a buy and sell trade, the counterparties are seller and buyer respectively If the transfer type is trade, then both buyer and seller must be manually defined |
| Trade Currency | Specifies the currency of the trade. It is a mandatory field. The value must be one among the allowed currencies that are defined in the trade product |
| Trade Amount | Specifies the amount of the trade in the trade currency. It is a mandatory field |
| Trade Date | Specifies the date when the trade takes place. It can be the current bank date or back value, but cannot be a forward date. If left blank, the default value is current bank date |
| Booking Date | Maintains the system date on which the trade is captured into the system. It cannot be a forward or back-value date |
| Exp Settle Date | Specifies the date that is set as a standard for each and every trade product. It is configured according to the trade market standards. |
| Actual Settlement Date | Specifies the actual settlement date of the trade and it must be always on or after the Trade Date . Once Exp Settle Date is defined, system automatically defaults the same date to Actual Settlement Date . Users can modify the settlement date using Actual Settlement Date. It is possible to change the Actual Settlement Date to a date beyond or after Exp Settle Date but not beyond the current system date. |
| Participation Type | Specifies one of the following values: Fixed - Does not increase the participant's share on a pro-rata basis when there is an increase in Global commitment Variable – Increases the participant's share on a pro-rata basis when there is an increase in Global commitment. Input is allowed only when Transfer Type is Risk Participation. |
| Status | Specifies the status of a trade. The status available are: Awaiting Confirmation Confirmed Documents Completed Settled Cancelled The system defaults the status and the user cannot change the status manually |
| Notes | Specifies the free text field which records any additional notes or information for the trade. It is non-mandatory |
| Bus Day Centres | Specifies the holiday calendars which are used to determine whether the expected settlement date is a working date or not It is mandatory when settlement happens on a working day The system defaults the Bus Day Centres from the Loan Trade Product when trade currency is defined. The user is allowed to change it only once. Once authorized the Bus day centre cannot be changed |

All the details may not be readily available during the initial stages of trade and so the user can initiate the trade with the barest of details which are mandatory. When the other details are available, the user can update them using the LOAN.TRADE.REPORT enquiry.

> **⚠️ Note:** The system defaults the values which were parameterised for that product in the LOAN.TRADE.PRODUCT application based on the type of trade product the user selects. These values can be modified accordingly during the trade capture.

Once the trade is captured and committed, the ‘ Status ’ of the trade changes to ‘Awaiting Confirmation’.

When the user commits the trade, it can be authorised or deleted in AUTHORISE/DELETE.LOAN.TRADE enquiry from the User Menu. All the authorised trades are available under LOAN.TRADE.REPORT enquiry.


##### Credit Agreement Details Tab

All the details of the underlying loan (Deal or Facility or Drawing) are captured using this tab. Credit agreement is a contract document between the borrower and lenders which contains all the basic details and terms and conditions like borrowing party, amount, currency and so on.

When the user initiates a trade capture using the LOAN.TRADE application, the credit agreement details for the trade are defined using the fields mentioned below.

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Reference | Mention the arrangement ID of a particular deal, facility or drawing in the Reference field to indicate that, it is the loan being traded Instead, a user can mention any relevant reference id in the Reference field and later can create an arrangement and modify with the correct arrangement ID before settlement |
| Title | Indicates the title for the trade and is a mandatory field. It is either automatically defaulted based on the reference ID of the arrangement or user can input the title |
| Borrower’s ID | Specifies the borrower involved in the credit agreement. This can be either left blank or a valid customer ID can be given as an input to automatically default the borrower’s name during trade capture |
| Borrower’s Name | Specifies the borrower’s name When the borrower is a valid customer in transact, then the customer ID of the borrower can be defined in the Borrower’s ID field. The borrower’s name is automatically defaulted upon validation When the Borrower is not a valid customer in transact, Banks can manually key in the Borrower’s name and leave the Borrower’s ID blank |
| Start Date | Specifies the start date of the credit agreement or deal. In case of an existing arrangement, the Start Date is defaulted with Arrangement’s start date |
| Currency | Specifies the currency of the credit agreement or Deal. In case of an existing deal or facility or drawing, the Currency field is defaulted with Arrangement’s currency |
| Amount | Specifies the global amount of the credit agreement or Deal. In case of an existing deal or facility or drawing, the Amount field is defaulted from Arrangement’s term amount property class |
| Agent Bank | Specifies whether the Agent Bank is Own Bank or some other bank If owning bank’s role is Agent/Agent cum Participant, then the user should select Own Bank If owning bank is a participant such as a buyer or a seller, then the user should select Other. When Agent Bank is Other, Agent Bank’s ID and Name should be inputted before the Trade is confirmed |
| Agent Bank’s ID | Specifies the agent bank’s ID If the Agent bank’s ID is available in Transact, Banks can input the ID and Agent bank’s name will be automatically defaulted If Agent bank’s ID is not available, it can be left blank, and the name can be input manually |
| Agent Bank’s Name | Specifies the agent bank’s name for the credit agreement or deal |
| Additional Info | Specifies any additional information of the credit agreement or deal that the system needs to record in a trade |


##### Settlement Instructions Tab

When a loan is traded, during settlement all the transactions like charges, share transfer are made using the beneficiary or account details mentioned in this tab.

Settlement Instructions tab defines the settlement details of the various parties involved in a trade. Depending on the trade type and parties involved in the trade, this tab contains the settlement instructions for

- Counterparty
- Agent Bank
- Own and
- Third parties (if any)

It can be defined or left blank while capturing a new trade. User must fill the necessary details before initiating the trade’s settlement.

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| SSI Party | Specifies the party to the trade (Seller/buyer) based on the transaction type captured. Other third parties like broker can also be defined |
| SSI Ccy | Specifies the currency to which the settlement instruction refers to. Different currencies can be defined for one party |
| SSI Product | Specifies the payment order product or payment channel to which the settlement instruction refers to. It must be a valid payment order product |
| SSI Beneficiary | Specifies the account details of the settlement party. It must be a valid record in BENEFICIARY table |
| Agent Beneficiary | Specifies the beneficiary details of the agent bank |
| Agent Ccy | Specifies the currency specific beneficiary account of the agent bank |
| Agent PO Product | Specifies the payment order product or payment channel for the transfer of funds to the Agent. It must be a valid Payment Order Product |
| Own Bank Account No | Specifies the owning bank's Nostro account for the currency specified. Currency of the account should match with the currency of the Nostro account. If Nostro accounts are not specified, then the system will use the Nostro Account table to pick the Nostro account for the settlement |
| Own Bank Ccy | Specifies a valid currency for which the Nostro account attached |
| Own Bank PO Product | Defines the Pay in payment order product |

> **⚠️ Note:** When Agent Bank is given as Own Bank, then the system declines the settlement instructions for agent as input and throws an error. For Buy or Sell trade, SSI Party can only be Seller or Buyer respectively.


##### Third Party Consents Tab

A credit agreement usually contains the terms and conditions for secondary loan trading, which includes whether transfer of ownership is allowed for a credit agreement. That is, whether the assignment form of transfer is allowed for a credit agreement, and the various consents needed for the same.

This tab is used to capture whether the required consents are received to settle a trade as per the credit agreement.

The fields available in this Tab are as follows:

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Consent Type | Specifies the type of consent, which is mandatory for the trade. It is a no-input field and is defaulted from Participant property class of the arrangement being traded. |
| Consent Party | Specifies the party or parties whose consent is mandatory for a share transfer. The options available in this field are, BORROWER AGENT It is a no-input field and defaulted from Participant property class. |
| Consent Given | Specifies the status of consent. The options available are Yes and No. |
| Consent Date | Specifies the date when the consent is provided. |

The user captures an LMA-Par buy trade(Assignment) for 1 Million, where the minimum trade amount is USD 250,000. The user should obtain consent from the borrower and the agent and settlement details are provided as below:

- Creating a new facility and configuring the Participant Property class to allow trade and defining minimum trade amount, commit, and authorise the new facility.

- Capturing the LMA-Par buy trade and mentioning the existing Facility ID for reference in credit agreement tab.

> **⚠️ Note:** Only the Title , Trade Currency and Counterparty are mandatory.

When the reference ID is defined and validated, the system defaults all the relevant credit agreement details automatically. If the reference ID is not linked to a valid Deal/Facility ID before settlement, the system will throw an error during settlement.

- Defining the Standard Settlement Instructions for the Seller and Agent.

- Updating the Consent Type and Consent Date for the Assignment trade.

> **⚠️ Note:** Consent Type and Consent Party are automatically defaulted from the Participant property class.

- Logging in using Authoriser credentials and authorising the trade.

- Viewing the authorised trade in LOAN.TRADE.REPORT enquiry.


##### Capturing Trade Details Tab

This tab captures the details of the underlying loans of a trade including,

- The details of the deal, facility, or the drawings that are traded
- Whether the loans are traded at a premium, discount or at par
- The drawn and undrawn portions of the commitment amounts.

The Trade Details tab also captures other details of the trade such as Allow BoCR , Allow Netback and Settlement Option .

The user must provide the master arrangement which can be a deal, facility, or a drawing, in the Reference field under the Credit Agreement Details tab to define the facility or drawing arrangements which are being traded. The facility or drawing mentioned in the Trade Ac field should belong to the master arrangement mentioned in the Reference field.

If a deal is mentioned in Reference , then all the facilities under the deal is listed in the Trade Ac . If a standalone facility is mentioned in Reference , then the same facility is listed in Trade Ac . and if a standalone drawing is mentioned in the Reference , the same drawing is listed in the Trade Ac .

Once the user defines and validates the Trade Ac field, the system defaults all the arrangements under it to Loan Ac along with the Nature , Ccy , Tot Trade Amt , Drawn and Undrawn amounts of the arrangements in a chronological order.

While the system attaches the existing arrangements in Transact, arrangements which are Expired, Matured, Closed or Pending Closure, cancelled and new offer status cannot be defined in Trade Ac .

The user can capture a trade initially by just defining the Commitment without mentioning Trade Ac and Loan Ac under it. Later, when the user creates the underlying arrangements, it is possible to attach the same. The user can modify Trade Ac of a trade before entering value in Exp Settle Days , and authorise the trade. However, once the value is entered in Exp Settle Days and authorised, the Trade Ac cannot be changed.

The system automatically calculates and populates the value in Share Percent based on the Commitment amount for each Trade Ac individually. Once Share Percent is calculated, the system automatically calculates the total trade, drawn, and undrawn amounts for all the underlying Loan Ac and populates the values in the appropriate fields.

The user captures an LMA-PAR Sell trade, where Bank A is holding USD 10 Million, which is tradeable and sells USD 3 Million out of it to Bank B.

Three Facilities are traded with USD 1 million each, which makes the share as 10% each (1Million/10Million). Based on the calculated share percent, the system defaults 10% of the drawn amount of the existing facility and its underlying drawings automatically to ‘Drawn’ and 10% of the undrawn amount of the existing facility and its underlying drawings is automatically defaulted to ‘Undrawn’.

If the trade is a Buy trade, and the buyer is a ‘New Buyer’, then the user must attach ‘Memo arrangements’ to the trade and the system defaults the value of Tot trade Amt entirely to Undrawn amount. The user is allowed to change the value of Drawn and Undrawn amounts manually any time before the settlement of the trade.

The screenshotS below shows the record before and after attaching the reference arrangement respectively.

Refer to the Working with Share Transfer section for more information on how to create a ‘Memo arrangement’.

Following are the fields available in Trade Details Tab.

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Price | Specifies the price applicable to the entire trade. The values can be entered from 0.01 to 999.99. For trade priced more than 100 is referred as Premium Trade and for a trade priced less than 100 is referred as discounted Trade. For Transfer type trade, it is automatically defaulted to 100. It cannot take a value greater than or less than 100. |
| Share Percent | Specifies the percentage of share a participating bank is selling from this share, or a new buyer is buying from the global amount. The system automatically updates this field only when Exp Settle Date is input. Bank A sells USD 3 Million out of total amount USD 10 Million eligible to sell. The share percent is updated as 30. Bank B is an Agent cum Participant and buys USD 3 Million from Bank A who is an existing participant. The total amount available for trading with Bank A is USD 10 Million. The share percent is updated as 30. Bank A is a new buyer who buys USD 2 Million in a syndication of USD 10 Million, the share percent is 20. |
| Settlement Option | Specifies the method of final settlement between the buyer and seller. The allowed options are: Net – Settlement happens after netting all amount that is payable to and receivable from the counter party. Gross – Settlement happens without netting the payable and receivable amount. Counterparty account is credited for the total payable amount and debited for the total receivable amounts. By default, the option is ‘Net’ |
| Allow Netback | Specifies whether to calculate the net back amount for the undrawn amount based on the Price field. |
| Allow BoCR | Specifies whether to calculate the benefit of Commitment Reduction if applicable. |
| Trade Ac | Specifies the Facility or the Drawings that is being traded. The system shows all the available arrangements under the Reference field in Credit Agreement Details tab is defined in Trade Ac . If a deal is linked in the Reference field, this field becomes a drop down displaying all the facilities under that deal. If a facility or drawing is linked in the Reference field, this field becomes a drop down displaying the linked facility or drawing. This becomes a read-only field once the user provides a value in Exp Settle Date and authorises the same. |
| Commitment | Specifies the amount being traded under a facility or drawing that is provided in the trade account. This is an associated field to Trade Ac and if user has selected any arrangement in Trade Ac , this field becomes mandatory. The system allows the user to give input without trade account as well. The sum of the Commitment of all the Trade Ac cannot be greater than the value in ‘Trade Amount’ provided in the LOAN.TRADE application. |
| New Buyer | Specifies whether the buying counterparty to the trade is a new Lender. The system updates this field and the user cannot check or uncheck this field manually. The system checks whether the ‘Buy-Counterparty’ is available in the provided Trade Ac . If the counterparty is already available, it means that the buyer is an existing participant. If the counterparty is not available in the Trade Ac , it means that the buyer is a new buyer and system automatically checks the New Buyer field. If New Buyer is selected and the trade is a ‘Buy’ trade, then the values of Drawn and Undrawn is not automatically defaulted and must be manually entered by the user. |
| Issue Pricing | This field helps to inform the bank user when a pricing letter needs to be issued or when it needs to be re-issued due to changes in trade balances or settlement amount. If this field is checked, the system does not allow the user to settle the trade. It is a no-input field when Trade type is Transfer. Once the trade is executed and ready for settlement, the responsible party (seller or buyer) must issue the pricing letter, which contains the settlement amount and all the details of the underlying loans being traded. When there is any change in the settlement amount, the pricing letter is re-issued. If this field is checked by the system, it indicates that the pricing letter is yet to be issued or the pricing letter is to be re-issued due to the changes in the settlement amount. The user can proceed to settle the trade by one of the following options: Issue or re-issue the pricing letter using ISSUE.PRICING-TRADE activity Disable the Issue Pricing field to override and proceed for settlement |
| Loan Ac | Specifies the facility or the Drawings that is being traded. Once the user defines the Trade Ac and validates the trade, all the facilities and drawings under the underlying asset mentioned in Trade Ac are defaulted in a chronological manner. The system updates this field and user cannot input values manually. |
| Nature | Specifies the account’s nature or product to which the selected Loan Ac belongs. For example, Term Facility Libor Drawing Once the user defines Loan Ac , the system updates this field automatically and user input is restricted. |
| Ccy | Specifies the currency of the account. This is a read-only field and once the user defines Loan Ac , the system updates this field automatically. |
| Tot Trade Amt | Specifies the total commitment amount being traded. Based on the value in Share Percent , the system calculates the pro-rated value for the underlying Loan Accounts and auto-populates this field. |
| Drawn | Drawn amount is shown for every Loan Ac , If Drawn is shown for a facility, it specifies the trading portion of utilized commitment in the facility by the underlying drawings. If Drawn is shown for a Drawing, it represents the principal amount of the drawing. This is an auto-populated read-only field. If the trade is a buy trade and New Buyer is checked, then the system allows the manual input |
| Undrawn | Specifies the trading portion of unutilized commitment in the facility or the drawing. This is an auto-populated read-only field. If the trade is a buy trade and New Buyer is checked, then the system allows the manual input. |


###### Storing Trade Balances inLOAN.TRADE.BALANCES

LOAN.TRADE.BALANCES is a live application that records the trading position of a trade from the date on which the underlying loan accounts are linked and the expected settlement date is finalized and provided. It contains the details of all loan accounts and its trading amount under each drawing. The users can update or amend the trade details using the AMEND.COMMITMENT-TRADE activity.

The user can define the Trade Details tab

- Either during the trade capture and modify it later.
- Or after the system captures the trade using the AMEND.COMMITMENT-TRADE activity.

Whenever the user amends or updates the Trade details, the system recalculates the values in LOAN.TRADE.BALANCES application and stores it.

Refer to the Managing Trade- Working With section- Amend Commitment for more information on AMEND.COMMITMENT-TRADE activity.

The following are the fields available in the LOAN.TRADE.BALANCES application:

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Price | Defaulted from LOAN.TRADE application |
| Txn Date | Specifies the date on which the system updates the LOAN.TRADE.BALANCES application. If there is any amendment of trade details, the system creates a new record with the date of amendment as Txn Date |
| Loan Ac | Defaulted from LOAN.TRADE application |
| Name | Defaulted from LOAN.TRADE application |
| Nature | Defaulted from LOAN.TRADE application |
| Ccy | Defaulted from LOAN.TRADE application |
| FX Rate | Specifies the rate applied on Drawings if facility currency is different from Drawings. A facility and its underlying drawings can be in different currencies. System uses ‘FX rate’ as the exchange rate to convert all the drawings in the same currency which is the facility’s currency as well |
| Tot Trade Amt | Defaulted from LOAN.TRADE application |
| Drawn | Defaulted from LOAN.TRADE application |
| Undrawn | Defaulted from LOAN.TRADE application |
| Premium/Discount | Specifies the value of the loan for the drawn amount at the given price. The system updates this field when the Transaction Type is BUY or SELL. The system calculates the premium or discount only after the trade is ‘Executed’ using EXECUTE-TRADE activity |
| Netback | Netback is the compensation given by the counterparty on the undrawn amount of the loan being traded when the loan is bought or sold at discount or premium. The system performs the following: Calculates the value of this field based on the undrawn portion of the Facility or drawings. Calculates the netback amount and auto-populates this field, only when it is agreed in the trade agreement and the Allow Netback field is checked. Updates this field when the Transaction Type is BUY or SELL. Calculates netback only after the trade is ‘Executed’ using EXECUTE-TRADE activity |
| BoCR | The system calculates and updates the value of this field at the Facility level, Only when there is permanent reduction of commitment or prepayment of principal by the borrowed from trade date to settlement date (inclusive of both). The user must check the Allow BoCR field. When the Transaction Type is BUY or SELL. Only after the trade is ‘Executed’ using EXECUTE-TRADE activity. This is an auto-populated read-only field |
| Net Settlement | Specifies the net settlement amount related to the Facility or drawings. The system calculates the net settlement amount and updates this field, When the Transaction Type is BUY or SELL. Only after the trade is ‘Executed’ using EXECUTE-TRADE activity. This is an auto-populated read-only field |

Based on the Share Percentage and the Commitment amount, the system lists the underlying drawings of the facilities in a chronological order in Loan Ac along with the pro-rated values of drawn and undrawn amounts.
- The user commits and authorises the trade.

This enquiry displays the list of loan trade records that are pending for authorisation. The user can authorise, edit, delete, or view the unauthorised records.

To view the loan trade records, follow the below steps:

1. Authorise/ Edit/ Delete Loan Trade .
2. In the Unauthorised Loan Trade – Summary screen, click the View option corresponding to a record to view the details of loan trade. The Create Trade screen displays the record in view mode.

To edit the loan trade records, follow the below steps:

1. Authorise/ Edit/ Delete Loan Trade .
2. In the Unauthorised Loan Trade – Summary screen, click the Edit option corresponding to a record.
3. In the Create Trade Screen, enter values in the required fields to be amended
4. In the Credit Agreement Details section, enter values in the required fields to be amended.
5. In the Settlement Instructions section, enter values in the required fields to be amended.
6. In the Third Party Consent section, enter values in the required fields to be amended.
7. In the Loan Trade Charges section, enter values in the required fields to be amended.
8. In the Trade Details section, enter values in the required fields to be amended.
9. Click the Validate icon to check for errors and overrides.
10. Click the Commit icon.
11. Accept the overrides, if any.

To authorise the loan trade records, follow the below steps:

1. Authorise/ Edit/ Delete Loan Trade .
2. In the Unauthorised Loan Trade – Summary screen, click the Authorise option corresponding to a record.
3. In the Create Trade screen, verify the details and then click the Authorise icon. The record is authorised.

To delete the loan trade records, follow the below steps:

1. Authorise/ Edit/ Delete Loan Trade .
2. In the Unauthorised Loan Trade – Summary screen, click the Delete option corresponding to a record.
3. In the Create Trade screen, click the Delete icon.

#### ⚙️ Configuration

This section details how the user can create loans with internal portfolios in Arrangement Architecture before capturing the trade in the LOAN.TRADE application.

Read Internal Portfolio Allocation in Facility for creating the facility with portfolios.


#### 🔧 Working With

This section details Secondary Loan Trading (SLT) with the internal portfolio allocation in a syndicated loan. The below are the scenarios which involve share transfers that can be made in a portfolio.

- Internal Transfer between Portfolios
- Sub-Participation Transfer (Portfolio: Buy)
- Participant Transfer (Portfolio: Sell)


##### Internal Transfer between Portfolios (Portfolio: Transfer)

In an internal portfolio transfer, the amount is transferred from one portfolio to another. The following is an example of an internal transfer between portfolios.

In this scenario, the own bank’s share is funded by three portfolios as shown in the below example. Portfolio 1001 buys from Portfolio 1002.

Create a deal for USD 10M and a facility for USD 2M with two participants of USD 500T each, set the bank’s role as agent cum participant with the portfolio allocated as below.

- Portfolio 1001 - USD 300T
- Portfolio 1002 - USD 300T

### 3.21  Loan Trade Products


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The Secondary Loan Trading (SLT) module involves the trade of syndicated loans in the secondary loan market by primary lenders or the subsequent purchasers to,*
> 
> **Applications:** `AC.ALLOCATION.RULE`, `CATEGORY`, `LOAN.TRADE.CHARGE.CONDITIONS`, `LOAN.TRADE.PRODUCT`, `LOAN.TRADE.PRODUCT.CATALOG`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Action*, *Activity ID*, *Allowed Ccy*, *Allowed ccy*, *Bus Day Centers*, *Category*, *Charge Name*, *Closure Days* ... +24 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

The Secondary Loan Trading (SLT) module involves the trade of syndicated loans in the secondary loan market by primary lenders or the subsequent purchasers to,

- Manage their loan portfolios more efficiently
- Deleverage their balance sheets for regulatory reasons
- Maximise shareholder value
- Sell a stressed loan

In Transact, secondary loan trading can be captured in various currencies. The allowed and restricted currencies along with the governing body for a trade can be controlled using the LOAN.TRADE.PRODUCT application. Depending on the agreement between buyer and seller, a loan is traded at par or distressed value.

- Par trade occurs when loans are traded at or very near to the face value.
- Distressed trade occurs when the loans that are traded are much below the face value because they are unlikely to be repaid in full. Generally, non-performing loans are treated as a distressed trade.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

Create Loan Trade Product to access this catalogue. The trade products allow banks or financial institutions to pre-define certain trade conditions which the system defaults when a new trade is captured using the said trade product in the LOAN.TRADE.PRODUCT application. The following fields are available in the LOAN.TRADE.PRODUCT application:

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Short Desc | Specifies the short description of the trade type |
| Full Desc | Specifies the full description of the trade type. |


##### Default Values Tab

Users can define the basic features of the trade, such as the type of trade, governing body, and the allowed or restricted trade currencies in this tab.

The following are the fields in this tab.

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Type Of trade | Specifies the type of trade being performed. The types available are: Par – For capturing a par trade Distressed – For capturing a distressed trade |
| Governing Law | Specifies the trade’s governing body. The allowed options are: LMA – Loan Market (EMEA) LSTA – Loan Market (America) APMLA - Loan Market (Asia and Pacific) Others – Loan Market (Others) |
| Trade Currency (allowed) | Specifies the list of currencies in which the trade is allowed. Helps banks to control the list of currencies in which loans can be traded. When a currency is added or removed and the product is published, then all the new trades follow the updated setup. If currency is not defined in allowed or restricted currency, it means that trade is allowed in all the currencies. The values in the Allowed Ccy and Restricted Ccy fields are mutually exclusive where either value can be defined. |
| Trade Currency (restricted) | Specifies the list of currencies in which the trade cannot be performed. Helps banks to control the list of currencies in which loans can be traded. When a currency is added or removed and the product is published, then all the new trades follow the updated setup. The values in the Allowed ccy and Restricted Ccy fields are mutually exclusive, that is, if users define any value in one field, they cannot define any value in another field. |
| Closure Days | Specifies the number of days after which the trade records in CANCELLED or SETTLED status are moved to history for the product. |
| Category | Specifies the category code under which the profit and loss entries are raised for the product. The value must be in the range of 35001-35010 and a valid record in the CATEGORY application. |


##### Control Tab

This tab allows banks and financial institutions to define the default Settlement Days for different currencies and define the holiday calendars to calculate Settlement Days automatically based on the common working days of the business units.

The following are fields in this tab:

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Settlement Currency | Specifies the trade currency for which the default Settlement Days is specified while creating the product |
| Settlement Days | Specifies the default Settlement Days for a trade. When a trade is captured using this product, the system uses this value to calculate and default the expected settlement date for a trade, that is, the value 10W indicates the settlement date as T+10 working days where T is the trade date. This field is a mandatory when the Settlement Currency is specified. |
| Bus Day Centers | Specifies the region wise holiday calendars which determines the expected settlement date based on the Settlement Days defined. This field can be multivalued to define multiple calendars for a single trade currency. This field is a mandatory field when Settlement Days is specified in working days. |


##### Charges Tab

This tab is used to configure charges for various trade activities like capturing a new trade, updating the trade, amending the trade commitment and so on.

The Activity ID field captures the activity for which a charge should be levied.

The Charge Name field captures the charge condition, which should be a valid charge record from the LOAN.TRADE.CHARGE.CONDITIONS application. It is also possible to levy multiple charges for the same activity by sub valuing this field. Once the product is published and an activity is triggered, the system defaults the charge if it is configured in the LOAN.TRADE.PRODUCT application. Read Working with Trade Charges for more details on charges.


##### Accounting Tab

The Accounting tab in the LOAN.TRADE.PRODUCT application enables the user to configure the accounting conditions for income and expenses arising out of a trade.

The following fields in the Accounting tab helps the user to set the accounting conditions for income and expenses for a trade.

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Inc Premium Sale | Specifies the PL category to which the income of the premium sale is to be credited. If the value is set as amort, this field specifies the charge property under which the amount is parked. The value must be a valid ID in LOAN.TRADE.CHARGE.CONDITIONS with type as ‘Receive’. |
| Inc Discounted Purchase | Specifies the PL category to which the income of discounted purchase to be credited. If the value is set as amort, this field specifies the charge property under which the income to be posted. The value must be a valid ID in LOAN.TRADE.CHARGE.CONDITIONS with type as ‘Receive’. |
| Exp Premium Purchase | Specifies the PL category from which the expense of the premium purchase to be debited. If the value is set as amort, specifies the charge property under which the amount is parked. The value must be a valid ID in LOAN.TRADE.CHARGE.CONDITIONS with type as ‘Pay’. |
| Exp Discounted Sale | Specifies the PL category to which expense of the premium sale to be debited. If the value is set as amort, this field specifies the charge property under which the amount is parked. The value must be a valid ID in LOAN.TRADE.CHARGE.CONDITIONS with type as ‘Pay’. |
| Rule Id | Specifies the rule for accounting entries generated after the settlement of a trade. The value must be a valid record in AC.ALLOCATION.RULE . |


##### Publish Tab

Once the product in the LOAN.TRADE.PRODUCT application is configured using the Default Values, Control and Charges tabs, it needs to be published to move the product to LOAN.TRADE.PRODUCT.CATALOG . Any amendments made in a product is reflected in the product catalog only after it is published

Once the product is published here, the product moves to the LOAN.TRADE.PRODUCT.CATALOG . The following fields of the Publish Tab helps the user to control and modify the products available in the product catalogue.

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Effective Date | Specifies the date from which the current product is available in the trade product catalogue to capture a trade. This field is defaulted automatically to the system date when the product is published. |
| Expiry Date | Specifies the date from when this product ceases to exist or suspended. New trades cannot be initiated under the product after this date. After expiry, the product is not available in the catalogue. Users can input current and future dates. Once expired, the product cannot be modified or amended. |
| Action | Users can publish the product using the option Publish in this field. Transact validates whether all the mandatory input fields are defined when the user publishes the product. Once the product is published, it is listed in LOAN.TRADE.PRODUCT.CATALOG . |


#### 📋 Tasks

The Secondary Loan Trading (SLT) module involves the trade of syndicated loans in the secondary loan market by primary lenders. The secondary loan trading can be captured in various currencies. The LOAN.TRADE.PRODUCT application controls the allowed and restricted currencies along with the governing body for a trade.

In Loan Trade Products, the user can perform the following activities:

| Loan Trade Product | Enter Loan Trade Product Name ID and click the Edit icon. |
| Loan Trade Product | Enter values in the following fields: Short Desc Full Desc In the Default Values section, enter values in the following fields: Type of Trade Governing Law Trade Ccy (Allowed) Trade Ccy (Restricted) Closure Days In the Control section, enter values in the following fields: Trade Ccy Settlement Days Bus Day Centers In the Charges section, enter values in the following fields: Activity ID Charge Name In the Accounting section, enter values in the following fields: Inc-Premium Sale Inc-Discounted Purchase Exp-Premium Purchase Exp-Discounted Sale In the Publish section, enter values in the following fields: Action Expiry Date Click the Validate icon to check for errors and overrides. Click the Commit icon. Accept the overrides, if any. |

### 3.22  Managing Trade


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
>

Once the trade is captured, the trade status is awaiting confirmation, and when the trading parties confirm the trade, the trade moves to the conf...*
> 
> **Applications:** `AA.PROPERTY`, `AC.ALLOCATION.RULE`, `AC.BALANCE.TYPE`, `LOAN.TRADE`, `LOAN.TRADE.BALANCES`, `LOAN.TRADE.CHARGE.CONDITIONS`, `LOAN.TRADE.CHARGES`, `PAYMENT.ORDER`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Actual Settlement Date*, *Actual settlement date*, *Allow
										Netback*, *Allow BoCR*, *Allow Netback*, *Amort Property*, *BoCR*, *Bus Day Centres* ... +46 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

A trade is initially captured with the minimum details such as trade type (buy, sell, or transfer), trade amount, counterparty, transfer type, and so on. Once the trade is captured, the trade status is awaiting confirmation, and when the trading parties confirm the trade, the trade moves to the confirmed status.

When the trade is in awaiting confirmation or confirmed status, if required, the user can sub-allocate a sell trade to new buyers without canceling the original trade. When a sell trade is sub-allocated, the system automatically creates the child trades and the original parent trade cannot be further modified or settled. The child trades created can be executed and settled manually on different settlement dates to different buyers.

Before sending the pricing letter, the bank validates the correctness of the trade and the underlying loan trade balances by executing the trade using execute trade activity. Once the trade is executed, the status moves to awaiting settlement, and the user issues a pricing letter, which contains the loan and the counterparty settlement amount details.

For an assignment type of trade, if the credit agreement explicitly states to obtain consent from the borrower or agent, it is mandatory for the user to record the consent details using update consent trade activity. An assignment trade cannot be settled without obtaining the necessary consent. However, the user can convert an assignment type of trade to sub-participation using update trade activity, if the consent from the borrower or agent cannot be obtained.

On the settlement date, the user manually settles the trade to adjust the books and remit the balances to the counterparty. The Pending Settlement Trade enquiry is used to view and settle the trades awaiting settlement.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

To validate the trade balances, to sub-allocate a trade and to settle a trade, the following service /configurations must be initiated at the backend.


##### Accounting Configuration

A charge which is attached to a trade can be posted to the profit and loss account of the bank directly or can be set to amortise over the maturity of the underlying loan. Read Configuring Trade Charges to know how to create a charge condition in secondary loan trading.

Similarly, the income or expenses arising from a trade can be posted to the profit and loss account of the bank directly or can be set to amortise over the maturity of the underlying loan. Read Working with Loan Trade Products to know how to create an accounting condition in secondary loan trading and how to attach the accounting condition to the product.

The user creates a valid property in AA and provides the property as Amort Property in SLT to amortise a charge or income or expense. To configure accounting for amortisation of charges and income or expense from a trade in AA:


###### Step 1

Set the Property Type field to Non Customer and Credit for a payable charge and expenses. Set the Property Type field to Non Customer and Debit for a receivable charge and income. For example, if you have a fee in SLT with TRANSFERFEE, which is set to amortise, then you can create a new property as TRANSFERFEE in the AA.PROPERTY application as shown in the below screenshot.

> **⚠️ Note:** A charge condition must be created in loan trade charge conditions along with amort property. The property created in AA.PROPERTY must be the same as defined in the Amort Property field in the LOAN.TRADE.CHARGE.CONDITIONS application.


###### Step 2

Once a new property is created for the charge, add the charge property in the accounting product condition ( AA.PRD.DES.ACCOUNTING ) of the Facility and Drawings under which the charge is to be amortised and configure the condition as shown in the below screenshot.


###### Step 3

Once the charge is added to the product condition as mentioned above, configure a new event type CHARGE-TRADE.AMORT-ACC in the AC.ALLOCATION.RULE application as shown in the below screenshot.


###### Step 4

Create ACC BALANCE TYPE for the charge (TRANSFERFEE) in the AC.BALANCE.TYPE application as shown in the below screenshot.

> **⚠️ Note:** For both charges and income or expenses on account of premium or discount trades, the above setup is required to amortise the same in the underlying loan.


#### 🔧 Working With

Managing Trade capture includes activities such as updating trade, amending commitment, and so on, by choosing the relevant options in Loan Trade Report enquiry.

Below are the various activities that can be performed as part of managing a trade after it is created.

Banks and financial institutions can update or modify the relevant trade details when those are available or negotiated. The UPDATE-TRADE activity is used to update or modify the loan trade details after it has been captured. Users can update a trade by selecting the ‘Update trade’ option from the list of drill-down options available in the following enquiry screens - Loan Trade Report, Pending Confirmation trade, or Pending Documentation trade.

The Exp Settle Date field in the LOAN.TRADE application is optional and can be defined later during the Update Trade activity. However, once it is defined and authorised, it cannot be amended again. Similarly, the Bus Day Centres field cannot be amended once the Exp Settle Date is set. It can be amended before the expected settlement date is fixed.

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Trade Amount | Specifies the total trade amount that is to be traded. During amendment, it can be increased or decreased. |
| Price | Specifies the trade price in percentage. If the price is not defined while capturing the trade, it can be defined later using Amend Commitment Trade activity. Once the price is defined, it cannot be changed. |
| Settlement Option | Settlement Option (Net/Gross) can be amended during the Amend Commitment activity . |
| Allow Netback | Specifies Allow Netback (Yes/No). It can be checked or unchecked during the Amend Commitment activity. |
| Allow BoCR | Specifies if the BoCR needs to be calculated. It can be checked or unchecked during the Amend Commitment activity. |
| Trade Ac | Specifies the Facility or the Drawings that is being traded. It can be amended during the Amend Commitment activity if Exp Settlement Date is not defined yet. It becomes a no-change field if expected settlement date is already defined. |
| Commitment | Specifies the amount being traded under a facility or drawing that is provided in the trade account. Commitment can be increased or decreased during Amend Commitment. The sum of all the Trade Commitment cannot exceed Trade Amount . |

Banks can update the third-party consent details required to perform an assignment trade using the UPDATE.CONSENT-TRADE activity. The user can select the Record Consent option available in the enquiries under secondary loan trading and update or amend the Consent Given and Consent Date fields for trades with Transfer Type as Assignment and Consent Required (defined in Participant Property Class) as Yes.

This option is available once a valid deal, facility, or arrangement reference is defined under the Credit Agreement Details tab in Secondary Loan Trading, where Consent Required is set as Yes. If a valid arrangement is not defined in the Reference field under the Credit Agreement Details tab, the user cannot trigger this activity.

Once the terms and conditions for a trade are finalised with the counterparty (buyer or seller), users can confirm the trade using the CONFIRM-TRADE activity. Once the trade is confirmed, the status of the trade automatically changes to ‘Confirmed’ from ‘Awaiting Confirmation’.

Confirm Trade option is available in Loan Trade Report and Pending Confirmation Trades enquiry under Secondary Loan Trading.

If the Agent bank details are mandatory for Trade Confirmation, the system throws an error if the same is not updated.

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Buyer | Indicates the buyer to whom the trade is to sub-allocated. |
| Trade Ac Ref | Indicates the loan which is sub-allocated. The value provided must be one of the loans which are attached to the parent trade in Trade Ac . All loans mentioned in the Trade Ac field must be sub-allocated. |
| Buyer Share | Specifies the commitment amount which is to be sub-allocated to each buyer for each loan. The sum of all the values defined in the Buyer Share field must be equal to the total value defined in the Commitment field defined at the parent trade. |
| Linked Trade | Specifies the child trade IDs which are automatically created by the system. |

|  | Total Amount | Available Amount | Utilized Amount | Total Amount for sale | Tot Trade Amt (50%) | Undrawn | Drawn | Netback |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Facility | 100000 | 35000 | 65000 | 100000 | 50000 | 17500 | 32500 | -1750 |
| Drawings | 70000 | 5000 | 65000 | 70000 | 35000 | 2500 | 32500 | 0 |

The Pricing letter consists of all the information related to the trade settlement and states the amount to be transferred between the trading counterparties as of the settlement date.

In most cases, the seller of the position provides the Pricing letter, but there are exceptions where the buying bank can also provide the Pricing letter if the selling counterparty is a fund.

Once the expected settlement date is agreed upon between the trading parties and the trade is executed, the user generates the Pricing letter for the trading counterparties to agree on or before the settlement completion by triggering the Issue Pricing activity. The seller or the buyer of the trade issues the Pricing letter to the counterparty, as shown below.

When the user executes the trade and the trade status is ‘Awaiting Settlement’, the seller or the buyer issues the Pricing letter through the ISSUE.PRICING.TRADE activity. Like other activities, ISSUE.PRICING.TRADE is available as a drop-down option in Loan Trade Report enquiry and Pending Settlement Trades enquiry for all trades in ‘Awaiting Settlement’ status.

To preview the Pricing letter, the user can navigate to Loan Trade Report enquiry and select View Pricing Advice from the list of options.

When the Issue Pricing is completed and authorised, the system generates the Pricing letter, which the bank sends to the counterparty.

Before authorising, the user can click the icon to preview the Pricing letter. A sample Pricing letter is shown below:

Between Trade date and Actual settlement date , there can be a change in the balances in the underlying Trade Ac or Loan Ac due to any other financial activity like principal prepayment or further loan disbursement.

In such a case, the actual balances of the loans and the balances captured in the trade can differ. As mentioned in the configuration section above, the bank must run the LOAN.TRADE.SERVICE service at the Start of Day (SOD) to update the trades with the latest balances. This service updates the trade only once a day. The lender has to re-issue the Pricing letter for all the trades that are impacted due to changes in balances. Whenever there is a change in the balance after the service is run, the system automatically updates Issue Pricing as ‘Yes’ in LOAN.TRADE .

> **⚠️ Note:** The lender can query the trades that need re-issue of the Pricing letter from the Loan Trade Report enquiry by setting Issue Pricing to ‘Yes’ as the selection criteria.

Issue Pricing is enabled in LOAN.TRADE when the user tries to settle the trade. If the field is marked as Yes, the user must issue or re-issue the Pricing letter as explained above to continue to settle the trade. In case the user is not the responsible party for the issuance of the Pricing letter, then the user can manually uncheck the field to proceed to settle the trade.

A trade can be cancelled any time before settlement. To cancel a trade, the user can click the Cancel Trade option and trigger the CANCEL-TRADE activity from the secondary loan trade enquiries. The user can enter the reason for cancelling the trade in the Notes field. Once the cancel-trade activity is authorised, the trade status is changed to Cancelled.

| Enquiry | Report |
|---|---|
| Authorise/Edit/Delete Loan Trade | Allows to view, edit, authorise, or delete unauthorised trade records. |
| Loan Trade Report | Lists the authorised trades. The banks can record the trade consent, view, update, update consent, confirm, execute, issue pricing, settle, or cancel a trade from this enquiry. |
| Pending Confirmation Trades | Lists the trades in the ‘Awaiting Confirmation’ status. The banks can record the trade consent, view, update, confirm, or cancel a trade from this enquiry. Once the trade is confirmed, the user can view it under the Pending Documentation enquiry. |
| Confirmed trades | Lists the trades that are in the ‘Confirmed’ status. The banks can record the trade consent, view, update, execute, or cancel the trade from this enquiry. |
| Pending consent | Lists the trades for which the third-party consents are not yet obtained as mentioned in the credit agreement. The banks can view, record the trade consent, update, execute, or cancel the trade from this enquiry. |
| Pending Documentation Trades | Lists the trades in the ‘Confirmed’ status but with incomplete documentation. The banks can record the trade consent, view, update or cancel a trade from this enquiry. |
| Pending settlement trades | Lists the trades that are executed and ready for settlement in the ‘Awaiting settlement’ status. The banks can view, record the trade consent, update, execute, issue pricing, settle or cancel the trade from this enquiry. |
| Settled trades | Lists the settled trades. The banks can view all the settled trades from this enquiry. |
| Loan Trades Booked Today | Lists the trades booked on that day (the booking date is the system date). |

To understand Trade Management in secondary loan trading, consider the following scenario:

12. Select the Settle Trade activity from the Loan Trade Report enquiry and authorise the trade after the Pricing letter is issued.

#### 📋 Tasks

After a trade is captured with minimum details and the participation is through assignment, the bank or the financial institution can update the consent from the borrower or agent separately. In the event the trade does not get through, the user can cancel it too.


##### Workflow

In Trade Management, the user can perform the following activities:

This enquiry displays the list of loan trade records that are pending for confirmation.

To confirm the loan trade records, follow the below steps:

1. Pending Confirmation Trades .
2. In the Pending Confirmation Trades – Summary screen, click the Confirm Trade option corresponding to a record.
3. In the Confirm Trade screen, verify the details and then click the Commit icon.
4. Accept the overrides, if any.

Sub allocate activity is a Trade Management feature that is used to sub allocate a sell trade.

To sub allocate a loan trade record, follow the below steps:

1. Loan Trade Report .
2. In the Find Loan Trades screen, click Find.
3. In the Loan Trade – Summary screen, click Sub Allocate corresponding to a record.
4. In the Create Trade screen, go to Sub Allocation tab and provide values to all the fields, verify the details, and click Commit icon.
5. Accept the overrides, if any.
6. Authorise/Edit/Delete Loan Trade .
7. Approve the record.

This enquiry displays the list of loan trade records that are pending for Execution.

To execute the loan trade records, follow the below steps:

1. Confirmed Trades .
2. In the Confirmed Trades – Summary screen, click the Execute Trade option corresponding to a record.
3. In the Execute Trade screen, verify the details and then click the Commit icon.
4. Accept the overrides, if any.

This Enquiry displays the list of loan trade records that are pending for settlement.

To settle the loan trade records, follow the below steps:

1. Pending Settlement Trades .
2. In the Pending Settlement Trade – Summary screen, click the Settle Trade option corresponding to a record.
3. In the Settle Trade screen, verify the details and then click the Commit icon.
4. Accept the overrides, if any.
5. In the Settlement status screen, the settlement status of the loan trade is displayed. Run the BNK/LOAN.TRADE.SERVICE processing service.

Update Trade activity is used to amend the trade details after it is captured.

To update the trade, follow the steps below

1. Pending Confirmation Trade .
2. Select Trade ID of the trade that must be updated.
3. Verify the details, then click the Commit the deal icon.
4. Accept the overrides, if any.
5. Authorize the record.

The amend commitment activity is used to amend few details like the commitment amount, expected settlement date.

To amend commitment, follow the steps below

1. Pending Confirmation Trade .
2. Select the amend commitment activity for the trade that needs the change.
3. Verify the details, then click the Commit the deal icon.
4. Accept the overrides, if any.
5. Authorize the record.

Record Consent activity is an activity used to record the consent from the required parties to move forward with the trade. This activity has to be recorded when at the participation level, the consent is recorded as ‘Yes’.

To record consent, follow the steps below.

1. Pending Confirmation Trade .
2. Select the record consent from the dropdown of the trade, enter the consent given as ‘yes’ and the required date on which the consent was given
3. Verify the details and click the Commit the deal icon.
4. Accept the overrides, if any.
5. Authorize the record.

The Cancel Trade activity is used to cancel any trade before it is settled.

To cancel trade, follow the steps below.

1. Pending Confirmation Trade .
2. Select the Cancel Trade from the dropdown of the trade that must be cancelled.
3. Verify the details, then click the Commit the deal icon.
4. Accept the overrides, if any.
5. Authorize the record.

The amend charge activity is used for any amending the Loan trade charges fields alone.

To amend charge, follow the steps below

1. Pending Confirmation Trade .
2. Select the Amend Charge activity from the dropdown of the required trade.
3. Amend the required loan trade charge section, verify the details and click on the Commit the deal icon.
4. Accept the overrides, if any.
5. Authorize the record.

All the trades must be issued before it goes into settlement stage.

To issue pricing, follow the steps below

1. Loan Trade Report .
2. Select the Issue Pricing activity from the dropdown of the required trade.
3. Verify the details, then click the Commit the deal icon.
4. Accept the overrides, if any.
5. Authorize the record.


#### 📊 Outputs

The user can view the below list of enquiries related to loan trades, pending confirmation trades, pending consent trades, pending settlement trades, settled trades, loan trades, and loan trade classes in Temenos Transact .

Loan Trade Report .

This enquiry displays the list of loan trades in various statuses such as awaiting confirmation, confirmed, sub allocated, awaiting settlement, settled, and cancelled. The user can view trade, update trade, amend commitment, record consent, confirm trade, cancel trade, amend charge, execute trade, settle trade, issue pricing, view pricing advice and view settlement advice.
