### 4.4  Charge-off and Write-off


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *A bank is required to charge-off the principal balance of a loan for financial and regulatory reasons. This is determined by the bank. or bank examiners determine if a borrower is high risk and/or the loan is considered under-collateralised. The borrower is unaware if the loan is charged-off, borrow...*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Bill Status*, *Billed Amount*, *Charge Off Order*, *Chargeoff Category*, *Chargeoff Special Income fields*, *Full Chargeoff*, *Outstanding*, *Participant Accounting Type* ... +2 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

A bank is required to charge-off the principal balance of a loan for financial and regulatory reasons. This is determined by the bank. or bank examiners determine if a borrower is high risk and/or the loan is considered under-collateralised. The borrower is unaware if the loan is charged-off, borrower’s loan record exists, and payments are processed accordingly.

In case of club loans, own bank’s share is only charged off. The participant bank’s shares cannot be charged off. Participant banks can charge-off in their system, if required.

Charge-off is not loan default. Loan default is when the borrower fails to make a payment for an extended period, whereas charge-off is when there is no longer a reasonable expectation of further payments. The borrower and the participant banks are not aware of charge-off and related activities in the loan.

The bank can charge-off the principal balance of a loan if it is deemed doubtful. The loan may or may not be in non-accrual status during a charge-off. The pending principal, charges, and interest of a loan can be completely charged-off or the loan principal alone can be charged-off fully, partially or in a series of partial charge-off transactions on loan principal.

Write-off is an accounting action that reduces the value of an asset. In case of financial institutions, asset refers to loan. When the entire loan or a part of the loan is unpaid and the bank has exhausted all the ways of recollecting the loan from the borrower, the banks will decide to write-off the loan.

In case of Club Loans, if the bank writes-off a borrower balance, then balances of the participating banks are written-off proportionately.

- All Balance Charge-off – If the Temenos Transact owning bank is agent and participant or participant alone, then the principal outstanding, interest and charges are charged-off. If the bank is an agent alone, then only the charges are charged-off as the agent bank does not contribute to the loan.
- Principal Charge-off – If the Temenos Transact owning bank is agent and participant or participant alone, then the principal outstanding is charged-off. If the bank is an agent, the principal balance cannot be charged-off.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

- Charge-off Property must be created and attached to the Charge-off Property class of the product.
- The appropriate product condition must be attached to the Charge-off Property in the Product Designer.
- Product must be proofed and published.


##### Accounting Condition for Charge-off

When a charge-off is triggered, the loan principal moved from the assets of the bank and booked in the PL indicated in the Charge-off category in the Account Property or Property Class.

The Chargeoff Category and Chargeoff Special Income fields in Accounting Property class are used for an All Balance charge-off. The billed and unbilled components (properties) of the own bank are charged-off.

During an All Balance charge-off, the charge properties like activity charges, periodic charges are also charged-off as indicated in the Chargeoff Category field.


##### Dual Accounting

Activities that affect the principal or interest balance require dual accounting (that is, accounting on the customer’s view of own bank’s balances and the actual bank balances). The key activities that require dual accounting are listed below:

When the principal or interest is due, AA raises credit entries for current balances (that is, CUR and ACC ) and debit entries for due balances (that is, DUE and DUE ). The accounting process of the borrower and participant lender balance remain the same before and after charge-off. However, in case of own book balances, debits and credits are performed on customer balances (that is, the CUST versions) and bank balances in case of own book balances.

Apart from dual accounting to apply credit to a loan, a different order of payment is required for own bank’s balances, as the charge-off balances must be credited once the bank balances are exhausted.

When the Overdue Property Class is configured and the principal or interest is aged, AA raises the following entries:

- Credit the existing due or delinquent balances (for example, DUE or DEL )
- Debit the next ageing balance (for example, DEL and DEL )
- Temenos Transact raises bank entries and the customer entries using the internal accounting.


##### Balances after Charge-off

In a principal or all balance charge-off, the following balances are maintained for own bank:

- CUR – Principal balance outstanding after charge-off
- CUR CUST – The balance before charge-off that is projected to the customer.
- CUR CO – Balance that is charged-off

Hence, the following accrual balances are maintained per Interest Property and each accrues interest at the same rate based on their balance.

- ACC is accrued on CUR
- ACC CUST is accrued on CUR CUST
- ACC CO is accrued on CUR CO

Multiple interest accruals are done based on different balances definition of source balance for each type of accrual is not required. The interest is calculated on CURACCOUNT as source. The corresponding accruals in All Balance charge-off loan are:

| Balance | Source |
|---|---|
| ACC | CURACCOUNT |
| ACCINTERESTCO | CURACCOUNTCO |
| ACCINTERESTCUST | CURACCOUNTCUST |


#### 🔧 Working With

This section explains charging-off a club loan arrangement.


##### Triggering the Charge-off Order

When the Charge-off activity is triggered and if the transaction amount is greater than zero, then increase charge-off is triggered, the charge-off amount is based on the charge-off order.

- If the Charge Off Order field is set to Newest First, then the amount is allocated from CURACCOUNT balances first. If balance amount exists, then it is allocated from bills (dated new to old).
- If the Charge Off Order field is set to Oldest First, then the amount is allocated from bills (dated old to new). If balance amount exists after allocating the Account Property amounts from bills, then the charge-off amount is allocated from CURACCOUNT balance.

When the LENDING-CHARGE-OFF-ACCOUNT activity is triggered and if the transaction amount is less than zero, then decrease charge-off processing is triggered.

- If the Charge Off Order is set to Newest First, then the amount is allocated from due account charge-off balances (dated old to new) first. If remainder amount exists, then the Account Property balance is allocated from CURACCOUNT charge-off balance.
- If the Charge Off Order is set to Oldest First, then the amount is allocated from CURACCOUNT charge-off balance. If remainder amount exists, then charge-off amount is allocated from due or overdue charge-off bill balances (dated new to old) balance.

> **⚠️ Note:** The order in which balances are impacted are defined based on the status of the loan. This option is available in Charge Off Property Class and Payment Rules Property Class.


##### Account and Bill Details

The AA.ACCOUNT.DETAILS application stores the details of various event dates and also the reference of all bill ID of the CHARGE-OFF.REFERENCE and CHARGE-OFF.BILL.ID arrangements.

The CUR of the loan is charged-off partially or fully. This results in separate accruals for interest for customer and bank balances against the respective source balances.

| Balance | Source |
|---|---|
| ACCINTEREST | CURACCOUNT |
| ACCINTERESTCO | CURACCOUNTCO |
| ACCINTERESTCUST | CURACCOUNTCUST |

On bill generation (for the own bank’s bill), the AA.BILL.DETAILS application is updated with the customer and bank due amounts for each of these accruals.

The AA.BILL.DETAILS application stores the own bank related billed balances before and after the charge-off of the arrangement. Once a charge-off is done, the customer balances are stored in the amount related fields and bank balances are stored in bank related fields. The borrower bills and the participant bank bills are generated as usual as they do not have charged-off balance.

Overdue processing is triggered based on the delayed bills. The Outstanding and Billed Amount field of the bill are based on the customer balances (original amount) and regular overdue processing is triggered for the same.


##### Illustrating Principal Balance Charge Off

Banks process full or partial charge-off of the loan principal using the Charge-off Property Class. The LENDING-CHARGEOFF-ACCOUNT activity triggers the charge-off in parts. The Charge-off Property Class dictates the order in which the own bank’s account balances are impacted (for example, current first against oldest aged balance first) and the application order is followed when a principal or interest payment to the own bank’s bank balances are applied.

The Loan Arrangement Overview screen is displayed as shown in the below screenshot.

1. The corresponding Charge-off Activity is listed as shown in the below screenshot.

##### Illustrating All Balance Charge-off

A complete charge-off is done using the LENDING-CHARGEOFF-ARRANGEMENT activity. Once a complete charge-off is performed in the arrangement, the Full Chargeoff field set to Yes in the AA.ACCOUNT.DETAILS application.

During charge-off, the own bank’s share of principal amount in the loan is charged-off to the PL category assigned to the Account Property Class. The interest is charged-off to the PL Category assigned to the Interest Property Class. Tax (if any) is charged-off to the PL Category is assigned to the Tax Property Class.

During All Balance charge-off, the own bank’s balances in the arrangement are moved to the Charge-off PL. As part of shadow accounting, CUR CUST and CUR CO balances are maintained, during an All Balance charge-off. This results in the accrual of balances per Interest Property for each of the principal balances. Each of the principal balances accrue interest at the same rate but based on the balance. ACC CUST is accrued on CUR CUST and ACC CO is accrued on CUR CO.

> **⚠️ Note:** Though multiple interest accruals are done based on different balances, definition of source balance for each type of accrual is not required.

The interest is calculated on Interest Property Class and the source is CURACCOUNT. The corresponding accruals in an All Balance charge-off loan are:

| Balance | Source |
|---|---|
| ACCINTERESTCO | CURACCOUNTCO |
| ACCINTERESTCUST | CURACCOUNTCUST |

> **⚠️ Note:** An arrangement with interest and charge bills can be fully charged-off, including the interest and charges in the bills along with outstanding principal. Only the own bank’s share of charges are charged-off. Activity charge, periodic charge and rule break charge are also charged-off. This is subject to the following evaluation. The system evaluates if- There are any outstanding pay charges and raises an error to indicate that the same must be settled. There is charge collected that is undergoing amortization and it does not allow to charge-off that arrangement.

##### Illustrating Charge-Off for Contracts with Risk Participant

This section explains charging-off an arrangement with risk participants. Risk participants cover a part of risk in the loan so that, when the borrower fails to repay the loan, risk participant repays the own bank. Since a part of risk is covered, the loan can be charged-off only to the amount that is not covered by the risk participant.

Temenos Transact allows the bank user to partially charge-off the principal balances of an arrangement with risk mitigated to risk participants. When the risk is sold to another participant, charge-off can be performed only to the extent of the risk that the own bank holds, that is, charge-off can only be done to the extent of [Own Book Balance – Sold Risk]. The LENDING-CHARGEOFF-ACCOUNT activity is used to charge-off principal balance. When this activity is triggered, user must enter the amount to be charged-off in the Txn Amount field in AA.ARRANGEMENT.ACTIVITY ). This amount must not exceed the own bank’s risk exposure.

All Balance charge-off is restricted for arrangements with risk participants. It charges-off all the balances of the arrangement (interest, charges, outstanding principal and so on). However, the principal balance cannot be charged-off completely with risk participation.


##### Writing-Off for Contracts

Temenos Transact allows the bank to write-off either a balance or a bill that is unpaid. For Club Loans, the bank writes-off the borrower balances and then the corresponding balances of the participant banks are also written-off.

The bank can write-off:

- A bill
- A balance
- The entire arrangement

The respective activity can be invoked from the list of activities under the New Activity section of the Loan Arrangement Overview screen.

When a principal due or outstanding amount is written-off, the utilised commitment balance of the loan is reduced by the amount of principal that is written-off.

1. When the customer writes-off a borrower bill, then all the participant’s balances who have a share in the bill, is also written-off. The borrower’s bill before charge-off is as shown in the below screenshot.

1. The participant bank bills with the share details are as shown in the below screenshots.

1. When the bank user invokes write-off bills’ activity, the system lists the bills that are outstanding. The Write Off Bill field must be set to YES against the bill that must be written-off.

1. When the activity is committed, the bill gets written-off along with the participant’s bills. The bills are updated with the Bill Status as WRITEOFF as shown below.

1. Similarly, the participant’s bills are also written-off as shown in the below screenshots.

Like write-off bills, the write-off balance activity is used to write-off any balances. When a balance is written-off, all the participant banks share area also written-off proportionately.

When the write-off arrangement is executed, then the entire loan is written-off. All the principal outstanding, interest, charges, and bills are charged-off for own book and the participants.

### 4.5  ClubLoans


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Syndicated loans are a type of large credit facility issued by a consortium of lenders to a sole borrower. The amount of one syndicated loan is so big that one lender cannot fund or take on the debt single-handedly. The credit agreement for these types of loans is usually very complex in nature and ...*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Agent Bank
 Benf-Beneficiary*, *Agent Bank Benf- PO Product*, *Agent Bank Benf-Ccy*, *Allow
 Trading*, *Allow Trading*, *Amount*, *Balance Treatment*, *Banks Role* ... +34 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

Syndicated loans are a type of large credit facility issued by a consortium of lenders to a sole borrower. The amount of one syndicated loan is so big that one lender cannot fund or take on the debt single-handedly. The credit agreement for these types of loans is usually very complex in nature and attracts several fees such as upfront, arrangement, commitment and unutilised fees for the borrower and huge income to the bank.

The key role that connects the lender and the borrower group is the administrative agent. One bank from the lender group is appointed as an administrative agent and referred to as the agent bank.

Apart from funding a substantial portion of the loan, the Agent Bank is also responsible for:

- Servicing the loan to borrower.
- Maintaining the loan positions of each participant.
- Monitoring the performance of the borrowing group.
- Monitoring the covenants and notifying the participants.
- Sending notifications to the other participants on events such as but not limited to borrower funding request and interest rate changes.
- Distributing cash flows to other participants upon repayments.

The Participant Property Class helps to manage club loans with single or multiple participants.

This type of syndication usually entails a smaller amount, typically between USD 25 and USD 150 million. The main feature that makes this type of syndicated loan unique is the fact that the lead agent and other members of a club deal consortium share equal, or nearly equal, parts of the fees earned from the loan facility.

A loan, where a single bank cannot fund the complete loan amount, multiple banks get involved and share the total loan amount granted to the borrower. The main bank which is granting the loan to the customer is the agent bank and the other lenders are called the participant banks. The share amounts are agreed based on agreements from the agent bank and the participants. The agent bank can also underwrite the loan amounts. There can be participant or sub-participants to the loans. The Agent or Lead bank maintains beneficiary accounts to which the settlement has to be done to the participants. The various interest, fee and charges to be charged and the share of those charges are agreed with participant and accounting for them is also agreed.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The Participant Property Class holds share details of various lenders participating in the loan. In addition, it also has each lender’s role and their beneficiary details, which are used for funding as well as paying out their share upon borrower payment.

Only few fields like Negative Rate and Participant Accounting type allow input while creating the product condition to be attached to the product. The rest of the fields are no-input fields and can be input only while creating the arrangements. Hence, this product condition is marked as non-tracking in the product designer.

The Participant Accounting Type field is used to capture the accounting style and depending on the flag, the facility/lending module performs accounting to maintain these balances. The options are Memo and Contingent.

When the Participant Property Class is attached to the product and the participant accounting has to be generated, the Balance Treatment should be selected as Participant. The accounting entries to be generated are decided based on the following two criteria.

1. Role of the agent bank This is based on the role of the Temenos Transact owning bank. The role is defined in the Participant Property Class.

- If the agent bank’s role is Agent, then no accounting entries for commitment are required to be generated for the bank. Only the accounting entries of related fees and charges are generated.
- If the agent bank’s role is Agent cum Participant, then non-contingent accounting entries are required to be generated for it. The customer balances are always memo balances. The balances are maintained under balance types suffixed with ‘PARTINF’.

1. Participation accounting type The participant balances are selected based on the Participation Accounting Type. The accounting types can be either Memo or Contingent. Memo – The participant balances are maintained as memo balances with suffix ‘PARTINF’. Contingent – The participant balances are maintained as contingent balances with suffix ‘PART’ and are reported as contingent liabilities in the off-balance general ledger.

> **⚠️ Note:** The Participant Property Class is only applicable to the Facility and Drawing products but not Deal products.

When a drawing is created under the facility which has the participant details, the system defaults them from the Facility to the Drawing and they can be amended at the Drawing level except for the share percentage. When any changes are done in the Participant Property Class at the Facility level, the changes are reflected only for new Drawings created under the Facility.

> **⚠️ Note:** The list of participants and their share amounts cannot be changed after authorization of the club loan.


#### 🔧 Working With

The participants (the lenders) for each contract are different and according to the type and size of the deal, their share contribution, charges, etc. are agreed between the borrower, agent and the participants. This is why all the details in the Participant Property Class are captured at the arrangement level.

> **⚠️ Note:** The participant details can be captured at the Facility level, and it cannot be modified in the Drawings.

The Participant Property Class can be attached to both Facility and Drawing arrangements.

When the Participant Property Class is attached to the product and participant accounting has to be generated, the Balance Treatment should be selected as Participation.

In the following screenshot, an arrangement is being created and Participation is selected in the Balance Treatment field.


##### Participant Tab Attributes

It has the primary details like the role of the Temenos Transact owning bank, the list of participants and their share amount.

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Banks Role | Specifies the role of the Temenos Transact owning bank. Allowed values are: Agent, Agent Cum Participant and Participant. |
| Participants | Specifies the Participant ID of each of the lenders who are part of the contract. It should be a valid customer (Customer ID or Mnemonic from the customer application). |
| Share Amount | Specifies the participant commitment share amount on the total loan amount. Validation is made to ensure the sum of participant share amount including Own Share amount does not exceed the borrower amount or the loan commitment amount. |
| Share % | Indicates the participant commitment share in percentage on the total loan commitment. This is a system-calculated field. |
| Own Share | Specifies the owning bank commitment share in amount. The system populates the own share amount based on the participant’s share amount. The net share amount of the owning bank and the participant banks’ amounts must be equal to the borrower amount. |
| Own Share% | Specifies the owning bank commitment share in percentage. It is system calculated based on the owning bank share amount. |
| Participant Role | Specifies if a participant is a silent or sub-participant. The allowed values are Yes and Null. |

- Amount – 50M commitment amount
- Term – 5 years

Participant details are:

- Bank Role – Agent Cum Participant, meaning the Temenos Transact owning bank is the Agent and also contibutes a share in the total amount of the contract. If the Bank Role is Agent, then the Temenos Transact owning bank is an Agent only. If the Bank Role is Participant, then the Temenos Transact owning bank is a Participant in a contract where the bank is one of the lender in the contract where some other bank is an agent bank; the participant bank only records their share amount to track their fund movements.
- Participant – Bank of Ireland
- Share Amount –25 Million.

Multiple participants can be added with their share amount. On validating the arrangement, the own share amount (the difference between the borrower commitment amount and the participant share amount), share% and the participant role are updated by the system.


##### Settlement Instructions Tab Attributes

This specifies the settlement instructions of the participant banks. The participants list gets picked from Facility Arrangement (Parent) to the Participant tab. The other details have to be input.

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Currency | Specifies the currency to match currency-specific beneficiary account for the participants. The allowed values are valid currencies in AA. |
| Property Class | Specifies the property class to match property class-specific beneficiary account for the participants. The allowed values are valid property classes in AA. |
| Property | Specifies the property to match property-specific beneficiary account for the participants. The allowed values are valid property in AA. |
| Beneficiary ID | Specifies the participant beneficiary account details for cash outflow (specific to Currency/Property/Property Class or a combination). The account indicated in the beneficiary is used to credit participant share upon borrower repayment. The allowed values are valid ID from the BENEFICIARY application. |
| Beneficiary PO | Denotes the payment order product that should be used by the agent to settle the participants share when a repayment is made by the borrower. |

In the following screenshot, the settlement instructions for the participant Bank of Ireland have been given for the arrangement currency Euro by providing the Beneficiary ID which contains the account details or the IBAN/BIC details and the Beneficiary PO product which has to be used to indicate whether the payment is through an account transfer or SWIFT. Different beneficiary IDs can be given for each currency involved and for different Property Classes or properties such as charge and interest.


##### Skims Tab Attributes

This is used to capture the skim details of the participant banks. The participants list gets picked from the Participant tab. The other details must be input.

The interest charged is distributed to the participants according to their share percentages if there is no skim defined for the Participant.

Skim is a feature by which the agent bank can assign a different rate to the participant(s) than what the borrower is going to repay. It can be either higher or lower than the price agreed with Borrower depending on the demand. These skims can be reported to a different Income PL. Also, at any point of time, the bank can see the accrued skim income from each of the participants. Any rounding difference is posted to the Own participant.

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Property | Specifies the property for which skims and margins are to be applied. Only Interest is allowed. |
| Operand | Specifies the skim and margin operand to be used. The allowed value is Sub. |
| Skim rate | Specifies the skim margin rate that needs to be applied for the participant share. |
| Negative rate | Specifies when the skims have to be blocked in case of All-in-Rate results in a negative rate after deducting the skims. The options allowed are: NO - Rate for the participant is applied as zero. Block Margin - Rate for the participant is applied as borrower rate and skim rate is ignored. |

In the above screenshot, the facility fee that is collected from the borrower is to be distributed between the own bank and the participant (Bank of Ireland) in this case.


##### Charges Tab Attributes

This tab is for charges of the participant banks. The charges collected from the borrower are distributed to the participants according to their share percentages. However, some of the fees such as upfront fee and agency fee are distributed to specific group participants (for example, in case of upfront fee, each participant is paid at a different fee rate or fee amount) In those cases, the charge which has to be given to the specific participant and in what rate, amount or ratio can be defined here.

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Charge | Specifies the charge property for which different rate, amount or ratio will be applied for distributing the fee (charged to the borrower) to the participants. Below are examples, where there are two participants Bank A and Agent bank (Own) and the borrower is charged a fee. Scenario 1 : If a rate is defined for each participant, the fee to be distributed to the participant is calculated as a rate on current commitment amount of the participant. In the following example, the fee rate is defined as .08 and .12 for Bank A and agent bank, respectively; hence the fee to be distributed is USD 160 to Bank A and USD 840 to agent bank. Charge - Upfront Fee Participant 1 - Bank A Current Commitment - 200,000 Fee Rate (percentage) - 0.08 Fee - 160 Participant 2 - Agent Bank (Own Share) Current Commitment - 700,000 Fee Rate (percentage) - 0.12 Fee - 840 Scenario 2: If an amount is defined, it is treated as the fee amount to be distributed to the participants. In the following example, the fee amount is defined as USD 200 and USD 700 for Bank A and Agent bank, respectively.Hence, the fee to be distributed is USD 200 to Bank A and USD 700 to Agent bank. Charge - Upfront Fee Participant 1 - Bank A (Swedbank) Fee - 200 Participant 2 - Agent Bank (Own share) Fee -700 Scenario 3 : If a ratio is defined for each participant, the fee to be distributed to the participants is calculated as a percentage on the amount charged to the borrower. In the following example, the fee ratio is defined as 100% for Bank A; hence, the fee charged to the borrower of USD 500 is given entirely to the Agent bank. Charge - Agency Fee Participant - Agent Bank (Own share) Charge Amount - 500 Fee Ratio(percentage) - 100 Fee - 500 |
| Participant | Allows to select a valid Participant ID for which the defined charge is calculated and distributed based on the definition of Participant Fee share details (rate, amount or ratio) here. Input here ignores the charge pro-rata (based on the participant commitment share percentage). The allowed values are: Valid Participant of the arrangement. OWN (refers to the agent bank) |
| Rate | Specifies the fee rate per participant. The fee amount for each of the specified participant is calculated as a rate on the current commitment amount (available+ utilised) of that participant. |
| Amount | Specifies the fee amount per participant. |
| Ratio | Specifies the fee ratio per participant. The fee amount for each of the specified participant is calculated as a percentage on the total fee amount charged to the borrower or customer. |

In the above screenshot, the upfront fee that is collected from the borrower is to be distributed between the own bank and the participant (Bank of Ireland) in this case. If this definition is not given, the fee is distributed in their share ratio, that is, 50% each but now 60% belongs to the own bank and 40 percent to the participant bank.


##### Trading Tab Attributes

The credit agreement generally states whether:

- The loans or facility can be traded in secondary market
- Consent is required from the concerned parties
- The minimum trade amount

The following fields in Participant property class captures if transfer of shares is allowed in assignment form or not.

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Allow Trading | Allows to select whether trading is allowed for the facility or drawing. Allowed options are ‘Yes’ and ‘No’. If set as ‘Yes’, assignment transfer is allowed for the arrangement. If set as ‘No’ share transfer to existing or new participants won’t be allowed. |
| Min Trade Amt | Specifies the minimum share transfer amount. It is optional field where, Blank means trade allowed for all amounts. Input is not allowed when the Allow Trading field is set to No |
| Min Trade % | Specifies the minimum share transfer amount as a percentage of agreement Amount that is defined in Term Amount property class . Input is not allowed when Allow Trading is set as ‘No’ Min Trade Amt & Min Trade % are mutually exclusive to each other and user can input either one. |
| Consent Required | Specifies if share transfer requires third party consent. It is an optional field. Default option is ‘No’ If the Allow Trading field is set to No, automatically this field is defaulted to No |
| Consent Type | Specifies the consent which is mandatory for a share transfer or a loan trade transaction. The option available is Trade Acceptance. It should be a valid option in the EB.LOOKUP table Input is mandatory if the Consent Required field is set to Yes. |
| Consent Party | Specifies the party whose consent is mandatory for share transfer. The options are: BORROWER AGENT Banks can have other custom options by adding it to EB.LOOKUP table Input is mandatory if the Consent Required is set as Yes. |

In the screenshot below, the Allow Trading is set to ‘Yes’, Min Trade Amt is specified as USD 250,000, Consent Required is ‘Yes’, and the Consent Type is ‘Trade Acceptance’. The Consent parties are borrower and agent.

The attributes under Trading tab in Participant property class are valid only for assignment transfer (for new or existing participants).

> **⚠️ Note:** All the attributes defined above for trading are amended using the Update Participant activity. It can be defined or modified at any time during the life of an arrangement until its maturity . Any amendments done are verified and validated before settlement or share transfer is initiated.


##### Additional Tab Attributes

This tab is to capture the own bank and agent bank’s beneficiary details. When the own bank’s role is Agent or Agent cum Participant, then the own bank beneficiary details should be captured.

When the own bank’s role is Participant, then both the own bank and agent bank’s beneficiary details should be captured. The agent bank’s beneficiary details should be captured only when the own bank’s role is Participant.

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Participant acctng type | Specifies the participant accounting style for a club loan or loan participation product. The allowed options are: Memo Contingent Once an option is chosen, it cannot be changed later. |
| Own Bank Nostro-Ccy | Specifies the currency to match currency-specific beneficiary account for the own bank. |
| Own Bank Nostro-Account No. | Specifies the owning bank’s Nostro account for the currency specified. |
| Own Bank Nostro-Payin PO | Specifies the Pay-in Payment Order Product. |
| Agent Bank Benf-Ccy | Specifies the currency to match currency-specific beneficiary account for the agent bank. |
| Agent Bank Benf-Beneficiary | Specifies the agent bank’s beneficiary account details for cash outflow. It is currency specific. |
| Agent Bank Benf- PO Product | Specifies the Payment Order Product that should be used to transfer the fund from own bank to the agent bank. |

The Participant details in the overview screen are displayed as below for Facility and Lending arrangements.


##### Disbursement

- When the own bank’s role is Agent or Agent cum Participant, For a disbursement, the loan arrangement account is debited and the customer or borrower account is credited. The funds from each of the lenders would have been credited to the escrow account of the Agent, and during disbursement, the escrow account is debited and the syndication settlement account is credited. Thereon, the syndication settlement account is debited and the customer or borrower account is credited.
- When the own bank’s role is Participant, the disbursement can be done in two ways. The loan arrangement account is debited and the agent bank’s account is credited, so funds move from the participant bank to agent bank. Here, the amount to be disbursed is the participant amount and based on that, the borrower amount is disbursed in the arrangement. Instead of using the disbursement activity, the LENDING-DISBURSE-PO.WITHDRAWAL activity is used, the amount being the borrower amounts. The own bank loan account is debited and the agent bank’s account is credited.

#### 📋 Tasks

Related topics:

- Create Deal Arrangement (Corporate)
- Create Facility Under Deal Arrangement (Corporate)
- Perform Drawings Under Facility Arrangement (Corporate)
- Issue Guarantee Under Facility (AA) (Corporate)

Syndicated loans are type of large credit facility issued by a consortium of lenders to a sole borrower. The amount of one syndicated loan is huge, such that one lender cannot fund or take on the debt alone. The credit agreement for these type of loans are complex in nature and attracts various fees, such as upfront fees, arrangement fees, commitment fees, unutilised fee and so on to the borrower and huge income to the bank. The structure starts at the deal and the most fundamental aspect are the Facilities which make up the deal, which are drawn down using the drawing products.

Facility Product Line provides deal functionality for Temenos Transact . This feature allows the user to create a deal by using the AA framework under the Facility Product Line.

### 4.6  Facility Charges


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Charges can be scheduled on,*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

Charges can be scheduled on,

- Regular frequency
- Occurrence of a specific activity
- Breaching the terms and conditions accepted during arrangement creation.

Charges can be fixed amount or calculated amount or combination of both and it is calculated on tiered amounts from the facility. It can be accrued or amortised over a period. It can be negotiated while processing Facility arrangements. It can be collected on facility and it can be skipped or ignored at drawing level.


##### Upfront Fees Accounting Treatment in IFRS9

The upfront fee accounting treatment describes the accounting treatment applicable to commitment fee and loan origination fee in bank books. As per IFRS9 standards, in Club Loans, loan originating fees received by the owning bank at facility defers the postings to P and L till the maturity of the facility. The upfront fees collected at facility must be transferred on a pro-rata basis to the drawings when the drawings are disbursed under the facility and moves the fees transferred to drawings is moved to P and L from the drawings on the maturity date. If any fees remain at facility on the maturity date due to partial drawdowns, then it is moved to P and L directly from the facility.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

To set the accounting of Upfront Fee as per IFRS9 standard, the user should configure the upfront fee Charge Property as below.

Set the Property Type field to ‘ITEMIZED.AMORTIZATION’ for the charge property in AA.PROPERTY.


#### 🔧 Working With

This section details about the transfer of Upfront fees from the Facility to the Drawing in Club Loans.


##### Transferring Upfront Fee from Facility to Drawings

Consider a lender creates a Club facility for USD 1 million and collects two charges at facility level-Upfront fees and Coordination fees. If the lender wants only the Upfront fee to be accounted as per IFRS9 standards, then the system posts the other charge of Coordination fee to P and L immediately from the facility. Consider the lender charges USD 10,000 as upfront fee from the borrower. And, if the owning bank’s share is USD 700,000, then the own bank’s share of the upfront fee is USD7000. Only this Own Bank’s share of the Upfront fee USD7000 is transferred to the drawings on a pro-rata basis when a drawing is created under the facility and is posted to P and L from the drawings on the maturity date. On the maturity date if any Upfront fee remains at facility due to partial drawdown, then it is posted to P and L directly from the facility.

The below screenshots show the contract balances when a facility is created.

We can see the Upfront fees share of USD7000 of the Owning Bank in the above screenshot.

The below screenshot shows the record in EB.ACCRUAL for the facility. EB.ACCRUAL gives a more detailed information on the charge being amortized at facility and drawing level.

Transfer of upfront fee happens only when facility commitment is utilized. In the below case, drawdown is created which does not utilize the facility commitment and so the upfront fees is not transferred to the drawings. The upfront fee at facility is transferred to the drawings on a pro-rata basis only when the Update Commitment field at drawing is set to Yes or when the drawing is disbursed.

The below screenshot shows the contract balances at drawing when the drawing is created with Update commitment as ‘No’ and not yet disbursed.

In the above screenshot, we can see there is no upfront fees entry at drawings as the drawings is not yet disbursed.

Now the user disburses the drawing fully. The system transfers the pro-rated Upfront fee of USD 4200 to the drawings from the facility Upfront fee of USD7000.

The Upfront fee is calculated on a pro-rata basis based on the below formula.

= 600,000 / 1,000,000 = 0.6

=0.6 * 7000 = USD 4200

We can see the upfront fees transferred to the drawings in the below ECB screenshot.

The below screenshot shows the record in EB.ACCRUAL for drawings.

Upfront fees at facility after the transfer to drawings are shown in the below screenshots.

We can see the remaining upfront fees(USD2800) at facility after the pro rata transfer of upfront fees to the drawings in the above screenshot.

The below screenshot shows the record in EB.ACCRUAL of facility after the drawing is disbursed.

If the facility and drawings are getting matured on the same date, upon maturity, the system posts the upfront fees at facility and drawings to P and L under CATEG entries.

The Contract wise Balances enquiry shows the upfront fees at facility after maturity.

Upfront fees of USD 2800 which was remaining at facility posted to P and L as shown in the below screenshot.

The Contract wise Balances enquiry shows the upfront fees at drawing after maturity as shown in the below screenshot.

Upfront fees of USD 4200 which was transferred to drawing posted to P and L is shown in the below screenshot.

Upfront fees amortization is also applicable for multi-currency contracts. For example, when the facility is in USD and the drawing is in GBP, the system considers the exchange rate from the exchange rate table and accordingly the fee transferred to the drawing will be in GBP and the fee deducted from the facility will be in USD (as the facility is in USD).

### 4.7  Facility Payoff


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Facility pre-closure is used when a customer pays all the loans under a facility ahead of the loan tenure. For example, the pre-closure of a corporate loan implies that a customer is willing to close the loan before the maturity date. Options are available for the bank to levy a charge as a pre-clos...*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Arrangement*, *Closure Reason*, *Credit Amount*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

Facility pre-closure is used when a customer pays all the loans under a facility ahead of the loan tenure. For example, the pre-closure of a corporate loan implies that a customer is willing to close the loan before the maturity date. Options are available for the bank to levy a charge as a pre-closure fee.

Pay-off of the loan is handled like repayment. The agent bank uses it to settle the borrower’s account. Subsequently, the agent bank credits the payments to other participants in the club loan based on their contribution share percentage. A consolidated pay-off statement is generated at the Facility level with the breakup of individual bill details for all drawings under the facility.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The configuration is similar to bilateral facility pay-off. Read Configuring Combined Payoff for more information.


#### 🔧 Working With

There is hardly any difference between the execution of pay-off for club loan and that of a retail loan.


##### Bank Role: Agent cum Participant

When the customer requests for a combined pay-off statement, the bank generates a pay-off statement and provides it to the customer. The pay-off statement includes outstanding amounts in facility and the underlying drawings.

Although there is a consolidated statement, individual pay-off information bills are created for each Drawing and Facility. The combined pay-off statement can be issued to the customers, holding the bills IDs of the individual bills.

For each arrangement, multiple pay-off bills are generated.

- Bill for customer
- Bill for each participating lender

Payoff bills are info bills. When the pay-off simulation is run again, the old pay-off bill gets deleted and a new pay-off bill is generated. Each bill contains the break-up of outstanding amount with the participant share.

When the customer does a pay-off, the agent bank executes the respective repayment activity for pay-off. The repayment first settles the borrower loan account. Then, it takes own bank’s share out of the repayment and settles their account. Later, it credits the respective bank’s share to the beneficiary (settlement account number) captured in the Participant Property Class.

Illustrations of the Pay-off Statement simulation option and Pay-off Statement are shown below.


##### Bank Role: Participant

When the customer requests for a combined pay-off statement to the Agent bank, the bank generates a pay-off statement and provides it to the customer. The pay-off statement includes outstanding amount in Facility and the underlying Drawings.

The agent bank also intimates the participants that the borrower has requested for a combined pay-off statement. On receiving the intimation, the bank runs a simulation in their system and generates a combined pay-off statement.

Although it is a consolidated statement, individual pay-off info bills are created for each Facility and Drawing. The combined pay-off statement can be issued to the customers, holding the bills IDs of the individual bills.

Illustrations of Pay-off simulation option from overview screen and a Combined Pay-off Statement are shown below.

In club loans, for each arrangement, two pay-off bills are generated.

- One bill for customer
- One bill for own bank with its share

Pay-off bills are Info bills. When the pay-off simulation is run again, the old pay-off bill is deleted, and a new pay-off bill is generated. Each bill contains the break-up of outstanding amount with the participant share.

When the customer does a pay-off, the agent bank executes the respective repayment activity for pay-off. It first settles the borrower loan account. The agent bank, after receiving the repayment amount towards pay-off from the borrower, credits the respective bank’s share to the beneficiary (settlement account number) captured in the Participant Property Class.

After the agent bank has credited the repayment amount, then the own bank has to mark that the borrower has paid off the loan. The own bank then executes the Payoff activity.


#### 📋 Tasks

Related topics:

- Lending Processes (Corporate)

Facility pre-closure is used when a customer pays all the loans under a facility ahead of the loan tenure. For example, the pre-closure of a corporate loan implies that the customer is willing to close the loan before the maturity date. Options are available for the bank to levy a charge as a pre-closure fee.

Pay-off of the loan is handled as repayment. The agent bank uses it to settle the borrower’s account. Subsequently, the agent bank credits the payments to other participants in the club loan based on their contribution share percentage. A consolidated payoff statement is generated at the Facility level with the breakup of individual bill details for all drawings under the facility.

### 4.8  Facility Rollover


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *In corporate lending scenarios, similar to loan renewal, a facility also needs to be periodically examined and renewed by the bank. The facility needs to rollover and the facility maturity date needs to be set based on the rollover product conditions set by the bank.*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Arrangement*, *Change Activity*, *Event Date*, *Next Date*, *Renewal Date*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

In corporate lending scenarios, similar to loan renewal, a facility also needs to be periodically examined and renewed by the bank. The facility needs to rollover and the facility maturity date needs to be set based on the rollover product conditions set by the bank.

Any facility sanctioned for the borrower has a certain maturity date. Before setting up the facility, the bank generally assesses the eligibility of the borrower based on various aspects like financial rating, management scoring and industry trends. On a periodic basis, the bank reviews the borrower’s position and accordingly extends the maturity date of facility.

In addition, when all drawings under facility are not repaid within the facility maturity date, the bank might decide to rollover the facility for an additional period and extend the maturity date of the facility. Also, when certain eligibility conditions are met for a facility, the facility rollover can be triggered.

Options are provided to renew or rollover a facility on certain conditions. Temenos Transact supports the manual and automatic scheduling of the Renewal or Rollover Activity.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The Change Product Property Class is added to the Facility Product Line to rollover the facility arrangement when required.

In a corporate scenario, the facility is governed by a strong credit agreement and there is no scope for changing a facility product during the life of the facility arrangement, unless restructuring happens; in which case, a new facility is created by the bank. Hence, resetting of conditions to facility arrangement also becomes irrelevant. Hence, the Change Product Property Class is added to the Facility Product Line with the following restrictions.

- Only FACILITY-ROLLOVER-ARRANGEMENT Rollover Activity Class is released for the Facility Product Line.
- Change Product Activity and Reset Activity are not released.

For Facility, the Change Activity field, which determines the activity to be triggered during a loan renewal, will have only the rollover option.

Facility renewal can be set up on a specific date or after a specific period. Also, facility renewal can be initiated automatically or manually. The Change Product Property Class can be used to parameterize these conditions and they can be set at the product condition and attached to the product or can be set at the arrangement level, as per the other features attached. Read the Change Product Property Class user guide for more information.


#### 🔧 Working With

- Lending Processes (Corporate)

In club loan scenarios, similar to loans, a facility should be examine periodically and renew by the bank. The facility needs to rollover and the facility maturity date should be set based on the rollover product conditions set by the bank.

Any facility sanctioned for a borrower has a certain maturity date. Before setting up the facility, the bank generally assesses the eligibility of the borrower based on various aspects, such as financial rating, management scoring and industry trends. On a periodic basis, the bank reviews the borrower’s position and accordingly extends the maturity date of facility.

### 4.9  Financial Reporting for Club Loans


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The Reporting Property Class is used as an interface to the common cash flow engine, which provides information on cash movements of assets and liabilities.*
> 
> **Applications:** `EB.CASHFLOW`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Exclude Eir*, *Exclude.Eir*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

The Reporting Property Class is used as an interface to the common cash flow engine, which provides information on cash movements of assets and liabilities.

According to the international regulatory standards, based on the business models, the bank considers all the cash in-flows and out-flows of the respective contracts and arrives at an Effective Interest Rate (EIR).

In a club loan, cash flows may not be the same for all the participating banks. It depends upon the role of the bank, the level of participation and the terms agreed between the participant and the agent bank. Therefore, it is necessary to segregate the cash flows pertaining to the own bank whose role can be a participating bank or an agent bank.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The bank needs to add a Reporting Property class as part of the loan product. Read Reporting Property Class to configure the required regulatory standards.

As part of the own bank’s cash flow, any interest or charge skims that are received from other participants’ shares are also included. The bank should set the ‘Skims’ option in the Exclude Eir field of the respective property to exclude the skims from any properties from the EIR calculation as shown in the screenshot below.

- The Skims option can be set only for Interest and Charge properties.
- If the Exclude.Eir field is selected as Yes for any interest or charge property, then both the interest and it's skims cash flow are excluded from the EIR calculation.


#### 🔧 Working With

When the club loan product has a reporting condition defined, the system updates the EB.CASHFLOW application with the own bank’s cash flow for the loan. The EB.CASHFLOW application calculates the Effective Interest Rate (EIR) based on the cash flow.

The ID of the EB.CASHFLOW record is the same as the own bank’s ECB record Id as shown in the below format.

*

A bank has provided a club loan for USD 10 million to the customer and the own bank’s share is USD 6 million in the loan.

The loan has a quarterly repayment schedule.

The reporting condition is defined as below.

When the loan is created and disbursed, the EB.CASHFLOW is updated with the own bank’s cashflow.

> **⚠️ Note:** The EIR is calculated based on the own bank’s cash flow.

Read the International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) guide for more information on the treatment of the loan.


##### Skim

Skim is a profit component that the own bank uses to assign different interest rates to the participant banks, other than the borrower’s interest repayment. The difference between the borrower’s interest and the interest paid to the participant is the skimmed interest to the own bank.

Since skim is also a source of revenue, it is considered as own bank’s cash flow and included in the EIR calculation.

In the previous example, assume the bank has defined a skim rate for the participant as shown below. The own bank takes 1% of interest paid by the borrower to the respective participant as a skim.

Since it is received along with the interest payment, the cash flow with skim is updated in the EB.CASHFLOW based on the interest repayment cycle.

After the cash flow is updated with skim, the system displays EB.CASHFLOW as shown below.

> **⚠️ Note:** If the bank does not want to include the skims in the EIR calculation, then it should be configured as mentioned in the configuration section.

### 4.10  Higher or Lower Interest Rates


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The bank can define multiple rates (like LIBOR, EURIBOR or Federal fund rate and so on) for a particular loan contract and the system is configured to select the highest or lowest rates among the defined rates as contract’s interest rate. The interest calculation for an interest period is based on t...*
> 
> **Applications:** `EB.LOOKUP`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Compare Rates*, *User Compare Rates*, *User Margin Type*, *User Spread Rate*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

The bank can define multiple rates (like LIBOR, EURIBOR or Federal fund rate and so on) for a particular loan contract and the system is configured to select the highest or lowest rates among the defined rates as contract’s interest rate. The interest calculation for an interest period is based on the interest rate configured for the contract. The banks configure the higher or lower interest rate calculation to include the bank’s spread and customer margin, along with the base rate (if required).

A tier based (level or band) definition can be defined using the highest or lowest interest rate configuration.

This feature is applicable for Lending, Club Loan and Facility contracts.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The Compare Rates field in the Interest Property Class is used to configure the higher or lower interest rates, when multiple interest rates are defined in Lending, Club Loan or Facility contracts.

The banks can define multiple interest rates with pricing spread, customer margin and tier type details. Select the Pricing Spread value in the Margin Type field to capture the bank’s pricing spread on top of the base rate.

The margin defined using pricing spread margin type is included in the calculation of higher or lower interest rate, whereas the other customer margins are not.

Temenos Transact facilitates the user with the flexibility to decide if a margin should be included in the calculation of higher or lower interest rate.

Set the Data Name field as Compare Rates and the Data Value field as Include in the EB.LOOKUP for a margin to include the values in the calculation of higher or lower interest rate.

If the customer margin or any other margin is to be included in calculation of higher or lower interest rates, then the bank can create or modify the margin type record in EB.LOOKUP .

For an amount-based tier rates definition (level or band definition), the bank can:

- Define multiple interest rates for the same tier amount
- Select the highest or lowest rate among the definition as the effective rate
- The defined tier amount must be from the lowest to the highest

In the case where the customer margin is derived from the Pricing grid, in the Interest condition, the Use Pricing Grid field should be set to ‘Yes; and the bank should define the multiple interest rates in the user set of fields.

In general, while defining the interest condition, the pricing spread is defined in the

field. But, when the highest or lowest of interest rate is configured along with a pricing grid, any other margin like pricing spread that is not inherited from the pricing grid should be defined in the

set of fields instead of the usual

set of fields.

Refer to the Configuring Pricing Grid section for more information about the configuration of pricing grid.


#### 🔧 Working With

Multiple interest base rates can be defined by configuring the Compare Rates field as highest or lowest in the Interest Product Conditions. Based on the definitions in the Interest Product or Arrangement Condition, the system calculates the higher or lower interest rate and applies it on the Lending, Club Loan or Facility contracts.

Even when there are multiple periodic interest rates defined, the user can define a periodic reset period for one of the periodic interest definitions that is used to reset the interest rates on a defined period. If no reset period is defined, then the interest rate gets reset only if there is any change in the arrangement’s interest condition. In case if a floating index is defined, then the interest is reset whenever there is a change in its rate.

### 4.11  Limits


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The corporate lending structure is decided by the credit committee of the financial institutions or banks. The credit agreement is defined with the details on commitment conditions, borrower’s detail, pricing options or drawing rights, limit and collaterals, etc.*
> 
> **Applications:** `LIMIT.PARAMETER`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *.*, *Admin Limit*, *Admin Limit Ref*, *Admin Limit Serial*, *Advised Amount*, *Arrangement Level*, *Cash Flow Check*, *Catch All* ... +22 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

The corporate lending structure is decided by the credit committee of the financial institutions or banks. The credit agreement is defined with the details on commitment conditions, borrower’s detail, pricing options or drawing rights, limit and collaterals, etc.

The corporate lending structure in Temenos Transact flows from deal to facility to drawings. Also, it can be a single-level facility(SLF) without a deal or can be linked to a deal at the later stage of the contract.

- The first layer begins with Deal and it is the cap facility of the overall lending agreement of the bank’s customer, with multiple facilities under it.
- The second layer is the Facility that controls how the commitment can be utilised and whether drawings are permitted under certain conditions.
- The final level is the Drawings, where the customer is allowed to draw under the facility in line with the terms and conditions defined in the facility.

The cap limit (validation limit) is attached to the Deal and the facility limit (utilisation limit) is attached at the facility level. This is to capture the actual exposure that the financial institution or banks have taken against the individual customer or the group. This includes further structuring of sub-limits (restriction limit) for controlling the drawings under the facility, that is, to restrict or allocate the limits based on currency, borrower or product.


##### Validation Limit

The cap limit decided in the origination stage by the credit committee is the internal amount updated on the validation limit at the deal level. This limit is created and linked manually to the deal by the user. The purpose of this limit is to restrict the total amount of Facility being created against the Deal. The validation limit of the deal is linked to the Utilisation limit at the facility level. Hence, arrangements and contracts cannot be linked to validation limits.

The approved validation limit serves as the cap of the underlying approved utilisation limits. The approved amount of the validation is always greater or equal to the sum of the approved utilisation limits at the facility level.


##### Utilisation /Credit Limit

The utilisation limit or credit limit is the facility level limits in a structure. These are the limits that are advised to the customers. The internal and advised amount for a product is set at this level. Hence, the arrangements can be linked to Utilisation limits and limit checking occurs only at this level. This only records the own bank’s commitment amount and is the reporting limit. Read Link to be provided for more information.

The validation limit’s advised amount is the sum of the underlying Utilisation limits’ advised amounts, that is, the sum of all utilisation limits internal amount cannot exceed its parent validation limit’s internal amount.


##### Sub-limits

The sub-limits or restriction limits represent maximum utilisation caps under the facility, by restricting or allocating a shadow limit within the facility or utilisation limit as per the sub-limit structure decided at the origination stage. These limits are designated to limit the risk based on the borrower, currency, product line, product group and product.

The following are the Sub-Limits that allow a maximum of:

- USD 2 M for Borrower A
- Up to USD 8 M for Standby Letter of Credit(SBLC)
- Up to USD 5 M for long-term loans

When a new Facility is created, new sub limits (with a new Limit type as Restriction) for each criterion are created in the Limit based on the sub-limit definition. And whenever the limit check is done for the utilisation limit, it is also done for the sub-limits.


##### Admin Limit

In addition to credit limit, there is an Admin Limit that represents the total exposure of the bank towards the borrower in a particular contract. In a club loan, more than one lender is involved. This means, unlike bilateral loans, the exposure of the own bank in the club loan is different from the overall exposure of the arrangement. Therefore, in a club loan, the exposure of the Temenos Transact owning bank is recorded under credit limit and the total exposure towards the borrower is recorded under the admin limit.

This includes both the own bank’s exposure as well as the third-party (or external lender) exposure. In case of a bilateral facility or loan, the admin limit is equivalent to the own bank share, which means there won’t be any difference in terms of limit amount between the credit limit and admin limit. The admin limit performs sub-limit check and cash flow check for the facility and drawings.

> **⚠️ Note:** This limit cannot be used for reporting purposes.


##### Credit Limit

The existing utilisation limit is called as credit limit. This only records the own bank’s commitment amount and is the reporting limit. Read Link to be provided for more information.


##### Cash Flow Check

A Cash Flow check is essential to any corporate that transacts under multiple business commitments to ensure smooth flow of the future commitments without any breach of the various scheduled activities during a specific period. This check finds out the negative and positive flow of commitment in a lending structure and therefore acts on rectifying the foreseen breach of the commitment, if any.

In corporate banking, at any point of time, there are likely to be multiple commitment conditions in place for a Facility. For example, commitment schedule, unavailability periods and drawings cash flow. Whenever any activity or transaction occurs against a facility or any drawing associated with it, all commitment availability schedule and the future drawings cash flows should be examined for adherence to the rules.

The Forward Limit check, that is, the cash flow check is an option for any bank to control or monitor the scheduled commitments that is expected to happen on a future date and within the commitment condition, that is, the system should ensure that there will not be any breach of commitment at any point in future throughout the facility maturity or for a specific period.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

To create LIMIT records that are part of the new Validation or Utilisation Limit structure setup, Limit products have to be created for each level (that is, Utilisation for child products and Validation for parent products).

Limit products are created from the bottom way-up approach , that is, from the lowest level so the child Utilisation products have to be created first.

> **⚠️ Note:** A parent Validation product must end with at least two zeros, which means that the child product cannot end in more than one zero.

For example, if we are to create a child Utilisation product with ID 6710, this is how it would look:

> **⚠️ Note:** Reducing Limit is neutral for Validation and Utilisation products implying the limit type (reducing or non-reducing) is determined at the Drawdown level.

The above child product is linked to the parent Validation product with ID 6700 this way and updated in the limit parameter accordingly:

After the Limit products are created, a Limit record can be created for them. Unlike products, Limit records are created from the top way-down approach that is, from the highest level. This means that the parent Validation Limit record has to be created first:

Then, the child Utilisation Limit record can be created.


##### Validation Limit Rules

Below are rules that need to be followed by the user while creating and attaching the validation limit,

- For bilateral lending or multi-layered facility, the validation limit has to be created manually by the user and attached to the deal arrangement. And the validation limit is cascaded to the facility arrangement, when the master arrangement ID pertains to the deal product.

- Validation limit is mandatory at the deal arrangement level, only when the Limit property is attached to the deal product.

- Limit Type should be defined as Validation in the limit reference record.

- Deal currency and validation limit currency should be the same.

- Deal commitment amount and the validation limit internal amount should be the same or validation limit can be greater than the deal commitment amount.
- Validation Limit can be attached to only one deal and cannot be shared with other deals.
- Expiry date mentioned in the validation limit is the Limit available date at the deal level. So, the expiry date of the limit is equal to or greater than the maturity date of the deal. Otherwise, the system throws an error: Expiry date of the limit is lesser than the contract maturity date.
- Validation limit customer(s) are created based on the deal customer(s) and sub-arrangement rule definition of the deal. If the sub-arrangement rule of the deal and the Facility defined as ANY customer, the ANY needs to be decided and has to be part of the limit customer at the time of validation limit creation itself.
- Deal or facility or drawing arrangement cannot be committed in the lending structure if the customer is not part of the Validation limit and/or Utilisation limit.
- For a single level facility (SLF), the deal arrangement is not created but validation limit has to be created manually and linked to the utilisation limit of the facility arrangement and its underlying drawings. In this scenario, the user attaches the utilisation limit in the Limit ID field of the facility arrangement. Then, the system defaults the validation limit of that utilisation in the Validation Limit field.
- No Limit processing or update is done against the validation limit, that is, no limit movement happens for the validation limit. Limit check is called from the facility level without any limit movement. Only validation check is done every time. The facility is created under the deal to restrict if the sum of facility under the deal does not exceed the deal validation limit.

If,

is set to Yes in the

application, then the

and

fields are reduced upon repayments.

> **⚠️ Note:** Deal commitment is non-revolving in nature and any revolving or non-revolving nature of the facility has no impact on the deal. The sum of the facility commitment under the deal is validated based on the internal amount and not on the balance movements.

##### Utilisation Limit Rules

There is no configuration required at this level. In a lending structure (for bilateral lending or multi-layered facility), creation of utilisation Limit records is managed by Temenos Transact at the facility level, that is, the Utilisation limit record is created automatically in the LIMIT application.

- The utilisation limit is created for the Facility amount in facility currency.
- Limit Reference or Product is based on the Limit Parameter.
- Customer is the Facility Account Customer, that is, the Customer updated in the underlying account record.
- Allowed Customer(s) are updated based on the sub-arrangement rule definition.
- When Manage Limit and Single Limit is set to Yes, It enables the limits to be managed by Temenos Transact.
- Limit parameter should be updated for linking the facility products and the limit product. At the facility arrangement level, a valid limit reference in the Limit Reference field and value NEW in Limit Serial creates the Limit record automatically accordingly to the limit parameter setup.
- The limit reference should also be linked to the validation limit as child reference.
- Facility expiry date captured in the Expiry Date field of the Facility arrangement is the Limit expiry date. In case, the facility expiry date is blank, the maturity date of the facility becomes the limit expiry date.
- Utilisation limit customers are the Facility Customer(s) and the customers additionally defined under the Sub-arrangement rules property of the facility.
- Facility currency is passed as Limit currency.
- Facility amount is the limit amount. This amount is mapped to limit's internal amount. In case of increase or decrease in the commitment schedule, it will be honored by the LIMIT. Like, when commitment decrease is scheduled on a particular day, that decreased amount will be updated in the LIMIT amount.
- For commitment with future start date, the limit change is triggered through the new activity increase or decrease commitment schedule activity at COB on the respective commitment start date. Increase or decrease in the TOT and the CUR balance of the facility triggers an impact on Online Limit and Commit Amt Avail in the LIMIT application.
