Below are the activities that can trigger update in the utilisation limit (contingent and non-contingent utilisation of facility).

- New facility creation.
- Decrease of facility commitment.
- Increase of facility commitment schedule.
- Decrease of facility commitment schedule.
- Mature and expiry of the facility commitment.
- Closure of the facility commitment.
- New Drawings under Facility with Update Commitment set to Yes.
- Reinstate of the commitment for a revolving Facility (Repayment/Prepayment in Drawings).
- Disbursement of a Drawing with Update Commitment set to No.
- Capitalisation of interest and charges.
- Take over and adjust balance process


##### Creating Utilisation Limit Manually

Only in case of Single Level facility, Utilisation limit record can be created manually and attached to the facility arrangement. Or a system generated limit can be created by updating the limit reference and serial as NEW.

When the master arrangement ID (Deal arrangement ID) is blank in the facility arrangement, the Validation Limit field is allowed for input by the user, that is, when the system does not default the validation ID.

For single Level facility, deal arrangement is not created but validation and utilisation limits have to be created manually. At the time of facility arrangement creation, the utilisation limit has to be input in the Limit ID field and its respective validation limit ID is defaulted in the Validation ID field.


##### Linking SLF to Deal Arrangement

SLF can be linked to the new deal arrangement in the later stage of the contract. The linking can be established by validation limit.


###### Scenario 1

Consider Utilisation limit ID of the existing facility is auto-generated

1. Deal arrangement is created with the Validation limit key of the existing Facility arrangement.
2. In the Facility arrangement overview screen, New Activity (Link to deal Arrangement) has to be chosen, only the Deal ID has to be input by the user. This FACILITY-LINK.MASTER-ARRANGEMENT activity class does all the validations and accounting (with the exchange rate fixed on link date in case of multi-currency facility) that is done during a new Facility creation under a Deal. Along with this new sub-limit, key is also auto-generated, if the Sub-Limit Property Class is attached to the facility product.


###### Scenario 2

Consider the Utilisation limit ID of the existing facility is manually created and attached by the user

1. Deal arrangement is created with the Validation limit key of the existing Facility arrangement.
2. In the Facility arrangement overview screen, Link to deal Arrangement activity has to be chosen, only the Deal ID has to be input by the user here. This activity class does all the validations and accounting (with the exchange rate fixed on link date) that will be done during a new Facility creation under a Deal.
3. Temenos Transact populates the change of the utilisation limit key, to manage the utilisation ID created by AA Transact. Along with this new sub-limit, key is also auto-generated, if the Sub-Limit Property Class is attached to the Facility product.


##### Sub-Limits

The risk elements that frame the sub-limits are called the Criterions. These are defined in the AA.DATA.ELEMENTS application.

- Only the data element marked as Sub-Limit in the Used Prop Class field is allowed for defining the criterion in the Sub-Limit Property Class at the product condition level.
- The Arrangement Source field allows fetching the source data from AA.ARRANGEMENT .
- The Arrangement Level is defaulted as SELF, when the Used Prop Class field is updated as Sub-Limit.
- Any validation with regards to the Catch All field is ignored at the Sub-Limit Property Class. This allows blank value in the criterions for sub-limit definition.

The following screenshots show the risk elements Borrower and Product created in AA.DATA.ELEMENTS .


###### Attributes

- Used Prop Class – In the Sub-Limit PC, the data elements defined with Used Prop Class as Sub-Limit are the allowed risk criterion.
- Risk Criterion – This is a multi-value field that allows defining the risk criterion for the sub-limits up to ten criterions. Also, this field allows the user to define the order of the sub-limit combination based on which the underlying sub-limit column values are set.
- Criterion – Allows defining the values for the respective risk criterion set in the RISK.CRITERION field . This is a multi-value as well as sub-value field that will have up to ten criterions (for example, CRITERION.1, CRITERION.2 to CRIETERION.10). The Risk Criterion and Criterion fields are associated fields. When risk criterion is set as CURRENCY in the Risk Criterion field, it allows to define the value, that is, valid currency in the associated Criterion field; up to 10 set of associated fields can be created.
- Sub Limits Ccy – Defaults the facility currency as the sub-limit currency. A valid currency record from the CURRENCY application is the allowed input in this field. This Sub-Limit Property Class is defined with the property class type as: Non-TrackingAlso, only one property for this property class should be attached at the facility arrangement level. And each property class can be defined with multiple product conditions but only the current condition applies.

> **⚠️ Note:** Backdated conditions are not allowed. When backdated arrangement is entered, sub-limits are created only on the current system date and not for the backdated date.

The following screenshot shows a simple sub-limit product condition configured based on couple of data elements (Borrower and Product).


###### Example

Consider the facility currency as EUR. The sub--limit definition is as follows:

1. Maximum of EUR 8,000,000 equivalent to USD currency.
2. Maximum of EUR 4,000,000 equivalent to GBP currency.
3. Borrower 100100 is restricted to utilise a maximum of EUR 2,500,000 either for LIBOR loan or EURIBOR loan.
4. Borrower 190251 is restricted to utilise a maximum of EUR 2,000,000 equivalent USD currency for guarantees or borrower 190252 to utilise a maximum of EUR 2,000,000 (No currency, product restrictions here).

The multi-value fields cannot have blank values across all the five criterions. Meaning, a row cannot be blank completely like highlighted in the below screen shot. At least one criterion has to be entered with a value.


##### Admin Limit

Admin limit is created automatically by Temenos Transact in the following scenarios:

- If either sub-limits or cash flow check is enabled as part of the contract, and a valid limit reference product is specified in the Admin Limit Ref field and the Admin Limit Serial field is set as NEW in the Limit Property Class.
- If both sub-limits and cash flow check are enabled as part of the contract, and a valid limit reference product is specified in the Admin Limit Ref field and the Admin Limit Serial field is set as NEW in the Limit Property Class.
- If both sub-limits and cash flow check are not enabled as part of the contract, but a valid limit reference product is specified in the Admin Limit Ref field and the Admin Limit Serial field is set as NEW in the Limit Property Class.

Admin limit cannot be attached manually to a contract. The Admin Limit field is not available for the user to enter values. Temenos Transact auto-populates the Limit ID in the Admin Limit field based on the scenarios listed above. Admin limit is not applicable for Deals. In case of a Deal-Facility-Drawings structure or single-level-facility structure, the admin limit is attached to the facility. The same Limit is used by the drawings beneath the facility. In case of a standalone lending contract, the admin limit is attached to the drawing itself.

> **⚠️ Note:** The limit reference mentioned in the Admin Limit Ref field should be a valid product from the LIMIT.REFERENCE apppplication. The product should have the Limit Type as Standalone. In addition, the Reducing Limit field should be Neutral and the Key Type field should be Txn Ref.


###### Enabling Cash-flow Check

Cash flow check is performed based on future disbursements and repayments scheduled for the drawdowns under a facility or standalone drawing to find the commitment available for the borrower to withdraw at any point of time.

The user has to select Global in the Cash Flow Check field in the Limit Property Class. This enables the system to perform cash flow check on the total commitment towards the borrower in a contract.

> **⚠️ Note:** When cash flow check is enabled in the Limit Property Class, the user must ensure that the limit reference specified in the Admin Limit record and Cash Flow has to be enabled in Cash Flow Check .


#### 🔧 Working With

The following section explains the limits processing feature with illustrations.


##### Validation Limit

Attach the validation Limit ID at the deal level under the Validation Limit field.

The facility created under this deal with the master arrangement being the deal arrangement ID has the validation limit defaulted from the deal. The utilisation limit is created by Temenos Transact by giving a valid Limit reference and Serial as NEW or valid serial number as shown below.

Attach the Sub-Limit condition to the facility arrangement for the below scenario:

| BORROWER | CURRENCY | PRODUCT | SUBLIMIT |
|---|---|---|---|
| 190279 |  | Libor | 5 Million |
|  | USD |  | 8 Million |
| 190278, 190280 |  | Libor, Euribor | 4 Million |
|  |  | Fixed Rate Loan | 4 Million |

The Sub-Limit condition at the facility level applies to all the drawings created under the facility. In the above example, if a user tries to book a fixed rate drawing beyond 4 M, an override message is generated while disbursing the loan.

The above override message says that the restriction limit LI20108T8CR1 (automatically created by the system based on the sub-limit condition) with respect to FIXED.RATE.DRAWINGS product has been exceeded by 1 million. Meaning, the total utlisation allowed under the FIXED.RATE.DRAWINGS product is 4 Million but the user has breached the limit by creating utlisation for 5 Million under the FIXED.RATE.DRAWINGS product.

Restriction Limit is created for each of the sub-limit defined in the AA.ARR.SUB.LIMITS application. In the example, there are four restriction limits created under the parent utilisation limit available at the facility level.


##### Limit Processing in Bilateral Loans

The admin limit is updated with both contingent and non-contingent balances similar to the credit limit. The updated balances in admin limit are of borrower’s balance, unlike the credit limit, which is updated with own bank’s balance of the loan.

An illustration of an admin limit and credit limit automatically created by the system in a bilateral loan is shown below. There is no change in the limit amounts between the credit and admin limits in all the scenarios where a facility is created, drawings created and disbursed, increase or decrease in commitment amounts, expiry or maturity.


##### Limit Processing in Club Loans

The limit processing for club loans takes place in the exact way as a bilateral contract, except that both the limits, that is, the credit and admin limits, are updated with different transaction amounts.

Whenever the transactions, such as new drawing creation, disbursement, repayment and capitalisation, take place, the limits are updated as explained below.

- The credit limit is updated with the own bank’s share of the transaction.
- The admin limit is updated with the borrower’s share, that is, the entire amount of the transaction.

If the own bank role is:

- Agent cum Participant or Participant – The own bank’s exposure in the loan or facility is updated to the credit limit.
- Agent – There is no exposure for the own bank in the arrangement. Therefore, there is no update on credit limit.

During share transfer, the admin limit is not affected. Only the credit limit is updated whenever the own bank acts as a buyer or a seller. So, when the credit limit is a:

- Auto-created limit (that is, limit managed by AA) – The internal amount and online limit are updated based on the share that the own bank bought or sold.
- Manually created one (and attached to the arrangement) – The internal amount and online limit are not updated.

Also, if the own bank:

- Bought a huge amount of share, which adds up with the existing own bank exposure of the arrangement, to an amount more than the limit sanctioned, then the limit is updated as if it has been over utilised.
- Sells its share and the total exposure of bank is less than the limit sanctioned, then the limit is updated as if it has been under utilised.

An illustration of working of an admin limit and credit limit automatically created by the system in a club loan is shown below.

In the above scenario, both the credit and admin limits have the same limit balance 10 million in the initial stage. Later, when Temenos Transact owning bank sells a portion of its share (3 million) to an external lender – Bank of America, the credit limit undergoes a change.

The online limit is reduced by 3 million under credit limit, but there is no change towards the Online Limit field under admin limit because the commitment towards the borrower is still 10 million.

Similarly, the online limit is reduced by another 2 million under credit limit when Temenos Transact owning bank sells a further 2 million of its share to Citi bank. Again, there is no change towards the Online Limit field under the admin limit.

On the other hand, when there is a buyback, the credit limit is increased. In this example, Temenos Transact owning bank buys back 1 million from Citi bank, due to which the online limit under credit limit is increased by 1 million. Again, there is no change towards the Online Limit field under the admin limit.


##### Enabling Cash Flow Check

The cash flow check is performed on the admin limit of the contract. In case of a Deal-Facility-Drawing structure and single-level-facility structure, the cash flow check is performed at the facility level, taking all the drawings under the facility into consideration. Cash flow check is also enabled for standalone drawings.

The cash flow projection of a contract is maintained in the LI.CASHFLOW table. The primary key for LI.CASHFLOW is the admin limit ID of the contract. This gives the overall projection of the facility or standalone drawing. In addition, a key beginning with the admin limit ID and followed by the utilisation limit ID gives the projection of the individual utilisation contracts.

For example, a facility having two drawings beneath it has four records in LI.CASHFLOW as detailed below.

| CONTRACTS | ADMIN LIMIT ID | UTLISATION LIMIT ID | LI.CASHFLOW RECORD |
|---|---|---|---|
|  | LI201089GC7B |  | LI201089GC7B |
| Facility |  | AA12345678 | LI201089GC7B.AA12345678 |
| Drawing 1 |  | AA87654321 | LI201089GC7B.AA87654321 |
| Drawing 2 |  | AA98765432 | LI201089GC7B.AA98765432 |


###### At Facility Level

The commitment schedule and unavailability period are considered for computing the cash flow balance.

1. Commitment schedule defines the total commitment amount of a Facility at any given point of time. The commitment amount of a facility can be defined as constant , increasing, decreasing or custom (that is, increasing and decreasing).
2. Unavailability Schedule defines the unutilised commitment amount that is unavailable for utilisation at any given point of time. When not defined, the available commitment amount is equal to unutilised commitment amount. for more details on the Unavailability Schedule.

For example, an USD 500,000 facility has both commitment schedule and unavailability schedule on a particular date. Where,

- USD 300,000 – The amount in commitment schedule.
- USD 100,000 – The amount in unavailability schedule.

Therefore, the commitment amount available USD 200,000 is what Temenos Transact considers for calculating the cash flow. The following events at the facility level result in a cash flow update:

- New facility creation or takeover
- Commitment schedule
- Amendment of commitment schedule
- Commitment expiry schedule
- Scheduled unavailability period
- Amendment of unavailability schedule
- Ad hoc unavailability
- Manual increase or decrease of the facility commitment
- Change in the term
- Impact of capitalisation of drawing’s interest and charges at the facility level
- Reinstate or revolve or reduce the facility commitment based on the nature of the facility commitment at the time of repayment of the underlying drawings


###### At Drawing Level

Disbursement and repayment schedule is considered as one of the cash flow events (only principal movement is considered as a cash flow event).

> **⚠️ Note:** A consolidated cash flow balance, which measures the breach and override message populated by the system while committing the contract, is maintained.

Consider the same example of USD 500,000 facility with commitment and unavailability schedules. Also, note that there are two drawings, USD 100,000 and USD 150,000, beneath the facility. And for the same date where commitment schedule has USD 300,000 and unavailability schedule has USD 100,000, there is also repayment schedules under drawing 1 for an amount of USD 10,000 and under drawing 2 for an amount of USD 50,000.

Now, the cash flow check considers the commitment schedule, unavailability schedule and the repayment schedules for that particular date and updates the consolidated amount in LI.CASHFLOW as (50,000) projecting a breach in the facility and limit.

> **⚠️ Note:** If the Update Commit Limit field is set to one of the following values under the drawing: Yes – The cash flow is updated with the drawing details as soon as the drawing contract is created in Temenos Transact. There is no update towards the cash flow when the drawing is further disbursed on a future date. No – The cash flow is not updated with the drawing details when the drawing contract is created but only updated during disbursement.

The following events at the drawing level result in a cash flow update:

- New drawing creation
- Disbursements
- Capitalisation of the drawing’s interest and charges
- Repayment or prepayment of drawing
- Amendment of disbursement or repayment schedule
- Manual increase or decrease of the drawing commitment
- Change in the term

Only the principal amount of the repayment schedule is considered for cash flow projection ignoring the interest portion. But if the interest is set to capitalise, then it is considered for cash flow projection because it gets added to the principal portion of the loan.

Related topics:

- Lending Processes (Corporate)

Limit is the total exposure that a bank can take on a particular client for facilities offered by the bank. Limits are recorded or controlled using the Limit Property Class (PC) in Facility arrangements. Validation and utilisation limits are created and attached to Facility arrangements. Transact can validate the utilisation limit amount when further drawings are created. The system prompts override or error message when the drawing amount exceeds.

In Limits, the user can perform the following activities:

To create a validation limit using the LIMIT application, follow the below steps:

1. Create Secured Limit .
2. Click the New Deal icon.
3. Enter values in the following fields: Customer.1 Limit Product
4. In the Limit Details tab, enter values in the following fields: Currency Internal Amount Expiry Date
5. Click the Validate icon to check for errors and overrides.
6. Click the Commit icon.
7. Accept the overrides, if any.

To create an utilisation limit using the LIMIT application, follow the below steps:

1. Create Secured Limit .
2. Click the New Deal icon.
3. Enter values in the following fields: Customer.1 Limit Product
4. In the Limit Details tab, enter values in the following fields: Currency Internal Amount Expiry Date Country of Risk Country Percent Online Limit Date Max Total Offered Until Available Marker Liability Number
5. Click the Validate icon to check for errors and overrides.
6. Click the Commit icon.
7. Accept the overrides, if any.

### 4.12  Loan Payoff


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Loan pre-closure is used when a customer repays the loan ahead of the loan maturity date. For example, the pre-closure of a corporate loan implies that a customer is willing to close the loan before the maturity date. Options are available for the bank to levy a charge as a pre-closure fee.*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Arrangement*, *Closure Reason*, *Credit Amount*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

Loan pre-closure is used when a customer repays the loan ahead of the loan maturity date. For example, the pre-closure of a corporate loan implies that a customer is willing to close the loan before the maturity date. Options are available for the bank to levy a charge as a pre-closure fee.

Pay-off of the loan is handled like repayment. The agent bank then uses it to settle the borrower’s account. Subsequently, the agent bank credits the payments to other participants in the club loan based on their contribution share percentage.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The configuration is similar to bilateral loan pay-off. Read AA Retail Lending Pre-closure Configuration for more information.


#### 🔧 Working With

There is hardly any difference between the execution of pay-off for club loan and that of a retail loan. Read AA Loan Pre-closure for more information.

This section explains the club loan-specific pay-off features.

When the customer requests for a pay-off statement, the bank generates a pay-off statement and provides it to the customer. The pay-off statement includes all the principal, interest and charges that are due as a result of pay-off.

In club loans, multiple pay-off bills are generated.

- One bill for customer
- One bill for each participating lender

Pay-off bills are info bills. When the pay-off simulation is run again, old pay-off bill is deleted and a new pay-off bill is generated. Each bill contains the break-up of outstanding amount with the participant share.

When the customer does a pay-off, the agent bank executes the repayment activity for pay-off. The repayment first settles the borrower’s loan account. Then, it takes the own bank’s share out of the repayment and settles their account. Later, it credits the respective bank’s share to the beneficiary (settlement account number) captured in the Participant Property Class.

In case of pay-off, where the borrower has repaid an amount less than the pay-off amount, there is an amount outstanding in the loan account. But, if the outstanding amount is within the tolerance amount allowed, then the outstanding amount is written off.

The participant lenders’ account is written off proportionately based on their share in that particular balance. For example, if the written off amount is principal balance, then all the participant lenders’ principal outstanding is written off proportionately based on their share. Whereas, if the written off amount is agent fee, then only the agent bank’s agent fee is written off and other participant lenders’ account is untouched.

The pay-off statement simulation option is shown below.

The pay-off statement is shown below.

The pay-off bill for borrower is shown below.

The pay-off bill for own bank is shown below.

The pay-off bill for participant bank is shown below.

Pay-off of the loan is handled as repayment. The agent bank then uses it to settle the borrower’s account. Subsequently, the agent bank credits the payments to other participants in the club loan based on their contribution share percentage.

### 4.14  Misc


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Syndicated loans or club loans are a large credit facility issued by a consortium of lenders to a sole borrower. The amount of one syndicated or club loan is so high that one lender cannot fund or take on the debt alone. The credit agreement for these types of loans is very complex in nature and att...*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Balance Treatment*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction


#### 📖 Introduction

Syndicated loans or club loans are a large credit facility issued by a consortium of lenders to a sole borrower. The amount of one syndicated or club loan is so high that one lender cannot fund or take on the debt alone. The credit agreement for these types of loans is very complex in nature and attracts several fees such as upfront fees, arrangement fees, commitment fees and unutilised fee for the borrower and this becomes a huge income to the bank.

These loans are provided to medium-to-large corporates to help their business expansions as well as day-to-day business operations. Examples of these loan types are project finance loans, working capital loans, construction finance and standby letter of credits.

The lenders are composed of banks, but financial institutions like mutual funds and insurance companies may also participate in this type of lending. Depending on the type of the deal, the complexity of the credit agreement structure and the financial need of the borrower, there are many different parties or roles that a lender or bank can be assigned such as:

- Book Runner
- Lead Arranger
- Co-Lead Arranger
- Joint Lead Arranger
- Lead Arranger
- Letter of Credit Issuer
- Swing Line Lender
- Bid Bank
- Administrative Agent
- Collateral Agent
- Documentation Agent
- Book Manager

However, the key role which conduits between the lender and borrower group is the administrative agent. Typically, one bank from the lender group is appointed as administrative agent and referred as Agent Bank.

Apart from funding a substantial portion of the loan (however, in some cases, the administrative agent need not fund the loan), the lead agent is also responsible for:

- Servicing the loan to borrower
- Maintaining the loan positions of each participants
- Monitoring the performance of the borrowing group
- Monitoring the covenants and conditions and notify participants
- Sending notifications to the borrower and other participants on events such as, but not limited to – borrower funding request and interest rate changes.
- Distributing cash flows between the borrower and the other participants.


##### Club Loans in Temenos Transact

Temenos Transact supports the Club Loans functionality. A Transact bank can create club loan contracts and the following features are supported:

- Participant details can be captured at the facility level and the share details are automatically followed at the drawing level
- The Transact bank, called as the owning bank, can record contracts where they are the administrative agents (both funding and on funding) and also where they are just participants.
- If the owning bank takes the agent role, then all the other participant balances and details are recorded off the book. This is for administrative purpose.
- If the owning bank is just a participant, then the bank’s own balances are recorded on the book. The global amount that is funded is recorded off the book for information purpose.
- Shares can be transferred from one of the participant to another during the course of the club loan
- Most of the other AA Loan and AA Facility functionality is available for Club Loans as well.


##### Configuring Club Loans

To configure a loan as a club loan, the loan product should have the Participant Property Class attached to it. Because the lender participant details are contract-specific information, they are captured during every contract creation.

Apart from attaching the Participant Property Class, the Balance Treatment field in the Account Property Class has to be set to Participation. If this field is not set to Participation, then the user cannot capture loan participant details even if the Participant Property Class is attached. This field acts as a switch to define whether the contract is a bilateral (one lender to one borrower) or a club loan.

After a club loan or facility is created, the lender participants can choose to sell their shares or to buy more shares from other lender participants. This is achieved by the process of share transfer. To do a share transfer, the bank user should use the Capture Share Transfer activity. The activity opens the Share Transfer Transaction Class where the necessary details can be captured.

Club Loans and facilities have the parameters setup similar to a normal loan or facility except that the Product should have the Participant Property Class. Because the details captured in the Participant Property Class are contract specific, no details are set up at the Product Condition level. Read the AA Loans and AA Facility sections for more information on model parameter set up.

The below Property Classes are applicable to the Club Loans Product Line.

- Account
- Accounting
- Activity Charge
- Activity Presentation
- Activity Mapping
- Activity Messaging
- Alerts
- Balance Maintenance
- Closure
- Change Product
- Customer
- Eligibility
- Limit
- Officers
- Payoff
- Payment Schedule
- Pricing Grid
- Payment Priority
- Settlement
- Sub Arrangement Rules
- Statement
- Term Amount
- Participant
- Exchange Rate
- Sub-Limit
- Share Transfer
- Sub Arrangement Condition
- Evidence


##### Illustrating Model Parameters

This section covers the model parameters required for the club loans.

The Account Property Class is used by all products, which are account based. This Property Class primarily controls the description of the account. The Account Property allows the user to define and control balance treatment, posting restriction, linked account number (for memo accounts), currency market, date convention related setup for the account.

Although the account names are account specific, generic titles can be defaulted from the product and can be replaced or given additional detail at the arrangement level. Each Temenos Transact product defined and processed in Arrangement Architecture (AA) can have a single ACCOUNT Property defined.

The Accounting Property Class is used by all products. AA uses activity-based accounting. Each Property has different actions, which require accounting. For each action, a corresponding allocation rule definition is required. Allocation rules can be defined either at Property or Property Class level. The categories to which the interest or charges have to be posted are also defined in this Product Condition. In Model Bank, the charges are amortised.

The Activity Presentation is an optional Property Class that allows to define versions used for various Properties during arrangement activities. The versions can be defined at Property Class, Property and Activity levels.

The Activity Mapping Property Class provides the link between external applications and arrangement activities when a transaction is performed on an arrangement account. A debit or credit to an arrangement account triggers the applications such as, Funds Transfer, Teller, Clearing, and so on, which are linked by relevant transaction codes using this Product Condition.

The Activity Messaging Property Class is used to link the Soft Delivery module to AA module. Messages are sent based on the role and activity performed on an arrangement. This record allows either specific Activities or Activity Classes to be defined and linked to the records of EB.ADVICES .

The Activity Charge Property Class defines the charges that has to be applied when a particular activity is triggered on the arrangement. The charges so applied can be made due, capitalised or deferred. In the model bank, for a Term Facility product Upfront Fee and Coordination Fee are applied when a new arrangement is created.

The Alerts Property Class is used by all products. It enables alerts to be sent to the customer for various activities in an arrangement. Alerts can be subscribed at the arrangement level by using EB.ALERT.REQUEST . Multiple owners of the arrangement are allowed to subscribe different alerts on that arrangement. The subscription of alerts can be restricted based on the role of the customer in that arrangement.

The Balance Maintenance Property Class allows the user to capture bills and balances and adjust the balances of the bill for the contracts, which have been taken over from existing legacy system or Temenos Transact Lending module into Temenos Transact AA module. The actions such as, CAPTURE.BILL, ADJUST.BILL, and so on, help in capturing the bill and its balances into the new system.

The Closure Property Class defines the rules and behavior for processing closure of an arrangement. An arrangement account can be closed automatically or manually and it is defined in the product condition. On reversal of a new arrangement, closure is triggered automatically.

The Change Product Property Class is used by all products, which allow for a change of product during their lifecycle. When a new product is applied to the existing arrangement, the user loses all the negotiations done as part of the old product. This table allows a list of products to which the old product can change and also define time-scales as to when the event should happen.

The Customer Property Class is used by all products. This Property Class is used to define all the parties involved in an arrangement and their respective roles. The customer is always defined at the arrangement level. Each arrangement can have one or more legal owners defined in OWNER.

The Eligibility Property Class is used to evaluate eligibility of a customer for a specific product based on a set of rules. The eligibility evaluation is triggered at a given frequency or when there is a static change for the customer. In Temonos Transact, first the EB.CONTEXT has to be created. Based on this, rules are defined using Rules Engine. Once these rules are validated, the EB.RULES.VERSION and EB.RULES are created in the system.

Evidence (Covenant and Conditions) Property Class refers to conditions, which a borrower must comply with to avail a Facility or a Loan. A Covenant must be valid throughout the life of an Arrangement (for example, Deal or Facility) and it must be validated on a certain frequency. A Condition must be true for certain activities to occur. Evidences is validated during creation of a new arrangement, update activity and closure of activity. Evidence Property Class is applicable for Deal, Facility and Drawing Product Lines and it is an optional Property Class.

The evidence requirement is captured in EV.EVIDENCE.REQUIREMENT . The category of the evidence requirements are created in EV.REQUIREMENT.CATEGORY (virtual table). The consequences are the actions taken by the bank in situations where the covenants and conditions are not satisfied. So, the consequences are tagged to AA.ACTION for which the activity type is configured as Evidence Check in the relevant record of AA.ACTIVITY.CLASS .

The Limit Property Class primarily controls the use of Limit module by the product. The user can set up single or shared limit and can define Limit Reference applicable for a specific product such that the same is set as default in an arrangement. For a new limit, at the arrangement level, the user should provide New in the Limit Serial field. Further limits can be set to use the Limit module or it can be managed only within the arrangement architecture framework.

The Officers Property Class enables the user to define:

- Product
- Arrangement specific officers
- Officer’s roles
- Primary officer
- Additional officer

Each Temenos Transact product defined and processed in AA can have a single OFFICERS Property defined.

The Payoff Property Class is used to produce a payoff statement, which is given to a customer when a loan payoff is considered. It shows the current status of the account, including the updated accrued interest and penalty applicable, if any. An expiry date can be defined for the payoff statement and the loan statement shows the additional daily interest to be charged till the expiry date. The payoff amount is calculated by using the simulation framework.

The Payment Schedule Property Class is used by all products which have amounts billed (that is, made due or capitalised or pay). A Payment Schedule can be comprised of one or more payment definitions with conditions such as, payment type and method, arrangement properties, dates and amounts. The AA.PAYMENT.TYPE file is used to define the standard payment types such as, Constant, Combine Bill and Combined interest, and so on, which can be used by a product. This payment type is then attached to each payment schedule definition. The start and end date can be specified. The user can specify the repayment of arrangement to commence after ‘n’ months from the arrangement date or ‘n’ months before the maturity or ‘n’ months after the change product or reset and rollover has happened.

The Pricing Grid Property Class applies to the Facility and Lending Product Lines. The Pricing Grid Property Class provides a mechanism to define the criteria used to determine the margin(s) or spread(s) for interest or fee that apply to base rates at the various levels of the credit agreement such as, deals, facility and drawing. Pricing Grids can be configured by selecting criteria, which is used to determine the margin (for interest) and/or the rate (for fee) to apply to a Property. A Pricing Grid is comprised of elements that determine the criteria for one or more elements to specify what is set on the interest condition. The user can select both the user-defined data criteria and their order of precedence. Grids can be defined at the deal, facility and/or drawing levels.

- Deal level Pricing Grids defines the rates for Deal level fees.
- Facility Level Pricing Grids defines the rates for Facility level fees and the margins for drawings level interest.
- Drawing Level Pricing Grids defines the margins for drawings level interest.
- Pricing Grids that are defined for Facility level can be negotiated at the Drawings level

The Payment Priority Property Class is used by Facility Product Line to define the order in which the combined repayment is allocated between the facility dues on the facility and dues on drawings under the facility. Combined payment received at the Facility level is allocated to individual Drawing arrangements based on the rules defined in this Property Class. The user can create multiple drawings under a single Facility and the bills will be combined at facility level. The user can make a single payment using Facility arrangement and is allocated to each drawings based on the rules set in Payment Priority. The priority is based on different factors such as, Product Group, product, bill date, bill type and so on.

The Settlement Property Class is used for various Product Lines to control the settlement related functions of all the Product Lines. Settlement can be handled by linking any Temenos Transact account, the account and bank details of another bank by using Direct Debit and beneficiary of the customer. The Default Settlement Account is considered as the default account for both Pay-in and Pay-out Activities, if the Pay in or Pay out account is not specified. But, if the accounts are specified for the Pay-in or Pay-out, then those accounts precedes over the specified default settlement account.

The Sub-Arrangement Property Class allows the user to define the conditions for the Sub Arrangements (drawings) of the facility. The Sub-Arrangement Rules Property Class is available for the Facility Product Line. This Property Class enables to set rules for the sub-arrangements under a master arrangement.

It is attached to the Facility product to control the allowed customers, currencies and products of the drawings under the Facility. Similarly, it is attached to the Deal product to control the allowed customers, currencies and products of the facility and drawings under the Deal.

The Sub Arrangement Condition Property class is used to define condition or validation for processing or creating Drawing Arrangements. Banks can define various criteria in Sub-Arrangement condition either at deal or facility level. When a drawdown is created under a Facility, the system validates against the conditions and raises override or error message whenever any condition is breached.

The Statement Property class is used to define the legacy ACCT.STATEMENT feature at AA level. Statements may be produced daily (every working day), every 1-9 weeks, twice a month (on the 15th and the last day of the month) or every 1-12 months on any day of the month. Up to nine statement cycles may be specified for each Account and each statement cycle is independent. In addition to this, special interim statements can be enabled. This property class also controls if advices are to be produced or not, when interest and charges are applied, and whether detailed interest statements (interest scale) should be produced.

The Term Amount Property Class is used by financial products which involve an amount of money that is lent for a specified period of time. This property class controls the commitment made by the bank to the customer.

PARTICIPANT property class is used to hold the information of the various lenders (participants) participating in the loan facility contract. It contains details, such as Participant's role, the Participant IDs and share amounts contributed by the lenders to the loan. Also, contains the settlement instructions of the participants, such as beneficiary details that are used by the Owning Bank to transfer the funds between the borrower and the participants. It is also used to define the charges and interest skim rates applicable to each participant.

Exchange Rate property class is to define the Exchange Rate (FX), Rate Tolerance and Prior Days, Advance FX Fix Activity, and so on to support the Advance FX fixing requirement.

Sub Limits Property class allows the user to define the multiple shadow limits within the facility or utilisation limit by restricting or allocating the limit, based on the risk factors or criterions. At the time of creating the facility arrangement, the sub-limit(s) limit record will be created as per the definition in the sub-limits PC. The restrictions and allocations are regulated based on the risk elements, borrower, currency and product (Product, Product group, and Product line).

Share Transfer is a transaction type property class. The purpose of this property class is to transfer the share of an existing participant of a club loan to another existing participant or to a new participant. It is also used to capture the settlement instructions and skim details in case of selling the shares to a new participant. In case where the buyer is a new participant for a loan, the settlement instruction is mandatory and skims is optional. In case where the buyer is an existing participant, collecting the settlement instructions and skims details are optional. In such situations, if the details are entered, then the system overwrites the previously stored details of the participant.


##### Illustrating Model Products

All the products in model bank under the Product Groups Corporate Facilities (Facility Product Line) and Corporate Drawings (Lending Product Line) have the Participant Property Class attached to them. During runtime, the user can make use of the Balance Treatment field in the Account Property Class to capture the club loan details.

| Sl.no | Product Name | Product Attributes |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Corporate Deal | Deal |
| 2 | Corporate Facilities | Revolving Facility Term Facility |
| 3 | Corporate Drawings | Annuity Drawings Euribor Drawings Fixed Rate Drawings Index Based Drawings Construction Loan |

### 4.15  MultiCurrency Facility Drawings


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *A borrower may withdraw funds from the facility in more than one currency by creating multi-currency drawings. Multi-currency drawings are useful to multinational corporations that prefer to reduce the foreign exchange risk in financing a project that may need to occur in several countries at once.*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Allowed Currency*, *Allowed list*, *Base Ccy Amt*, *Base Ccy Ovd Amount*, *BaseCcyAmt*, *BaseCcyCur*, *BaseCcyOvdAmount*, *BaseCcyRate* ... +11 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

A borrower may withdraw funds from the facility in more than one currency by creating multi-currency drawings. Multi-currency drawings are useful to multinational corporations that prefer to reduce the foreign exchange risk in financing a project that may need to occur in several countries at once.

Similarly, the facilities under a deal can be in different denominations. A GBP-denominated deal can have facilities in USD, EUR, etc.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The user should do the configuration under the Sub-Arrangement Rules Property Class for enabling multi-currency drawings or facility. Read the Sub-Arrangement Rules Property Class section for more information.


##### Sub-Arrangement Rules Property Class

1. The Currency field in the Sub-Arrangement Rules Property Class should be set to one of the following values detailed below to enable drawdowns or facilities in a currency other than the facility or deal currency.

- Allowed list –Enables the user to mention a list of currencies in which the drawdowns can be made under a facility if the Sub-Arrangement Rules Property Class is attached to the facility. Similarly, it enables the user to mention a list of currencies in which the facilities can be created under a deal if the Sub-Arrangement Rules Property Class is attached to the deal. Allowed Currency – The currencies have to be listed in this associated field if Allowed list is chosen.
- Any – Enables the user to create drawdowns in any valid currencies defined in the CURRENCY table of the bank, if the Sub-Arrangement Rules Property Class is attached to the facility. Similarly, it enables the user to create facilities in any valid currencies defined in the CURRENCY table of the bank, if the Sub-Arrangement Rules Property Class is attached to the deal. Allowed Currency – The user should enter a value in this associated field if Any is chosen.

1. The Currency Market field should have a valid input from the CURRENCY.MARKET application with which currency conversion happens for the drawing(s). The default value for this field is 1.
2. The Exch Rate Type field should have an input with respect to Buy-rate, Sell-rate or Mid-rate with which currency conversion happens for the drawing(s). The default value picked up is Mid-rate if the user fails to give the input when the Currency field has either Any or Allowed List.


##### Exchange Rate Property Class

The user should do the below configuration under the Exchange Rate Property Class.

User has to mention the exchange rate to be applied in the Exchange Rate field for the system to convert the facility or drawing balances to its parent currency.

The system picks the exchange rate as the Mid-rate from the CURRENCY application if the user does not specify a rate in the Exchange Rate field.


#### 🔧 Working With

The following section describes the Multi-Currency Facility and Drawings feature with examples.

In case of a Deal-Facility-Drawing structure where the deal is in GBP, facility is in USD and drawing is in EUR:

- The exchange rate (USD to GBP) from the ExchangeRate Property Class of the facility stored in the BaseCcyRate AA.ACCOUNT.DETAILS application of the facility to hold the conversion history at the facility level. The same rate used throughout the life of the facility for internal book keeping in maintaining the deal utilised or unutilised or overdrawn commitment balance.
- The exchange rate (EUR to USD) from the ExchangeRate Property Class of the drawing stored in the BaseCcyRate AA.ACCOUNT.DETAILS of the Drawing to hold the conversion history at the drawing level. The same rate used throughout the life of the drawing for internal book keeping in maintaining the facility utilised or unutilised or overdrawn commitment balance.
- The BaseCcyAmt in AA.ACCOUNT.DETAILS of Facility holds the utilised amount (UTL + ) of the facility arrangement equivalent to deal currency. In case Update Commit On Cap is marked as OVERDRAW, then over utilisation is captured separately under the Base Ccy Ovd Amount . New facility creation, capitalisation and increase of the facility add to the amount stored in the Base Ccy Amt . Conversely, repayment, decrease and mature of the facility reduce the utilisation of the deal balances.
- The BaseCcyAmt in AA.ACCOUNT.DETAILS of Drawing holds the utilised amount (UTL + ) of the drawing arrangement equivalent to facility currency. In case UpdateCommitOnCap is marked as OVERDRAW, then over utilisation is captured separately under the BaseCcyOvdAmount . New drawing creation, disbursement, capitaliation and increase activity of the drawing add to the amount stored in the BaseCcyAmt . Conversely, repayment, decrease and mature activity of the drawing reduce the utiliation of the facility balances.
- In addition, BaseCcyTot and BaseCcyCur in AA.ACCOUNT.DETAILS of Facility hold the total commitment balance and the available commitment balance of the facility equivalent to the deal currency.
- This way of storing the balances of facility and drawings in the parent currency help the bank to overcome any rounding issues due to multiple currencies involved. At the time of maturity of the facility, when the total commitment of the facility is reduced to zero, but the BaseCcyTot has difference due to rounding issues, AA Transact reduces the difference to zero in this field. When the available commitment of the facility is reduced to zero, but the BaseCcyCur has difference due to rounding issues, AA Transact reduces the difference to zero in this field. Similarly, whenever the drawing commitment balance is reduced to zero (utilised (UTL) or overdrawn (OVD)) but the BaseCcyAmt has difference due to rounding issues, Temenos Transact reduces the difference to zero in this field which enables the user to mature the facility whose drawings are all repaid and closed

Consider that a $100,000 facility is utilised to an extent of €25,000. The exchange rate is 1.170822 for EUR-USD.

Facility balances before utilisation are:

- TOTAL COMMITMENT - USD 100,000.00
- UNUTILSIED COMMITMENT - USD 100,000.00

AA.ACCOUNT.DETAILS of the drawing contract:

- BASE.CCY.RATE - 1.170822
- BASE.CCY.AMOUNT - 29,270.55

Facility balances after utilisation are:

- TOTAL COMMITMENT - USD 100,000.00
- UNUTILISED COMMITMENT - USD 70,729.45
- UTLISED COMMITMENT - USD 29,270.55

- Update Commitment - Yes at both facility and drawing level
- Revolving Nature - Yes at both facility and drawing level
- Update commitment on Capitaliation - OVD

Exchange difference in the BaseCcyAmt becomes zero, when the utilised balance and other balances in drawing commitment are zero.

- Update Commitment - No, at both facility and drawing level
- Update commitment on Capitaliation- OVD

- Combined Bills – The combined bills generated at the facility level based on the currency, bill date and payment date are not supported when the drawings are in different currency other than the facility currency.
- Combined Pay-off – The Combined Pay-off feature at the facility level, which calculates the payoff amount for all the underlying drawings and generates a combined payoff statement, is not supported when the drawings are in different currency other than the facility currency.


#### 📋 Tasks

Related topics:

- Create Deal Arrangement (Corporate)
- Create Facility Under Deal Arrangement (Corporate)
- Perform Drawings Under Facility Arrangement (Corporate)
- Lending Processes (Corporate)

A borrower may withdraw funds from the facility in more than one currency by creating multi-currency drawings. Multi-currency drawings are useful to multinational corporations that prefer to reduce the foreign exchange risk in financing a project that may need to occur in several countries at once. Similarly, the facilities under a deal can be in different denominations. A GBP-denominated deal can have facilities in USD, EUR, and so on.

### 4.16  Notices


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *As part of bilateral or club facility, it is required to generate notices or advices to the corporate customer.*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Advice*, *Bank Customer*, *Bank Role Type*, *Msg Content*, *Role Advices*, *Role Send*, *Send Advice*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

As part of bilateral or club facility, it is required to generate notices or advices to the corporate customer.

- The funding or owning bank generates the notices for bilateral loan.

- The agent bank generates the notices in club or syndicate loan.

In case of a club loan, it is required to send notices to all the parties involved. Parties involved in the club loan can play different roles such as borrower, participant, sub-participant and risk participants. Based on role and the transaction activity, it is required to generate notices. Various notices for corporate lending are:

- Intent notices
- Notices for rate fixing
- FX fixing, payment notices
- Rate change or loan payoff notices
- Combined bill notices
- Advance rate fix notices
- Forward dated share transfers notices
- Notices for risk participants

It is possible to notify the customers on occurrence of specific activities. A pre-notification can be enabled for the scheduled activities before the event takes place.

AA is integrated with the Document Management and Image Management modules for managing the documents and images.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The Activity Messaging Property Class is used to configure the advices to be generated for the Activity Class or Activity for each customer role. The customer preferences can be configured for the same.

Pre-notification (Delivery Advice) is available for all scheduled activities across Product Lines using the Activity and Days fields in the Activity Messaging PC. Pre-notice days can be indicated for the respective activity.

To setup a different advice format for corporate customers with respect to club loans, the Activity Messaging product condition has been enhanced.

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Role Advices | Specifies the role-specific advice format. It is an optional field. All valid records in EB.ADVICES are displayed in this field. If advice is configured for multiple roles, then role-based advices take priority. If role-based advice is not set up, then the default advice setup in the Advice field is picked up for delivery. |
| Role Send | Sets whether advice needs to be sent for the specific role. This is an optional field. The options available are Blank, YES and NO. If this field is set as Blank, then it refers to option set up in the Send Advice field for sending the advice. If this field is set as Yes, then it refers to advice set up in the Role Advices field for sending the advice. If this field is set as No, then advice set up in the Role Advices field is not sent. |

The Document Management module can capture and upload (store) the documents, and the Image Management module is used to store and retrieve images at the arrangement level.

To send notification based on the customer roles, the following two fields are available in the AA.CUSTOMER.ROLE application.

| Field | DEscription |
|---|---|
| Bank Customer | Defines whether the linked customer is a participant customer. This is an optional field. |
| Bank Role Type | Configures the role of participant customer. The allowed values are: Participant Sub Participant Risk Participant Agent |


##### Delivery

The Delivery(DE) module facilitates the generation of advices or notices for various Transaction events. The following sections explain the steps needed to configure the printing or delivery of advices or notices.


##### Delivery Address

The DE.ADDRESS application contains the names and addresses of customers. The basic postal address of each customer is updated automatically when the customer address changes through customer maintenance (the CUSTOMER application). A record is created in the DE.ADDRESS application with ID as COMPANY ’.C-’ CUSTOMER ’.PRINT.00001’

The address of the customer needs to be updated through the CUSTOMER application. The SWIFT IDs, telex numbers and alternative print addresses are maintained in DE.ADDRESS . These records may be input and amended through DE.ADDRESS .


##### Delivery Format

This Delivery Format application holds the definition of all printed messages in the Delivery module. The ID of the DE.FORMAT.PRINT record is NNNN.AANNNN.NNN.AA , where:

- NNNN is the message type.
- AANNNN is the application format, which is either application code or numeric or application code followed by up to four numeric characters.
- NNN is the format version number.
- AA is the language.

If the message type is 320, the application format is MM1030, the format version is 20 and the language is FR, then the ID of DE.FORMAT.PRINT record is 320.MM1030.20.FR.

The EB.ACTIVITY table is used to configure the event and number of days prior the notices has to be sent before the activity. The EB.ADVICE table is used to configure the mapping record.

In the AA.PRD.DES.ACTIVITY.MESSAGING application, the Msg Content field has the following options:

- All – Values present in all the properties belong to the Activity handed over to the hand-off file.
- Change – Changed values in the relevant properties belong to the Activity handed over to the hand-off file.

The content of the notice can be configured using the details present in the hand-off file. Because all the values are passed to the hand-off file, it can impact the performance.

Instead of passing all the values, it is prudent to pass only the necessary values pertaining to the Activity in the hand-off file.

To control the data sent to the hand-off file, a table is available to capture the hand-off routine details that control the data handed over to the hand-off file. This table is linked to the Msg Content field in AA.PRD.DES.ACTIVITY.MESSAGING .

While configuring Activity messaging for a product, the user needs to configure the message content that requires to be handed off as part of the activity.

Read the Activity Messaging Property Class, Document Management and Customer Preferences for Advices and Alerts sections under Arrangement Architecture for more information.
