### 4.17  OfferArrangement AdvanceRateFix


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The drawdown or rollover process in corporate lending consists of the following stages:*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Adv Rate Fix Days*, *Adv Rate Fix Days.*, *Amount and Term*, *Attribute*, *Category code*, *Change Activity*, *Change Period*, *Default Activity* ... +20 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

The drawdown or rollover process in corporate lending consists of the following stages:

1. Drawdown or Rollover Request – Systematically record the duly completed request for the new drawdown or rollover and request funds from participants (in case of syndicated).
2. Rate Setting – Fix the interest screen rate and margin for the drawdown or rollover requested.
3. FX Setting – Fix the base currency rate for the drawdown or rollover request. It is applicable only if the drawdown base currency is different from the facility currency.
4. Drawdown or Rollover Completion – Activate the drawdown or rollover. Eventually remit the funds to the borrower in case of new drawdown.

Although these stages are within the same drawdown transaction, they essentially work like an individual transaction or task with their own transactional rights and Temenos Transact has to provide a workflow for instigating these stages and track their completion.

Depending on the credit agreement, currency and interest pricing option selected for a drawdown request, processing of these stages within the drawdown or rollover request do or do not occur on the same day.

Consider the below example of the schedule indicated in a credit agreement for a GBP Facility and can be drawn down in GBP or EUR and USD currencies.

| Activity | Schedule |  |  |
|---|---|---|---|
|  | GBP | EUR | USD |
| Drawdown Request | D-1 | D-3 | D-3 |
| Rate Setting | D | D-2 | D-2 |
| FX Fixing | N/A | D-2 | D-1 |

Where, D is the date of drawdown complete stage. The schedule mentioned in the table is business days and should use the holiday calendars provided if being applied across a deal, facility or loan.

Although the schedule of these stages can differentiate between the credit agreement, the banks may choose to specify a system-wide default setting by the drawing product (currency wise), which is negotiated at the individual facility or deal level.

Furthermore,many banks prefer to automate the processing of these stages and Temenos Transact has to allow them to define whether these stages can be automatically processed by the system or require user instigation. In some cases, banks may also prefer to amend a stage that is already completed (for example, change the screen rate previously set). It is important that Temenos Transact allows such amendments with a drawdown transaction.

The following steps explain the general flow of a simple drawdown process.

The drawdown steps are:

1. Creation of new drawdown request (New Arrangement Offer Activity).
2. Fixing of interest screen rate plus margin (Rate Fix Activity).
3. Fixing of exchange rate, if applicable (Update FX Activity).
4. Completion of drawdown (New Arrangement Activity).

The rollover steps are:

1. Creation of rollover request (Rollover Intent Activity).
2. Fixing of interest screen rate plus margin (Rate Fix Activity).
3. Fixing of exchange rate, if applicable (Update FX Activity).
4. Completion of rollover (Rollover Arrangement Activity).

To start the process of the customer requesting the drawdown, an offer drawing arrangement is created by the user. This offer arrangement can be used for drawdown requests. Using this offer, the interest rates and exchange rates can be fixed before the real drawdown or the drawing arrangement is live.

The currency in which the drawdown happens can be different from the currency in which the facility has been taken by the borrower. In such cases, the bank may prefer the exchange rate to be fixed by the system based on the current market conditions and prevailing rates or the customer can negotiate the rate with the bank.

The screen rate of interest is fixed for the forthcoming interest period of that loan. In such cases, the bank might choose the interest rate to be fixed by the system based on the prevailing rates or the customer can negotiate the rate with the bank.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The following sections describe the steps involved in a drawdown or rollover process.


##### Offer Arrangement

Offer capabilities available in the Accounts module is extended to the Facility and Lending modules as well. There is a set of activities available under Facility and Lending for this purpose.

The Account Property Class is used to define the Drawdown Name , Category code and Holiday calendars , and in addition to this, the following fields are used to define the Drawdown Notice days and Drawdown Completion .

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Drawdown Notice days (OFFER.NOTICE.DAYS) | Specifies the number of days in advance; a new drawdown offer has to be requested. Override or soft warning is provided if the number of days is less than the one indicated here. The notice days can be entered as a number of business working days (W) or calendar days (C/number). If the user prefers to mention two working days, then it is 2W. If the user prefers to mention two calendar days, then it is 2C/2. |
| Drawdown Completion (OFFER.EXECUTION) | Specifies the initiation type for the Drawdown Completion Stage. The options are: Auto – Drawdown is activated automatically on the effective date. Manual – The user has to activate the drawdown on or before the effective date. |

When a new drawdown offer is created with Drawdown Completion set to:

- Auto – Temenos Transact schedules and updates the AA.SCHEDULED.ACTIVITY table and automatically processes the drawdown activity on the drawdown effective date.
- Manual – Temenos Transact updates the USER.ACTIVITY table, and user can process the drawdown activity on drawdown effective date.

Notice days represent the number of days before which the customer has to notify the bank about the drawdown. If the number of days are breached, the following override message is displayed:

- Request breaches the minimum required notice days.


##### Fixing Rate in Advance

To enable the rate fixing in advance feature for a new drawdown or rollover or repricing, the following fields in the Interest Property Class can be used.

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Adv Rate Fix Days (PRIOR.DAYS) | Specifies the number of days in advance the Interest Index or Screen Rate needs to be fixed for an arrangement that is due for repricing. The Prior Days can be entered as a number of business working days (W) or calendar days (C/number). If the user prefers to mention two working days, then it is 2W. If the user prefers to mention two calendar days, then it is 2C/2. The Rate Fix Period field in Product Designer is superseded by this setting. |
| Initiation (INITIATION.TYPE) | Specifies whether the rate fix is Manual or Auto. The default option is Auto. Auto – The interest rate fix activity is triggered automatically. Manual – The user has the option to trigger exchange rate fix activity manually. |

When a new drawdown or rollover offer is created and Initiation is set to:

- Auto – Depending on the Adv Rate Fix Days , Temenos Transact schedules the activity to process on T-nD with effective date as T. The Event Date field is used to store the effective date in AA.SCHEDULED.ACTIVITY . Where, T – New drawdown or rollover or repricing date nD – Number of business days specified in Adv Rate Fix Days.
- Manual – Depending on the Adv Rate Fix Days , Temenos Transact updates the AA.USER.ACTIVITY table, the activity to process on T-nD with effective date as T. Where, T – New drawdown or rollover or repricing date nD – Number of business days specified in Adv Rate Fix Days.

For Holiday Calendars, the arrangement currency calendar is referred for fixing the date for advance rate fix.


##### Fixing the Exchange Rate in Advance (Update FX Activity)

To fix the exchange rate in advance for new drawdown or rollover or repricing where the master or parent arrangement and the child arrangement are in different currencies, the Exchange Rate Property Class is available.

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Prior Days | Specifies the number of days in advance the exchange rate need to be fixed for an arrangement that is due for pricing. The prior days can be entered as a number of business working days (W) or calendar days(C/number). If the user prefers to mention two working days, then it is 2W. If the user prefers to mention two calendar days, then it is 2C/2. |
| Initiation (INITIATION.TYPE) | Specifies whether the Exchange Rate fix Activity is Manual or Auto. The default option is Auto. Auto – The exchange rate fix activity is triggered automatically. Manual – The user has the option to trigger exchange rate fix activity manually. |
| Exchange Rate | Specifies the exchange rate that needs to be applied for the drawdown to affect the facility utilisation. This field is defaulted with exchange rate from the Exchange Rate when the parent arrangement and child arrangement are in different currencies. It can also be captured by the user. |
| On Activity | Specifies the valid set of activities that can inform the system to evaluate and default new rate (if required) from the FX table. This field works in conjunction with the Recalculate field and it dictates the activity (for example, New Drawdown, Rollover activities) that can default the rate from the FX table or when recalculation of exchange rate has to be done by the system. |
| Recalculate | Specifies whether the exchange needs to be revised for the activity specified in On Activity or not. The allowed option is Exchange Rate. |

In a multi-currency credit facility, the exchange rate is applicable if a drawdown is made in a currency different from the facility currency, and it is the rate at which the drawdown utilises the facility balances. Exchange rates are fixed at the time of new drawdown and reviewed on every rollover date and are revised depending on the exchange rate tolerance as part of the servicing. However, in some cases, banks may prefer to change as an ad-hoc basis as well.

Mostly, exchange rates are fixed by the system, but bank users may also want to override the defaulted rate, especially in syndicated deals where multiple lenders are involved.

This EXCHANGE.RATE property is added to the below set of activity classes and the user can update the exchange rate through any of the below activities or set the system to recalculate these activities, provided On Activity or Recalculate option is set.

| Activity Class | Description |
|---|---|
| LENDING-NEW-ARRANGEMENT | New Arrangement Activity |
| LENDING-CHANGE.PRODUCT-ARRANGEMENT | Change Product Activity |
| LENDING-ROLLOVER-ARRANGEMENT | Rollover Activity |
| LENDING-RESET-ARRANGEMENT | Reset Activity |
| LENDING-RENEGOTIATE-ARRANGEMENT | Renegotiate Activity |
| LENDING-CHANGE-EXCHANGE.RATE | Exchange Rate update activity |
| LENDING-RATE.FIX-EXCHANGE.RATE | FX Rate Fix Activity |
| FACILITY-NEW-ARRANGEMENT | New Arrangement Activity |
| FACILITY-RENEGOTIATE-ARRANGEMENT | Renegotiate Activity |
| FACILITY-ROLLOVER-ARRANGEMENT | Rollover Activity |
| FACILITY-CHANGE-EXCHANGE.RATE | Exchange Rate update activity |
| FACILITY-RATE.FIX-EXCHANGE.RATE | FX Rate Fix Activity |

When a new drawdown or rollover offer is created and Initiation is set to

- Auto and depending on the Prior Days , Temenos Transact schedules the activity and updates in the AA.SCHEDULED.ACTIVITY table specified in the Change Activity to process on T-nD with effective date as T. Where, T – New drawdown or rollover effective date nD – Number of business days specified in Prior Days

- Manual and depending on the Prior Days , Temenos Transact updates the AA.USER.ACTIVITY table, the activity to process on T-nD with effective date T. Where, T – New drawdown or rollover effective date nD – Number of business days specified in Prior Days

For Holiday Calendars, the arrangement currency calendar is referred for fixing the date for advance rate fix.

The Completion Activity fixes the exchange rate based on the currency table rate.

When there is a cross currency transaction, that is, the facility currency is different from the drawing currency, the Exchange Rate field is defaulted from the CURRENCY table. And whenever the exchange rate changes,

- Facility utilisation has to be updated based on the new rate.
- FX pricing notice is sent to all parties.

Consider the following example.

|  | Fx Rate | Drawdown Amount | Facility Equivalent | Available Commitment |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Initial | 1.29 | 20,000.00 | 25,703.22 | 74,296.78 |
| Revised | 1.04 | 20,000.00 | 20,703.22 | 79,296.78 |
|  |  | Diff | 5,000.00 | 5,000.00 |

Facility Unutilised (CUR ) and Facility Utilised (UTL ) balances are adjusted with the difference.


##### Creating Rollover Request (Rollover Intent Activity)

The Change Product Property Class is used to define the rollover date or period and other attributes such as Prior Days, Rollover Initiation type (Auto or Manual), Rollover activity . Depending on the condition, the rollover activity is processed automatically or manually on or before the scheduled rollover date.

The existing fields are enhanced to cater to the corporate lending requirement, that is, the existing rollover process has to be split into Request and Completion.

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Prior Days | This is an existing field. Numeric values are accepted.The Prior Days can be entered as a number of business working days(W) or calendar days (C/number). If the user prefers to mention two working days, then it is 2W. If the user prefers to mention two calendar days, then it is 2C/2. |
| Initiation (INITIATION.TYPE) | This is an existing field. If the Initiation Type is set to: Auto – Rollover Activity is automatically turned live. Manual – The user has the option to trigger any Renewal Activity Manually. If the user does not trigger any Renewal Activity within the specific days, then the system automatically triggers default Activity from the Default Activity field. |
| Change Activity | This is an existing field and allows to define offer activities. If offer activity is specified and depending on the Prior Days , the system triggers the Offer activity in advance prior to the actual rollover date and at the same time also schedules the Interest Rate, FX and Rollover completion activities depending on their Prior Days . However, if Live Activity is specified, then it processes the rollover as existing behavior. |

A default activity is introduced for intent activities. The Rollover Intent Activity can be given as default activity in the Change Product Property Class, if any of the intent activities are given as the change activity. If the intent activity is not executed by the due date, the default activity is executed by the system, which schedules or updates in the user table the rate fix and the change activity. If the completion activity is not executed by the user, then the default change activity is performed by the system.

When the Rollover Intent gets processed, it schedules the Rate Fix, FX Fix and Rollover Activity, which refreshes the previous pending activities in the AA.USER.ACTIVITY and AA.SCHEDULED.ACTIVITY . Once the Rollover is processed, it schedules or updates the Rollover Intent Activity. If any rate fix activities are performed between the intent date and the actual rollover for any effective date before the rollover effective date, it is changed to the rate fixed with the effective date as the rollover date.


##### Sub-Arrangement Condition PC

The Sub-Arrangement Condition Property Class is enabled with Optional Currency type. To allow the user to define product- and currency-wise Adv Rate Fix Days and Adv FX Fix Days, the AA attributes are added, which can be defined in the Sub- Arrangement Condition PC at the facility or deal product as a system-wide setting for currency GBP as below and can be negotiated at the individual facility arrangements.

The Sub-Arrangement Condition product condition can be added to the Deal product or at the Deal arrangement. Using the Inheritance PC, when a Facility is created under the Deal, the conditions at the Deal are inherited to the Facility Sub-Arrangement Condition.


#### 🔧 Working With

The following section describes the steps in the drawdown or rollover processes along with illustrations.


##### Offer Management

New offer deals, facility or drawing arrangements can be created using the New Offer option in the product catalogue.

The offer can be created with a future date by when the bank user expects to finalise the contract with the customer and go live with the customer. The input date can be back dated or it can be the current date, which represents when the initial offer negotiations have started with the customer. Mandatory fields do not apply at the offer stage as an offer arrangement can be opened for a prospect with just basic details of the customer, so the fields such as Amount and Term , which are generally mandatory, are not mandatory at the offer stage.

The Deal Offer Overview page is shown below.

The Deal Overview screen shows what has been agreed at the offer stage till date. The offer date is on 13 October 2020, and the offer is for a future date on 16 October 2020. The actions that can be performed in the Deal Overview screen are:

- New Facility Offer – Creates a new facility offer under this deal where the deal is the master arrangement.
- Renegotiate Offer – Amends or modifies any condition.
- Activate Offer – Moves the deal arrangement from offer to live arrangement.
- Cancel Offer – Cancels the offer arrangement if the bank could not go ahead with the customer due to any reason during the negotiations.

When the New Facility Offer Option is selected, the Product Catalogue screen appears, with the only option to create an offer facility as the deal is still in offer stage. If a live facility has to be created, then the deal must be made live.

The facility offer arrangement reference is updated in the Deal Overview screen. When the user clicks the drilldown option, the Facility Offer Overview screen opens.

The features of the Facility Offer Overview screen are same as discussed above for a deal; the option New Facility Offer is replaced with New Drawing Offer option, which is a new drawing offer that can be created under this facility (the facility is the master arrangement).

When the New Drawings Offer option is selected, the Product Catalogue screen appears, with the only option to create an offer drawing as the facility is still in offer stage. If a live drawing has to be created, then the facility must be made live.

The drawing offer arrangement reference is updated in the Facility Overview screen. When the user clicks the drilldown option, the drawing offer overview screen opens.

The above drawing offer creation date is 16 OCT 2020 and start date is 19 OCT 2020. As mentioned in the configuration, on 19 OCT 2020, the configuration of the Offer Execution field in the Account PC determines whether the conversion of offer to live arrangement is performed by the system or the user. The following screenshot shows the Account condition of the above drawing offer where the Offer Execution is Manual, so the new arrangement activity is updated in the AA.USER.ACTIVITY table (shown below), and on 19 OCT 2020, the system expects the user to perform the LENDING-NEW-ARRANGEMENT(converting to live). In the USER.ACTIVITY table, the Due Date is the target completion date of the activity, which on or before the activity needs to be completed and the Effective Date is the actual effective date of the activity.

When the Offer Execution is Auto, the new arrangement activity is updated in the AA.SCHEUDLED.ACTIVITY table (shown below), and as shown below on 23 Oct 2020, the system performs the LENDING-NEW-ARRANGEMENT (converting to live).

The user can create a new offer drawing arrangement and a lending new arrangement activity can be performed on the effective date, meaning the actual drawdown happens. All the attributes and conditions agreed at the offer stage flow when the offer arrangement gets converted to live arrangement.


##### Fixing Rate in Advance

The Advance Rate Fix functionality is applicable to new drawdowns or rollover arrangements. In the below Offer drawdown, the interest rate fix date is 19 OCT 2020.

In the Interest Condition of this arrangement (shown below), the Prior Days is 0. So, the interest has to be fixed on the date of arrangement creation. Hence, the Due Date and the Effective Date are the same. The Initiation Type is updated as manual so it is updated in the AA.USER.ACTIVITY table(shown below), and on 19 Oct 2020, the system expects the user to perform the LENDING-RATE.FIX-PRINCIPALINT activity.

If the Initiation Type is updated as Auto, it is updated in the AA.SCHEDULED.ACTIVITY table (shown below), and on 19 Oct 2020 given as Next Date (based on Prior Days ), the system initiates and performs the LENDING-RATE.FIX-PRINCIPALINT activity and picks the rate as on 19 Oct 2020 with Effective Date as 23 OCT 2020, which is the arrangement effective date.

The pending drawdown or rollover request enquiry lists the pending actions to be completed by the user. As shown in the screenshot below, there is a pending interest rate fix activity to be done maunally on 19 Oct 2020.

On completion of the Interest Rate Activity, the status changes to Pending Completion and Interest Rate activities are removed from AA.USER.ACTIVITY .

The Completion Activity fixes the interest rate based on the rate table.


##### Fixing the Exchange Rate in Advance (Update FX Activity)

The Advance Exchange Rate Fix functionality is applicable for new drawdowns or rollover arrangements. In the below offer drawdown, the Exchange Rate Fix Date is 19 OCT 2020.

In the exchange condition of this arrangement (shown below) , the Prior Days is 1W, meaning one working day, so the Exchange Rate Fix Date falls on 19 OCT 2020, one working day before 23 OCT 2020 due to holidays on other days. The exchange rate has to be fixed on or before 19 OCT 2020 and the Initiation type is updated as Manual. So, it is updated in the AA.USER.ACTIVITY table (shown below), and on 19 OCT 2020, the system expects the user to perform the LENDING-RATE.FIX-EXCHANGE.RATE activity.

Also, the On activity and Recalculate rate options are given, so the exchange rate gets recalculated when either the user or system performs the below activity.

If the Initiation type is updated as Auto, it is updated in the AA.SCHEDULED.ACTIVITY table (shown below), and on 19 OCT 2020, the system performs the LENDING-RATE.FIX-EXCHANGE.RATE activity.

The pending drawdown or rollover request enquiry lists the pending actions to be completed by the user. As shown in the screenshot below, there is a pending Exchange Rate Fix Activity to be done manually on 19 OCT 2020.

On completion of the Exchange Rate Activity and the interest rate fix automatically by the system, the Rate fix activities are removed from AA.USER.ACTIVITY and AA.SCHEDULED.ACTIVITY tables and the status changes to Pending Completion.

The Completion Activity fixes the interest rate based on the rate table.


##### Creating Rollover Request (Rollover Intent Activity)

In the below drawdown arrangement, the Rollover Date is 20 OCT 2020.

In the change product condition of this arrangement (shown below), the Change Period is 1 Day and the Initiation type is updated as Auto. So, it is updated in the AA.SCHEDULED.ACTIVITY table (shown below), and on 20 OCT 2020, the system performs the LENDING-ROLLOVER.INTENT-ARRANGEMENT activity.

After the intent activity is performed by the system, the rate fix activities and the rollover arrangement activity are scheduled by the system.

If the Initiation type is updated as Manual, as in the below arrangement, and a default activity is given, the intent activity is updated in the AA.SCHEDULED.ACTIVITY and the AA.USER.ACTIVITY tables (shown below).

If the intent activity is performed by the user, the rate fix activities and the rollover arrangement activity are scheduled or updated in the AA.USER.ACTIVITY table by the system, and the user can perform the rate fix and manual rollover.

If the intent activity is not performed by the user and default activity has been given, the system performs the default intent activity on the Next Date and the rate fix activities and the rollover arrangement activity are scheduled or updated in the AA.USER.ACTIVITY table by the system, and the user can perform the rate fix and manual rollover. If this step is also not done by the user, then the system performs the rollover. If there is no default activity, then there will be no action until the user performs it.

The AA.LENDING.ROLLOVER.MAT.7D enquiry can be used for the list of pending rollovers.


##### Sub-Arrangement Condition

The Sub –Arrangement Condition product condition can be added to the Deal product or at the Deal arrangement. When a Facility is created under the Deal, the conditions at the Deal are inherited to the Sub-Arrangement Condition Facility. When a drawing is created under the facility, based on the fields mentioned in the Attribute field of the Sub- Arrangement Condition, the values given to each of the attributes flow down to the fields or attributes of the drawing arrangement conditions. If no values are provided here, the fields take the values given at the product or arrangement conditions of the drawing.

This is the Sub-Arrangement Condition defined at the Deal and Facility level.

The Account Condition has Initiation as Manual and Prior Days is 1W.

### 4.18  Participant Charges


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The Participant Charges feature is applicable for club loans and facilities. It is part of the Participant Property Class. It is possible to configure charge split as percentage or amount in the finance arrangements for which the Participant Property class is attached.*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Amount*, *Arrangement*, *Charge*, *Rate, Amount or Ratio*, *Ratio*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

The Participant Charges feature is applicable for club loans and facilities. It is part of the Participant Property Class. It is possible to configure charge split as percentage or amount in the finance arrangements for which the Participant Property class is attached.

> **⚠️ Note:** This feature is applicable only for agent banks or banks who have sold their shares to a secondary or sub-participant.

The user can use the participant charge–related set of fields to define the charge split among the participating banks in a club loan or facility.

- If the user does not capture any information in these fields, then the charges are split on a pro-rata basis based on the current commitment percentage of the participating banks.
- If the user captures values in these fields, then the charge is split accordingly.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

To charge the borrower on a club loan, the user should use the existing definition in the Charge Property Class. To distribute the collected charge among the participating banks, the bank should use the Charges section of the Participant Property Class.

The Charges section of the Participant Property Class allows the user to define charge split based on the following criteria. The user can specify:

- A percentage rate based on which the charge must be split
- A ratio based on which the charge must be split
- An absolute number (amount) to be given to the participant

The fields used for defining the charge distribution are as follows:

- Charge – To mention the charge for which split is defined. It is mandatory to define the participant customer number and the split details if a Charge Property is defined in this field.

- Rate, Amount or Ratio – To define the split. These fields are mutually exclusive. The user can enter only one definition per Charge Property. Rate – To define the percentage of current commitment of the participant to pay out as charge to the participant.

- Amount – To define the absolute amount to be paid out as charge to the participant.
- Ratio – To specify the ratio in which the collected charge is to be distributed. When the user decides to split a charge based on Ratio, then the sum of ratios should be 100.

- If the user does not capture any detail for a charge, then the charge gets distributed on pro-rate, based on the current commitment percentage of the participants.

The user can input or edit the charge definition during the following activities:

- New arrangement activity when the participant details are captured
- Share transfer activity
- Update participant details activity


##### Accounting

The following balances are accounted for whenever charges are due in a club loan:

| Column 1 | Column 2 |
|---|---|
| Borrower Accounting |  |
| Dr DUE INF | For the charge amount |
| Participant Accounting |  |
| Accounting Type is Memo: Cr DUE PARTINF | For the calculated charge amount for participant |
| Accounting Type is Contingent: Cr DUE PART Dr DUE PARTBL | For the calculated charge amount for participant For the calculated charge amount for participant |
| Own Book Accounting |  |
| Dr DUE | For own book calculated charge |
| Cr Charge P/L | For own book calculated charge |

The system calculates the charge distribution among the lenders based on the information given in the Charges section. The calculated amount can be lesser than the actual charge levied to the borrower or borrower group. If that is the case, then the system credits the difference amount to the Charge P/L.

- Dr DUE SKIM: for the additional amount after distribution
- Cr Charge P/L: for the additional amount after distribution

The system settles the due balance when the borrower or borrower group pays the charge. Read the Participant Accounting user guide to know more about detailed participant accounting and fund distribution to the participant accounts.


#### 🔧 Working With

The system distributes the charge levied and collected from the borrower or multiple borrowers on a club loan or facility among the lenders based on the information captured in the Charge section. It is possible to setup the definition in the following ways:


##### Pro-rata Distribution

If there is no definition for a Charge property, then the system distributes charges on a pro-rata basis based on the current commitment share percentage of the participants.

Consider the following scenario for example:

- Upfront fee on a club loan – USD 500.00
- Borrower current commitment – USD 100,000.00
- Participant current commitment values are as follows:

- Participant A – USD 30,000.00
- Own bank share – USD 70,000.00

In this case, the charge split is calculated as follows:

- Charge split for Participant A = 30% of USD 500.00 = USD 150.00
- Charge split for own bank = 70% of USD 500.00 = USD 350.00


##### Non Pro-rata Distribution

If there is a definition for a Charge property, then it distributes charges on a non pro-rata basis. Refer below scenario with charge details:

| Charge | Participant | Rate | Amount | Ratio |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Upfront Fee | Participant A | 0.4 |  |  |

| Charge | Participant | Rate | Amount | Ratio |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Upfront Fee | Participant A |  | 200 |  |

| Charge | Participant | Rate | Amount | Ratio |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Upfront Fee | Participant A |  |  | 40 |
|  | Own book |  |  | 60 |


#### 📋 Tasks

Related topics:

- Lending Processes (Corporate)

To charge the borrower on a club loan, the user should use the existing definition in the Charge Property Class. To distribute the collected charge among the participating banks, the bank should use the Charges section of the Participant Property Class.

| Authorised | Enter facility arrangement ID in the Arrangement field. Click the FIND button. Click the Overview icon. |
| Arrangement Overview (Facility) | Click the New Activity option. |
| New Activities | Click the Do Activity Today icon corresponding to Update Participant Activity under Participant. |
| Arrangement Activity | In the Charges tab, enter values in the required fields. Click the Validate icon to check for errors and overrides. Click the Commit icon. Accept the overrides, if any. |

### 4.19  Participant Migration


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *When Temenos replaces the existing core banking system, all the existing contracts have to be migrated to Temenos Transact. This section deals with the takeover of club loans, specifically takeover of participant balances. For detailed steps and a general approach towards loan or facility takeover, ...*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Adj Prop Amt*, *Adjustment Amount*, *Adjustment Amt*, *Balance Type*, *Bill Reference*, *New Balance Amount*, *New Balance Amt*, *New Prop Amt* ... +6 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

When Temenos replaces the existing core banking system, all the existing contracts have to be migrated to Temenos Transact. This section deals with the takeover of club loans, specifically takeover of participant balances. For detailed steps and a general approach towards loan or facility takeover, read the following sections:

- Loan Migration
- Facility Migration

The takeover process should follow the steps mentioned in the Loan Migration section. If it is a club loan, in addition to those steps, follow the below steps during takeover:

1. Capture participant balances or bill amounts along with borrower balances or bill amounts during capture activities.
2. Adjust participant balances or bill amounts along with borrower balances or bill amounts during adjustment activities.

The bank should follow a similar procedure during facility or deal takeover. All the steps and approaches remain the same. In addition to that, the bank should capture or adjust the participant portion of the bills and balances.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

To capture the participant balances or bills, the user should use the respective set of fields in the Balance Maintenance Property Class. The following section describes the fields related to:


##### Balance Capture/Adjust

The following screenshot shows the fields related to participant balances.

| Field Name | Description |
|---|---|
| Participant | Holds the participant IDs. This is a multi-value field. The allowed values are valid participant IDs of the arrangement. |
| Balance Type | Specifies the balance type that the user captures or adjusts |
| Orig Balance Amt | Displays the original balance amount of the balance type. This field is populated by the system during adjustment |
| New Balance Amt | Displays the amount for the corresponding Balance Type. This field takes value for both capture and adjust. This is a no-sign field. The sign of the borrower New Balance Amount field determines whether the entry should be credit or debit. |
| Adjustment Amt | Displays the adjustment amount for the corresponding Balance Type. This is a no-sign field. The sign of the borrower Adjustment Amount field determines whether the entry should be credit or debit. |


##### Bills Capture/Adjust

The following screenshot shows the fields related to participant bills.

| Field Name | Description |
|---|---|
| Bill Reference | Specifies the bill reference of the adjusted bill. |
| Property | Specifies the property for which the bill is captured. |
| Participant | Specifies the participants. |
| Orig Prop Amt | Displays the original property amount for a participant in a bill. |
| O/s Prop Amt | Displays the outstanding property amount for a participant in a bill. |
| New Prop Amt | Displays the new amount for a property of a participant in a bill. This can be given during both capture and adjust. |
| Adj Prop Amt | Displays the adjustment for a property of a participant in a bill. This can be given during adjust. |


#### 🔧 Working With

The following section describes the activities used in participant migration.


##### Capture Balance Activity

While capturing the balances, if the loan or facility has participants, then the system expects the user to capture balances for participants. If the user captures only the borrower balance, the system throws an error.

- However, the system does not verify whether the balances captured are pro-rata balances based on participation percentage.
- The system does not validate whether balances for all participants are captured.
- The system validates whether the borrower balance is sum of all the participant balance in case if the own bank’s role is Agent or Agent cum Participant. If the own bank’s role is Participant, then the system does not perform this validation.
- The system allows the user to capture zero balance for a participant.
- The system validates the capture of overdraw (OVD) Commitment balance based on the setup in Term Amount. For example, if the Update Commitment on Capitalisation field in the Term Amount Property Class is set to Current and Overdraw, then the system allows to capture OVD balance only when the current (CUR) commitment balance is zero.


##### Adjust Balance Activity

Similar to the Capture Balance activity, the Adjust Balance activity also verifies if the user adjusts the participant balances when borrower balance adjustment takes place.

Apart from the validation points mentioned in the Capture Balance Activity section, the system checks whether the sum of CUR Commitment (Unutilised Commitment) and UTL Commitment (Utilised Commitment) does not exceed TOT Commitment (Total Commitment) value.


##### Capture Bill Activity

Similar to the Capture Balance Activity while capturing the bills, the system expects the user to capture bill details for participants. If the user captures only the borrower bill details, the system throws an error.

- However, the system does not verify whether the bill details captured are pro-rata bill amounts based on participation percentage.
- The system does not validate whether bill details for all participants are captured.
- The system validates whether the borrower bill amount is sum of all the participant bill amounts in case if the own bank’s role is Agent or Agent cum Participant. If the own bank’s role is Participant, then the system does not perform this validation.
- The system allows the user to capture zero bill amount for a participant.
- Suspended balances can be captured only for own book (bank’s own book).


##### Adjust Bill Activity

The Adjust Bill activity performs similar validations as the Capture Bill activity. Therefore, the user must make sure the bill amount and other details are entered correctly.

> **⚠️ Note:** The system does not perform any other integrity checks concerned with balances, and it is the users’ discretion to enter the values of balances correctly. This is applicable to all activities mentioned above.


#### 📋 Tasks

There are no Tasks available for Participant Migration feature.


#### 📊 Outputs

There are no Outputs available for Participant Migration feature.

### 4.20  Repayment-ParticipantRole

>

The amount repaid by the borrower against the payment schedule can then be used by the agent bank for settling the borrower’s outstanding amount. Subsequently, the ...*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Own Nostro*, *Payin Settlement*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

The borrower of the club loan deals only with the agent bank. Based on the agreed repayment schedule, the borrower makes the repayment. The amount repaid by the borrower against the payment schedule can then be used by the agent bank for settling the borrower’s outstanding amount. Subsequently, the agent bank distributes the payment amount to the other participants in the club loan based on their contribution share.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

Based on the repayment instructions received from the agent bank, the participant bank should use the LENDING-REPAY-PAYMENT.RULES repayment activity to settle the repayment. The amount repaid by the borrower needs to be captured (not the own bank’s share of repayment) in the repayment activity.

- The Payin Settlement field of the Settlement Property Class can have the following values: Yes - Recognises the repayment made towards the loan No - Does not recognise the repayment
- It is not mandatory to capture the Payin Account number in the settlement instruction. The account number captured in the Own Nostro field of the Participant Property Class gets debited to settle the repayment towards the loan.


#### 🔧 Working With

The repayment procedure is explained below:

1. The agent bank, after receiving the repayment amount from the borrower, credits the respective bank’s share to the beneficiary (settlement account number) captured in Participant Property Class.
2. Once the agent bank credits the repayment amount, the bank must mark that the repayment is paid by the borrower so that the bank can execute the repayment activity.
3. When the repayment activity gets executed, it debits the own bank’s share from the account number provided in the Own Nostro field and credits the own bank’s book in the loan account. The borrower’s share is also marked as repaid in the borrower’s books.

Once the repayment activity is completed, both the bills are marked as settled.

After settling the repayment, two bills are generated.

- One for the borrower with the amount to be repaid.
- Another for internal purpose with the bank’s share in the repayment.

The bill for the borrower is shown below.

An example of the own bank’s bill based on its share in the club loan is shown below.

The amount repaid by the borrower against the payment schedule can be used by the agent bank for settling the borrower’s outstanding amount. Subsequently, the agent bank distributes the payment amount to the other participants in the club loan based on their contribution share.

### 4.21  Risk Participation


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *A loan is associated with a credit risk as there is a chance for the borrower to default on the repayments. The banks need to ensure that the borrower repay the loans without fail. The banks mitigate the risk exposure in the loan by selling the risk exposure to other banks. This helps them to divers...*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Arrangement*, *Margin Operand*, *Participants*, *Participation Type*, *Participation Type set*, *Share (Amount)*, *Share Type*, *Type* ... +5 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

A loan is associated with a credit risk as there is a chance for the borrower to default on the repayments. The banks need to ensure that the borrower repay the loans without fail. The banks mitigate the risk exposure in the loan by selling the risk exposure to other banks. This helps them to diversify the Risk Portfolio. The banks that share the risk exposure from the owning bank are called Risk Participants. The owning bank can sell the risk exposure (full or partial) to the risk participants, so that the risk exposure is shared between the banks accordingly. Risk participants only share the risk and do not provide any funding to the borrower. In case of any default by the borrower, the risk participants pay the amount to the owning bank which then is decided based on the share of the Risk exposure which the Risk Participants hold.

The following are the two types of risk participants:

- Fixed Risk Participants - Risk exposure is based on a specific commitment amount of the Book commitment.
- Variable Risk Participants - Risk exposure is based on a certain percentage of the Book commitment.

Though Variable Risk Participant comes with certain percentage of commitment, the system captures only the share amount of that participant and not the percentage

During a loan sanction, corporate loans might not have risk participants attached to the contract. Later during the life term of the loan, the owing banks may have to make changes in their risk portfolio. They may prefer to increase or decrease their risk exposure in a loan. This section gives a brief description on the following concepts:

- Owning bank decreasing their risk in a loan by selling the risk exposure to risk participants
- Owning bank increasing their risk exposure in the loan by partial or complete buyback of its risk sold to the risk participants

Risk Participants receive income in the following ways and it depends on the agreement between the buying and selling counterparties.

- Flat Fees

- Risk Fees and Risk Margin


##### Write-off for Loans

Bank can write-off a loan or a bill when it has not received the repayment due for a certain period and has to follow the regulatory compliance.

As risk participants cover a portion of the loan, the risk participants pay the written off amount proportionately. These settlements happen outside the loan contract. As the risk participants pay the portion of the loan amount, the corresponding amount should be reduced from their commitment.

A loan contract can be partially or fully written off.

- When the loan is written off completely, then all the risk participants balances are reduced to zero. The bank can write off the entire funding portion it holds irrespective of the risk exposure sold.
- When there is a principal write off, that is, either the outstanding principal amount or a specific bill is being written off, then the risk participant’s balances are reduced proportionately based on the principal amount that is being written off.

In both the cases, the adjusted or reduced amount is settled by the risk participant to the own bank outside the contract.

Bills such as risk fees and risk margin that the own bank needs to pay to risk participants cannot be written off, as it is the own bank’s responsibility to pay those bills.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

A Participant Property of property Type as Risk Participant is created to add risk participant to a loan contract and then add it to the product at the product designer level.

For adding the fund participants and risk participants, two separate properties need to be created and added to the product, that is, one property with property Type set as Participant and the other with Type as Risk Participant as shown in the below screenshot.

> **⚠️ Note:** A single Participant property cannot have both the Participant and Risk Participant property types.

The bank user creates separate properties for the fund participants and risk participants, and they are added to the Participant Property class at the product group level. At product designer level, both the properties have their respective product conditions attached to them.

> **⚠️ Note:** If property type is not selected the system defaults it to Participant.

The user configures the following property classes, to calculate the Risk fees, Risk Margin and Flat Fees for the bilateral contracts or club loan contracts.

Interest Property Class is used to define the risk fees and risk margin and it can accrued and paid to the Risk participant.

To differentiate the risk participant’s Risk Fee and Risk Margin property from the other regular interest properties, the Interest property, which is created for paying out risk fee or margin consists of the Risk Participant property type along with existing Non Customer property type.

The screenshot below shows the Non Customer Interest Properties created to pay the risk margin and risk fees to the risk participant.

Charge property class is used to define the flat fees that is to be paid to the risk participants. It can be configured as an activity charge or as a scheduled charge, which can be defined in the Payment schedule.

To differentiate the Charge property that is used for paying flat fees to the risk participants from the other regular charge properties, the Charge property created for paying out the flat fees consists of the ‘Risk Participant’ property type along with existing ‘Non Customer’ and ‘Credit’ property type.

The screenshot below shows the Non Customer Charge Property created to pay the flat fees to the risk participant.

The properties created are attached to the respective Property Class of the Product in the Product Group as can be seen below

In the Product Designer, appropriate Product Conditions are attached to the Interest and Charge Properties which are attached to the Product are shown below:

The screenshot below shows the calculation source balance is defined for the Interest properties.

Once the product is published, the bank uses the risk fees and risk margin at the arrangement level.

> **⚠️ Note:** Irrespective of the bilateral or club contract with risk participants, a syndication settlement account is created. The risk fees and margin to be paid out are initially credited to the syndication settlement account and then a payment order created to pay out the funds to the respective risk participants.


#### 🔧 Working With

This section describes about selling the risk participation and risk share transfer in club loans.


##### Selling the Risk Participation

The user can add the risk participants directly while creating a new arrangement or later using Share Transfer. The Participant condition attached to a Participant property with property Type set as Risk Participant captures the risk participants while creating an arrangement contract. The following attributes are used for enabling Risk Participation:

| Field | Attribute |
|---|---|
| Participants | Defines the risk participants for the contract. It is a multi-value field and allows the banks to define multiple risk participants for the same loan contract |
| Share Type | Defines the Participant type as Risk Participants |
| Share (Amount) | Defines the share amount of the risk participants Share amount for the risk participants cannot be greater than the own bank share amount, as the total amount of risk sold cannot be greater than the risk at hand. |
| Participation Type | Captures the risk participation type, the available options are: Fixed - The participant’s share is fixed, and does not increase on a pro-rata basis when there is an increase in the global commitment. Variable - The share increases on a pro-rata basis when there is an increase in the global commitment. |

When there is a decrease in the global commitment, the participant’s share for both the Fixed and Variable type is reduced on a pro-rata basis along with own bank’s share.

The Participation Type field can be updated from Fixed to Variable and vice versa during the arrangement’s lifetime using the Update Activity for the Participant property class.

##### Risk Share Transfer

When the owning bank sells to risk participants, the formulas listed below are used to calculate the maximum amount that can be transferred, share transfer ratio and the balances of risk participants after the share transfer.

At Facility or Standalone Loan

1. Maximum Transferable Amount = Current Commitment of the Owning Bank - Current Commitment of all the Existing Risk Participants

1. Share Transfer Ratio = (Share Transfer Amount / Own Bank’s Current Commitment) * 100
2. Total = MINIMUM (Transfer Amount | Own Bank’s CUR\ + UTL + UTL )
3. CUR of RP3 = Own Bank’s CUR * Share Transfer Ratio
4. UTL of RP3 = Buyer Participant’s TOT -CUR
5. OVD of RP 3= Transfer Amount- (Buyer Participant’s CUR +UTL

At Drawing under a Facility

The transfer amount at drawing is calculated by the share transfer ratio which is calculated at the facility.

1. Transfer Amount = Own bank's current commitment * Share transfer ratio

1. TOT = MINIMUM (Transfer Amount | Own Bank’s CUR +UTL +UTL )
2. CUR = Share Transfer Ratio*Own Bank’s CUR
3. UTL = Buyer Participant’s TOT -CUR
4. OVD = Transfer Amount-(Buyer Participant’s CUR +UTL

> **⚠️ Note:** When the share transfer is done to an existing risk participant in the contract, the calculated balances are added to the already existing balances of the risk participant to whom the share transfer is done.

When the owning bank buys back its risk from the risk participants, the formulas listed below are used to calculate the maximum amount that can be bought by the owning bank, the share transfer ratio, and the balances of risk participants after the share transfer.

At Facility or Standalone Loan

1. Current Commitment = CUR + UTL + OVD
2. Share Transfer Ratio = (Share Transfer Amount/ Selling RP Current Commitment) *100
3. Total = MINIMUM (Transfer Amount | selling RP CUR +UTL
4. CUR = Selling RP CUR * Share Transfer Ratio
5. UTL = Buyer Participant’s TOT -CUR
6. OVD = Transfer Amount- (Buyer Participant’s CUR +UTL

At Drawing under a Facility

1. Transfer Amount = Selling RP current commitment * Share transfer ratio
2. TOT = MINIMUM (Transfer Amount | Selling RP CUR +UTL
3. CUR = Share Transfer Ratio * Selling RP CUR
4. UTL = Buyer Participant’s TOT -CUR
5. OVD = Transfer Amount-(Buyer Participant’s CUR +UTL

> **⚠️ Note:** The balances derived are subtracted from the existing balances of the risk participants.

##### Risk Margin and Risk Fees Operands

Risk Margin or Risk Fees Operands are available under Risk Participant Property. Default values of Risk fees and Risk margin for the contract can be entered in the respective properties. Banks can alter the default risk fees or margin for a particular risk participant by adding or reducing a margin for that particular risk participant using the Operand field in the risk participant tab.

The following Margin Operand are applicable for Risk Participants.

The Bank reduces the Risk Margin and Risk fees for a specific risk participant using Operand. The value entered in the Margin Rate field is subtracted from the default risk margin and risk fees of the contract to obtain the effective risk margin rate.

If the default risk fees defined in the contract is 0.5% and below definition is given for a risk participant, then the Risk fees paid for the risk participant becomes 0.3%.

It is used to increase the default risk margin or risk fees. The value entered in the Margin rate field add up to the default risk margin or risk fees of the contract.

When the default risk fees defined in the contract is 0.5% and below definition is given for a risk participant, then the Risk fees to be paid for the risk participant becomes 1.3%.

It is used to override the default risk margin or risk fees. The value entered by the user replaces the default risk margin or risk fees of the contract.

When the default risk fees defined in the contract is 0.5% and below definition is given for a risk participant, then the Risk fees to be paid for the risk participant becomes 1%.


###### Calculating Risk Margin and Risk Fees for Club Loan Contracts

A Club Loan Facility is created on May 24, 2021 for USD 1 million between the two risk participants MNO Bank (100114) and XYZ Bank (100369).

When the bank collects the risk fees and risk margin at the facility level,

- Risk fees is 1% (In Risk Fees Interest Property defined at Arrangement level)
- Risk margin is 0.5% (In Risk Margin Interest Property defined at Arrangement level)
- Risk margin and Risk fees due once a month
- Frequency of risk margin and risk fees to be paid are defined in payment schedule. Bill type in payment schedule condition is ‘Internal’.

MNO Bank Risk Participant

When the bank wants to customise the default risk fees or risk margin in the contract for the risk participant Barclays alone, then it uses the Operands in the risk participant property.

- The bank pays an extra 0.3% in addition to the default risk fees defined in the contract as shown in the below screenshot.

- The risk fees paid is 1.3%

- The bank pays 1% as the risk margin instead of the default 0.5% and uses the Operand ‘Override’ as shown in the screenshot below .

###### Calculating Flat Fees for the Club Loan Contracts

When a customer takes a drawing under the facility for USD 600,000, the bank collects the flat fees at the drawing level.

If the bank pays a flat fee (Non Customer Charge) of USD 5,000 to all the risk participants in the contract for every new drawing by the customer under the facility, then the bank uses the activity charge to pay this flat fee to the risk participant. Charge Method is pay .

If the bank customises this noncustomer charge for Barclays alone, then the bank pays USD 7,000 to Barclays and USD 5,000 to JP Morgan. The change in flat fee charge for Barclays is done in the Charges tab under the Risk Participant Property as shown in the screenshot given below.

Flat fees bills paid are seen in the Drawing Overview screen as below. The bills are auto settled.


##### Activities for Loan Write-Off

Following are activities for loan write-off:

- LENDING-WRITE.OFF.BILL-BALANCE.MAINTENANCE - Use to write off only the bills of the loan.
- LENDING-WRITE.OFF.BALANCE-BALANCE.MAINTENANCE - Use to write off specific balances of the loan like outstanding principal (partial write off)
- LENDING-WRITE.OFF-BALANCE.MAINTENANCE - Use to write off the entire loan (full write off)

### 4.22  Share Transfer


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *In a syndicated or club loan, some banks prefer to reduce their share in the loan or completely sell off their share, by transferring it to the existing banks in the loans or to a completely new bank. This can be done using share transfer.*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Arrangement*, *Buy Participant*, *Consent Party*, *Consent Type*, *Consent required*, *Min Trade %*, *Min Trade Amt*, *Own Bank* ... +4 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

In a syndicated or club loan, some banks prefer to reduce their share in the loan or completely sell off their share, by transferring it to the existing banks in the loans or to a completely new bank. This can be done using share transfer.

Transfer of shares can be done in two ways:

- Assignment sell – The transfer is done with the knowledge of the borrower and other participants. The new lender who bought the shares acts as an assignee.
- Participation sell – The transfer need not be done with the knowledge of the borrower and other participants. The new lender who bought the shares acts as a sub-participant or a risk participant. Sub participation – The original participant or seller owns the risk of default from the borrower side as well as the sub-participant side. Risk participation – The original participant or seller continues to lend the borrower but the risk of default from the borrower side is borne by the risk participant for which they receive a fee income.

In club loans, an agent acts as a moderator between the borrower and the group of lenders. If a participant transfers its share with the approval of the borrower, then the agent performs the share transfer and maintains the accounts for the changes done during the share transfer in the system and for the new participant. The agent might charge a fee to do the share transfer. In case if the participant sells to lenders without the knowledge of borrower and other lenders, then they do the share transfer only in their system and the new participant acts as a sub participant or risk participant.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

There is no configuration required from the user side to perform a share transfer.

The share transfer can be executed from the Share Transfer Property Class at the arrangement level. It is a transaction class rather than a property class, which means it is not required for the user to attach the Share Transfer Property Class at the product designer level to perform share transfer at the arrangement level.


#### 🔧 Working With

The user can initiate the share transfer activity by clicking on the arrow mark available beside each of the participant in the Overview screen of the facility or drawing contract as shown in the following screenshot:

The user has to provide the details of the buyer and the seller in the respective fields in the Share Transfer Property Class. If own bank is a buyer or seller, then the Own Bank field should be updated with either BUY or SELL option.

If Temenos Transact owning bank acts as an agent or agent cum participant and share transfer happens between the participants, then both the Sell Participant and Buy Participant fields must be updated.

When the buyer is a new participant and not an existing participant in the contract, then the user should update the role of the buyer under the Participant Role field and his beneficiary details in the Settlement Instructions tab as part of the share transfer activity.

Any skims for interest or fee agreed as part of the share transfer is recorded in the SKIMS tab. The transfer amount has to be entered in the Amount field.

The maximum amount that can be transferred from an existing participant can be the sum of available commitment amount (CUR COMMITMENT) and the outstanding amount (CUR ) excluding the amount which has been made due (DUE ).


###### Examples:

Consider a term loan of USD 1M created for a customer on January 1, 2019. The loan consists of two participants:

- RBS – Own bank who is an agent cum participant and responsible for 20% of commitment amount
- SEK Bank of Sweden – Participant (Participant ID – 100001) responsible for 80% of commitment amount.

Consider a disbursement of USD 600,000 has been made already. Therefore, the balances will be as below:

On January 15, 2019, a principal of USD 100,000 is made due and repayment is yet to be made. Now, the balances will look as below.

Consider, on January 15, 2019, the SEK bank performs a share transfer of USD 300,000 to Deutsche Bank (Participant ID - 100002) who is a new participant to the loan.

Now, SEK bank’s available amount for transfer is not 800,000, which is their total share in this contract. Rather, they are eligible to transfer only 720,000, which is the sum of available commitment (320,000) and utilised commitment (480,000) excluding the delinquent balance (80,000).

Out of their available amount for transfer (720,000), SEK transfers 300,000 only to Deutsche bank. So, the ratio at which share transfer is performed can be calculated as below:

(300,000/720,000)*100 = 41.6666666666667% (Rounded to 13 decimal places)

Total commitment of the buyer is minimum of either the transfer amount or the seller’s (CUR + UTL ). Here, TOT of the new buyer is calculated as Minimum of (300,000, (320,000 + 480,000)) = 300,000.

The available commitment CUR of the buyer is calculated as CUR of the seller * transfer Ratio. Here, the available commitment of the buyer CUR = 320,000 *41.6667 % = 133,333.33

The utilized commitment (UTL ) of the buyer = the total commitment (TOT ) of the buyer - the available commitment (CUR ) of the buyer. Here, UTL = 300,000 –133,333.33 = 166,666.67

The principal outstanding with the customer (CUR ) of the buyer = CUR of the seller * Transfer Ratio. In the example,

CUR (B) = 400,000* 41.6667 = 166,666.67

The overdrawn commitment (OVD ) of the buyer = Transfer amount - (CUR of the buyer + UTL of the buyer). Here, OVD of the buyer is 300,000 – (133,333.3333 + 166,666.6667) = 0

Finally, the balances look like below post share transfer.

After the share transfer is done, the interest calculation of the transferred amount is done for the buying participant from the day of effective share transfer. The interest accrued until that date remains with the seller participant bank.

Share transfer after Partial Disbursement

Consider a term loan of USD 1M created for a customer on April 18, 2023. The loan consists of two participants:

- Own bank who is an agent cum participant and responsible for 20% of commitment amount
- Abn Amro Securities (Cust ID: 100112)– Participant (Participant ID – 100112) responsible for 80% of commitment amount.

The system capitalises the activity charge of USD 500 creating for upfront when the arrangement and disburses a loan amount of USD 600,000 to the borrower.

Borrower balance is shown in the screenshot below.

Consider that the own bank performs a share transfer of USD 120,000 to JP Morgan Chase (Participant ID - 100115) who is a new participant to the loan on April 19, 2023.

Now, own bank’s Maximum transferrable amount is

CUR (80,000) + CUR (120,100) = USD 200,100.

Formula to calculate the new participant balances after the share transfer is

Transfer Ratio (TR) = (Transfer Amount / Max Transferrable amount) * 100%.

Here, the transfer ratio = (120,000/200,100) * 100% = 59.97%.

Total commitment of the buyer is minimum of either the transfer amount or the seller’s (CUR + UTL ) *Transfer Ratio. Here, TOT of the new buyer is calculated as Minimum of (120,000, [(80,000+120,000) *59.97%] =119,940.03

> **⚠️ Note:** When the Update Commit on Capitalization is set as ‘Overdrawn’, the total commitment of the buyer is calculated considering the transfer ratio. When the Update Commit on Capitalization is set as ‘Current and Overdrawn’, TOT of the new buyer is Minimum (Transfer Amount, (CUR + UTL ) Whereas, Update Commit on Capitalization is set as ‘Overdrawn’, TOT of the new buyer is Minimum (Transfer Amount, [CUR + UTL ] *Transfer ratio)

The available commitment CUR of the buyer is calculated as CUR of the seller * Transfer Ratio. In the example, the available commitment of the buyer CUR = 80,000*59.97% = 47,976.01.

The Utilized commitment (UTL ) of the buyer is calculated as the total commitment (TOT ) of the buyer minus the available commitment (CUR ) of the buyer. In the example, UTL = 119,940.03 – 47,976.01 = 71964.02

The principal outstanding with the customer (CUR ) of the buyer is calculated as CUR of the seller * Transfer Ratio. In the example, CUR (B) = 120,100 * 59.97% = 72,023.98

The overdrawn commitment (OVD ) of the buyer is calculated Transfer amount minus (CUR of the buyer plus UTL of the buyer). In the example, OVD of the buyer is 120,000 – (47,976.01 + 71,964.01) = 59.97.

###### Third Party Consent for Assignment Trades

Assignment type of trade requires consent from the borrower, agent, and other relevant stakeholders in the syndication. Participant property class defines the requirement of the consent and the parties from whom the consent is required.

The Third Party tab comprises of the following fields:

- Consent Type – Indicates the type of the consent given
- Consent Party – Indicates the party who is giving the consent
- Consent Given – Indicates whether the consent is given or not (Yes or No). If consent given is ‘No’, assignment transfer will not be allowed for that arrangement.
- Consent Date – Indicates the date on which the consent is given

The Third-Party tab captures the consent status and the consent date for an assignment type of trade.

The Consent Type and Consent Party fields are defaulted automatically in the Share transfer Property Class when defined in Participant Property Class. It is mandatory to define the Consent given and the Consent date fields in Share transfer Property Class to initiate an assignment transfer, that is transfer of shares to existing or new participants.

If the Consent required is set as ‘No’ in Participant Property Class, it is not mandatory to define anything under the Third Party tab.

> **⚠️ Note:** If Min Trade Amt or Min Trade % is specified in Participant Property Class, the same are validated in Share Transfer Property Class once the amount is defined. Third Party tab is not valid for participation (sub-participants) or risk participant transfer.

### 4.23  Splits Merge Rollover


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Throughout the lifetime of the deal or facility, the drawings under them are rolled over and repriced multiple times in synchronous with the interest periods. During such rollovers the bank and the borrower can decide to do one of the following:*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Arrangement*, *Charge, Charge Participant, Charge Part Rate, Charge Part Amount, Charge Part Perc*, *Rollover Type*, *Skim Property, Margin Oper, Margin Rate, Negative Rate*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

Throughout the lifetime of the deal or facility, the drawings under them are rolled over and repriced multiple times in synchronous with the interest periods. During such rollovers the bank and the borrower can decide to do one of the following:

- Straight rollovers (one-to-one) - Rollover and reprice a contract with no change in terms and conditions.
- Conversion during rollovers (one-to-one) - During rollovers the bank and the borrower can decide to change the product of the drawing from one to another, resulting in change of terms and conditions.
- Splits (one-to-many) - During rollover a drawing can be split into multiple drawings, each with different terms and conditions.
- Merge (many-to-one) - During rollover multiple drawings can be merged into a single drawing, with or without changes in terms and conditions.
- Merge (many-to-many) – During rollover, multiple drawings can be partially merged into more than one drawing. The original loans are retained with revised principal balance.

While rolling over into a contract with new terms and conditions (points 2, 3 and 4), the workflow remains similar to a new drawing creation (i.e.) the new rolled over arrangement can be created in either as an offer or directly as an arrangement. Terms and conditions, interest rate, forex rate and so on are fixed in advance.

A corporate borrower can make multiple drawdowns under a commitment. Two or more drawdowns can be merged into one drawdown, or a single drawdown can be split into more than one drawdown based on borrower’s request. For club loans under the facility, the amortisation of charge happens only for own bank share.

During the split or merger transition, the unamortised upfront fee parked in the suspense account of the original drawings are transferred to the new drawing created on a pro-rata basis. The transfer of fee modifies the cash flow of the drawings involved in the transactions. When the Facility commitment is not fully utilised, the upfront fee will be recognised to PL on facility expiry or maturity date.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The SPLITS.MERGES transaction class is used to either split a single loan into multiple loans, merge multiple loans into a single loan, or rollover a loan or keep the original loan active during split or merge or simply rollover a loan.

Read Configuring Splits, Merge and Rollover - Bilateral Loans for more information.


#### 🔧 Working With

The merge, rollover and split process is same as bilateral splits and merges except for the participant lender(s) related shares and bills in the Target arrangements.

In the Target arrangement, the lender shares are calculated based on the outstanding balance at the source.

- The Participant property class inherits the definitions of Skim And Charges tab from the facility to the drawing(s) created under that facility. Skims – The Skim Property, Margin Oper, Margin Rate, Negative Rate fields are allowed for negotiation at the drawing level. Charges – The Charge, Charge Participant, Charge Part Rate, Charge Part Amount, Charge Part Perc are allowed for negotiation at the drawing level.
- Rollover bills are issued to the borrower and participants for their respective shares.
- Rollover bills are re-issued if there is a change in the lender shares of the source arrangement(s) due to share transfer.
- Rollover bills are made due for the outstanding amount both for borrower and participants on effective date of rollover.

Refer Splits, Merges and Rollover to more about the Merge, Split and Rollover Processing in detail.

During the split or merge of a club loan, the unamortised fee of own bank share is transferred from the source loans to the new loans on pro-rata basis of the share in the new loans. If the target arrangement has increase in commitment, then an additional portion of the fee (Itemized type) from the facility is transferred to the drawing. If there is a rounding-off difference, then it is realized in the P and L category.

### 4.24  SubParticipant


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *In a club loan or facility contract, any bank in the consortium may prefer to sell a part of their share to another bank that is not a part of the consortium. Transact supports this sub- participation and a bank that is not necessarily an agent can sell a part or entire share to another bank which i...*
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Banks Role*, *Limit Id*, *Participant Role*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

In a club loan or facility contract, any bank in the consortium may prefer to sell a part of their share to another bank that is not a part of the consortium. Transact supports this sub- participation and a bank that is not necessarily an agent can sell a part or entire share to another bank which is not a part of the club loan consortium. The Sub-Participant role enables this feature.

The bank user can use the Participant Role field in the Participant Property Class to define the sub-participants.

- If the role is Participant, the lender is officially part of the consortium and they are obliged for their share in the club loan.
- If the role is Sub-Participat, the lender is not officially part of the consortium. It means that one of the lenders have sold their share outside the consortium. In this case the obligation lies with the bank which has sold its share to another bank which is not part of the consortium and not with the bank which has bought the share.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The bank user can use the Banks Role field to define whether the participant is part of the consortium or the participant is a secondary participant to whom the bank has sold a part of its share unofficially to another bank.

- If the Banks Role is set as Agent , then it can have both participants and sub-participants because they manage the consortium and also can sell their share to a bank not part of the consortium.
- If the Banks Role is set as Participant, then they can have only sub-participant definitions in the Participant Property Class as they cannot manage the consortium or they don’t store the consortium bank share details.

Accounting entries are similar to Participant accounting. Read the Participant Accounting user guide for more information.


#### 🔧 Working With

The working is similar to the Participant workflow. The only difference is that the Sub-participant is not obliged to the club loan consortium rather only to the bank which sold their shares to them. Similarly, the bank which sold the shares outside the consortium is obliged to the consortium.

Read the Participant user guide for workflow information.


#### 📋 Tasks

Related topics:

- Lending Processes (Corporate)

In a club loan, any bank in the consortium may prefer to sell a part of their share to another bank that is not a part of the consortium. Transact supports sub- participation and a bank that is not necessarily an agent can sell a part or entire share to another bank which is not a part of the club loan consortium. The Sub-Participant role enables this feature.

The bank user can use the Participant Role field in the Participant Property Class to define the sub-participants.

- If the role is Participant, the lender is officially part of the consortium and they are obliged for their share in the club loan.
- If the role is Sub-Participant, the lender is not officially part of the consortium. It means, one of the lenders have sold their share outside the consortium. In this case, the obligation lies with the bank that has sold its share to another bank which is not part of the consortium and not with the bank that has bought the share.

In the Facility Commitment and Term section, enter values in the following fields: Under Basic Amount Term Schedule Commitment Type Start Date End Date Amount In the Limit section, enter a value in the following field (Optional): Limit Id (create validation and utilisation limits in the LIMIT application) In the Exchange Rate section, enter values in the required fields. ### 4.25  Tax


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The financial institution applies tax on interest and charges levied on the club facility and club loan. The tax functionality supports calculating proportional tax when there is a change in the tax structure during the interest payment period. The Tax property class is optional at the product line ...*
> 
> **Applications:** `TAX`, `TAX.TYPE`, `TAX.TYPE.CONDITION`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Arrangement*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

The financial institution applies tax on interest and charges levied on the club facility and club loan. The tax functionality supports calculating proportional tax when there is a change in the tax structure during the interest payment period. The Tax property class is optional at the product line level for Lending and Facility.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

During issuing bills, the system calculates tax, collects it as a debt, and capitalises the respective interests or charges. The calculated tax is updated against the TAX property in the bill.

The system calculates tax with the support of the following core tables:

- TAX : Provides the percentage rate of tax, category, and tax operand details for each code.
- TAX.TYPE : Provides the ID for the tax.
- TAX.TYPE.CONDITION : Includes the TAX.TYPE record and the TAX code.

The financial institution can define tax ( TAX or TAX.TYPE.CONDITION ) at the AA product level, at either property class or property level and can amend or remove the values at the arrangement level to allow zero or no tax calculation.

Sample product conditions for defining tax are given below.


#### 📋 Tasks

Tax property class primarily controls the taxes applicable for the arrangement. Taxes can be based on properties of interest and charges property classes.
