**ClubLoans**

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Banks Role | Specifies the role of the Temenos Transact owning bank. Allowed values are: Agent, Agent Cum Participant and Participant. |
| Participants | Specifies the Participant ID of each of the lenders who are part of the contract. It should be a valid customer (Customer ID or Mnemonic from the customer application). |
| Share Amount | Specifies the participant commitment share amount on the total loan amount. Validation is made to ensure the sum of participant share amount including Own Share amount does not exceed the borrower amount or the loan commitment amount. |
| Share % | Indicates the participant commitment share in percentage on the total loan commitment. This is a system-calculated field. |
| Own Share | Specifies the owning bank commitment share in amount. The system populates the own share amount based on the participant’s share amount. The net share amount of the owning bank and the participant banks’ amounts must be equal to the borrower amount. |
| Own Share% | Specifies the owning bank commitment share in percentage. It is system calculated based on the owning bank share amount. |
| Participant Role | Specifies if a participant is a silent or sub-participant. The allowed values are Yes and Null. |

**ClubLoans**

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Currency | Specifies the currency to match currency-specific beneficiary account for the participants. The allowed values are valid currencies in AA. |
| Property Class | Specifies the property class to match property class-specific beneficiary account for the participants. The allowed values are valid property classes in AA. |
| Property | Specifies the property to match property-specific beneficiary account for the participants. The allowed values are valid property in AA. |
| Beneficiary ID | Specifies the participant beneficiary account details for cash outflow (specific to Currency/Property/Property Class or a combination). The account indicated in the beneficiary is used to credit participant share upon borrower repayment. The allowed values are valid ID from the BENEFICIARY application. |
| Beneficiary PO | Denotes the payment order product that should be used by the agent to settle the participants share when a repayment is made by the borrower. |

**ClubLoans**

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Property | Specifies the property for which skims and margins are to be applied. Only Interest is allowed. |
| Operand | Specifies the skim and margin operand to be used. The allowed value is Sub. |
| Skim rate | Specifies the skim margin rate that needs to be applied for the participant share. |
| Negative rate | Specifies when the skims have to be blocked in case of All-in-Rate results in a negative rate after deducting the skims. The options allowed are: NO - Rate for the participant is applied as zero. Block Margin - Rate for the participant is applied as borrower rate and skim rate is ignored. |

**ClubLoans**

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Charge | Specifies the charge property for which different rate, amount or ratio will be applied for distributing the fee (charged to the borrower) to the participants. Below are examples, where there are two participants Bank A and Agent bank (Own) and the borrower is charged a fee. Scenario 1 : If a rate is defined for each participant, the fee to be distributed to the participant is calculated as a rate on current commitment amount of the participant. In the following example, the fee rate is defined as .08 and .12 for Bank A and agent bank, respectively; hence the fee to be distributed is USD 160 to Bank A and USD 840 to agent bank. Charge - Upfront Fee Participant 1 - Bank A Current Commitment - 200,000 Fee Rate (percentage) - 0.08 Fee - 160 Participant 2 - Agent Bank (Own Share) Current Commitment - 700,000 Fee Rate (percentage) - 0.12 Fee - 840 Scenario 2: If an amount is defined, it is treated as the fee amount to be distributed to the participants. In the following example, the fee amount is defined as USD 200 and USD 700 for Bank A and Agent bank, respectively.Hence, the fee to be distributed is USD 200 to Bank A and USD 700 to Agent bank. Charge - Upfront Fee Participant 1 - Bank A (Swedbank) Fee - 200 Participant 2 - Agent Bank (Own share) Fee -700 Scenario 3 : If a ratio is defined for each participant, the fee to be distributed to the participants is calculated as a percentage on the amount charged to the borrower. In the following example, the fee ratio is defined as 100% for Bank A; hence, the fee charged to the borrower of USD 500 is given entirely to the Agent bank. Charge - Agency Fee Participant - Agent Bank (Own share) Charge Amount - 500 Fee Ratio(percentage) - 100 Fee - 500 |
| Participant | Allows to select a valid Participant ID for which the defined charge is calculated and distributed based on the definition of Participant Fee share details (rate, amount or ratio) here. Input here ignores the charge pro-rata (based on the participant commitment share percentage). The allowed values are: Valid Participant of the arrangement. OWN (refers to the agent bank) |
| Rate | Specifies the fee rate per participant. The fee amount for each of the specified participant is calculated as a rate on the current commitment amount (available+ utilised) of that participant. |
| Amount | Specifies the fee amount per participant. |
| Ratio | Specifies the fee ratio per participant. The fee amount for each of the specified participant is calculated as a percentage on the total fee amount charged to the borrower or customer. |

**ClubLoans**

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Allow Trading | Allows to select whether trading is allowed for the facility or drawing. Allowed options are ‘Yes’ and ‘No’. If set as ‘Yes’, assignment transfer is allowed for the arrangement. If set as ‘No’ share transfer to existing or new participants won’t be allowed. |
| Min Trade Amt | Specifies the minimum share transfer amount. It is optional field where, Blank means trade allowed for all amounts. Input is not allowed when the Allow Trading field is set to No |
| Min Trade % | Specifies the minimum share transfer amount as a percentage of agreement Amount that is defined in Term Amount property class . Input is not allowed when Allow Trading is set as ‘No’ Min Trade Amt & Min Trade % are mutually exclusive to each other and user can input either one. |
| Consent Required | Specifies if share transfer requires third party consent. It is an optional field. Default option is ‘No’ If the Allow Trading field is set to No, automatically this field is defaulted to No |
| Consent Type | Specifies the consent which is mandatory for a share transfer or a loan trade transaction. The option available is Trade Acceptance. It should be a valid option in the EB.LOOKUP table Input is mandatory if the Consent Required field is set to Yes. |
| Consent Party | Specifies the party whose consent is mandatory for share transfer. The options are: BORROWER AGENT Banks can have other custom options by adding it to EB.LOOKUP table Input is mandatory if the Consent Required is set as Yes. |

**OfferArrangement AdvanceRateFix**

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Drawdown Notice days (OFFER.NOTICE.DAYS) | Specifies the number of days in advance; a new drawdown offer has to be requested. Override or soft warning is provided if the number of days is less than the one indicated here. The notice days can be entered as a number of business working days (W) or calendar days (C/number). If the user prefers to mention two working days, then it is 2W. If the user prefers to mention two calendar days, then it is 2C/2. |
| Drawdown Completion (OFFER.EXECUTION) | Specifies the initiation type for the Drawdown Completion Stage. The options are: Auto – Drawdown is activated automatically on the effective date. Manual – The user has to activate the drawdown on or before the effective date. |

**OfferArrangement AdvanceRateFix**

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Adv Rate Fix Days (PRIOR.DAYS) | Specifies the number of days in advance the Interest Index or Screen Rate needs to be fixed for an arrangement that is due for repricing. The Prior Days can be entered as a number of business working days (W) or calendar days (C/number). If the user prefers to mention two working days, then it is 2W. If the user prefers to mention two calendar days, then it is 2C/2. The Rate Fix Period field in Product Designer is superseded by this setting. |
| Initiation (INITIATION.TYPE) | Specifies whether the rate fix is Manual or Auto. The default option is Auto. Auto – The interest rate fix activity is triggered automatically. Manual – The user has the option to trigger exchange rate fix activity manually. |

**OfferArrangement AdvanceRateFix**

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Prior Days | Specifies the number of days in advance the exchange rate need to be fixed for an arrangement that is due for pricing. The prior days can be entered as a number of business working days (W) or calendar days(C/number). If the user prefers to mention two working days, then it is 2W. If the user prefers to mention two calendar days, then it is 2C/2. |
| Initiation (INITIATION.TYPE) | Specifies whether the Exchange Rate fix Activity is Manual or Auto. The default option is Auto. Auto – The exchange rate fix activity is triggered automatically. Manual – The user has the option to trigger exchange rate fix activity manually. |
| Exchange Rate | Specifies the exchange rate that needs to be applied for the drawdown to affect the facility utilisation. This field is defaulted with exchange rate from the Exchange Rate when the parent arrangement and child arrangement are in different currencies. It can also be captured by the user. |
| On Activity | Specifies the valid set of activities that can inform the system to evaluate and default new rate (if required) from the FX table. This field works in conjunction with the Recalculate field and it dictates the activity (for example, New Drawdown, Rollover activities) that can default the rate from the FX table or when recalculation of exchange rate has to be done by the system. |
| Recalculate | Specifies whether the exchange needs to be revised for the activity specified in On Activity or not. The allowed option is Exchange Rate. |

**Splits Merge Rollover**

| Field Name | Description |
|---|---|
| Rollover Type | Defines the type of rollover is Split, Merge or Rollover. |
| XX | Captures the source arrangement ids that are to be merged or split. In case of standalone loan splits/merges, the source arrangement id ise auto populated. In case of loans under facility the source arrangement id will have to be entered. |
| XX - Source Arrangement Product | Displays the product of the source arrangement and is a system maintained field. |
| XX - Source Currency | Displays the currency of the source arrangement and is a system maintained field. |
| XX - Outstanding Principal | Displays the outstanding principal amount and is a system maintained field. |
| XX - Repay Amount | Defines the amount that the borrower is willing to repay on the split or merge date. It must not be greater than the outstanding amount. But this field is restricted for the source arrangements that are retained as a part of the rollover. |
| Source Rollover Amount | Indicates the net outstanding amount after the borrower repayment that is available for rollover, splits and merges. This is a system maintained field. |
| XX | Holds the target arrangement id and is a system maintained field. If NEW value is entered in this field, the system generates a new ID on its own. Alternatively, and users can define their own ID. Likewise, if the user wishes to continue with the original loan, then the loan ID of the original loan must be entered in this field. |
| XX - Target Arr Product | Defines the product of the new target arrangement. The user can change the product of the target arrangement and the same should be one among the allowed products defined at the parent level. Change of product is not allowed for the target arrangements, which are one of the source arrangements that are retained as part of the rollover. |
| XX - Target Currency | Displays the currency of the target arrangement and is defaulted based on the source arrangement currency. |
| XX - Target Rollover Amount | Displays the amount that is rolled over to the target arrangement. |
| XX - Commitment Increase | Defines any increase in commitment of the loan during the loan rollover. |
| XX - Total Target Amount | Displays the net amount for which the new target arrangement is created. This is a system maintained field. |
| XX -Target Repricing Period | Defines the repricing period for the target arrangements. This will be used to calculate the next interest rate repricing period and the next rollover date. It can be given as a period, not as a date. The valid suffixes are D/W/M/Y. |

**Misc**

| S.NO | Parameters | Description |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Account | The Account property class is used by all the products which are account based. This property class primarily controls the description of the account. The ACCOUNT property allows the user to define and control balance treatment, posting restriction, linked account number (for memo accounts), currency market, date convention related setup for the account. Although the account names are account specific, generic titles can be defaulted from the product and can be replaced or given additional detail at the arrangement level. Each product defined and processed in AA can have a single ACCOUNT Property defined. |
| 2 | Activity Charges | The Activity Charges property class defines the charges that have to be applied when a particular activity is triggered on the arrangement. The charges so applied can be made due, capitalised or deferred. The user can enable auto settle the charges made due from unallocated credit balance by setting this to Yes. In accounts, charges are enabled for dormancy, settle payoff and ageing. This property class is also extensively used for all AA related modules, charges are set for various other activities. |
| 3 | Activity Restriction | The Activity Restriction property class is used to specify a restriction on a particular transaction. The restriction rules including the relevant periodic attributes and activities are defined in the product condition. These rules are then used to define activity based or property based restrictions. A rule if broken can be set to result in an override or error. A charge can be attached for this and can be set to be made due, capitalised or deferred. For the AR module, activity restriction is extensively used for restricting transactions by number, type, and so on. This is also extensively used in other modules to restrict the user from doing various user activity based on the life cycle status of contracts. |
| 4 | Balance Availability | The Balance Availability property class allows the user to control the following features pertaining to AR module: Notice amount and period, which needs to be given by a customer for withdrawing money from his account. Default Credit Check and Available Balance update related set up. Activity class or Activity specific credit check, and NSF related fees pertaining to it Tolerance Amount or Tolerance Currency - To indicate the grace amount, which is the allowed overdraft before the bank imposes NSF or OD fees. Overdraft Grace Period - To waive the NSF fee levied on the account, if the customer clears the debit balance within the stipulated grace period. |
| 5 | Dormancy | The Dormancy property class allows the user to control the parameterisation of inactive or dormant accounts and movement of the same into various buckets at the arrangement or product level. The same can be controlled based on period, and some exceptions or rules also can be added for evaluation and movement. The user can include or exclude certain activity or activity class for the evaluation. It is possible to, Configure different Dormancy status based on the period of inactivity Specify different charges and charging frequency for each Dormancy status Apply some exception rule filtering at an individual arrangement level (for example, account is in debit balance) and such rules can either be an API or a rule created using the Rules Engine Specify notices and notice frequency for each Dormancy status Specify Activities or Activity Classes or Activity Initiation Types which are qualified to keep an account active. Auto Reset can be enabled based on status or on Activity Type. |
| 6 | Facility | The Facility is a service component for financial products designed using arrangement architecture. The Facility property class controls the list of available services for an arrangement account. When an external activity (financial or non-financial) is triggered and the corresponding service group is mapped to an activity through Activity Mapping and EB.EVENTS . And the same came allowed or restricted or charged corresponding error message is raised to stop the activity. |
| 7 | Inheritance | The Inheritance property class is used for BN pool structure for inheriting the product conditions set at Parent level arrangement to the Child level arrangement accounts. The product conditions that are set for inheritance are attached to Property records with type as Inheritance Only. The properties to be inherited can be controlled both at source and target level. |
| 8 | Interest | The Interest property class is used for all interest definition and processing in AA. A product defined and processed in AA can have multiple interest properties defined (for example, principal interest, penalty interest, commission, etc. Interest rates can be defined as fixed , floating , periodic or linked rate (referring an INTEREST property from other arrangement), routine based calculation. Tiered interest can also be defined. Further it is possible to define a negative rate, minimum interest amount and waive the interest. Interest adjustment can be done in run time, and adjustment related detail or values can be captured in adjustment related fields. |
| 9 | Limit | The Limit property class primarily controls the use of LIMIT module by the product. We can set up single or shared limit. We can define the LIMIT.REFERENCE applicable for a specific product such that the system defaults the same in an arrangement. For a new limit, at the arrangement level, the LIMIT.SERIAL has to be given as NEW. The AR module can have self-contained secondary limit without having actual limit attached to it. Overdraft status or notice for AR module is handled inside the Limit Property class. Further Limits can be set to use the LIMIT module (AL and AD) or it can be managed only within the arrangement architecture framework. |
| 10 | Payment Schedule | The Payment Schedule property class is used by all products which have amounts billed (that is,made due) or capitalised or Pay. A Payment Schedule can be comprised of one or more payment definitions with conditions such as payment Type and Method, arrangement properties, dates and amounts. The AA.PAYMENT.TYPE application is used to define the standard payment types such as constant, linear, actual and fixed equal and so on, that can be used by a product. This payment type is then attached to each payment schedule definition. The start and end date can be specified, the user can specify the repayment of arrangement to commence after ‘n’ months from the arrangement date or ‘n’ months before the maturity or ‘n’ months after the change product or reset and rollover has happened. |
| 11 | Periodic Charges | The Periodic Charges property class acts as a container to group different charge properties and calculate a periodic charge amount. The Payment Schedule property class drives this property class. A periodic charge property can be attached in payment schedule and on schedule date periodic charge amount is calculated. At the arrangement level adjustment can be done by the user on whole periodic charge. |
| 12 | Statement | The Statement property class is used to define the legacy ACCT.STATEMENT feature at the AA level. Statements may be produced daily (every working day), every 1-9 weeks, twice a month (on the 15th and the last day of the month) or every 1-12 months on any day of the month. Up to nine statement cycles may be specified for each account, and each statement cycle is independent. In addition to this, special interim statements can be enabled. This property class also controls whether or not advices are to be produced when interest and charges are applied, and whether detailed interest statements (interest scale) should be produced. Within a statement cycle, it is possible to define multiple frequencies with a combination of weekly and monthly, such that statements are produced on the dates specified by both frequencies, but only contain details of entries since the last statement in that cycle. |
